author: jblakey-google
body:
## Overview
This PR introduces end-to-end integration support for **Genesys Cloud** voice interactions with **Google Agent Assist** embedded directly inside the **Salesforce Lightning Experience (LWC)**. 

It establishes real-time bi-directional audio streaming via Genesys AudioHook, asynchronous conversation provisioning and Redis-backed session discovery, OIDC-based service-to-service authentication, and resilient cross-tab conversation state management in the Salesforce LWC runtime.

---

## Key Changes & Architecture Highlights

### 1. Salesforce LWC Platform Service (`GenesysCloudPlatformService.js`)
- **Interaction Discovery**: Implemented listeners for Genesys Open CTI softphone `postMessage` window events, cross-tab `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` events, and URL parameters.
- **Apex Fallback**: Integrated fallback lookup via `AgentAssistAuthController.getLatestInteractionId` against `Task.CallObject` for screen-popped case records.
- **Resilient Polling & Stale State Eviction**: Implemented exponential backoff polling (`/conversation-name?conversationIntegrationKey=<UUID>`) to bind Dialogflow CX conversation profiles once provisioned by the backend, with automated cache invalidation upon call completion.

### 2. Backend & AudioHook Integration
- **AudioHook Connector**: Added Redis caching of conversation mappings (`conversationIntegrationKey` <-> `conversation_name`) supporting both Genesys UUIDs and ANI phone numbers.
- **UI Connector Service**: Added `/conversation-name` lookup endpoint with OIDC service-to-service authentication to avoid unnecessary external token exchanges.
- **Security & Secret Hygiene**: Standardized environment variable ingestion across services with sanitized configuration templates.

### 3. Salesforce Apex & Security Metadata
- **Apex Controller**: Added `AgentAssistAuthController.cls` to execute server-to-server OAuth Client Credentials token exchanges, avoiding browser CORS constraints.
- **CSP Trusted Sites**: Added CSP metadata for Genesys PureCloud/MyPureCloud endpoints and Google Cloud Run (`connect-src`, `frame-src`, `img-src`, `style-src`, and WebSockets `wss://`).
- **Remote Site Settings**: Added regional Genesys Cloud and Cloud Run remote site definitions.
- **Call Center & Omni-Channel Automation**: Added Apex setup scripts (`create_callcenter.apex`, `setup_omnichannel.apex`) and Call Center metadata for rapid scratch org provisioning.

### 4. Comprehensive Documentation & CI Pipeline
- **Integration Guide**: Added [`GENESYS_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md`](file:///Users/jblakey/projects/agent-assist-integrations/GENESYS_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md) detailing architecture, sequence diagrams, environment setups, and step-by-step deployment runbooks.
- **CI Workflow**: Configured GitHub Actions matrix pipeline running automated test suites across all backend components and LWC Jest.

---

## Testing & Verification

All automated test suites pass across Python backend services and JavaScript / SFDX LWC:

- **LWC Jest Unit Tests**: `113 / 113` passing (`npm test` in `salesforce/aa-lwc`)
- **Apex Unit Tests**: 100% pass rate with code coverage on `AgentAssistAuthControllerTest.cls`
- **UI Connector Tests**: `unit_test.py` passing (auth, endpoints, redis mapping)
- **AudioHook Tests**: `test_dialogflow_api.py` passing
- **PubSub Interceptor Tests**: `unit_test.py` passing
- **GitHub Actions CI**: Verified passing on [Run #33128747077](https://github.com/jblakey-google/agent-assist-integrations/actions/runs/33128747077)

---

## Checklist
- [x] Code adheres to Google Python and JavaScript style guides.
- [x] Secrets and credentials sanitized (environment variable placeholders used).
- [x] Unit tests added and passing across all modules.
- [x] Deployment and runbook documentation added.

author: chelseakr
body:
Phase 3 of [`docs/18-ASSURANCE-PROGRAM.md`](docs/18-ASSURANCE-PROGRAM.md). Decision in [ADR 0007](docs/adr/0007-declared-analysis-scope.md).

**Stacked on #45, which is stacked on #44.** Base is `assurance/phase-2-boundary-covers-metadata`, so this diff is phase 3 only.

## The third state nothing could see

After #44, every gate can tell "I looked and found nothing" from "I could not look". None of them can tell either of those from **"nobody ever pointed me at that tree."**

`tools/` held five gate implementations that between them decide whether anything merges, and it was outside the marker scan and outside the coverage floor. Both gates reported clean, correctly, over the trees they had been given. Nothing in the repository was in a position to notice a third tree of Python existed. #44 closed those two holes by hand; nothing stopped the next one.

Asking the same question of the other analyses found a hole still open: `make typecheck` was `mypy --strict src`, so the gate programs were never type-checked. Seven errors, **six of them `# type: ignore[arg-type]` comments on calls to `parse_bundle`, whose three parameters are declared `object`.** Suppressions that suppressed nothing — a claim about a problem that is not there, sitting in the same `tools/` tree as the gates this program exists to make honest.

## What this adds

`tools/scope_gate.py`, wired in as `make scope`. It scans no files. It compares the trees each analysis *claims* against the tracked Python that exists.

A claim is read from the configuration that makes it, never from a copy: `marker-scan` from `hygiene_gate.MARKER_ROOTS` **by import**, `strict-typing` from `[tool.mypy] files`, `branch-coverage` from `[tool.coverage.run] source`. For that to mean anything the commands must not override it, so `make typecheck` now passes no path and `make test` passes a bare `--cov` — and the gate reads both recipes and **refuses to run** if either passes an argument that would win against the config.

Three rules: `unclaimed-file` (the `tools/` hole), `empty-claim` (a claimed root with nothing under it, so the analysis covers less than its configuration says), `stale-exception` (an exception excusing nothing describes a repository that is not this one).

Two declared exceptions, both `tests/`, both printed on **every** run with their reason, so coverage declared away is as visible as coverage achieved.

## Proof, three states

```
### CLEAN ###
scope: clean - 3 tracked Python file(s) checked against 3 analysis claim(s): marker-scan [src tests tools], strict-typing [src tools], branch-coverage [src tools]
EXIT=0

### DIRTY: narrow MARKER_ROOTS and [tool.mypy] files back to what main carried ###
scope: 10 finding(s) over 51 file(s)
  unclaimed-file: marker-scan:tools/a11y_gate.py: tracked Python outside every root the analysis claims, and outside every declared exception
  unclaimed-file: marker-scan:tools/hygiene_gate.py: ...
  unclaimed-file: marker-scan:tools/i18n_gate.py: ...
  unclaimed-file: marker-scan:tools/publication_sweep.py: ...
  unclaimed-file: marker-scan:tools/scope_gate.py: ...
  unclaimed-file: strict-typing:tools/a11y_gate.py: ...
  unclaimed-file: strict-typing:tools/hygiene_gate.py: ...
  unclaimed-file: strict-typing:tools/i18n_gate.py: ...
  unclaimed-file: strict-typing:tools/publication_sweep.py: ...
  unclaimed-file: strict-typing:tools/scope_gate.py: ...
EXIT=1

### COULD NOT RUN: the command overrides the configured scope ###
scope: the `typecheck` target passes `src`, which overrides the scope configured in pyproject.toml, so what this gate reads is not what that command examines.
scope: this is a failure to run the gate, not a clean result.
EXIT=2

### COULD NOT RUN: nothing to compare against ###
scope: git lists no tracked Python file in ..., so every claim would hold vacuously, and a comparison against nothing is not a pass.
scope: this is a failure to run the gate, not a clean result.
EXIT=2
```

The refusal set is wider than the two shown: no `git`, an unreadable or unparseable `pyproject.toml`, a missing config key, an empty list, a missing or unrecognised Makefile recipe, and a `hygiene_gate.py` that will not import or defines no `MARKER_ROOTS`. `tests/test_scope_gate.py` covers all of them, plus `test_the_refusal_is_a_distinct_exit_code_from_a_finding`, and `test_a_prefix_match_is_on_path_segments_not_characters` so `src` cannot claim `srcery/` by accident. 24 tests; `tools/scope_gate.py` is at 97% branch coverage.

## The typing fix

`mypy --strict tools` before this change reported 7 errors. All fixed: the six dead `type: ignore` comments are deleted, with a comment saying why they were never doing anything, and `reference_document` returns the `dict[str, JsonValue]` it actually returns, with its three consumers taking a covariant `Mapping`. `mypy --strict` now reports `no issues found in 28 source files`, up from 22.

## Gate output

`make verify`, exit 0:

```
Success: no issues found in 28 source files
Required test coverage of 90% reached. Total coverage: 96.08%
801 passed in 31.74s
hygiene: clean - 58 tracked file(s) under src, tests, tools ... 3 exemption(s) honored, 123 tracked path(s) checked
scope: clean - 51 tracked Python file(s) checked against 3 analysis claim(s): marker-scan [src tests tools], strict-typing [src tools], branch-coverage [src/contextsafe tools]
publication-sweep: clean over 123 of 123 source(s), tracked files, no denylist supplied
a11y-gate: clean
```

## Definition of done

- ISO/IEC 25010: **Maintainability** (analysability and modifiability of the gate surface), **Reliability** (maturity).
- Deliberately out of scope and **declared rather than silent**: `tests/` is not strictly typed. `mypy --strict tests` reports 127 errors in 16 files, mostly pytest and Hypothesis signatures. That is its own change with its own review; the declared exception carries the measurement and the date, and the `stale-exception` rule means the declaration cannot outlive the gap.
- Also deliberately out of scope: ruff, the publication sweep and the stray-config check all already read the whole tracked tree, so none of them has a scope that can silently narrow, and adding them would be three rows that cannot fail. Adding a genuinely scoped analysis later is one table entry and a claim source.
- Operational assumption: none new. The gate is stdlib (`tomllib`) plus `git`.

author: abrichr
body:
Removes `public/product-preview/dashboard-walkthrough.mp4` (1,204,990 bytes) and its entry in `public/product-preview/MANIFEST.json`.

Two reasons, and the second stands on its own.

**It is out of date and it is not good enough to ship.** It was captured on 2026-07-18 against a Cloud commit that is two months stale, at 1280x800, while the still beside it in the same manifest was re-shot on 2026-08-28 at 2560x1440 on the current palette. A visitor who found the video would see an older product than the one the rest of the page shows.

**Nothing renders it.** Every place a reference could live was searched first, and the manifest entry was the only mention in the repository:

| search | result |
| --- | --- |
| `grep -rn 'dashboard-walkthrough'` | 2 lines, both in `public/product-preview/MANIFEST.json` |
| `grep -rniE 'dashboard[-_. ]?walkthrough'` | the same 2 lines, so no separator variant hides elsewhere |
| `grep -rni 'walkthrough'` | unrelated: the `local-cli-walkthrough` testid in `pages/start.js` and `cypress/e2e/public-surface-coherence.cy.js`, the prose "five-minute walkthrough" in `components/InstallSection.js`, and an "Evidence walkthrough" label in an openIMIS manifest |
| `grep -rn 'product-preview'` | every hit names `dashboard-workflows.png` or the manifest itself; none names the video |
| grep for `` `${...}.mp4` ``, `+ ".mp4"` | only `data/referencePresentationAssets.mjs`, which builds the four reference replay paths — no runtime concatenation can produce this filename |
| `grep -rn 'manifest.assets'` | the product-preview manifest is read by key (`dashboard-workflows.png`) in `tests/dashboardShowcase.test.js`; the `Object.entries` loop is in `tests/desktopPreview.test.js`, over a different manifest |
| `grep -rn '<video\|videoSrc\|poster='` | `RdpHybridPresentation.js`, `AnimatedBackground.js`, `EvidenceMediaPlayer.js`; none points at `product-preview` |

Scope covered `components`, `pages`, `tests`, `lib`, `utils`, `cypress`, `data`, `scripts`, `.github`, and `public`. `components/DashboardShowcase.js` renders `/product-preview/dashboard-workflows.png` and nothing else from that directory, so no page changed and no reference needed removing.

**The hash pin moves with the manifest.** `lib/publicJsonArtifacts.mjs` pins the manifest's sha256 and `tests/jsonArtifacts.test.js` asserts it, so the pin goes from `12784aeb…` to `850ec5b5…` in the same commit. It was recomputed from the edited file, not regenerated wholesale — the diff is that one line.

`presentation` and `source` in the manifest are unchanged. They describe the capture lineage of the PNG that stays.

**Checks:** `npm test` — 252 pass, 0 fail. `npm run verify:presentations` — 4 assets verified.

Same reasoning as 1aa98dd, which removed 23 unreferenced cloud-preview assets.

author: fuller-stack-dev
body:
AI-assisted. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the iOS sidebar returning `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` and an empty pinned/recent roster when a multi-agent gateway requires explicit agent ownership. The app selected an agent in the UI but did not carry that owner through the complete selected-agent roster lifecycle.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Swift request builder accepts the selected `agentId`, and every page of the selected-agent roster supplies it. Responses are fenced by both gateway and agent. Agent changes restart roster refresh, clear stale share-route state, and prevent asynchronous results from the previous owner from being applied. Global session-change events and cached prepaint are evaluated in the active-agent scope.

Offline rosters are stored in bounded `(gateway, agent)` SQLite cache partitions, so agent A and B can both retain a legitimate `global` row. Empty replacement and corruption cleanup affect one agent only, while mixed-owner snapshots are rejected before deletion. The old gateway-wide roster is discarded because its owner cannot be inferred; transcript caches remain intact. The approved persistence design is recorded in [this maintainer decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/131356#issuecomment-5448118785).

The gateway's fail-closed ownership rule remains unchanged; the client supplies the verified owner it already has. Configured-agent child-session discovery remains intentionally federated because narrowing that separate request would hide valid dynamic child sessions.

Production delta: +286/-67 (net +219). Test delta: +329/-21 (net +308). The production growth establishes one ownership boundary across request, pagination, cache storage, refresh identity, observer, share-route application, and offline fallback while preserving unscoped public cache conformers and failing closed when a legacy conformer cannot honor agent ownership.

## User Impact

On a multi-agent gateway, iOS users can open the sidebar and see the selected agent's pinned and recent sessions. Switching agents cannot publish cached or in-flight rows from the previous owner, and switching back while offline restores that agent's last verified roster.

## Evidence

Before, opening the sidebar on a multi-agent gateway failed and showed no recent sessions:

![Before: iOS sidebar shows an agent-selection error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5de20a53-b13b-4f9f-bf4d-c3c706a3286e)

After, the same physical iPhone loaded the selected agent's pinned session without the ownership error:

![After: iOS sidebar shows the selected agent's pinned session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e58c598f-d5c8-433c-af57-43f1ccbd2d59)

The author also recorded a signed physical-device run against the same live multi-agent gateway: select another agent, switch back, force-quit, and relaunch all retained the correct roster. The later cache-owner repair does not alter the captured request path; it adds deterministic A→B→offline-A coverage.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.list-explicit-ownership.test.ts` — 1/1 passed; the request contract is unchanged on the final head.
- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter 'ChatTranscriptCacheStoreTests|ChatViewModelTranscriptCacheTests|ChatGatewayRequestTests|ChatSessionSidebarModelTests'` — 141/141 passed after the final shared-kit edit, including A→B legacy-conformer read and write guards.
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter MacGatewayChatTransportMappingTests` — 17/17 passed after the macOS sibling repair.
- Cache-owner regression coverage — A and B `global` rows survive a cold reopen; empty replacement, mixed-owner rejection, corruption isolation, retention bounds, legacy-row discard without transcript loss, and gateway cleanup all pass.
- `swiftformat --lint --config config/swiftformat <changed Swift files>` — clean.
- Final focused `autoreview --mode local` passes for the macOS owner repair, iOS guard correction, and legacy-cache compatibility repair — clean; no accepted/actionable findings, confidence 0.98, 0.99, and 0.98.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Exact-head hosted CI/Testbox [run 33142116989](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33142116989) completed successfully for `96aeba87f83ef5790236c2ae73d7f1a2a297a71f`; iOS build and focused lifecycle simulator tests ([job 98755221630](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33142116989/job/98755221630)), macOS Swift ([job 98755221593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33142116989/job/98755221593)), macOS Node ([job 98755221632](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33142116989/job/98755221632)), and both iOS screenshot shards passed. Exact-head iOS, shared-kit, and macOS Periphery runs `33142117003`, `33142117010`, and `33142117180` also passed.
- Source-blind behavior validation passed on the final head (confidence 0.92) from 141/141 shared tests, the 1/1 gateway ownership test, the hosted iOS lifecycle job, and the visible before/after evidence. It did not count the preserved physical-device switch/offline/relaunch claim as proof; those transitions are covered by exact-head executable regressions.
- Exact-head ClawSweeper found no actionable defect and judged this the best owner-level fix; its only rank-up move was the exact-head native validation completed above.

Local `xcodebuild test` could not start because this Xcode exposes the iOS 26.5 SDK while the installed simulator runtime is iOS 27.0. Hosted native CI is the authoritative exact-head iOS proof.

author: bluefa
body:
## What

The 협업 채널 card at the top of the guide rail: 시안 A + C + E from its third
design benchmark (오너 지시 2026-08-28: 「A,C,E적용」).

Artifact: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/99e825b8-d78d-4a59-804a-1c1864ab18a4
Decision record: `docs/ux/benchmark/guide-rail-collab-card.md`

## Why

「강약의 개념이 없어. 좌측에 너무 쏠려있어서 그런가」. Measuring it split that into two
defects with different causes, which is why one lever could not fix both:

- The emphasis peak sat on the **label**, not the payload. 「협업 채널」 carried three
  levers (16 + 700 + darkest ink); `BDCDIP-1002` carried one and a half. Carbon's rule
  is that a lighter face outranks a bold one only when it is "significantly larger",
  and 16/14 = 1.14x does not clear that — so the label won on size *and* weight at once
  and the only clickable thing in the card was its quietest ink.
- The card's padding **equalled its corner radius** (12 on `rounded-xl`), so the content
  rode the curve. That is the 조잡함, and it is a 수치 위반 rather than a preference.
- The state dot sat 206px from the label whose state it reports — 26x the widest
  label-to-indicator distance across the three systems benchmarked.

## Changes

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| issue key weight | 400 | **600** |
| card padding | 12 | **16** |
| tail offset | `after:left-3` | **`after:left-4`** (coupled) |
| dot to label | 206px | **6px** |
| ink above head | 14 | **16** |
| card height | 110 | 118 |

**A** — `14/400` was byte-for-byte Carbon's `bodyCompact01`, the token for a value inside
a component. 600 is `heading01`. Atlassian reaches the same value from the other side:
"don't use heading text in components, instead use body text with a heavier font weight".
Weight, not size — 16 would tie the head and collapse the rail's 12/14/16 ladder.

**C** — the dot moves off the far edge onto the label (`gap-1.5`). This reverses the same
day's 「우측 끝에」, on the strength of three systems agreeing without exception
(Cloudscape KeyValuePairs 0px, Ant Descriptions 8px, Primer ActionList a leading column);
all three reserve the far edge for an *action* or leave it empty. The 209px right of the
head is now deliberately empty — Cloudscape recommends exactly that, and emptiness reads
as margin once nothing is left hanging in it.

**E** — `p-3` -> `p-4`, and `railStyles.bubbleTail` moves with it. Those two numbers are
one measurement written across two files.

## Not in scope

- The guide card stays at `p-3`, so the two zones no longer share a padding. Deliberate;
  raising it costs 8px of the rail's vertical budget and shortens its scroller.
- The dead `font-mono` declaration stays. It changes no pixel (`--font-mono` is aliased to
  the sans face; the anchor's resolved family measures as `pretendard`), and a zero-pixel
  cleanup was not part of the instruction.
- 시안 B / D / F are recorded in the decision record with what each would cost.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean · `vitest` **3200/3200** · `design:check` 0 errors · pre-commit green
- Measured in the browser at 1900x1052, rail asserted at 319px (unfolded) before reading
- **Mutation-tested.** The first pass shipped A and E with *no* tripwire — removing
  `font-semibold` and reverting `p-4` each left all 35 tests green. Four assertions were
  added and each was independently confirmed red, then green on restore:
  `gap-1.5` -> `justify-between`, `font-semibold` removed, `p-4` -> `p-3`, and
  `after:left-4` -> `after:left-3` (half the couple).

Yukon submission `14574660-7ef9-4a3d-9e49-89a105638348` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/mlxfast-gemma4-26b-a4b-engine at `3ab9bd49c71eb69bd807ff5065e0513ab2574556`.

Current best score: 1.42692794534779. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)
Harness: Claude Code

# LMH-001: tight-grid dispatch for the tied lm_head ordinary QMV at batch eight

Effort: max

## Summary

The tied lm_head's ordinary quantized matvec is dispatched from a custom kernel
whose x grid extent is two instead of eight, so the six threadgroups per y-group
that the promoted large-N tier already returns from immediately are never
launched. The computation, its pointer arithmetic, and its arithmetic order are
unchanged; only the grid and the dispatch site differ.

Files changed, both editable:

- `Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ContinuousBatchingV2/TiedLMHeadQMVV1.swift` (new)
- `Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLLM/Models/Gemma4Text.swift`

No weight, quantization representation, router decision, KV value, mask, scale
semantics, sampler, prompt handling, worker protocol, cache layout, draft depth,
or scoring behavior changes. No existing kernel source is edited.

## The launched-but-idle groups

`Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp`, in `qmv`:

```cpp
int bn = 8;
int bk = 32;
MTL::Size group_dims(bk, 2, 1);
MTL::Size grid_dims(M, (N + bn - 1) / bn, B);
...
compute_encoder.dispatch_threadgroups(grid_dims, group_dims);
```

The x extent of the grid is `M`, the cohort row count, which is eight on the
scored decode path. The promoted large-N tier in
`backend/metal/kernels/quantized.h` claims four cohort rows per threadgroup:

```cpp
if (out_vec_size >= 8192) {
  const int first_m = int(tid.x) * 4;
  if (first_m >= 8) {
    return;
  }
  qmv_affine4_g64_quad_impl<T, 64, 4>(...);
  return;
}
```

`tid.x` runs 0..7 and only 0 and 1 satisfy `first_m < 8`. Six of every eight
x-groups are launched and retire at that `return`, for every y-group and every
call that reaches this tier.

On the tied head that is the largest grid of the decode step. With
`hidden_size` 2816 and `vocab_size` 262144 (tied embeddings, so `lm_head` is
absent and `Gemma4TextModel.applyLMHead` goes through
`model.embedTokens.asLinear`), the y extent is `262144 / 8 = 32768`, so
`8 * 32768 = 262144` threadgroups are dispatched and 196608 of them exist only
to hit that early return.

The host grid is computed in `backend/metal/quantized.cpp`, which is not an
editable path, so it cannot be narrowed in place.

## The change

`CBv2TiedLMHeadQMVV1` declares one `MLXFast.metalKernel` and dispatches it with

```swift
grid: (xGroups * 32, yGroups * 2, 1),      // xGroups = 8 / 4 = 2
threadGroup: (32, 2, 1),
```

`MLXFast` custom kernels dispatch by threads (`backend/metal/custom_kernel.cpp`
calls `dispatch_threads`), so this is two x-threadgroups by `N / 8` y-threadgroups
over the same `(32, 2, 1)` threadgroup the stock path uses.

`first_m` is kept as `tid.x * 4`. With `tid.x` in {0, 1} the two surviving groups
claim rows 0-3 and 4-7 — exactly the two groups that were already doing the work,
with the same rows, the same weight/scale/bias pointers, the same `out_row`
derivation from `tid.y` and `simd_gid`, and the same per-thread `simd_lid`
offsets. The six groups that are no longer launched are precisely those whose
only action was the early `return`.

The kernel body is `qmv_affine4_g64_quad_impl` with `load_vector`,
`load_vector_safe` and `qdot_affine4_quad` expanded in place. Every expression is
copied verbatim. In particular the `T` operands are left as `T`: `bfloat16_t` is
Metal's native `bfloat`, so `x[i] + x[i + 1] + x[i + 2] + x[i + 3]` rounds in
bf16, and rewriting those additions in float would change results. The per-row
dot is also written the way the helper writes it — into a `dot` local, then
`result[row] += dot` — rather than folded into one expression, because folding
lets the compiler contract the multiply-adds differently.

## Fail-closed gating

`Gemma4TextModel.tiedLMHeadTightGrid` returns `nil`, and the caller keeps
`model.embedTokens.asLinear`, unless all of:

- `lmHead == nil` (the tied configuration);
- `model.embedTokens` is a `QuantizedEmbedding` with `groupSize == 64`, `bits == 4`;
- activation is bf16, 3-D, `[8, 1, inDim]`;
- `scales` and `biases` are bf16 and `biases` is present;
- `weight` is uint32 `[outDim, inDim * 4 / 32]`;
- `scales` is `[outDim, inDim / 64]` and `biases` has the same shape;
- `outDim >= 8`, `outDim % 8 == 0`, `inDim % 64 == 0`, `inDim >= 512`.

Every dimension is checked against every other, so the gate is a full shape pin
at runtime. Any other batch width, dtype, quantization geometry, or module type
falls through to the established path unchanged. `DARKBLOOM_CBV2_TIED_LMHEAD_QMV=0`
restores the stock path inside the same executable.

## Bit-exact validation

A temporary runtime test (no model load; not an editable path, and removed before
this submission) built deterministic bf16 activations and randomly filled packed
4-bit weights, scales and biases, and compared this kernel against MLX's own
`quantizedMatmul` element by element, as exact bf16 equality rather than a
tolerance:

| in_vec_size | out_vec_size | elements | mismatches |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2816 | 1024 | 8,192 | 0 |
| 2816 | 2048 | 16,384 (x3 fills) | 0 |
| 2816 | 4096 | 32,768 (x2 fills) | 0 |

122,880 elements, zero mismatches, on Apple M1 Max.

Two notes on why those shapes: `qmv()` selects `_qmv_fast_` when
`N % bn == 0 && K % 512 == 0`, which is a different kernel from the pair/quad
impl this one copies; the tower's `hidden_size` is 2816 and `2816 % 512 == 256`,
so the scored path always takes the plain `qmv`. And `get_qmv_batch_limit` on
this machine routes `M = 8` away from `qmv` entirely once `out_vec_size` passes
4096, so the comparison is run at the largest `out_vec_size` that still reaches
the kernel here.

## Validation on the tree

- `swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions` and the same build with
  `--scratch-path .build-worker` both pass; `tools/stage-runtime-worker.sh`
  staged the worker and its sibling `mlx.metallib`.
- `./benchmark.sh --local-iterate` against
  `correctness_prompts/public_longcopy_gate_english_1024_256.json`:
  `passed_correctness: true`, `max_abs_diff: 0.0`, 130 checked steps, no golden
  drift.
- `git diff --check` clean. The kernel is JIT-compiled from Swift source, the
  same mechanism as the promoted batch-wide decode attention, so no `_nax` or
  metallib coupling is involved.

## Local timing

No local timed number is claimed for this change. The correctness and bit-equality
results above are what the local runs are reported for here.

author: oittaa
body: Forked EXEC/SYSTEM/SHELL used pipes for unidirectional mode and whenever `fdin`/`fdout` was set, so inherited stdout was relayed. Classic `xio-progcall.c` defaults to socketpair; `fdin`/`fdout` only change Dup2 targets, and `pty` stays a PTY. Classic baselines: tag-1.8.1.3 `12c08bf66d709fba17035ce95d85bd218428d9ba`; official master `af5388c898c7bb60997935aee93c223deba60c4a` is the same `xio-progcall.c`. Official repository: https://repo.or.cz/socat.git. ## Observable mismatch With `SYSTEM:'printf O; printf D >&4',fdin=3,fdout=4`: - Before: inherited stdout was also on the data channel, so the peer saw `OD` (`FILE=OD`). - Classic and this PR: ordinary stdout stays inherited (`O`) and only fd 4 is relayed (`D`). Confirmed on classic 1.8.1.3 for default socketpair, explicit `pipes`, and `pty,fdin=3,fdout=4,raw,echo=0`. ## Transport selection - Default forked EXEC/SYSTEM/SHELL: socketpair, including `-u` and `fdin`/`fdout`. - User `pipes`: stay pipes, with descriptor mapping that does not leave extra copies on 0/1. - User `pty`: stay PTY (`fdin`/`fdout` do not disable PTY). `pipes`+`pty` warns and ignores `pipes`. - `end-close` still uses pipes here (`EXECENDCLOSE` / LISTEN,fork shared-FD). PASTSOCKET leftover-rejects rather than cancelling that safeguard. Socketpair for `end-close` is a follow-up. ## Child descriptor mapping `fdin` defaults to 0 and `fdout` to 1. ExtraFiles place the data fd at 3 (socket/PTY) or 3/4 (pipes). A `/bin/sh` `exec` prefix Dup2's onto the selected targets, inherits unrelated 0/1/2, duplicates stderr onto the effective fdo when `stderr` is set, and closes helper descriptors that are not final fdi/fdo targets. Overlapping pipe mappings save ExtraFiles onto unused **single-digit** temps in 3–9. Dash (`/bin/sh` on Ubuntu) rejects `10<&3` (`Syntax error: Bad fd number`). Runtime tests cover `pipes,fdin=4,fdout=5` and the swap `pipes,fdin=4,fdout=3` (inherited `O`, relayed `D`). `fdin`/`fdout` ≥ 10 cannot be represented through dash redirection (classic `dup2` takes unsigned short). They fail before fork with `file descriptor N cannot be applied through /bin/sh redirection` rather than a dash syntax error. Documented in README. A child helper that calls `dup2` would be needed for high descriptors. Preserved: `chdir`, `setsid`/`setpgid`, child environment, umask, CLOEXEC cleanup, EXEC child exit tracking, `socktype=` datagram. ## Leftover PASTSOCKET Explicit `pipes`, `pty`, and `nofork` still fail with `option "…" not inquired`. `pty,fdin`/`fdout` and `pipes,fdin`/`fdout` are leftover cases too. Default `fdin`/`fdout` uses the socketpair, so PASTSOCKET applies on the child endpoint. ## Darwin follow-up macOS poll on a socketpair or pipe after the EXEC child exits often reports POLLHUP without POLLOUT. `waitReadableAndWritable` then returned `ErrClosedPipe` before Read, and `copyDir` treated that as a hard `E <: io: read/write on closed pipe` even though Write already maps the same error through `isBenignClose`. The reverse direction now treats that poll error as a clean EOF. The child-fd leak test lists `/dev/fd` instead of Linux-only `/proc/self/fd`. ## Tests - Unidirectional `cat` with and without `so-priority`. - `fdin=3,fdout=4` inherit vs relay on socketpair, pipes, and PTY, with and without `so-priority`. - Pipe overlap inherit vs relay: `fdin=4,fdout=5` and `fdin=4,fdout=3`. - `fdin`-only ModeWrite and `fdout`-only ModeRead. - `stderr` with custom `fdout`. - `chdir` combined with `fdin`/`fdout`. - Child descriptor leak: only intended fdi/fdo remain open. - `socktype=SOCK_DGRAM` where supported. - `fdin=10` / `fdout=10` precise rejection. - Relay poll closed-destination is a clean EOF. `make check` passed on Linux. Native Windows `go test ./...` is not available in this environment; GitHub Actions covers Windows.

author: emilyekillingbeck
body:
## The bug

`95_celltype_umap.sh` derives the de-novo annotation table from `RUN` alone:

```
MAPPING="${PIPELINE_DIR}/reference/denovo_annotations/${RUN}.csv"
```

`RUN` is also the Kopah sub-prefix. Both studies call theirs `stage4`, and both clones are
the same repo — so `RUN=stage4` from the retina clone resolves to `stage4.csv`, the **GBM**
table. The file exists, so the `[[ -f "$MAPPING" ]]` guard passes and nothing errors; the
figure just comes out with the wrong legend.

Observed on Klone before the fix:

```
Relabeling 12 de-novo clusters from stage4.csv
```

The retina cohort's `a` (fibroblast/stromal — DCN, MGP, COL1A2) was printing as
`a - Myeloid/TAM`, and `m` through `s` were unlabelled because the GBM table stops at `l`.

## The fix

`ANNOTATION_TABLE` overrides the table name, falling back to `RUN` — so every existing
invocation is byte-for-byte unchanged. Data paths are untouched; the two studies were
already separated correctly by `KOPAH_PREFIX`.

```
RUN=stage4 ANNOTATION_TABLE=retina_stage4 sbatch pipeline/slurm/95_celltype_umap.sh
```

After, on the same run:

```
Relabeling 19 de-novo clusters from retina_stage4.csv
```

## The table

`retina_stage4.csv` annotates all 19 letters of the K=19 run, following the triage:

- **3 genuinely novel** (`o`, `m`, `a`) — labelled with our working guess and a question
  mark, so the legend does not pre-commit the neuropathologist. `o` reads `UNKNOWN` rather
  than its nearest-named "amacrine cell", which is not credible at cosine 0.824.
- **11 known types that failed to anchor** — labelled as the type they match plus
  `(unanchored)`, which puts the collinearity finding directly in the figure.
- **3 stress states**, and 2 set aside.

author: jag8765
body:
**Increment 4, round C** of `docs/proposals/team-pipeline-iac.md` §13 (ADR-0046 §1/§2; D3, D9, D26). Round A merged four pure decision modules and wired none of them; round B made the registration real. **This is their first production caller.**

`apps/server` only — no new route, no schema change, no codegen. It takes the **migration slot** (0101, appended after #315's 0100; journal contiguity verified after rebase).

## What lands

`config-source/sync-engine.ts` — one commit's worth of repo-driven delivery: select the changed paths that are manifests, read each, validate against `DesiredStateManifestSchema`, resolve which registration governs, resolve the acting team, run **the same plan/apply path `routes/plans.ts` runs**, and record a status *and* a Decision for every place it can stop.

`drizzle/0101` + `config-source/stack-delivery-repo.ts` — the D26 record.

## Your ruling, built (D26)

Two accepted clauses disagreed: §4 makes the explicit `stackTeams` map the D7 binding; D9 gives an unclaimed stack the registration's **default** team, which the merged matcher implements. Between them sat a stack the sync applies on every push while `findStackConfigSourceBinding` called it unowned — so a `scp apply` succeeded and the next sync silently reverted it. D7's own failure mode, reached by forgetting a line in a map.

**Ownership follows delivery.** The sync records each stack it applies; D7's predicate returns the explicit claims **union** that record. Two details are load-bearing:

- **`PRIMARY KEY (org_id, stack_name)`** makes one-stack-one-owner *unrepresentable*, not merely refused, and the upsert's `DO UPDATE` is **guarded by `config_source_id`** — a second config source's delivery updates zero rows and is reported as a refusal. Unguarded, it is silent last-writer-wins ownership transfer, in the one place a read-then-write race cannot see it.
- **The delivery is recorded *before* the apply.** The other order writes the graph and then discovers it was not allowed to.

## The shortcut ADR-0046 names, and does not take

The sync loop is not an HTTP caller and holds no credential, so calling `executePlanDiff` with a system actor would be the path of least resistance — and everything would still work, which is exactly why the ADR names it. The config source's resolved **team object** is the actor instead. Mutation-proved: with a system actor, an out-of-scope manifest applies and **no other test notices**.

One deliberate divergence from the route, about honesty rather than authority: the route calls `authorize()` and throws on the first denial; here every check is evaluated and every refusal collected, because this status is the only thing an operator sees. Reporting one refusal of three sends them round the loop three times.

## Failure is displayed, never inferred

Unreadable · unparseable · invalid · registration-ambiguous · stack-owned-elsewhere · authz-refused · freeze-held · applied · no-op — each produces a typed status and a Decision carrying the **commit SHA and manifest content hash** (D3: the boundary goes in the Decision, never `now`). A commit touching nothing the registration selects is a quiet no-op with **no** Decision.

Registration-level refusals are kept **distinguishable** from the six-way sync status rather than folded into it: "which registration governs this?" and "where did this attempt stop?" are answers to different questions, and collapsing them would make `sync-status.ts`'s deliberately exhaustive space quietly seven-way and untyped.

## A real defect the freeze case caught

`affectedObjectIds` first read resolution **ids only**. A `create` entry has no id until `executePlanDiff` runs it — so a create-only manifest asked about an **empty** target set, and an empty set produces no freezes, which is indistinguishable from "nothing is frozen". Freezes would have held edits to existing objects and waved brand-new ones straight through. Now `id ?? scopeObjectId`; the fallback is the resolved containment parent, which is what `freezesByTarget` walks. Mutation (6) in the test header is that bug, pinned.

## Verification

- **7 integration tests green**, plus the round-B doors suite, `plans`, and `governance-managed-write-doors` — **59/59** after rebasing onto the merged `main` (which now also carries the RBAC session's 0099 and the Argo session's #316).
- **Six mutations applied, watched fail, reverted, watched pass** — measured table in the test header; each fails exactly the case that names its property.
- `pnpm check`: nul-census **6 as expected**, prettier clean, lint clean, 71 typecheck tasks, `gen` **no drift**.

## What is still not here

**The trigger.** Nothing calls `syncConfigSourceCommit` in production yet — the webhook/poll wiring and the git-provider instance resolution (`readFileAtRef` through `plugin-host`'s `gitFileRead`) are the next piece, along with the status read surface, which needs the API slot. The `readManifest` seam is a parameter precisely so the trigger layer can own instance resolution and lifetime — an out-of-process RPC must not run inside the transaction this engine mutates the graph in.

So: the engine is real and proven, and it is **not yet reachable from a push**. Saying so is cheaper than discovering it.

author: stxkxs
body:
## The defect is the 401 path, not the typing

Three calls issued their own `fetch` with a hand-rolled `Authorization` header
from `localStorage`: the state-version download, the state-version drop, and the
config upload. Duplicating the client's **request** middleware is the visible
half. The half that hurts is the **response** middleware they never reached.

When a token expires mid-upload or mid-download, `onResponse` never runs — no
`localStorage` clear, no redirect. The user is told "Upload failed" and sits in a
session that cannot succeed. Invisible until a token expires at the wrong
moment, and nothing tested it.

## Why they bypassed the client — a defect in `client.ts`

    signal: AbortSignal.any([request.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(30_000)])

`AbortSignal.any` settles on the **first** signal to abort, so the 30s default
was a **ceiling**, not a default: a caller passing 120s still died at 30s. Config
archives need 120s, which was unreachable through the client. The comment above
that line called it a "default deadline" — the opposite of what the code did.
The bypass was not laziness; it was the only way to get the deadline that call
needs.

The deadline now attaches **per call**, where a caller's signal replaces it
rather than racing it. A call that supplies nothing still gets 30s.

That boundary is also the only place the two cases are distinguishable: the
`fetch` hook receives a `Request`, and a `Request` carries a signal whether the
caller supplied one or not — `MergedOptions` doesn't carry `signal` either, so
middleware can't see it. Hence the per-call wrapper.

## Proof the ceiling is actually lifted

Not taken on reading. The test asserts the request is **still alive** past the
default deadline when the caller supplied a longer one. Reverting `client.ts` to
the racing implementation and re-running:

    × lets a caller-supplied signal replace the default rather than race it
      Tests  1 failed | 2 passed

Restored: **9 passed**. The other two deadline tests pass under both
implementations — correctly, since they don't discriminate. Only the one that
tests the actual change fails when the change is removed.

Also covered: a call with no signal is still bounded, and a caller signal
*shorter* than the default is still honoured.

## Proof the 401 path works

Each of the three migrated calls, driven through the real client against a 401,
asserts the token is cleared and the redirect fires:

    ✓ clears the token and redirects on 401: state download
    ✓ clears the token and redirects on 401: state version drop
    ✓ clears the token and redirects on 401: config upload

Plus the request half — each sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from the
middleware rather than a hand-rolled header.

## The three calls

- **state-version drop** — plain `api.DELETE`, default deadline. It was a
  straight oversight.
- **state download** — `parseAs: 'blob'`, which types `data` as `Blob`. The spec
  keeps `application/json`: the handler sets `Content-Type: application/json`
  with `Content-Disposition: attachment`, so the response *is* JSON and
  declaring it binary would make the spec contradict the handler. The blob is
  how the client reads it, not what the server sends.
- **config upload** — multipart `FormData` at 120s, now a caller-supplied signal
  instead of a reason to leave the client. openapi-fetch forwards a `FormData`
  body untouched and leaves `Content-Type` unset so the browser writes the
  boundary.

## `Login.tsx` stays a bare fetch, deliberately

The `dev_login` probe runs before a token exists, so it carries no
`Authorization` header and has no 401 to act on — the client's middleware would
have nothing to add and nothing to handle. The reason is recorded in the code,
not only here, so it does not read as an oversight to be "finished" later.

## One type concession, stated

The upload body is cast: `formData as unknown as { file: string }`.
OpenAPI's `format: binary` generates `string`, and `FormData` is what carries
those parts on the wire. Path params and the response stay fully typed. This is
strictly more typed than the raw `fetch` it replaces, which had no types at all.
Removing the cast needs the generator's `transform` hook, which is Node-API only
and would mean replacing the CLI invocation — deferred rather than done here.

## Spec

The upload description said "the UI sends it with a raw fetch rather than the
typed client", which this PR makes false. Corrected, regenerated through
`tools/apigen`, and the drift gate confirms the one-line change.

author: sonichi
body:
## What

The Discord bridge loses messages that arrive during a gateway disconnect: Discord does not replay events missed across a session boundary, and the bridge had no recovery. Measured incident (2026-08-27): the gateway opened a new session at 22:10:09Z and the owner's 22:09 message never became a task — silent, no error, unfalsifiable until compared against the phone screen.

This adds reconnect backfill for the channels the bridge serves: a durable per-channel watermark (`state/discord-last-seen.json`, atomic tmp+`os.replace`, forward-only) advanced on every live message, and on `on_ready`/`on_resumed` a REST fetch of `history(after=<watermark>, oldest_first=True)` per configured channel, each recovered message routed through `_handle_discord_message` — the exact choke point live messages take, so allowFrom/tierMap/requireMention/collaborator gates apply identically to replayed traffic.

Guards: a channel with no watermark is initialized to its newest message id with ZERO replay (a fresh install must never ingest channel history as tasks); replay is capped at 50/channel/reconnect (fetches 51 so "at the cap" and "cap binds" are distinguishable; WARN names the remainder, which the next reconnect drains); self-authored messages advance the watermark without replay; a per-channel or per-message failure logs and continues — the live event loop is never blocked.

DMs are deliberately NOT tracked here: `state/discord-dm-checkpoint.json` + `_catchup_missed_dms` already own that exact policy (pinned by `tests/discord-bridge-dm-catchup.test.py`); duplicating it would double-replay DMs. Instead the shared watermark-storage policy was extracted (`_atomic_write_id_map`/`_load_id_map`/`_advance_id_map`) and both mechanisms delegate to it, and `_catchup_missed_dms` is now also scheduled on RESUMED so DM coverage matches channel coverage. The DM trio's behavior is unchanged; its suite passes.

## Evidence

At parent (6629b5d5): no watermark file, no backfill path — a message during a disconnect is simply gone (the 22:09 incident above is the field case).

At HEAD: `tests/discord-reconnect-backfill.test.py` → **10/10 pass**, covering: first-READY initializes without replay; reconnect fetches `after=watermark` and every fetched message goes through the SAME `_handle_discord_message` the live path uses (asserted on the choke point, not a copy); the 50-cap binds with the WARN; watermark advances on live messages; a failing channel doesn't stop the others; forward-only advance; untracked-channel exclusion; READY/RESUMED wiring.

body:
## Summary
- select Rustls' AWS-LC provider explicitly at Nyvexa startup
- add a direct Rustls dependency with the `aws_lc_rs` provider enabled
- avoid relying on transitive Rustls feature resolution when both AWS-LC and ring are present

## Why
On Windows, Nyvexa could compile successfully but panic at runtime with:

`Could not automatically determine the process-level CryptoProvider from Rustls crate features.`

Rustls explicitly recommends applications install a process-level provider early in `main` when multiple providers may be enabled by dependencies.

CI will run rustfmt, cargo check, Clippy with warnings denied, and the test suite on Rust 1.98.

body:
## Scope

F1.1 del roadmap de producto: el primero de los tres indicadores Pro que faltan.

Port pandas 1:1 de `pineforge/01_BudAI/Osciladores/Nivel_2_Avanzados/budai_oceanus.pine`, espejo del núcleo numpy ya parity-validado en `KryptoLab/indicators/oceanus.py`.

- `indicators/budai_oceanus.py` — `osc`/`trig` (WaveTrend normalizado 0-100) + MFI sobre hlc3, cruces y cruces fuertes con confirmación de flujo. Misma forma que los otros cuatro ports BudAI (`budai_oceanus`, `_all_timeframes`, `_summary`).
- `indicators_series._SERIES`: alta de `oceanus` con los params del Pine — `chanLen=9, avgLen=12, trigLen=4, normLen=100`, escala `0-100`, OB 80 / OS 20.
- `web/app.py`: el docstring de `/api/indicators/series` lista el nuevo `ind`.

## Fuera de scope (deliberado)

Las capas visuales del Pine — hyper wave doble-kernel, RVOL, LSMA dual, nodos, divergencias, glow — son presentación. El hub dibuja osc + trig + OB/OS, así que no se portaron. Queda anotado en `CLAUDE.md`.

`oceanus` **no** entra en `config.ALL_INDICATORS`: vive sólo en el hub, no en el prompt de la IA. También anotado.

## Validación

`tests/test_budai_oceanus_parity.py` (5 tests):

1. **Paridad Pine** — transcripción bar-a-bar independiente del bloque CÁLCULOS (loops explícitos, sin vectorizar): `osc`, `trig` y `mfi` iguales a 1e-9.
2. **Cross-check KryptoLab** — compara contra `oceanus_oscillator` del núcleo numpy cuando el checkout está dentro de signalsTrading (skip si no). `osc` y `mfi` bit-a-bit; `trig` sólo desde la barra `norm_len + trig_len` porque KryptoLab expande el `sma` en el warmup donde Pine (y este port, como pulse/athenea) da `na` — esos valores extra caen dentro de la ventana min/max de `f_norm`.
3. `osc_source` cambia `osc` pero **no** `mfi` (el Pine hardcodea hlc3).
4. Cotas 0-100 y que las señales fuertes sean subconjunto de los cruces.
5. Forma del summary.

Más `test_series_oceanus_shape` en `tests/test_indicators_series.py`.

```
$ python -m pytest tests/test_budai_oceanus_parity.py -q
5 passed

$ python -m pytest tests/ -q
6 failed, 143 passed
```

Los 6 fallos (`test_indicators_summary.py` ×5, `test_crypto_ohlcv_reader.py` ×1) son **preexistentes** en `origin/master`: verificado corriéndolos con este branch stasheado.

## Paridad live

Ninguno de los tres módulos núcleo (KryptoLab, PySignalGenerator, reconcile_daemon) se toca. Esto es sólo el hub de visualización: no ejecuta ni dimensiona nada.

author: chelseakr
body:
Phase 3 of `docs/EXPANSION-PLAN.md` (added in #102). Closes #70.

## The mechanism

`.github/workflows/currency.yml` ran every Monday and called
`gh issue create --title "... ($(date -u +%F))"`. Three compounding reasons it
could never converge: no deduplication of any kind on the source-currency
step, a date in the title guaranteeing a distinct title every run, and a
condition that stays red until a human acts. #63 and #65 are two weeks of one
problem.

The same step fired for three conditions with different owners and different
urgency, behind one heading: a changed source hash, an aged-out rule, and a
Golden regression. By the time the pile is three deep, nobody is reading which
one it is.

## What changed

- **Stable, dateless titles.** The run date, run link, and breakdown go in the
  body.
- **Search before create.** Both alerts look for the open issue and
  `gh issue comment` on it instead of filing a second one.
- **A `currency` label** on both, created idempotently so it can never fail a
  run that is already reporting a real problem.
- **Escalation without extra state.** Each repeat comment says how many days
  the condition has been open, from the issue's own `createdAt`.
- **Close on green.** A passing run closes the alert it opened, with a comment
  naming the run that cleared it. This also clears the #63/#65 backlog, since
  the letters close matches on title alone and those predate the label.
- **Exit 2 appears nowhere in the close step.** A source that could not be
  downloaded is evidence about the network. It must not open an alert, and it
  must not close one either, because nothing was learned about the law.
- **The harness says which condition fired.** `python -m permit_pathways.harness`
  now prints one machine-readable line on every run, including a clean one:

  ```
  currency signals: changed_sources=0 stale_rules=0 golden_regressions=0 unverifiable_sources=0
  ```

  Printed unconditionally on purpose: a signal that only appears on failure
  cannot be used to detect recovery. `main()` also takes an `argv` so this is
  testable without touching `sys.argv`.

## Proof each new test can fail

### The workflow tests

Ten new tests in `tests/test_currency_workflow.py`, against the pre-change
workflow:

```
FAILED test_no_issue_title_carries_the_run_date
FAILED test_the_currency_alert_searches_before_it_creates
FAILED test_both_alerts_carry_the_currency_label
```

### The scan-date tests

Four new tests in `tests/test_conformance.py` fail before (`main()` took no
argv and there was no per-slug date logic).

## The workflow shell is executed, not just matched

String assertions prove a workflow says the right words; they cannot prove it
runs. `_run_script()` lifts the step's own `run:` body out of the YAML as text
(the module deliberately avoids a YAML parser, since PyYAML is only a
transitive dependency here) and runs it under `bash` against a fake `gh` that
logs its arguments. That is what proves:

- one undated, labelled issue when none is open;
- a comment and **no** `issue create` when one is open;
- a body naming only the conditions that actually fired (a stale-only run does
  not mention sources or Golden cases);
- survival of a report with no signal line at all, falling back to alerting
  rather than crashing and leaving the condition unreported;
- the close step commenting and closing only the alert whose check went green.

Writing that test is also what caught a latent `set -euo pipefail` hazard: the
condition guards were `[ ... ] && fired=...`, and they are now explicit `if`
blocks so nothing about the exit status is subtle.

`zizmor --min-severity low --min-confidence low` is clean on the rewritten
workflow, and every `run:` body passes `bash -n`.

## Also: scan results stop being re-dated in passing

Weakness 3 from
`docs/findings/2026-08-15-multi-jurisdiction-adu-ordinance-scan.md`.
`scan_ordinances.py` took one global `scanned_on` and stamped it on all eight
results, including jurisdictions whose text had not been re-retrieved, so the
field recorded when the writer last ran rather than when that ordinance was
scanned.

Before, running the writer with a new date against the unchanged corpus:

```
$ .venv/bin/python scripts/scan_ordinances.py 2026-09-09
$ git diff --stat data/conformance/results/
 8 files changed, 14 insertions(+), 14 deletions(-)
```

After, the same command:

```
kept their own scan date (output unchanged): angels, capitola, folsom,
foster-city, san-diego, trinidad, watsonville
$ git diff --stat data/conformance/results/
(nothing)
```

Each result is re-derived with its own recorded date first; only ones that
come back different, or that have no published result yet, take the new date.
`--redate-all` covers a deliberate re-retrieval of the whole corpus. This also
stops the writer disturbing `san-diego.json` and `index.json`, which are
pinned by raw hash in the frozen schema-v1 export profile.

author: tcashel
body:
## What

R6 + R7 + R9 from a production incident postmortem, stacked on #183. Answering "is it running?" required reconciling five disagreeing fields (epic `active`, desired `running`, last outcome `exhausted`, `live: 0`, controller `unknown`); a 100%-deterministic per-child crash loop was indistinguishable from a transient blip on every durable surface, with the only evidence in controller-local log files; `submitted: true` said nothing about setup; two false controller-dead symptom attentions fired seconds after every submit; and single-writer serialization was only discoverable by diffing two children's admission blobs.

## How

- **One execution-health verdict** (`crates/forged/src/core/health.rs`): a single derivation over the desired row, controller knowledge, input-required/pause state, and the latest `forged.controller.terminal` marker. Closed set, precedence-ordered: `terminal > not-started > input-required > paused > halted / exhausted / stopped > queued > running > unsubmitted`. The desired row decides the doomed states before any liveness guess — a dead-but-budgeted controller is still `running` (the supervisor's restart IS the running state), while the incident's lookalikes (`halted`, `exhausted`) are separated via the shared halt-prefix const written by #183's supervisor. Emitted from `epic_status` (which also gains the epic-level `desired` row it previously omitted entirely), per-child in the status, `work_detail`'s status block, and every `operations_overview` entry.
- **`lastControllerFailure`** `{code, message, recoverable, generation, at}` from the latest controller-terminal marker, on `epic_status` (epic and per-child) and `work_detail` — the durable answer to "why is it not running" that previously lived only in `controller-<gen>.log`.
- **Submit readback (R6)**: every submit response shape now names its `phase` (`spawned` / `queued` / `recovered` / `already-running` / `stopped`) and fresh authorizations carry the minted `controlRevision` — a bare resubmit after exhaustion visibly answers `controlRevision: 2` instead of silently recovering. `epic submit --wait-setup` (params `waitSetup`, stripped before the fence so it never perturbs operation identity) polls read-only up to 30s and attaches `setup: "complete" | "failed" (+ evidence) | "pending"`.
- **Symptom debounce (R9a)**: the wake-overdue controller-dead symptom now requires the wake to be overdue by a 15s grace (3× the supervisor poll), so the post-submit admission storm self-heals inside the grace instead of minting false positives.
- **Wave-level deferral summary (R9b)**: `epic_status` gains top-level `deferred` (reason → count across non-terminal children), so `{"repository-write-capacity": 1}` reads as expected single-writer serialization rather than a stall.

All wire changes are additive; no existing field is renamed, removed, or re-typed.

## Deliberate scope cuts

- `authorize_tx` still sets `next_wake_at = now`: the attention grace alone retires the false positive, keeps the first reconcile immediate, and avoids time math in forged-ledger.
- `operations_overview` rows pass `input_required: false` (a portfolio row cannot cheaply prove it; drill-down surfaces own that verdict) and omit `lastControllerFailure` (one event query per row).
- Run-scope submit gains `phase`/`controlRevision` via the shared path but not `waitSetup` (an epic-setup concept).
- The closed attention condition/action enums are untouched (pinned across HTML assets, app fixtures, and the manage-work skill); a distinct `controller-halted` condition for richer UI treatment stays future work.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean · `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean · `cargo build --workspace --locked` clean
- `cargo nextest run --workspace` — 1154 passed, 3 skipped (bd-gated, expected)
- `cargo nextest run -p forged --features failpoints` — 545 passed, 2 skipped (one known herdr-orphan mock-socket flake failed the first pass under load; green in isolation and on the clean full rerun)
- New coverage: the health lattice unit tests (including the incident's exact five-field shape), grace-window supervise fixtures, and an end-to-end walk asserting the verdict and deferral summary from `epic_status`, `operations_overview`, and `work_detail` across unsubmitted → running/queued → paused, plus `--wait-setup` and resubmit `controlRevision` readback.
- The end-to-end deferral fixture went through two hardening rounds worth knowing about. Racing the epic's own two children against the single repository-write slot is **not deterministic**: under load, a slow child spawn releases and re-admits the slot, and one observed run ended with BOTH children `admitted | capacity-available` against `repository_write_active: 1` — an admission custody race in its own right, noted for follow-up, and exactly why the test now parks a standalone hang run on the slot (settled custody) before the epic dispatches, making both children defer deterministically. The wind-down asserts the durable paused verdict and reaps the detached controller's process group directly instead of waiting out its exit cadence; killed test runs previously leaked those controllers indefinitely.

author: robhunterclaude
body:
`main` is red: `test/feed-weekly-digest.test.ts` → "no entry has a future updated date" fails with `Date 2026-08-28T12:00:00.000Z should not be in the future`.

Each weekly Atom entry was stamped `new Date(newestChange + "T12:00:00Z")`. That was harmless while the newest recorded change was always a past day. The re-verification detector shipped in #1097 now records changes at 00:01Z every morning, so from the run until noon the feed publishes an `<updated>` up to 12 hours ahead of the present — and the feed-level `<updated>`, which reduces over the entry stamps, inherits it. A future `updated` is what an Atom reader sorts and de-duplicates on.

`feedEntryUpdated(day, now)` in `src/change-dates.ts` clamps the noon stamp to `now`, and falls back to `now` for an unparseable day.

Verified against a local server at 01:04:45Z: both entries now carry `2026-08-28T01:04:45.038Z` where they previously carried `2026-08-28T12:00:00.000Z`.

Four unit tests cover both sides of noon, a past day, and the unparseable input. Replacing the clamp with the bare noon stamp fails one of them.

No issue — this is the red-main gate, found on wake.

body:
## Summary

Make the shared REST label reader authoritative when verifying workflow label
writes. The implementation now requests explicit pages of 100 labels, validates
every row strictly, and fails closed when a page fails or the finite ten-page
ceiling cannot prove completeness.

Closes #7974
Refs #7971

## Why

The idempotent label-removal repair in #7973 still read only the first labels
page and silently dropped malformed rows. A label on page two could therefore
be missed and an incomplete response could be reported as a successful
readback.

## Changes

- Add deterministic `per_page=100&page=N` REST reads with a bounded ceiling of
  10 pages.
- Reject non-array pages, non-object rows, and missing or blank label names;
  never return a partial label inventory.
- Fail closed on later-page transport failures and on a full page at the
  ceiling, which cannot establish that the inventory is complete.
- Preserve the narrow concurrent-absent-label 404 behavior from #7973 while
  requiring strict complete readback before reporting success.

## Evidence / Claim Boundary

This is smoke-level workflow reliability evidence only. It makes no benchmark,
planner, scheduler, publication, provenance, or scientific-result claim.

## Validation / Proof

- `python -m pytest tests/dev/test_gh_pr_label_rest.py -q` — 25 passed.
- `python -m pytest tests/dev/test_gh_rest.py tests/ci/test_collect_pr_files.py -q` — 42 passed.

Not applicable — this is a support/workflow change with no benchmark artifact,

author: jvillad1
body:
Pedido del dueño: *«no me gusta que las categorías no estén tipo orden alfabético sino
en cualquier orden»*.

## Lo que había

`PREDEFINED_CATEGORIES` estaba en un orden **escrito a mano** —Comida, Transporte, Salud,
Educación…— que no era alfabético ni de frecuencia: era el orden en que alguien las
escribió. La pantalla «Más → Categorías» no aplicaba ningún criterio. Y el server
devolvía `… Zeta, Ácido, Ángel, Árbol, Ñandú …`: **todo lo acentuado después de la Z**,
porque ordenaba por código interno y no como palabras. Ese era el «cualquier orden».

## El criterio

`categorySortKey(name)` en `:core`: minúsculas, sin tildes ni diéresis, y **ñ → `n~`**
para que caiga justo después de la n. Desempate estable por el nombre crudo. Tabla a
mano, como `normalizeForMatch`, porque no hay colación Unicode común a los tres targets.

`normalizeForMatch` **no** servía como clave: mapea ñ→n a secas (pondría «Ñu» antes de
«Nube») y no tocaba la `ü`.

Comprobado con 17 categorías reales sembradas por API: `Ácido · Ángel · Árbol ·
Arriendo recibido · … · Nueces · Ñandú · Ñapa · Ñoquis · Oso · Otros · Pingüinos · Ropa ·
… · Transporte · Único · Vivienda · Zapatos · Zeta`. Orden de diccionario.

## Las dos decisiones

**Se sacó el bloque «catálogo antes que propias».** El KDoc lo justificaba por el *primer
lugar*; con orden alfabético el primer lugar lo decide la letra. Mantener dos bloques
dejaba el alfabeto arrancando dos veces, que es la queja misma. Lo único que dependía de
«la primera que se ofrece» era el **prellenado**, y se desacopló: `categoriaPorDefectoPara`
lee el catálogo en su orden, así que **Gasto sigue arrancando en «Comida» e Ingreso en
«Salario»** — verificado en pantalla por el autor y por la revisión.

**Lo tecleado rankea:** lo que **empieza** con lo escrito va antes que lo que apenas lo
**contiene**; alfabético dentro de cada grupo. Con «co»: `Crear "co"` → Colegio → Comida →
Bancolombia.

## Un bug que apareció al cerrar la diéresis

`categorySortKey` sacaba la `ü` pero `normalizeForMatch` no, así que «Pingüinos» **ordenaba**
como «pinguinos» y **no se encontraba** buscándola así. Al mirarlo de cerca era peor: el
campo tampoco la **reconocía** como nombre conocido, así que ofrecía **«Crear "pinguinos"»**
— partir la categoría en dos por una diéresis, que es justo lo que `nombreCanonicoConocido`
existe para impedir.

Las tres tablas cubren ahora las mismas letras y difieren en un solo punto, dicho en las
tres: para **buscar**, la ñ se aplasta contra la n («nono» encuentra «Ñoño»); para
**ordenar**, va después.

## El orden viejo tenía una razón, y está declarada

`CategoryRoutes.kt:476` documentaba «lo más usado primero — la pregunta que trae al dueño
acá es *qué sobra*». Se cambió igual porque es lo que el dueño pidió, y **el uso sigue
visible en cada renglón** («1 movimiento · $15.000» / «Sin movimientos»). El `ORDER BY` del
server quedó sin tocar: es trabajo muerto, pero sin contradicción visible, porque los tres
clientes pasan por el mismo `:shared`.

## Verificación

`:core:test :core:jvmTest :server:test :shared:testDebugUnitTest
:shared:compileKotlinWasmJs :shared:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

Revisión independiente que verificó **ejecutando** lo que más importaba: que el orden se
aplica **después** de los filtros, así que no puede reintroducir nada. Comprobó en la app
que ninguna reservada se cuela (y que el server sigue rechazando el POST con 422), que una
categoría escondida desaparece —escondió «Ácido», la primera del alfabeto, el peor caso
para un orden nuevo—, que el filtro por tipo aguanta, que «Crear "X"» sigue arriba de todo,
y que el prellenado no se rompió.

body:
## 概要

インフラを Terraform で管理できるようにし、**ステージング環境を GCP に構築した。**
`infra/` に共通モジュールと環境ごとの定義を置き、`tosyo-api-stg` に
Cloud Run（api / web）・Cloud Run Job（migrate / worker）・Cloud SQL・GCS・
Secret Manager・Artifact Registry・Cloud Scheduler の 50 リソースを構築して疎通を確認した。

**REQ-0053 を 2 本に分けた 1 本目**（設計書のフェーズ 2）。受入基準 11 件のうち 9 件を満たす。
残る CI/CD（Workload Identity 連携・自動デプロイ・業務シナリオ確認）は PR 2 で出す。

Refs: REQ-0053

## 変更内容

- `infra/modules/` に 9 つの共通モジュール、`infra/envs/staging/` にステージングの定義
- `infra/scripts/bootstrap-state-bucket.sh`（state バケットだけは Terraform で作れないため）
- `scripts/terraform-check.sh` を追加し、`quality-gate.sh` と `ci.yml` の両方から実行
- **ADR-0030 を起票**: 実行中のコンテナイメージを Terraform の管理対象にしない
- `api/tests/unit/test_config.py` に、Terraform へ写した定数のドリフト検知テストを追加

### 構築した環境

| | URL |
|---|---|
| API | `https://pod-admin-api-kkwi54ngsq-an.a.run.app` |
| 管理画面 | `https://pod-admin-web-kkwi54ngsq-an.a.run.app` |

## 品質検証

- [x] 静的チェック: `scripts/quality-gate.sh` 通過
- [x] `/simplify max` 実行済み
  - 指摘: 24 件 / 修正: 12 件
  - 主な修正: 設定同士の関係を機械が守る形にした（Terraform に写した定数のテスト固定、
    DB 接続数予算の `validation`、スケジューラ停止条件の導出、ディスク自動拡張の上限）。
    サービスレベル `scaling` に `var.min_instances` を渡していた矛盾を解消し、
    死んだ出力・未使用変数・実体を持たない IAM を削除した。
- [x] 静的チェック再実行: 通過

**振る舞いが変わった修正が 1 件ある。** `worker_schedule_paused` を単独の設定から
`var.worker_schedule_paused || var.illustrator_vm_base_url == ""` の導出に変えた
（下記「レビュー観点」3 を参照）。

## 受入基準の検証結果

| # | 基準 | 検証方法 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | apply 完走 | 50 リソース作成 |
| 2 | plan 差分ゼロ | `gcloud run deploy` **後**に `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` が 0（`No changes`） |
| 3 | state バケット | `gs://tosyo-api-stg-tfstate` — バージョニング・UBLA・公開防止 |
| 4 | `/health` | 200 `{"status":"healthy"}` |
| 5 | フロント→API | バンドルに `.../api/v1` が焼き込み済み（`localhost` フォールバック無し）＋ 実リクエストで `access-control-allow-origin` が返る |
| 6 | Cloud SQL 接続 | ログイン → `GET /orders` 200（ページング形式） |
| 7 | migrate Job | `alembic upgrade head` 完走 → 15 テーブル、単一ヘッド |
| 8 | GCS | チャット添付を投稿 → `gs://tosyo-pod-admin-stg/staging/chat/...` に保存 → 同一内容で取得 |
| 9 | Secret Manager | 4 シークレットを注入。鍵 JSON はリポジトリにも環境変数にも無し（Cloud Run の SA から ADC で GCS へ） |

### 実測値

- **Cloud SQL `max_connections` = 25**（`SHOW max_connections` で実測。設計書が「値を仮定しない」と指示していた箇所）
- **API のコールドスタート 約 15 秒**（下記「発見事項」）
- **設計書 7.1 の `DATABASE_URL`（Unix ソケット）を実地検証。**
  `?host=/cloudsql/PROJECT:REGION:INSTANCE` はコロンを含むため SQLAlchemy の
  multihost 構文と誤解釈される懸念があったが、`host='/cloudsql/...'` として
  正しく asyncpg に渡ることを確認した

## レビュー観点

1. **イメージを Terraform の管理対象から外した判断（ADR-0030）。**
   Terraform が持つと、デプロイ経路に state バケットの書き込み権限が要る。
   ADR-0027 のとおり state には DB パスワードが平文で入るため、
   **「アプリを更新できる」と「本番 DB の資格情報を読める」が同じ権限になる。**
   1 日に何度も走る操作に最も重い権限を載せるのは筋が悪いと判断した。
   代償として、Terraform の定義を読んでも動いている版は分からない。

2. **GCS のライフサイクルを設計書から変えた。**
   設計書は「本番 180 日 / ステージング 30 日」としていたが、**現行オブジェクトの削除は
   ステージングに限った**（本番は旧バージョンのみ）。本番で現行を消すと、DB に残った
   `file_path` が実体を失う。本番の保持方針は REQ-0054 で決めたい。

3. **スケジューラの停止条件を導出に変えた（振る舞いの変更）。**
   `illustrator_vm_base_url = ""` と `worker_schedule_paused = true` は必ず一緒に動く
   必要があるが、並べただけでは片方を変えた事故を防げない。VM 未設定のまま再開すると
   `run_generation` が `IllustratorVmError` を投げ、待ち行列の行が 5 分ごとに最大 20 件ずつ
   `failed` へ落ちる（`manufacturing_data_service.py` で確認）。導出に変えてよいか。

4. **`nfr.md` を 1 行直した（憲章の変更）。**
   「製造データ生成はプロセス再起動時に取り残しジョブを復旧する（`recover_stranded_generations`）」
   の関数は REQ-0052 で削除済みで、記述が事実と食い違っていた。約束の実質（取り残しの復旧）は
   ワーカー側に移って維持されているため、機構名の訂正にとどめた。
   **憲章の変更が Terraform のレビューのついでに承認されるのは望ましくない**ので、
   ここに明記する。切り離すべきなら分離する。

5. **ステージングのシードパスワードは `scripts/seed.py` の既定値のままにしてある。**
   検証のため `scripts/seed.py` を流した。ステージングは公開 URL なので
   一度ランダム値へ変えたが、**依頼を受けて既定値に戻した**（テスト時の利便性を優先）。
   `admin@example.com` / `admin123`、`operator@example.com` / `operator123`、
   メーカー 2 件 / `manufacturer123`。
   ステージングは本番データを持たないが、**URL を知っていれば誰でもログインできる状態**
   である点は認識しておきたい。

## ドキュメントの更新

- [x] 満たした受入基準を `[x]` にした（9/11）
- [ ] すべて満たしたので status を `done` にした
      → **`in-progress` のまま**（PR 2 で残り 2 件を満たして `done` にする）
- [x] 設計判断があれば ADR を起こした（ADR-0030）
- [x] 該当なし（不具合ではない）

## 発見事項

**REQ-0057（新規・`priority: undecided`）— 本番コンテナが起動のたびに依存を取り直している。**

```
00:36:46  インスタンス起動
00:36:47  Downloading mypy (13.0MiB) / ruff (13.6MiB)   ← 開発用ツール
00:36:56  Bytecode compiled 3768 files in 6.08s
00:37:01  Uvicorn running                                ← 15 秒
```

`uv run` が実行前に環境を同期し直すため、イメージから `--no-dev` で除いたはずのものが戻る。
Railway 時代からの性質で、今回の移行が持ち込んだものではない。
既存の受入基準（`nfr.md` の性能は「SLA 未定義」）に違反しないため、不具合ではなく要件とした。

**設計書 9.4 の判断に直接効く。** 「外部販売サイトのタイムアウトが 10 秒未満なら
`min-instances=1`（約 ¥6,000/月）」としているが、**アプリが動き出す前に 10 秒を使い切っている。**
直せば費用をかけずに済む可能性がある。

### `/simplify` の指摘のうち、今回直さずに記録したもの

- **`infra/modules/stack/` への切り出し**（2 エージェントが指摘）。
  `envs/staging/main.tf` にアプリ固有の知識（環境変数の一覧、シークレット名の対応、
  `CORS_ORIGINS` を JSON で渡す必要）が入っており、このまま `envs/prod/` を作ると複製される。
  ADR-0027 が選択肢 C を退けた理由がそのまま当てはまる。
  ただし今やると state のアドレスが変わり 50 件超の `terraform state mv` が要るため、
  **REQ-0054 の「`envs/prod/` を作る前に済ませること」に記録した。**
- **Job の起動コマンドの重複** — REQ-0057 を直すとき `api/Dockerfile` だけでは終わらず、
  Terraform 側の migrate / worker も直す必要がある。REQ-0057 に追記した。

### 人間の作業が残っているもの

- **SendGrid の鍵**（`gcloud secrets versions add sendgrid-api-key`）。
  Secret Manager は空のペイロードを拒否するため、Terraform は `REPLACE_ME` を入れている。
  そのままでもアプリは起動し業務フローも壊れない（送信系は例外を握って `False` を返す）
- **予算アラート**（請求先アカウントの権限が要るためプロジェクト所有者の作業。REQ-0053 のスコープ外）

author: myungwoo
body:
## 왜

오래된 화면이라 색만 바꿔서는 정리가 되지 않는 상태였다.

- Tailwind 기본 팔레트(`gray-50`, `blue-500` …)가 컴포넌트마다 흩어져 있어 라이트/다크 중 한쪽이 늘 어긋났다.
- 스탑워치↔타이머 전환이 **제목 `<h2>` 클릭**, 시간 수정이 **숫자 클릭**이었다. 눌러야 한다는 걸 알 방법이 없고 키보드로는 닿지 않았다.
- 정산 결과가 중첩 `<ul>` 나열이라 정작 자주 보는 5분당 수익을 찾으려면 목록 전체를 읽어야 했다.
- `md` 브레이크포인트 하나뿐이라 사실상 데스크탑 전용이었다.

## 무엇을

### 색을 토큰으로 모았다

`globals.css`의 `:root` / `.dark`가 색의 유일한 출처가 되고, `tailwind.config.ts`가 `bg-surface`·`text-muted`·`text-accent` 같은 이름으로 노출한다. 컴포넌트에서 팔레트 색을 직접 쓰지 않는다.

다크는 `.dark` 클래스로만 갈린다. `prefers-color-scheme`로 색을 정의하면 `layout.tsx`의 프리-페인트 스크립트가 정한 테마와 어긋나므로 쓰지 않는다. 이 규약은 `CLAUDE.md`에 항목으로 적어 두었다.

경험치·주요 액션은 accent, 메소·수익은 gold — 데이터의 의미를 색에 실었다.

### 레이아웃

헤더(로고 · 기록 · 테마) + 왼쪽 타이머·입력 / 오른쪽 sticky 정산 결과. 항상 왼쪽 칼럼을 차지하던 기록 목록은 드로어로 옮겼다.

모바일에서는 한 줄로 쌓이고 결과와 저장이 마지막에 온다. 측정 중에는 헤더에 시계가 떠서, 긴 폼을 내리는 동안에도 시간이 보인다.

입력 폼은 시작/종료를 좌우 칼럼으로 갈라 놓던 것을 **지표별 행**(레벨 `[시작][종료]`)으로 바꿨다. 실제로 비교하는 값끼리 붙고 320px에서도 안 깨진다. 아이템 표는 넓은 화면에선 표, 좁은 화면에선 필드별 라벨이 붙은 카드가 된다.

### 조작

- 모드 전환은 세그먼트 컨트롤, 시간 직접 입력은 버튼으로 드러냈다. 둘 다 키보드로 닿는다.
- 라벨을 `htmlFor`로 입력과 이었다.
- 카드마다 세 개씩 뜨던 직접 만든 툴팁을 네이티브 `title`로 정리했다 — 터치 기기에서는 아예 뜨지 않았다.
- 경험치·메소·아이템 개수·개당 가격에 세 자리 구분을 넣었다. 커서가 끝으로 튀지 않고, 쉼표 뒤에서 Backspace를 누르면 앞 숫자가 지워진다(그러지 않으면 쉼표만 지워졌다가 되살아나 아무 일도 없는 것처럼 보인다).

### 로직

정산 공식을 `src/lib/hunting.ts`로 분리했다. **식은 그대로다.** 폼과 결과 패널이 같은 값을 봐야 해서 `stats`/`items`/`note`를 `page`로 올렸다.

### 확인창을 앱 안으로

`window.confirm`은 문구를 다듬을 수도, 버튼을 늘릴 수도, 위험한 동작을 눈에 띄게 만들 수도 없다. 그래서 **기록 불러오기는 두 갈래 버튼에 세 갈래 뜻이 들어가 있었다** — "취소"가 곧 전체 교체라, 문구를 잘못 읽으면 저장된 기록이 통째로 사라졌다. 서버가 없어 되돌릴 방법도 없다.

`ui/Dialog.tsx`에 프로미스 기반 확인창을 두고 호출부는 `await` 한 줄로 남겼다(7곳에 상태를 따로 두지 않는다).

- 불러오기를 **[취소] [모두 교체] [기존에 추가]** 세 버튼으로 나눴다. 문구를 읽지 않아도 버튼에 적혀 있다.
- 진행 버튼에 "확인" 대신 "삭제"·"모두 지우기"처럼 무슨 일이 일어나는지 적고, 무엇을 잃는지도 설명에 적는다(기록 n건, 지금 표시된 시간 등).
- **되돌릴 수 없는 확인창은 안전한 쪽(취소)에 포커스**를 준다. Enter를 무심코 눌러 기록이 사라지면 복구할 수단이 없다.
- `role="alertdialog"`, Esc로 물러나기, Tab 가두기, 닫은 뒤 포커스 되돌리기.
- Drawer도 `document`에서 Escape를 듣고 있어, 확인창 층에서 온 키는 넘기게 했다. 그러지 않으면 Esc 한 번에 확인창과 서랍이 같이 닫힌다.

저장 시 사냥터가 비어 있을 때 띄우던 `alert`은 **그 칸 아래 인라인 오류**로 바꿨다. 대화상자는 정작 어느 칸이 문제인지 가려 버린다. 화면 밖에 있을 수 있으니 포커스와 스크롤도 그 칸으로 옮긴다.

### 마감

- **좁은 화면에서 아이템 삭제 버튼이 이름 입력을 덮고 있었다.** 390px 기준 이름 입력 72–329px, 삭제 버튼 293–329px로 **오른쪽 36px가 겹쳐**, 긴 이름의 끝을 누르면 삭제가 눌렸다. 이름 쪽에 자리를 비웠다(겹침 36px → 0).
- **정산 패널이 화면보다 길면 저장 버튼이 페이지 맨 아래에서만 눌렸다.** 아이템 12개·뷰포트 700px에서 패널이 1234px가 되어, 중간 스크롤에서 버튼은 화면 밖 1167px에 있었다. 결과만 패널 안에서 스크롤시키고 저장 버튼은 아래에 붙여 어느 위치에서든 보이게 했다. 좁은 화면에는 제약을 걸지 않는다.
- **서랍이 닫힐 때 애니메이션이 없었다.** 나가는 동안만 더 그려 두고 반대 방향으로 미끄러지게 했다. 그 사이에는 `role`을 떼고 클릭도 통과시킨다.

### 수익 표시 단위를 고르게 한다

사냥터마다 익숙한 단위가 다르다. 물약 소모는 분당이 편하고, 경험치는 5분당으로 재는 사람이 많고, 사냥터끼리 비교할 때는 시간당이 눈에 들어온다. 정산 결과 카드 헤더에서 **1분 / 5분 / 1시간**을 고른다.

- 기본값은 **5분** — 지금까지 보여 주던 단위라 기존 사용자에게는 숫자가 그대로다.
- 정산 결과, 기록 카드, 펼친 상세, 복사 문구까지 같은 단위를 따른다.
- 선택은 `ml:hunt:rate`에 남고, 모르는 값이면 기본값으로 본다.
- 계산은 늘 분당으로 해 두고 보여 줄 때만 곱한다. 단위를 바꿔도 저장되는 값은 달라지지 않는다.
- 분당 값은 반올림하지 않고 들고 있다가 **단위를 곱한 뒤 한 번만** 반올림한다. 먼저 반올림하고 곱하면 5분당 596,828이 596,830으로 어긋난다.

### 정산 결과를 저장하지 않는다

위 변경을 하다 보니 근본 문제가 드러났다. **결과는 전부 `stats`·`items`·`duration`에서 나오는 파생값인데 기록에 같이 저장하고 있었다.** 그래서 수치의 뜻을 바꿀 때마다 쌓인 기록을 전부 손봐야 했고, 예전 값과 새 값을 필드 두 벌로 들고 있어야 했다.

읽기를 계산으로 바꾸니 그 일이 통째로 사라졌다.

- `resultsOf(record)`로 그릴 때마다 낸다. 기록 목록은 `useMemo`로 목록이 바뀔 때만 계산한다 — 검색어를 칠 때마다 다시 돌 이유는 없다.
- 마이그레이션 코드를 지웠다. 읽지 않으니 맞출 것도 없다.
- 계산식은 최초 커밋 이후 바뀐 적이 없어서(그 뒤 변경은 다크 모드 색뿐), 옛 기록을 다시 계산해도 그때 보이던 숫자가 그대로 나온다.

**저장도 하지 않는다.** 기록은 재료만 들고 있다 — `id`, `timestamp`, `duration`, `location`, `stats`, `items`, `note`. 내보낸 파일도 같은 모양이다.

### 숫자 입력칸 우측 정렬

시작과 종료를 나란히 놓고 비교하는 구조라 자릿수가 맞아야 `8,500,000`과 `3,200,000`의 크기 차이가 눈에 들어온다. 레벨은 이득이 적지만 한 칸만 왼쪽이면 어긋나 보여 같이 맞췄다. 글자를 받는 칸(사냥터, 아이템 이름)은 왼쪽 그대로다.

## 딸려 온 버그 수정

아이템이 없는 기록을 불러오면 이전 아이템이 그대로 남아 있었다. `StatsForm`이 `initialItems.length > 0`일 때만 동기화하고 있었는데, 값의 주인을 하나로 만들면서 사라졌다.

## 건드리지 않은 것

`ml:hunt:` 접두어와 공유 `ml:theme` 키 규약, 레거시 키 마이그레이션, 실제 시계 기반 시간 계산, `output: "export"` 정적 빌드와 상대경로 에셋.

숫자 입력의 표시 서식은 화면에만 들어간다. 상태와 저장되는 기록은 숫자만 있는 문자열 그대로라, 기존에 저장된 기록이 그대로 열린다 — `parseInt('1,000,000')`은 1이 된다.

(없음)

## 검증

`npm run lint`, `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`(정적 export) 통과.

브라우저에서 데스크탑/모바일 × 라이트/다크로 확인했고, 사냥 기록 8건(레벨업 있음/없음, 아이템 0~2개, 순수익 마이너스 포함)을 넣어 불러오기·정산·검색·드로어·확인창을 확인했다. 앱이 다시 계산한 결과가 저장된 값과 일치한다. 저장된 `results`를 일부러 `999,999,999`로 오염시켜도 화면 숫자가 그대로였고, `results`를 통째로 지운 기록 8건도 정상 표시된다 — 파생 계산이 실제로 저장값을 읽지 않는다는 확인이다. 새로 저장한 기록의 `results`는 예전 배포가 읽는 모양 그대로였다.
