author: smerwin
body:
Fixes #395. Rebased onto `main` now that #401 has merged — this branch is one commit and
merges cleanly; its 34 cases were re-run against the new base.

## The defect

The broadcast banner is a **last-broadcast display and never clears**, so when the called
rat dies the banner still names it. `calledTargetIsLocked` is false — the thing is gone —
the arm answers `Just (lock it)`, and `lockCalledTarget` finds no overview row and answers
`waitForProgressInGame`: a wait with **no bound and no give-up**. Because the arm answered
`Just`, everything below it in the root — drones, guns, gate, approach — is unreachable
for the rest of the session, or until the FC calls another target.

Live: three of four wingmen killed **37 rats each** and stopped together, 25 repeats each
in a 400-line scrollback, `Weapons: nothing locked`. Identical kill counts across all
three is the tell — they stopped at the same moment, when the called target died. (Those
observations are #395's; there is no client, corpus or game log on the machine this was
written on, so nothing here recomputes them and no case rests on them.)

This is #360 and #389 in a third variant. #360 fixed "the banner names a target already
locked"; #389 fixed "locked but not recognised"; this is "not there any more", and that
branch has never had an answer other than waiting.

It builds on #401's `CalledNameNamesNoOverviewRow`, which is exactly this state already
named — one detector, not a second.

## The counter, not the latch — and why

#395 offers both shapes. The argument against a pure latch is that `fleetBroadcastFollowed`
bounds a **one-shot** action — the ESI route ask goes out once per banner — where a target
call is a **standing** instruction. #360's own fix re-derives "is it locked" every reading
precisely because a lock can break while the call is still live, so a latch fired when the
arm first acts would stop the bot re-locking a target it lost.

The only event a latch could honestly fire on here is *this call names nothing on the
grid*, which is the counter's verdict one reading early.

What the latch does contribute is the **name**. `BotMemory.calledTargetGone : Maybe
{ calledTarget, readings }` means a second call is never given up on with none of its own
readings spent — a bare counter would hand one call's arrears to the next, which is #145's
shape.

**One clause clears it**, covering all three ways the state ends: `calledTargetGoneAfterReading`
answers `Nothing` on any reading `calledTargetWithNoOverviewRow` does not answer `Just` for
— the row coming back, a different target being called, and the banner going away. A
different call restarts at one.

**The bound is 3, and it bounds a parse rather than a range.** `CalledNameNamesNoOverviewRow`
is not virtualisation — a scrolled-out row is still in the tree and answers
`CalledObjectIsNotAGate` — so a live target reaches this state only through the overview's
own range filter or a reading that did not parse. Three is the count CLAUDE.md's ship-loss
signal already gives that same doubt. It sits far below `weaponsAskedReadingsBound` (20)
and `accelerationGateRefusesThisShipTicks` (40), which is right: those bound a click the
client refuses, this bounds a reading with nothing to click.

`calledTargetWithNoOverviewRow` is the arm's own precondition — fleet-member guard included
— and the memory update asks it rather than restating it.

## The property asserted is the fall-through, not "it stops re-locking"

`test_the_reading_falls_through_once_the_call_is_stale`: spent memory gives `FELL THROUGH`,
and **the same fixture with `initBotMemory` must still print** `Lock the called target
'Centus Black Ops Veteran'.` in the same repl call — so a rule answering `Nothing` for
everything cannot pass.

The stronger one, `test_the_grace_is_bounded_by_the_real_memory_update`, folds the shipped
`updateMemoryForNewReadingFromGame` over a session of #395's own reading and then asks the
shipped arm about the memory that fold left: at the bound it is still trying, one past it
the arm hands the reading back. Counter, verdict and arm executed together rather than
separately. `test_the_session_really_counted_what_that_case_thinks` guards that fold
against being a counter that never advanced.

## Verification

`tools/macos-host/tests/test_wingman_called_target_gone.py`, **34 cases**, all passing,
0 skipped (`check_expected_skips.py` clean, no new skip reasons) — re-run after the rebase,
against `main`.

**Executed** through the real `Bot.elm` in `elm repl`, over readings from the real
`EveOnline.ParseUserInterface`: the precondition over five real readings, the counter folded
over sessions, the verdict at its boundary *and* at fixed values either side, the
fall-through, and both status clauses rendered from the record. **Read** from source
(comment-stripped, whitespace-collapsed): the memory update's single rule, the give-up's
placement ahead of the lock, that `lockCalledTarget`'s unbounded wait is now reachable from
one state only, and that exactly two declarations read the memory. No parser change.

**18 mutations, none survived**, including: the give-up dropped (4 cases, both
fall-throughs); the count never cleared; a different call inheriting the previous one's
count; the comparison `<=` and one late; the bound at 40 and at 0; the counter advancing on
every reading, on a not-drawn gate, and on a fleetmate; the update restating the
precondition; the give-up placed after the lock; and `overviewEntryForPilot` filtering on
`_display`.

## Not verified

Nothing has been flown. What to watch on the first run where a called target dies: the
status clause counting 1, 2, 3 and then the arm handing the reading back, with the guns and
the drones resuming on the next reading rather than `Weapons: nothing locked` continuing.

## Unrelated failure on main, filed as #406

`test_wingman_called_gate.py::test_the_row_selection_has_one_definition` fails on `67ae53c2`
— #396 lifted `overviewEntryForPilot` out of `calledTargetIsLocked` and #401's case still
pins the pre-#396 shape. Each PR was green alone. This branch neither causes nor fixes it.

## Filed, not fixed here

#395's second half — Greta's unrecognised message box — is **#402**. It is worse than that
section frames it: wingman has no `MessageBoxStandoff` at all, so an unrecognised dialog
owns every reading for the rest of the session (run 30's shape), and the give-up names
nothing about the box, which is why the dialog still cannot be identified.

author: koenvangeert
body:
## Summary

Repositories that require the merge queue are detected again, so a ready pull request offers Enqueue instead of a Merge button GitHub rejects with a 405. Enqueue plumbing already existed end to end; only detection was dead.

`parse_repository_policy` read `requiresMergeQueue` on `BranchProtectionRule`, which is not in GitHub's GraphQL schema, so `merge_queue_required` was never true. The fact now comes from `PullRequest.isMergeQueueEnabled`.

`isMergeQueueEnabled` is deliberately absent from `PR_READINESS_CORE_QUERY`. That query is the escape hatch when the primary one fails schema validation, so adding the new field there would break the fallback for exactly the tenants that reject it.

## Impact Analysis

| | |
|---|---|
| 🎯 **Blast radius** | The readiness pipeline in the Rust sidecar and `getMergeReadiness` in `plugin-sdk`. `merge_queue_required` left `RepositoryPolicyFacts`, which had no other reader. |
| 🔍 **Look closest at** | `finalize_readiness_facts_for_poll`: the promotion moved out of the `if let Some(snapshot)` block so a snapshot-less poll keeps the last persisted requirement. |
| ⚠️ **Risk** | A tenant permanently pinned to the core query never re-observes the field, so a persisted `true` sticks after the queue is disabled. Signal: an Enqueue action GitHub answers with "not in a merge queue". No ticket yet. |

author: andrebarthelmeshellmuth
body:
## Why

The `TermVectorSnapshot` provider/restorer seam is **owned by this package** — `TermVectorSnapshotProviderPluginInterface` / `TermVectorSnapshotRestorerPluginInterface` live in `Client/SearchFeedback/Dependency/Plugin/`. search-ranking *implements* feedback's interface; feedback has **zero runtime code reference** to search-ranking (`git grep` finds only doc-comment prose and a gitignored generated transfer).

Yet `composer.json` carried `spryker-community/search-ranking` in `require-dev` **plus a `repositories` VCS entry pointing at a personal GitHub URL**, purely to make it resolvable in CI. Nothing in the standalone/portable suite references a single search-ranking class — the existing provider/restorer tests already use PHPUnit interface mocks. That VCS URL is also a loose end for the community-namespace transfer.

## What

- **Remove** `spryker-community/search-ranking` from `require-dev` and delete the now-empty `repositories` block. `suggest` still names it — the optional integration is real (install both + register the plugin + enable specificity → tickets carry the term-vector snapshot), it just isn't a build-time dependency.
- **Add** `FakeTermVectorSnapshotProviderPlugin` / `FakeTermVectorSnapshotRestorerPlugin` — tiny concrete implementations of this package's own interfaces, standing in for search-ranking's `SearchFeedbackTermVectorSnapshotProviderPlugin`.
- **Add** `TermVectorSnapshotStandaloneRoundTripTest` — proves the string a concrete provider produces at capture time is exactly what a concrete restorer receives on replay, with nothing from search-ranking on the classpath.

## Verification

`composer validate` and `php -l` clean. The portable suite could not be run in my local shell (host PHP is 8.5 with no `ext-xmlreader`, so `generate-transfers.php` can't run) — **relying on CI's 8.3/8.4 portable matrix here.** The new test mirrors the setup of the existing `SearchFeedbackSnapshotResultFormatterPluginTest` / `SearchFeedbackClientTest` almost line-for-line.

No runtime `require` or behaviour change. For the **v1.5.x** line.

author: mraszyk
body:
If the `subnet_merged` marker is set, `process_batch()` now resets it and records all not yet responded ingress-induced canister call contexts as `Processing` in the ingress history, so that the corresponding ingress messages can be tracked to completion.

Subnet call contexts are ignored, as subnet merging ensures that the subnets being merged have no in-progress subnet call contexts.

A message that already has an ingress history entry is left alone. Its status is expected to be `Processing`; anything else raises the new `mr_unexpected_ingress_status_after_merge` critical error.

author: rossdrew
body:
## Summary
- Implements Phase 1 of the `Controller input: 2-4 players, keyboard or gamepad, Four Score` plan: bit-accurate protocol core, wired end-to-end through `NES`/`NESMemoryBus`, using `Controller.NONE` as the only input source that exists so far (no keyboard/gamepad yet - phases 2/3).
- New `com.rox.input` package: `Button` enum (ordinal = shift-register bit position, A/B/Select/Start/Up/Down/Left/Right), `Controller` interface (`isPressed`, `NONE` default, a `poll()` default method unused until phase 3), `ControllerPort` (bit-accurate strobe/shift-register/Four-Score emulation, pure and dependency-free), `ControllerConfiguration` (bundles all 4 player slots + Four Score flag, mirrors how `VideoOutput` was threaded through as one param).
- `NESMemoryBus`: $4016/$4017 reads now route to a real `ControllerPort` each instead of a "no buttons pressed" stub. $4016 writes strobe **both** ports simultaneously (matches real hardware - a single strobe line wired to every port) and no longer reach the device bus. $4017 write behavior (APU frame counter) is unchanged.
- `NES`: `ControllerConfiguration` threaded through every constructor overload exactly like `VideoOutput` was - each layer forwards `ControllerConfiguration.NONE` except one new public overload `NES(VideoOutput, ControllerConfiguration, Cartridge)`. No `NESTest` call site needed to change shape.
- Also updated two `NESMemoryBus` construction call sites the plan didn't originally list (`AudioSmokeDemo.java`, `NESMemoryBusIntegrationTest.java`), found at compile time.

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew test` - full suite passes
- [x] New `ControllerPortTest` (jqwik): bit-position-per-button property test, strobe-held-high live reads, exact 8-read drain order, reads 9+ always 1, Four Score secondary-controller + signature-bit layout, a button change after strobe-low doesn't perturb the already-latched snapshot, redundant strobe-high/strobe-low calls don't re-latch.
- [x] New `NESMemoryBusTest` coverage: routing to the right port, the single-$4016-write-strobes-both-ports regression, and a dedicated test proving the strobe's low transition actually stops "live" reading rather than getting stuck (kills an AND/OR-swap mutant on the strobe bit test).
- [x] New `ControllerConfigurationTest`, `ControllerTest` for the small bundling/interface types.
- [x] `./gradlew jacocoTestReport` - `com.rox.input` 100% line/100% branch; `NESMemoryBus.java` 100%/100%; `NES.java`'s new constructor lines are fully covered (its 3 remaining uncovered lines are the pre-existing `new SpeakerAudioOutput()`-opening public constructors, deliberately untested to avoid opening a real audio device in CI - same as before this change).
- [x] `./gradlew pitest -PpitestScope=com.rox.input.*,com.rox.mem.NESMemoryBus*,com.rox.NES*` - 96% line coverage, 94% mutation score (both above the 90/90 gate). The handful of surviving/timed-out mutants are all in `NES.java`'s pre-existing `powerOn()`/`powerOff()` clock-race handling (unrelated to this change - see the known, intentionally-deferred poweroff-race flake).

**Do not merge - awaiting manual approval.**

author: anjola-adeuyi
body:
## Summary

The Algolia MCP search tool sends filters in three shapes and "View all" handled one.

- A boolean facet was dropped. `facet_inStock: true` now refines on `inStock:true`, which is byte-identical to the server's own translation.
- A numeric facet was turned into a text refinement. `facet_price: ['<=1500']` became `price:<=1500`, which no record matches, so "View all" returned the wrong results rather than none.

Numeric facets are now applied properly, from the filters the server actually searched with. The MCP result carries `com.algolia/resolved-search-params` and Agent Studio forwards that key to the browser; Agent Studio's own playground already reads it and we didn't. Guessing cannot replace it: `facet_price: ['<=1500']` and a text facet whose value is literally `'<=1500'` are identical on the wire.

`ApplyFiltersParams` gains `numericFilters` and the connector applies each entry with `addNumericRefinement`. Without a single resolved-params bag the raw `facet_` keys still apply the string facets and the numeric value is skipped rather than turned into a refinement that matches nothing. That path covers a missing key and the bulk-search and multi-index shapes, which are not read here. A plain string entry in the server's `facetFilters` becomes its own single-value group, which is how Algolia reads it. The `facet_filters` path, the clear path and multi-query inputs are unchanged.

Two notes for review:
- The metadata is read from the message's `data-*` parts rather than through `onData`. That covers the live and the replayed conversation with one path and needs no new connector surface but it relies on the chat retaining transient data parts. `onData` exists in ai-lite and is not exposed by `connectChat`; exposing it would be a separate public-API change. Agent Studio uses `onData` for its live path and the persisted part for history ([AlgoliaWeb #29415](https://github.com/algolia/AlgoliaWeb/pull/29415)).
- The shape is implemented against the MCP server's own tests and Agent Studio's consumer, not against a payload captured from a live request. The LaunchDarkly flag `resolved-search-params-meta` gates it server-side, so behaviour with the flag off is the skip path above.

Related: [FX-3934](https://algolia.atlassian.net/browse/FX-3934)

[FX-3934]: https://algolia.atlassian.net/browse/FX-3934?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

body:
## What

`cloud org prometheus <id> --json` and `cloud service prometheus <id> --json` silently accept `--json` but always emit raw Prometheus exposition text (exit 0, not parseable as JSON). This is correct behavior — converting Prometheus text to JSON would lose the format contract — but it was undocumented, which is confusing, especially for agent consumers that expect parseable JSON.

## Why

Docs-only change, no behavior change:

- Added an `after_help` block to both `OrgCommands::Prometheus` and `ServiceCommands::Prometheus` clap variants stating that output is always Prometheus exposition text and `--json` is silently ignored.
- Sharpened the README's "JSON output" section to name both commands explicitly rather than referring to "Prometheus commands" generically.

## Test plan

- Added clap `--help` parse tests next to each command definition asserting the new help text is present (`org_prometheus_help_documents_json_is_ignored`, `service_prometheus_help_documents_json_is_ignored`), following the existing pattern used for `service query` and clickpipes postgres help.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`

- `cargo test -p clickhouse-cloud-api --test spec_coverage_test` (unaffected, all green)

Fixes #607.

author: marcomattes
body:
## Summary

The cover page (`/`) ranked behind the FAQ for the site's own head term. The cause is visible in the built HTML: the cover carried about **60 words** of body text — a headline, a lede, two buttons, three statistics — and the FAQ was the only page that spelled "e-ink" next to "web components" in prose. The page that should be the entry point had the least to match on.

This keeps the first screen exactly as it was and continues below the fold, the way a broadsheet front page continues: what EPaper is, the four constraints that make a component e-ink-ready, the install snippets, the component categories, the guides, and four question teasers. Each block states its point in a couple of sentences and links onward, so the cover and the section it points at are not two documents competing for one query.

The cover's `<main>` now renders **795 words**, up from ~60.

Changes:

- **`routes.ts`** — cover `title`, `description` and `heading` name e-ink as well as e-paper. Title is now `EPaper — E-Ink Web Components for E-Paper Displays`; the `<h1>` reads `Web components for e-ink & e-paper.`
- **`data.ts`** — new `HOME_INTRO` (three answer-first paragraphs) and `EINK_CONSTRAINTS` (the four rules of the medium). Deliberately not a reprint of `FEATURES`: page 2 states the library's design principles, the cover states the medium's constraints.
- **`faq.ts`** — `faqId()` moved here and exported (the cover deep-links into `/faq/#…`, and the markdown twin has to produce the same ids). New `homeQuestions()` resolves each cover question against the real FAQ and **throws at build time** if one is reworded, so a dead anchor fails the build instead of shipping. The teasers are written for the cover rather than copied, so the same paragraphs are not on two indexed URLs.
- **`content.ts`** — `coverFoldHtml()` renders the new sections as static markup (no custom elements, per the note at the top of that file: a crawler that does not run JS has to see every word). Category tallies and the answer count are computed, not authored.
- **`seo.ts`** — the cover's structured data gains `SoftwareApplication` (what to install, and that it is free — `SoftwareSourceCode` answers "where is the code", not "what do I install") and an `ItemList` of the site's sections. The cover's `WebPage` names the library as its `mainEntity`. `routeMarkdown` for `/` now mirrors the page, so `/index.md` and `llms.txt` are no longer thinner than the HTML.
- **`site.css`** — `.site-home*` styles for the new blocks. No transitions, no animations, no `:hover`.

- [x] Changes are scoped (no unrelated files touched)
- [x] Demo/story/docs updated if needed — site content plus its markdown/`llms.txt` twins; no library code touched
- [x] CSS output builds locally (`npm run build`)

## Testing

- [x] `npm run format:check`
- [x] `npm run type-check`
- [x] `npm run lint:check`
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm run build:site` — 38 files written; verified in the built output that all four `/faq/#…` anchors resolve to real ids on the FAQ page, that the JSON-LD parses (`WebSite`, `WebPage`, `SoftwareSourceCode`, `BreadcrumbList`, `SoftwareApplication`, `ItemList`), and that `index.md` carries the same prose as the page
- [x] Rendered at 1280px and 390px in Chromium: no horizontal overflow at either width

## Notes

**Not a hard ranking guarantee.** This fixes the two things that are actually in our control — the page had no keyword-bearing text and almost no text at all. Whether the cover overtakes the FAQ depends on how Google reweighs the site after a recrawl, and that takes weeks. Worth watching in Search Console rather than declaring done.

**The FAQ is deliberately untouched.** It ranks because it earned it; the fix is to make the cover competitive, not to weaken the page that works.

**E-ink considerations:** no transitions, animations or `:hover` in the new CSS; the added markup is static HTML with no custom elements, so nothing new renders client-side and the cover still paints in one pass.

**Two judgement calls worth a second opinion:**

1. The cover is a deliberate full-height "cover of a paper" and this puts 700 words underneath it. `.site-cover` keeps `flex: 1`, so the first screen is unchanged and the new content starts after a strong rule — but it is a change in what the page *is*, and that is an editorial call, not a technical one.
2. The nav label for `/` is still `Cover`, so every internal link to the home page uses that as anchor text. `Home` would be worth more to a crawler and less to the metaphor; left as-is on purpose.

---

body:
Adversarial test: "Rotationsaktuator för ATEX zon 1, vridmoment 50Nm... extremt hög cykelfrekvens" got 3 standard, non-certified Metal Work pneumatic rotary actuators presented as normal ranked options with **zero ATEX mention anywhere** — not the summary, not any option's why/cons, not even the CUSTOM-SOLUTION fallback.

Matches the same bug class as a previously-fixed 2026-08-16 ATEX hallucination incident documented in project memory (this time via silent omission rather than fabricated compliance) — and is exactly the gap that fix flagged as worth specifically probing: *"isPureRotary is yet another narrow code path with its own blind spots relative to the general options flow."*

**Root cause**: `isPureRotary`'s `CustomSolutionContext` hardcoded every hazard flag to `false` (isAtex, isWashdown, isVertical, isBatteryDryroom, isHydraulic, isSilSafety) regardless of what the customer said — despite all of them already being computed earlier in `handleOptions` for other purposes.

**Fix**: thread the real values through. Additionally, confirmed via direct `product_specs` query that **zero** rotary-actuator products have any ATEX/zone spec at all — there's nothing safe to recommend from stock, so an ATEX/ATEX-dust request now skips the catalog picks entirely and returns only the (now correctly ATEX-aware) custom-solution option, mirroring how the general options path already excludes standard electric categories for ATEX rather than presenting them with a disclaimer.

`handleOptions`-internal (impure) logic, not yet covered by `deno test` — verifying via live curl next.

author: patayencroute
body:
Lot **E4 — langue et devise au rendu**, exécuté d'après
[docs/plans/e4-langue-et-devise-au-rendu.md](docs/plans/e4-langue-et-devise-au-rendu.md)
(désormais périmé). L'ADR d'exécution
[0017](docs/adr/0017-langue-et-devise-au-rendu.md) fait foi.

La même facture de soixante lignes sort en **français/euros** et en **anglais/dollars** depuis
**un seul objet template**, sur **quatre feuilles A4** dans les deux cas.

## Ce qui change

**`@openview/core` — le site déclare son écriture.** Un binding, un compteur de page et un report
de page peuvent porter `format: { kind, profile }` : `kind` nomme lequel des trois formateurs C6
écrit la position, `profile` est un nom logique que l'auteur du modèle possède. Un compteur
n'accepte que `decimal`, un report `money` ou `decimal` — refusé au schéma, pas au rendu. Le profil
n'est **jamais** une clé de `presentations`, et c'est cette indirection qui fait qu'un même site
bascule de langue sans être édité. La collecte C10 lit désormais son attente sur le site
(`number` pour money/decimal, `civil-date` pour date, `printable` sans déclaration).

**Estampille 10 → 11**, migration par estampille seule : les trois champs sont optionnels, donc un
build v10 les dépouillerait en silence et un `onSave` persisterait la perte.

**`@openview/engine` — l'appelant choisit, le moteur applique.**
`RenderEngineOptions.presentationSelection` associe les profils aux écritures déclarées, **à la
construction du port**. `RenderRequest` reste `{ template, data }` : pas de troisième champ, pas de
clé réservée du jeu de données. Une `PresentationSession` vit le temps d'un rendu, résout à la
première utilisation et met en cache par clé d'écriture réelle — deux profils visant la même
écriture partagent une résolution, et `extendBands` réemploie la session du premier passage. Un
site qu'aucune page n'atteint ne résout rien.

**Échec, jamais blanc** : `presentation-refused` et `unformattable-binding-value`. Les `details` ne
portent que des littéraux fermés ; ni profil, ni clé d'écriture, ni valeur liée n'entre dans un
message. Un report est arrondi par `roundDecimal` **puis** écrit — `Intl` ne reçoit jamais de
`roundingMode` —, et une écriture dont l'échelle contredirait l'arrondi déclaré est refusée plutôt
que corrigée.

**La réserve de marqueur est mesurée sur les chaînes que l'écriture produit vraiment** : zéro, les
deux signes de la magnitude saturée des contributions, et une répétition de chaque chiffre aux
longueurs extrêmes que l'écriture autorise. Un marqueur sans écriture garde **exactement** la voie
canonique.

**Recette et vitrine.** La facture de référence prend une table d'écritures de site à côté de son
apparence : sans écriture, elle est **au caractère près** le document qu'E1, E3 et C11 impriment
déjà — leurs cas passent sans modification. Le playground expose deux sélecteurs indépendants ; le
pont n'accepte qu'un **identifiant** de variante vérifié dans sa propre liste blanche.

## Ce qu'un relecteur devrait savoir

- **J3 n'est pas atteint.** Les deux PDF diagonaux existent et sont valides, mais **aucune
  relecture métier n'a eu lieu**. C'est écrit tel quel dans l'ADR et dans les deux roadmaps.
- **E4-9** (« le même ICU à l'aperçu et au rendu ») reste une dette de **E5 / viewer** : aucun
  aperçu public n'existe, donc l'égalité n'est pas déclarée livrée.
- **Douze ablations sur douze sont tuées** (§ ADR). La treizième du plan — « coupler langue et
  sélection » — n'a pas de site de mutation : la propriété est l'**absence** de code de couplage,
  prouvée par les quatre paires du `it.each` Chromium et par le pont vérifié en direct.
- **Un défaut de la vitrine, trouvé pendant le lot et corrigé avec lui.** L'apparence A refusait ses
  quatre combinaisons de soixante lignes en `grid-content-overflow` : sa zone de titre déclarait deux
  rangs pour un titre qui en compose trois. Le moteur avait raison de refuser — une zone de grille
  n'est ni rognée ni redimensionnée — donc la correction est dans le modèle de démonstration et
  **aucune ligne d'`engine` n'est touchée**. La portée a été **mesurée** en rétablissant le span
  fautif, pas déduite : 4 des 16 combinaisons échouaient, toutes sur l'apparence A ; l'apparence B
  rendait déjà les quatre mêmes. Le discriminant est la **typographie du gabarit** (Georgia 9,5 pt
  contre Arial 8,5 pt), pas la donnée ni l'écriture. Les 16 combinaisons rendent désormais un PDF,
  vérifié contre le pont. Deux lectures antérieures de cette portée étaient fausses et l'ADR le dit.
- **Le plan s'est trompé sur trois points, corrigés et nommés dans l'ADR** : sa baseline était
  verte et non rouge ; `MarkerReserve` a dû changer de forme (elle perd `digits` et gagne
  `placeholderOf`) ; et la facture de référence garde ses deux orthographes au lieu d'être
  remplacée.
- **Le watchdog Chromium passe de 60 s à 120 s**, dans les deux fichiers de tests de l'adaptateur.
  Ce n'est pas un budget de performance mais une garde contre un navigateur bloqué — ce que le
  commentaire voisin disait déjà. Mesuré : le cas le plus lent du paquet fait **28 s** quand les
  deux fichiers tournent seuls, et le cas qui déclenchait la garde en couverture complète y fait
  **13,6 s** ; 60 s échouait sur la contention, pas sur une faute. Aucune assertion ne change.
  L'alternative — plafonner la concurrence dans `vitest.config.ts` — troque du temps mural contre
  du déterminisme et reste ouverte.
- **`biome.jsonc` épingle `$schema` en 2.5.8 alors que la CLI est en 2.5.10** depuis la montée de
  dépendances sur `main`. Le fichier est protégé par AGENTS §7, donc il n'est **pas** touché ici —
  mais les gardes ont été sondées plutôt que supposées : `noJsRestrictedProperties` refuse toujours
  `Date.now`, `Math.random` et `process.env`, et `noRestrictedImports` refuse toujours `core`
  important `engine`. L'épinglage mérite une ligne de la part de qui détient le fichier.

## Les quatre portes

Rejouées après rebase sur `main` (correctifs Sonar + montées de dépendances, dont
puppeteer 25.8.0, biome 2.5.10, vitest 4.1.11) :

| Porte | Résultat |
| :--- | :--- |
| `pnpm run lint` | ✅ exit 0 |
| `pnpm run build` | ✅ 6/6 |
| `pnpm run type-check` | ✅ 11/11 |
| `pnpm run test:coverage` | ✅ **1784/1784**, 64/64 fichiers, 0 dépassement de délai, 0 seuil franchi |

Couverture : instructions 93,57 % · branches 90,42 % · fonctions 98,38 % · lignes 93,47 %. Les
planchers par paquet `packages/core/src/**` et `packages/engine/src/**` passent. **Les branches
sont à 0,42 point du plancher** — ça passe, mais la marge est mince.

Deux conflits de rebase, résolus dans le sens des correctifs Sonar : `Set<OccurrenceKey>` →
`Set<string>` dans `pagination/reports.ts`, et les libellés enveloppés dans `<span>` dans
`RenderDownloadPanel.tsx` (appliqué aux **trois** sélecteurs, pas aux deux qui conflictaient).

---

## 🛡️ Vérification de Sécurité & Checklist

### 🔒 Sécurité
- [x] Aucun secret, clé API, jeton d'accès ou fichier d'environnement (`.env`) n'est présent dans les modifications.
- [x] Tout contenu ou template rendu/injecté est assaini pour éviter les failles XSS. Les chaînes des formateurs traversent le sérialiseur existant ; aucun chemin d'échappement n'est modifié, et le pont du playground n'accepte qu'un identifiant de variante vérifié dans une liste blanche locale, jamais une table envoyée par la page.
- [x] Aucune nouvelle dépendance contenant des vulnérabilités connues n'a été ajoutée. **Aucune dépendance n'est ajoutée.**

### 🧭 Périmètre
- [x] Aucun nom de champ réservé, aucune structure de données attendue de l'intégrateur. Le profil appartient à l'auteur du modèle et ne rejoint jamais `collectDataPaths()`.
- [x] Aucune lecture d'environnement introduite dans `core`/`engine`. Les seuls appels `Intl.*` restent ceux de `core/presentation/format.ts`, avec la locale que le **modèle** déclare. Vérifié par sonde après la montée de Biome.
- [x] Aucune règle métier (taux, barème, arrondi « légal ») n'entre dans le code. L'arrondi appliqué est celui q

author: kozanryusui
body:
### Description of Changes

Pad Ethernet frames shorter than 60 bytes before the UE PCB device sends them through its bulk-in endpoint.

This fixes network connectivity checks which rely on packets which can be shorter than the minimum required Ethernet frame langth.

### Rationale behind Changes

The minimum Ethernet frame size is 64 bytes when the four-byte frame check sequence is included. The UE PCB code receives frames without this sequence, so their minimum length is 60 bytes.

Some network backends can provide shorter frames, such as unpadded Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) frames. Passing these frames to the emulated device without padding produces an invalid Ethernet frame and can prevent network communication.

### Suggested Testing Steps

1. Build PCSX2x6 from the `netplay-uepcb` branch with this change.
2. Start up Druaga Online and enter the network test menu.
3. Start a connectivity test. If the configured IPs are reachable the test should now report success.

### Did you use AI to help find, test, or implement this issue or feature?

This patch was generated using ChatGPT-5.6-Sol. I have performed a manual review and clean-up afterwards to verify the implementation and make sure that the change scope is minimal.

### Related GameIDs

Druaga Online (NM00028)

author: baev
body:
<!---
Thank you so much for sending us a pull request!

Make sure you have a clear name for your pull request.
The name should start with a capital letter and no dot is required in the end of the sentence.
To link the request with issues use the following notation: (fixes #123, fixes #321\)

An example of good pull request names:
* Add Cucumber integration (fixes #123\)
* Add an ability to disable default plugins
* Support emoji in test descriptions
-->

### Context

<!---
Describe the problem or feature in addition to a link to the issues
-->

Adds an Allure-aware server-sent events factory for OkHttp so listener steps and HTTP exchange attachments are assigned to the test or fixture that opens each stream. Shared clients, factories, requests, and listeners can be created before the test; context is captured when the event source is opened, preventing reused dispatcher threads from carrying the first test’s context into later tests.

Use the new factory alongside the Allure interceptor:

```java
OkHttpClient client = new OkHttpClient.Builder()
        .addInterceptor(new AllureOkHttp3())
        .build();

EventSource.Factory eventSourceFactory = AllureEventSources.createFactory(client);
EventSource eventSource = eventSourceFactory.newEventSource(request, listener);
```

Event sources opened outside a running Allure test or fixture do not report callbacks against stale test results.

fixes #1036

author: tokuhirom
body:
`EVAL '$^a'` raised nothing at all, and `EVAL '@_'` raised `X::Undeclared`, where rakudo raises `X::Placeholder::Mainline` for both. A placeholder parameter used outside any sub or block is that error, and `@_` / `%_` are placeholders too — which is why the check has to run **before** the undeclared-variable check, or the `@_` case is reported as an undeclared variable instead.

## It was already implemented, in only one of two parallel check chains

`check_eval_mainline_placeholders` (`runtime/system_eval_vars.rs`) has existed for a while, complete with the `placeholder` attribute and rakudo's message text. Its only caller was `runtime/test_functions/throws_like.rs` — the **native** `Test` provider's `throws-like`, which parses its code string itself and runs its own chain of `check_eval_*` calls. The ordinary EVAL path (`parse_and_eval_with_operators`) runs the same chain and was missing this one member, so the check never fired for real `EVAL`.

That is why `roast/S32-exceptions/misc2.t` passed under the native provider and failed under `MUTSU_REAL_TEST=1`: the real `Test.rakumod`'s `throws-like` EVALs its string through the ordinary path.

The fix is one line, placed ahead of `check_eval_undeclared_vars`.

## The obvious follow-up was measured and reverted

"The native chain's copy is now a duplicate, delete it" is **false**: the native `throws-like` never goes through `parse_and_eval_with_operators` at all. With the line removed, `roast/S32-exceptions/misc2.t` test 14 (`throws-like '@_', X::Placeholder::Mainline`) fails under the *native* provider, since `check_eval_undeclared_vars` then reports `X::Undeclared` first. Both chains genuinely need the check; the call site now carries a comment saying so and naming the test that proves it.

Worth carrying forward as a shape: **a check reachable from only one of two parallel chains looks exactly like a native-provider leniency crutch** (the kind `news/2026-08/parse-error-exception-classes.md` correctly retired) **and is not one.** Measure the removal before believing the label.

## What it frees

| file | real Test before | after | native before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `S32-exceptions/misc2.t` | 3 failures (#13, #14, #15) | **PASS** | PASS | PASS |

Part of the campaign in `todo/deep/vendor-real-test-module.md`.

## Verification

* `make test` green — 3529 files, 35302 tests.
* Targeted roast sweep over the EVAL/exception consumers (`S32-exceptions`, `S02-names`, `S02-lexical-conventions`, `S04-exception*`, `S06-*`, `S12-*`, `S24-testing`, `S29-context`, `S05-*`, `integration`) — **483 files, 13617 tests, PASS**.
* The roast file green under **both** providers.
* Pin `t/eval-mainline-placeholder.t` — 15 assertions covering the mainline cases, the `placeholder` attribute and message, the `X::Placeholder::Block` cases that must stay distinct, the positions where a placeholder is legal, and an ordinary undeclared variable that must still be `X::Undeclared` — **green under real `raku`** as well as mutsu.

author: julialawrence
body:
Tapping an author filtered the shelf to what was **already held** — a smaller
question than the one being asked. Not *what of theirs do I have*, but *what
have they written*.

An index page describes twenty works for one request, so a catalogue is cheap
to know and expensive only to read. That's what makes the threshold work:

| Catalogue | What happens |
|---|---|
| under 200 works | walked on arrival — a handful of requests, and waiting for a tap only adds a tap |
| 200 or more | the size and time are shown, and it waits to be asked |

The first page is kept either way, since it's already paid for. **Their
bookmarks** are read the same way.

Everything found becomes a work you can search, filter and read about; nothing
is fetched until you open it. A blurb knows less than the work page a held copy
came from, so a listing can **never** replace a work already held —
`CONFLICT_IGNORE`, with `has_text` at 0.

### A regression found on the way

`keepAwake` was deleted by #39, which replaced the span of Java it happened to
sit in — the same way `markWork` went in #29. The screen has not stayed awake
while reading since v0.19.1, and nothing said so: the call is optional-chained
inside a `catch`.

The test that exists to catch exactly this read only `api.js`, while this call
is made from `app.js` — and once widened, its pattern still didn't match
optional chaining. **This time I checked it against a real deletion** rather
than assuming: it names `keepAwake` and fails.

341 tests.

author: marlodrews
body:
Records an observation about `ARCHITECTURE.md` itself, in the header, since the file had no introduction to put it in.

The `get_optional_user_id` entry claimed the function supplied "identity for the feed seed + rate-limit key". It supplied neither, and had no callers at all — `feed.py` derives both from `get_optional_user`. That claim was false before the function was dead, and nothing caused it: it was written, the code moved underneath it, and it sat there until someone deleting dead code happened to look.

That is the fourth of the same shape, all in this file, all found incidentally while looking for something else — alongside the `mobile/` entry describing a frozen app in the present tense, five drifted counts, and the CI note that blamed the server for the `battle_test.py` hang when the cause was the test harness.

Four is enough to treat as a property of the document rather than four coincidences: it describes behaviour, behaviour changes without the file being touched, and nothing catches it because nothing executes prose. The three gates compile, boot and test the code; none of them reads this file.

So the header now says that a claim here about behaviour is a lead rather than a fact and the code is the authority — which is more useful to a future session than any individual correction. No entry was changed and no code was touched.

author: talitamoss
body:
## What changed

Tal, on the deployed event detail: fix the duplicated \"Kalendar\" nav in the top-left; move RSVP / Invite / Share up next to the date/time block; icon-only, larger Kronk squares that fill in colour when selected.

### 1. Back chip label — \"All events\" (again)

The Frame's space header renders \"Kalendar\" directly above the KornerDetail's back chip. #1603 relabelled the chip \"Kalendar\" to match the korner identity, but stacked with the Frame's own header the two reads as the same word twice. Back to \"All events\" — the chip names its **destination** (the list face at `/hub/kalendar/list`), not the current korner. Rationale documented on the `back` prop so the next round doesn't re-litigate.

### 2. RSVP / Invite / Share as Kronk squares in the hero row

- New wrapper **`__hero-row`** pairs the `__when` block (flex 1 1 240px) with a stack of action buttons (flex 0 0 auto) side-by-side. On narrow viewports the flex-wrap drops the actions under the when block.
- **`__action-square`** — 52×52 Kronk-themed square button, icon-only. Base: soft purple wash + border, purple icon. Active (`--active`): filled `--kronk-purple-accent`, `--semantic-text-on-accent` icon, elevation shadow.
- **RSVP** shows active when `event.rsvp === 'going'` (tap toggles going ⇄ remove); **Invite** shows active when the invite panel is open (tap toggles); **Share** is a one-off action (no active state, `navigator.share` with clipboard fallback).
- Wording is out — the icons carry the meaning (check / person-add / share are unambiguous).

### 3. Bottom KornerActionBar → owner-only

RSVP / Invite / Share are gone from the bottom pill row. The action bar now only mounts for `event.is_owner` and only carries **Edit / Delete** — the \"admin\" operations remain pill-shaped there because they're of a different kind (destructive / editorial) than the social affordances.

## Why

Tal on the deployed screenshot: *\"We have an extra 'kalender' nav button in the top left, determine which is correct and clean it up. The rest is great, let's move the Rsvp options to the empty space above the 'copy' button and to the right of the Date/time. Remove the wording of 'RZVP, INvite etc', and just use symbols, larger kronk themed squares and fill in colour when selected.\"*

The empty space right of the when block was doing nothing while the primary affordances were parked at the bottom of the page. Moving them up puts the RSVP right where the temporal context is — decide when + decide yes in one glance. Squares over pills gives them the presence they were lacking, and icon-only is defensible here because the three symbols are common.

## How to test (shadow)

1. `/kalendar/park-hangs` (or any event) — the back chip in the top-left reads \"All events\", not \"Kalendar\". The Frame's own space header still shows \"Kalendar\" once above it — no duplication.
2. Right of the purple date/time block, three larger square buttons: RSVP (tick), Invite (person-add), Share (share icon). No text labels.
3. Tapping RSVP fills the square purple and flips going⇄remove; going_count updates. Tapping again unfills.
4. Tapping Invite opens the invite panel below (as before) and fills the Invite square while it's open. Tapping again closes and unfills.
5. Tapping Share opens the native share sheet on mobile / copies the URL on desktop.
6. As the event owner: the bottom action bar shows just Edit / Delete pills. As a non-owner: no bottom action bar at all.
7. Narrow the browser to phone width — the actions column drops under the when block rather than crushing it.

## Dependencies

Frontend only. No serializer / API / SCSS-cross-cutting changes — all new SCSS is scoped under `.event-detail`.

The first real run of the Swedish pack failed on a runner after 1m43s.

```
ogr2ogr …
[Error: EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read]
```

`ogr2ogr`'s CSV driver switches mode on the *file name*. Given anything that does not end in
`.csv` it reads the output as a datasource and writes a **directory** with the layer's file inside
it. The scratch file was named `se-tattbebyggt.csv.part`, so the built-up area was written to a
directory and then read back as a file.

It never showed locally because the work directory already held a `se-tattbebyggt.csv` from an
earlier run by hand, so `toLinework` was skipped every single time. **The path had never been
executed before it ran on a runner** — I added the write-aside-and-rename late and never exercised
it.

Reproduced first:

```
$ ogr2ogr -f CSV probe.part  …   →  drwxr-xr-x probe.part/NVDB_…_TattbebyggtOmrade.csv
$ ogr2ogr -f CSV probe.part.csv … →  -rw-r--r-- probe.part.csv
```

The scratch name is now `.part.csv`, and the cleanup before writing is recursive so the directory
left behind by the failed attempt is removed rather than tripping the next run. Rerun from an empty
work directory: 988,934 stretches, 8,403,880 cells, and the whole Swedish build through to the same
**46,284 signs in 2,836 cells, 100 files, 7,304 kB** as before.

Two things worth recording from that run, since both were untested until now:

- `gdal-bin` installs cleanly on the runner in 15 s alongside osmium.
- The 354 MB GeoPackage comes down from the release in 3.5 s.
- Geofabrik answered 502 for the Swedish extract and the OSM France mirror carried it, again.

**`publish` stopped on its own guard, *"Nothing to publish?"*, so the release was untouched.** That
check exists for exactly this, and it did its job.

## Which countries, and why

The section listing countries gave the numbers but not what they meant. It is one question — *is
there data that says where the towns begin?* — and after Norway and Sweden it has three answers: the
map knows, the road authority knows, or nobody knows yet.

The third is the one worth writing down, because it explains what is **not** built. A pack of a few
hundred signs for a country of two thousand towns is worse than no pack: it is silent in most places
and speaks in a few, which reads as a broken feature rather than an absent one. That was the whole
reason Sweden went to Lastkajen instead of shipping its 492 mapped signs.

There is also a table of what exists today, with source and licence:

| | signs | source | licence |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Denmark | 8,635 | OpenStreetMap | ODbL |
| Germany | 115,547 | OpenStreetMap | ODbL |
| Sweden | 46,284 | Trafikverket NVDB, via Lastkajen | CC0 |
| Norway | 6,852 | Statens vegvesen NVDB, open API | NLOD |
| France, Poland, Netherlands, Austria | — | OpenStreetMap | ODbL |

## Adding a country

The instructions still described a bounding box and how finely to tile the Overpass queries, both of
which went away in #11. They now describe the two shapes the work actually takes — a few lines in
`REGIONS`, or a module that brings its own signs the way Norway and Sweden do — and the two things
that decide whether a source is usable at all: the licence has to permit redistribution, since the
pack is a public file, and the coverage has to be national, or the pack is silent everywhere the
dataset is not.

And an issue form to start in, [*Add a country*](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/new-country.yml), asking the
questions that settle it rather than the ones that are easy to ask: a ready Overpass query with the
country code to swap, the national sign codes (or the fact that the sign does not exist, which is an
answer and an important one), what the road authority publishes, and a licence dropdown. The last
field asks whether you ride there and what a town entrance looks like — that has settled more than
one of these.

## Checked

- The failure reproduced, then the same step passing, from an empty work directory.
- Full Swedish build end to end: identical output to the run before the change.
- The issue form parses as YAML and its fields resolve.
- `node tools/verify-map-parity.mjs` passes; no code outside `tools/nvdb-sweden.mjs` is touched.

## Still to do

Re-run *Region packs* with `region: se` once this is on `main` — the run this fixes published
nothing. Then the rest, where France is the one to watch.

author: adamtheturtle
body:
A call bound to a new variable came out as

```swift
@discardableResult func check(s: Any = 0, n: Any = 0, b: Any = 0) -> Any { 0 }
let result: [Any] = check(s: "a", n: 1, b: true)
```

which `swiftc -typecheck` rejects: `cannot convert value of type 'Any' to specified type '[Any]'`. The annotation comes from the literal-binding formatter, which types the binding from the value being rendered. That is right for a literal and wrong for a call: the binding holds whatever the stub returns, and the argument list's own type has nothing to do with it.

Swift now uses its declaration style's own formatter for the call binding — `let result = ...` — and lets Swift infer. Verified with `swiftc -typecheck`.

I checked the other back ends for the same shape; Swift is the only one that puts a data-derived type on a call binding. Go, Odin and V use `:=`, Tcl `set`, Racket `define`, none of which name a type.

`call_variable_form_new` did not catch this because it binds a scalar, where Swift's hint rule already decided no annotation was needed. The new case gives the call an argument list, which is the shape that makes the wrong type visible.

Closes #4537

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Swift-only codegen change for call-result bindings plus new integration fixtures; no auth, security, or shared runtime paths affected.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **#4537**, where Swift call bindings used the literal declaration formatter and emitted a type from the input data (e.g. `[Any]`) that did not match the stub’s `Any` return, so `swiftc -typecheck` failed.
> 
> **Swift** now routes `format_call_variable_declaration` through the declaration style’s plain formatter (`let name = …`) so the compiler infers the binding type instead of annotating from the rendered value.
> 
> Adds integration case **`call_variable_form_new_multi_arg`**: `variable_form = "new"` with a **multi-argument call whose arguments come from a nested list**, which is the shape that exposed the bad annotation (scalar-only cases did not). Expected output for Swift is untyped `let my_data = record_entry(...)`. A newsfragment documents the bugfix.

body:
## Summary
- `docs/api/ia_utils_vector_healing.md` was an intro paragraph + an `mkdocstrings` directive, no worked examples. Rewritten in this project's guide style:
  - Step 1: a small synthetic sequence with one out-of-place value (foundational).
  - Step 2: a real, chemistry-specific case — a dissociation-curve point that failed to converge, healed against a real H2 potential-energy curve (`ground_state_energy_sparse`, 11 real bond-length points).
  - Details: `median_healing` vs. the hybrid Phi-Trigger path, `trigger_mode`, and two real **negative** results verified this session — healing correctly does *nothing* on a real 76-chunk paper's TF-IDF sequence (this project's own `quantumrag` index) and on a real, uncorrupted VQE convergence trace. Only an actual bad reading gets touched, confirmed directly rather than assumed.
- New `docs/concepts.md`: "healing" and "mitigation" read as near-synonyms because they share one literal function — `evaluate_phi_trigger` in `dense_evolution.mitigation.healing` — called from two unrelated places: ZNE's own healing-adapted extrapolation branch, and `ia_utils.vector_healing`'s default `trigger_mode`, applied to two different kinds of data (a noise-strength curve vs. an arbitrary vector sequence). Cross-linked from `mitigation.md`, `healing.md`, and `ia_utils_vector_healing.md` so the disambiguation isn't only discoverable by finding the new page first.
- Registered in `mkdocs.yml` nav, between Getting Started and Examples.

## Verification
- Every number in both examples actually run (`enhanced_dense_healing_hybrid` on the synthetic sequence and on the real dissociation curve) — no invented output.
- `mkdocs build --strict` passes (no broken links/nav errors); the only pre-existing warning is unrelated (`api/compiler.md`).

author: mohnqwerty
body:
## Problem
The captures map was rendered through a GPU PIXEL_SHADER that snapped every tile to a ~5dp grid and redrew it as 3-color blocks, making locations illegible.

## Fix
- SlippyPixelMap.kt — removed the pixel shader and cell grid; tiles draw at full resolution with FilterQuality.High. Capture pins render at their exact lat/lon with status colors, white rings, and SSID label badges (clusters collapse to a 'N captures' pin). Tap hits by pin proximity.
- TileMapLoader.kt — switched Carto tiles dark_nolabels -> dark_all so street names/labels are readable, with a new ca_ cache prefix.

## Notes
- Targets the API 33+ renderer. Android 12 and below still use the coarse PixelBasemap fallback (unchanged).
- Not build-verified locally (no Android SDK here).

author: planet6897
body:
## 무엇을 고쳤나

`#6284` — 그림 위쪽 캡션(`<hp:caption side="TOP">`)이 전혀 그려지지 않아, 캡션이
차지해야 할 띠가 사라지면서 그림이 그만큼 위로 올라온다.

## 근인 — 계약이 형제 함수에만 있었다

본문 그림을 실제로 그리는 **`layout_picture_full` 이 `picture.caption` 을 한 번도
참조하지 않는다.** 캡션 기계(띠 예약 + `layout_caption` 호출)는 형제 함수
`layout_body_picture` 에만 있었고, 이 문서는 그 경로를 타지 않는다.

파서는 무죄였다 — 프로브로 확인한 적재 상태:

```
[CAP] pic caption=Some((Top, 8504, 566, 1, Some("아동 삶의 만족도 (15세 아동)")))
...  25개 중 9개가 TOP 캡션 보유
[LPIC] layout_picture 호출 23회 중 9회가 캡션을 들고 들어옴
```

즉 캡션은 렌더러 문턱까지 **정상적으로 도착하고** 거기서 버려진다.

## 수정

캡션 방향별로 띠를 블록에 넣어 정렬을 계산한다(Top/Bottom 은 높이, Left/Right 는
폭). 그림을 띠만큼 안쪽에 놓은 뒤 캡션 노드를 방출한다. 캡션 문단 조판에 필요한
`styles` 를 `layout_picture` / `layout_picture_full` 과 그 호출부(12곳)에 배선했다.

## 결과 — 한글 2024 오라클 대조

| | 캡션 | 그림 상단 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 종전 | **없음** | 191.51pt |
| **수정** | **192.06 / 192.64pt** | **208.17pt** |
| 한글 2024 | 191.2pt | **207.13pt** |

캡션 상단↔그림 상단 간격은 **17.59pt 로 한글과 정확히 같다**(내부 기하 일치).

## 재현물 — 구조 보존 슬라이스

원본이 **7.0MB** 라 그대로 동봉할 수 없어, **BinData 이미지만 8×8 PNG 로 치환**해
**152KB** 로 줄였다. 조판은 `<hp:sz>` 선언 크기를 쓰므로 34쪽·좌표가 원본과 같다
(6쪽 캡션 192.06/192.64 · 그림 208.17 로 실측 일치). A/B 로 결함 재현(캡션 없음 ·
191.51)과 수정(캡션 출현 · 208.17)을 모두 확인했다. PNG 증적의 차트가 회색 판으로
보이는 것은 이 치환 때문이다.


## 시각 증적

물리 6쪽(원본 y 230~420px, `-p 5 --scale 1.5 --compat 2024`).

**수정 전** — 차트 위 제목이 없다

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/planet6897/rhwp/776dc2f7a8a1cedf0299fb9612ce9044d32652b9/mydocs/report/issue6284-picture-top-caption/before.png)

**수정 후** — `아동 삶의 만족도 (15세 아동)` · `아동·청소년 자살률 (’20)` 이 제자리에 놓인다

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/planet6897/rhwp/776dc2f7a8a1cedf0299fb9612ce9044d32652b9/mydocs/report/issue6284-picture-top-caption/after.png)

## 검증

- 잠금 테스트 `tests/cases/issue_6284_picture_top_caption_rendered.rs` 2건 —
  **음성 대조**: 수정 되돌리면 2건 모두 FAIL.
- `cargo nextest run --cargo-profile release-test --no-fail-fast` — 8526건 중
  **8525 통과**. 남은 `wmf_emf_goldens_lock_current_engine` 은 이 브랜치 이전부터
  실패하는 로컬 CRLF 잡음이다. 저장소 표본의 **BOTTOM 캡션 105개**가 이 게이트에
  걸려 있으므로, 방향별 회귀는 게이트가 함께 지킨다.
- `rustfmt`(변경 파일) · `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests` 무경고

## 미해결로 남긴 것 (중요)

### ① 축 ③(총 쪽수 34 vs 한글 35)은 고쳐지지 않았고, 이슈의 가설에 반증이 나왔다

이슈는 "캡션 17개 × 16~20pt 가 누적되면 한 쪽 분량"으로 봤지만, 실측은 그렇지 않다.
차트가 들어 있는 **셀의 선언 행 높이가 이미 캡션을 포함한다.**

```
DIAG_ROWH pi=25 r=0 c=0  decl=155.7  req=157.0  content=153.2
          그림 121.5 + 캡션 ~16 + 여백 → 선언 155.7 안에 든다
```

캡션 띠를 셀 콘텐츠 높이에 더해 봤더니 `content 153.2 → 153.9`(+0.7px)뿐이고
**쪽수는 34 그대로**였다. 근거 없는 변경이라 그 시도는 넣지 않았다. 쪽 배치 차이는
캡션 높이 누적이 아닌 **별개 축**이다.

### ② 이 수정은 좁다 — 캡션을 놓치는 경로가 더 있다

같은 형상으로 보이던 코퍼스 문서 6건(`156718897` · `156715282` · `156561331` ·
`156676988` 등)을 A/B 했더니 **전후 출력이 전부 동일**했다. 그 문서들의 캡션은
아직도 그려지지 않는다. 이 PR 은 `layout_picture_full` 경로만 메운다.

body:
## 变更内容

- **对象**：`skills/to-reference/SKILL.md`（新增）、`references/_inbox/README.md`（新增）、`CLAUDE.md`（Skills 清单四→五）、`README.{md,en.md}`（skill 表格 / 安装命令 / 跳转锚点）
- **动机**：执行 ADR-0008（PR #12）阶段 3——先验知识的注入入口。阶段 2 立好了空货架和校验（PR #14），本 PR 是"往货架上放东西"的入口：工程师随口一句经验、一份官方文档、或一组案例共性，都能以结构化 reference 草稿进入待审队列。

## 核心设计（to-reference SKILL.md）

| 维度 | 设计 |
|---|---|
| 四种输入 | 内联粘贴 / `--file` / `--ingest <url>`（官方文档爬取）/ `--ingest-cases "[ids]"`（案例归纳）——来源类型决定信任基础与审核深度 |
| 四阶段流程 | 提取 → 归类（`references/_types.yaml`）→ **grill** → inbox |
| grill 阶段 | 工程师输入逐项确认（意图 / 边界 / 出处 / 反例）；案例归纳确认不失真（共性 / 差异 / 覆盖）；URL 爬取标 `verification: auto-extracted` 交 reviewer spot-check。**grill 是第一道人审过滤**——用户否认的条目直接丢弃，不进 inbox |
| status 硬锁 | **任何路径都不能产出 `active`**——草稿永远是 `draft`，active 是 maintainer 审核后的状态 |
| 去重前置 | 进 inbox 前扫现有词条：完全覆盖 → 不产草稿并说明；变体 → 提示用户并/或独立；查不到 → 新词条 |
| 草稿完整性 | 草稿必须 schema 完整（基础元信息 + content 全填齐）——`verify_references.py` 对 `_inbox/` 同样校验（与 to-postmortem 草稿可残缺的差异，reference 更严） |
| type 纪律 | 不自行发明未登记 type；`type_uncertain: true` 交 maintainer 定夺 |

## 原则追溯

- **原则一（用结构承载规则）**：`status: draft` 硬锁 + 草稿 schema 完整性 + CI 校验 inbox——"不产出未审词条"从 prompt 纪律变成结构保证
- **原则十（诚实退化）**：grill 阶段用户否认即丢弃、宁少勿疑；`verification: auto-extracted` 如实标注模型抽取未经人核
- **是否修改了原则/理论本身的语义**：否

## 回归检查

- 未触及任何 case YAML / triage-tree / scripts（`verify_references.py` 未动——草稿校验能力阶段 2 已具备，本 PR 只是让 skill 产出满足它的草稿）
- `build_index.py --check` + `verify_references.py --check`：均通过
- **reviewer 复核建议**：本 PR 改的是 skill 本身，按 docs/eval.md 应跑 golden 回归——但 fixture 针对 `/skill:diagnose`，to-reference 是独立入口无 fixture 覆盖；建议 reviewer 在 agent 内手动跑一次 `/skill:to-reference --ingest-cases "[某组已知 case]"` 走通流程（golden 套件暂不覆盖 to-reference，roadmap O4/M3 范畴）

## 影响面

- 涉及的 skill：新增 `to-reference`；`knowledge-groom` 后续需把 `references/_inbox/` 纳入周批（ADR-0008 阶段 5 / groom 信号表扩展——独立 PR）
- CLAUDE.md / README：本 PR 已同步（five skills + 安装命令 + 跳转锚点）
- CONTEXT.md：术语表阶段 2 已加 Reference / ref_knowledge，本 PR 无需再动
- 安装粒度：`-s` 安装命令加入 to-reference（README 三处：推荐全装 / 自积累表格）

## 无高风险项

未触碰 case schema、triage-tree、common/、references/ 正式词条——不触发 kb/high-risk 双签。

## Description

https://github.com/ros2/rmw_zenoh/pull/1005 did the right thing by resetting the `wait_set_data->triggered` flag to `false` under global lock as [seen here](https://github.com/ros2/rmw_zenoh/blob/e3159856e3816e726f2c5f1f9b4858ad6b7ee63e/rmw_zenoh_cpp/src/rmw_zenoh.cpp#L2237-L2241) but it kept the reset in [check_and_attach_condition()](https://github.com/ros2/rmw_zenoh/blob/e3159856e3816e726f2c5f1f9b4858ad6b7ee63e/rmw_zenoh_cpp/src/rmw_zenoh.cpp#L2188-L2191) that is no longer called under the same lock. This leads to the executor waiting indefinitely if one of the entities received a message after the initial check in `check_and_attach_condition()` given the reset happens outside of a lock.






Fixes # (issue)

Yes. Fixes indefinite executor wait.

author: pupiltong
body:
Stacked on #158 (⑥). Part ⑦, closing the commit/compose pipeline split: the remaining scroll transport is deleted by making the state it carried unrepresentable.

Rebased onto the converged boot (#160/#161): the stack no longer ever grows scroll sequence numbers or a published-frame wrapper, so this PR is smaller than its first landing — what remains to delete is the per-event command itself.

## What changes

- **A windowed user scroll never crosses the command channel.** The presenting side's `ScrollIntents` are the offsets — composition and hit testing already read them (⑥ made the scroll frame a plane transform update). `MainCommand::ScrollBy` and `runtime::apply_scroll` are deleted.
- **`Refill` carries the offsets.** When an intent consumes past half its encode-window headroom, the one refill per commit writes the screen's offsets into the document (`scroll_to` per slot) and marks the paint stale; the next commit re-centers the windows on them. This is the only way a user scroll reaches the document, and intent reconciliation stays the value comparison it already was — now exact, because the document only ever stores what a refill wrote.
- **`MAX_COMMANDS_PER_ROUND` is deleted.** Its scenario was a scroll flood outrunning the committer. Scrolls no longer cross; every remaining producer is frame-rate bounded (`BeginFrame` once per frame) or event-rate bounded (input as the OS delivers it, pointer moves coalesced on the presenting side), so the round's drain terminates on its own.
- **The reduction pass rides along**: comments across the arc shrink to the constraints the code cannot show.

## Behavior change

Between refills, document-side scroll-offset reads lag the screen. Nothing engine-side reads them — routing uses the published frame plus intents — and no script API exposes offsets today; the constraint on a future one is recorded in `runtime-architecture.md`. The engine tests assert the sharper law directly: after a windowed wheel the document's offset is still zero, no command crossed, nothing recommitted, and the tap still lands on what the screen shows.

## Verification

Workspace tests (including the `scroll_compose` GPU test, whose deep-scroll capture exercises the offset write-back end to end), native + wasm32 clippy, and benches `--test` all green.

author: estebanzimanyi
body:
The S2 cell kernel lives in `meos/src/s2cell/`, alongside the H3 and
QUADBIN cell kernels it mirrors. It packs the cube face, the position
along the Hilbert curve and the level into a 64-bit `S2CellId`, and it
carries the validity, hierarchy, Hilbert-range, traversal, geometry and
metric primitives that the temporal layer lifts over time. It links only
libm: S2 publishes no maintained C API, and its C++ library is a heavy
Abseil-dependent blob. Where the kernel reads the highest set bit of an
identifier it calls `pg_leftmost_one_pos64`, the vendored PostgreSQL
primitive that `cbuffer.c`, `span.c`, `stbox.c` and `tbox.c` already read
for the same quantity.

`s2cell`, `s2cellset` and `ts2cell` take the contiguous catalog slots
after the pose chain types and stand in exactly the catalog predicates
their quadbin siblings stand in; `manifest.d/classes.yaml` names them in
the classes those predicates define, and `doc/reference_types.xml` gives
the family its row in the template-type table of both manuals. The
descriptor supplies the six shared cell operations and the geodetic point
type an S2 cell answers in, and `dggs_cellops` answers a temporal S2
value with it.

The extension declares the `s2cell` type with its parser, output, send
and receive, the six comparison operators over the identifier, the btree
and hash operator classes an exact-match index and a GROUP BY need, the
explicit casts to and from bigint that share its representation, and the
validity predicate. A type MEOS parses travels with the SQL that declares
it, so both sides run the one parser rather than drifting apart. The
output is S2's canonical token, the identifier with its trailing zeros
stripped, so a cell reads back from its own text, and a regression test
states the round trip, the ordering, the grouping and the two literals
that encode no cell.

The sources compile into the MEOS library under the `S2CELL` option that
`ALL` enables, and the public header travels with the install. The option
carries the static type's name rather than the grid's: a bare `S2` is a
stab-line endpoint in the vendored PostGIS geodetic code, which a
build-wide definition would rewrite into a numeric constant.

A geometry becomes the cell covering it, and a cell answers its geodetic
centre and the geodetic polygon of its boundary, so the SQL conversions
project the catalog rather than build geometry themselves and the cell
kernel keeps no geometry dependency. The four cells sharing an edge with
a cell and the children of a cell at a finer level answer as an
`s2cellset`, and the descriptor's centre and boundary wrappers state the
same adapters once.

An S2 cell is defined on the sphere, so the box of a cell is geodetic
where the Web-Mercator quadbin's is planar, and it comes from the
derivation the cell-index scaffolding shares rather than from the four
vertices. `s2cell_set_stbox` is what `stbox.c` reaches for when a Datum
carries a cell, so the box derivation travels with the static type, as h3
keeps `h3index_set_stbox` in `th3index_boxops.c`. A cell composed with a
time keeps the region it covers: the composing forms set the period and
the T flag directly, as `geo_timestamptz_to_stbox` and
`geo_tstzspan_to_stbox` do, rather than through a `*_set_stbox` helper
whose contract is to build a box from a time and which therefore opens by
zeroing the box.

author: axiomevi
body:
Two bugs, shipped together because either one alone breaks the other's population.

## The reference workbook moved

It was copied to a new document on 2026-08-28 and the previous one is frozen. The frozen one still answers, which is why nothing ever looked wrong: srs kept importing, from a document that had stopped receiving every retiming.

Repointing the constants alone would have moved nobody. The three tab urls are ordinary settings — `[SettingIgnore]` hides them from the menu, it does not stop them being serialized — and a stored value always beats a new default, so every player who has ever saved was pinned to whatever they first wrote. `LoadSettings` now substitutes the frozen document id in what is on disk, the id and nothing else: the new workbook is a Drive copy and kept its sheetIds, so every gid still names the same tab and a gid someone changed on purpose survives. A url naming any other workbook is left alone.

`SheetUrls` holds both ids and `SrsSettings` builds its three defaults from the current one, so a default and the migration target cannot drift apart the next time this happens.

## Three checkpoints were never imported

The same copy corrected three checkpoint spellings. `SheetData.Import` is an allowlist keyed on the reference's own labels, so `Unravelling` (5A), `Through the Mirror` (5B) and `Stubbornness` (Farewell) missed it and were dropped at import: no slider entry, no tier, no anchor for the run watcher. **It is the read path that was broken** — the export side already spelled all three correctly. 5A's row had been in that state since 2026-08-08, when the reference was repaired and srs was not.

The matching `CheckpointMap` entries are identities now. Two of the comments justifying them stated the reverse of the truth and are gone.

## Why one PR

Alone, the renames break the players still pointed at the frozen workbook: it feeds them the old spellings, which then miss the updated allowlist. The migration is what makes the renames safe.

## Testing

`Tests/SheetUrlsTests.cs`, 7 cases on the substitution itself: a stored url is repointed and keeps its gid, a gid changed by hand survives, a current url and a custom workbook come back untouched, the id is matched as a whole token and not as a prefix, and the whole thing is idempotent. Suite green at 120.

Fixtures refreshed from the new workbook, which is also how the three renames were measured: the label-column diff is exactly those three, plus one row deleted upstream that srs never imported.

Verified in game on an install that had never been migrated:

```
[srs] Repointed the stored sheet urls at the current reference workbook
[srs] Loaded 63 segments from cache
[srs] Downloading A/B/Farewell tab: .../d/1Gjr0t5N.../export?format=csv&gid=...
[srs] Sheet updated: 65 segments
```

The migration line appears once and not on the relaunch. 65 imported segments is the full size of `Import`, so nothing is dropped any more. The 63 read from the stale cache is the bug itself, measured: that cache came from the frozen workbook, whose two old spellings miss the updated allowlist, 65 − 2. It is the window this PR closes.

Not exercised in game, stated rather than hidden: a custom url left untouched (unit-tested only), and a stored selection naming one of the three old spellings.

## Not in this PR

No version bump: `everest.yaml` stays at 3.7.0 and the changelog entry sits under `Unreleased`.

body:
ページ「AI松井社長と 話す 準備を しよう」（`kaisha_matsui_junbi`）は **絵の わくが
ぜんぶ 空**だった（`status: "empty"` が 6か所）。ユーザー指定の 中身で 撮って 埋める。

## 1. 「これから 考える 5つの こと」— カード 5枚

| # | カード | 絵 |
| - | ------ | -- |
| 1 | NEXT MAKEの どこが 好き？ | カンボジアの 仕事と セキュリティドローンを 熱く 語る。吹き出しの 中は **絵だけ**（ドローン・椰子と 学校） |
| 2 | 自分の いい ところは？ | セキュリティ・ネットワーク・AIの プログラムを、部屋に ある 本物の 物で 見せる |
| 3 | NEXT MAKEで 何を やって みたい？ | ネクマックスに パソコンを つないで 動かす |
| 4 | カンボジアの いい ところは？ | カンボジアの いい ところを 学生が 教える |
| 5 | 松井社長に 何を 聞きたい？ | 手を 挙げて 質問する |

## 2. 「いっしょに 仕事を したい」の 1枚 → **A/B の 2枚 横並び**

`image` ブロック（1枚）を `cards` の 2列に 変えた。すぐ 上の 帯が
「あなたが 社長だったら、どんな 学生と 仕事を したいですか。」と 聞いて いるので、
**2枚 並べて 選ばせる** ほうが 問いに 合う。

- **A**「NEXT MAKEの ここが 好きです！」… 前のめりで 話す 学生と、目が ハートの 社長
- **B**「とくに ありません。」… 関心の 薄い 学生と、静かに 悲しい 社長

この 台帳だけ negative から「悲しい 顔の 禁止」を 外した（skill §7.2 の 前例と 同じ）。
**社長の 気もちが 問いの 中身その もの**なので、両方 おだやかに 描くと 選ぶ 意味が 消える。
外したのは 悲しさ までで、**怒り・こわい 顔・涙は 禁じた まま**。

## 3. まだ 画面に 出ない 2枚

くらべ（compare）の「ヘンディさんに 話した こと」「松井社長に 話す こと」も
**絵は 撮って ある**（`cmp_hendy` / `cmp_matsui`。同じ 部屋・同じ 光で 対に なる）。
ただし `compare` は 絵の わくを スキーマで 持って いないので **まだ 出ない**。
出すには `schema.ts` を 触る 横断変更が 要る → 別タスク。

## 台帳を 人物ごとに 分けた 理由

1つに まとめると **顔が 混ざる**（松井社長とヘンディさんの 設定画を 同時に 渡すと 起きる）。
ネクマックスも 別 —— ほかの 台帳は negative で `robots, mascots` を 禁じて いるので、
同じ 台帳に 入れると 出したい 絵にも 出ない。
さらに **ネクマックスは 原画だけだと 頭が 卵形に なった**ので、合格ずみの
`build.webp` も 参照に 足して 撮り直した（skill に 書いた）。

## 証拠

- `npm test` … 80 files / **1236 passed**
- `npm run lint:content` … **エラー 0**（警告1は はじまりの まんがの 既存分）
- `npm run typecheck` … 通過
- 差しこんだ 7枚は すべて 実在を 確認（`status: "done"` ＋ ファイル）

author: tangvarie
body:
## 背景（上传卡死排障第三弹）

#51 部署后重传截图仍"卡住且零日志"。排查出三个盲区：

1. **web 进程对 INFO 全盲**：root logger 无 handler → 只输出 WARNING+，`[kimi_client] 图片降采样` 等 INFO 诊断在 Railway 日志里根本不会出现（worker 能看到 httpx 刷屏是因为 worker 配了 basicConfig、web 没配）。"没看到降采样行"无法区分"没跑"和"跑了没显示"。
2. **httpx 分阶段超时对"缓慢滴灌"无效**：实测海外→`api.moonshot.cn` 上行仅 ~150KB/s（1.4MB body 9.6s）。慢速上传每次 write 都成功，connect/read/write 各自的 120s 超时永远不触发——单次尝试可以无限拖，这正是"不报错、纯卡住"的机制。
3. **Pillow 软依赖缺席静默**：没装时降采样悄悄跳过，无从得知。

## 变更

- `app.py`：启动即 `basicConfig(INFO)`（在 secret-masker 安装**之前**，让新 handler 被脱敏包装覆盖，见审计 SUP-005）；httpx logger 降到 WARNING 防刷屏；worker 同步 httpx 静音
- `kimi_client`：辅助调用外包**墙钟硬上限**（`KIMI_ASSIST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS + 60s`，独立线程 + `future.result(timeout)`，`shutdown(wait=False)` 不阻塞）；超限消息含 timeout 关键字保持 transient 分类可重试
- `_shrink_image`：Pillow 缺席时 warning 一次

## 新增：辩论历史增量缓存（ENABLE_DEBATE_HISTORY_CACHE）

首条真实 run 观察到 k3 基本吃不到缓存——结构性的（一次性 stage + 各 agent system prompt 互不相同）。真正的缓存红利在策略辩论循环：每轮把全部 `debate_history` 原样重发，而 system 级缓存盖不到它，到后几轮历史占输入大头且**全价重算**。

- `_strategy_loop` 把每轮发言序列化**一次**存成字节稳定的前缀文本段，经保留键 `_cache_prefix_blocks` 传给 BaseAgent
- `_call_model` 把前缀段逐段成 text block 前置在用户消息里，`cache_control` 断点只打在最后一段——下一轮前缀与本轮完全一致，命中「system + 全部历史轮」缓存（断点预算 system 1 + 消息级 1 = 2，远低于 4 上限）
- 缓存 400 自愈路径同步接入：剥 system 断点时把消息级断点一并剥掉，否则重试仍带 `cache_control`，同一个 400 原样再来
- GPT/OpenAI-compat 路径把前缀段拼回纯文本，历史不丢；开关关掉即回退老形态（`debate_history` 整个进尾部 JSON）
- K2.6 缓存命中省 83%、v4-flash 省 98%，辩论越深省得越多，延迟同步下降

版本 → **v0.36.1**（部署后看侧栏徽章确认新版已上线）。

## 验证

- 硬上限模式独立测试：挂死调用 1 秒内放弃、shutdown 不阻塞、消息被 `_is_transient` 判为可重试
- 缓存前缀 5 项逻辑测试（fake client 捕获请求）：无前缀不变；断点只在末段；400 自愈重试后 system 为纯串且所有消息块无 `cache_control`；缓存关闭时前缀照发不带断点；保留键不进尾部 JSON
- `compileall` 通过

## 部署后预期日志（这次一定看得见）

```
[kimi_client] 图片降采样 1228KB → xxxKB(...)   × 5 行
[screenshot_analyzer] ...                       成功或 6 分钟内明确失败
```

author: alecmarcus
body:
## Why

The PyO3 bridge built a `FileKeyCustody` when a caller passed `custody="platform"`, so the Python SDK named a platform-native key store and delivered an Argon2id and AES-256-GCM key file at `$HOME/.scp/keys.bin`. The NAPI and UniFFI bridges already answered that string with `SCP-IDENT-1003`. One name reached two different key stores depending on which SDK a participant used — the false guarantee about key protection that CLAUDE.md's builder tenet forbids.

Closes half (a) of story SCP-294, "Fail closed on the custody strings the bridges reject, and normalize the identity parameter across SDKs". Half (b), the optional identity parameter on Swift and Kotlin publish methods, is untouched and the story stays `pending`.

## The matrix, read from each bridge

`scp_platform::CustodyType` (`crates/scp-platform/src/traits.rs:223`) names the substrates a key can occupy — `InMemory`, `Hardware`, `Software` — and carries no `Platform` variant. `FileKeyCustody::custody_type` returns `Software` (`crates/scp-platform/src/file.rs:893`). The `KeyCustodyProvider` callback contract carries `hardware`, `software`, `software_biometric`.

### Before

| String | PyO3 / Python | NAPI / TypeScript | UniFFI / Swift + Kotlin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `in_memory` | `InMemoryKeyCustody` under `testing`; `SCP-IDENT-1008` shipped | same | same |
| `file` | **`FileKeyCustody`** at `$HOME/.scp/keys.bin` | `SCP-VALID-7005` | `SCP-VALID-7005` |
| `platform` | **`FileKeyCustody`** at `$HOME/.scp/keys.bin` | `SCP-IDENT-1003` | `SCP-IDENT-1003` |
| `software` | `SCP-VALID-7005` | `SCP-IDENT-1003` | `SCP-IDENT-1003` |
| anything else | `SCP-VALID-7005` | `SCP-VALID-7005` | `SCP-VALID-7005` |

### After

| String | PyO3 / Python | NAPI / TypeScript | UniFFI / Swift + Kotlin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `in_memory` | `InMemoryKeyCustody` under `testing`; `SCP-IDENT-1008` shipped | same | same |
| `file` | `FileKeyCustody` at `$HOME/.scp/keys.bin` | `SCP-VALID-7005` | `SCP-VALID-7005` |
| `platform` | **`SCP-IDENT-1003`** | `SCP-IDENT-1003` | `SCP-IDENT-1003` |
| `software` | `SCP-VALID-7005` | `SCP-IDENT-1003` | `SCP-IDENT-1003` |
| anything else | `SCP-VALID-7005` | `SCP-VALID-7005` | `SCP-VALID-7005` |

No custody string reaches Apple Keychain or Android Keystore on any bridge, before or after. A caller reaches either by injecting a `KeyCustodyProvider` through `identity_create_with_custody`.

## What changed

**Bridges.** `parse_custody_inner` (PyO3) fails closed on `"platform"`. `parse_custody_with_seed` (PyO3) guards its `SCP-VALID-7009` arm on `"file"`, and the NAPI bridge drops its seed check from the `"platform" | "software"` arm, so both judge the custody name before the seed pairing. `parse_custody_method` (UniFFI) rejects at the boundary, and `CustodyMethod` loses the `Platform` and `Software` variants every create path already rejected. `identity_create_with_custody` (UniFFI) stamps `CustodyMethod::Callback`, so `Identity::custody_type()` answers `"callback"` for an injected provider — the string PyO3 and NAPI already answered, in place of `"platform"`, which asserted a platform-native key store for a provider whose substrate the bridge cannot verify.

**Each SDK keeps the custody members it carried.** Python's `PLATFORM` stops being an alias for `FILE` and becomes what the other three already had: a name the bridge refuses with a typed code. Every member's documentation states what its bridge does with it, and none claims to reach Keychain, Keystore, or a credential manager. TypeScript's `identityCreate` takes `CustodyType` instead of `string`.

**Two fabricated references deleted.** The Python docstring claimed to mirror `scp_core::identity::CustodyType`, a path that does not exist. Four files cited `SCP-294a`, a story id absent from the repository and from the history of `.docs`.

**Documentation.** 23 files told a reader to pass `"platform"` for production. Each SDK README also gains a section recording that no shipped build creates an identity by any path yet, because `identity_create_with_custody` returns `SCP-IDENT-1059` until a real `PreRotationCustody` backend lands. Without that section, redirecting readers to the injection path would have replaced one false guarantee with another — a review caught exactly that.

## Local verification

CI clippy with the full feature set and `-D warnings`: clean. `cargo test`: PyO3 446, NAPI 330, UniFFI 242, zero failures. All 28 gate scripts pass. TypeScript: biome clean, `tsc --noEmit` clean, 848 pass. Python: ruff and ruff-format clean, 783 pass and 26 skip, against an extension rebuilt with `maturin develop --features testing`. Kotlin: detekt clean, 503 tests, zero failures. Swift: `swift test` 156 tests, zero failures, against an XCFramework built with `build-xcframework.sh --dev`; swiftlint and swiftformat clean.

The tracked generated bindings are current: regenerating `bindings/swift/Sources/SCP/Internal/ScpBindings.swift` from the release dylib through `uniffi-bindgen` produces a byte-identical file, and its `CustodyMethod` carries `inMemory`, `callback`, and `external` — the three variants the Rust enum now declares.

## This does not answer OQ-9

Section 3.2 of the identity spec owns the custody options and, on `main`, names four custody sources in prose and no option string. Pull request #2411 holds that file and raises OQ-9, which asks whether `CustodyType.platform` names an OS keystore or an encrypted key file, and assigns the answer to §3.2.

This change removes the collision by making `"platform"` mean one thing — refused, inject a provider — on all three bridges, which is convergence onto behaviour two bridges already had. It does not rename `"file"` to `"software"`, does not introduce `"hardware"`, and does not edit §3.2. An earlier revision of this branch deleted `platform` and `software` from the SDK enums; three reviews found that answered OQ-9 from downstream and produced a single-inhabitant type, so the members are restored with documentation that states the refusal. OQ-9 exists only on #2411's branch, so this branch cannot update it — the #2411 author should fold in whatever Alec decides.

**Note for whoever settles it:** only a Cargo feature separates the bridges. `crates/scp-ffi/Cargo.toml:80` enables `scp-platform/file`; the NAPI and UniFFI manifests do not. `FileKeyCustody` is production-real and durability-only, so no gate blocks it on the other two. No artifact records a decision to withhold it.

## Review status

Two full roster passes ran (black-hat, security, bug-catcher, completionist, inquisitor, api-design, alignment, simplifier). **This is not double-zero.** Pass two found a fresh crop of false sentences in material the branch had rewritten well beyond custody, so the branch was narrowed to the custody claim itself and the falsified statements were corrected. What remains open needs a human, not another pass:

1. **ADR-025 and ADR-027 decide that `custody: "platform"` selects the platform adapter.** That factory was never built, and this change makes the string fail closed, so the ADRs and the code disagree. Each ADR now carries an additive note recording the disagreement; neither ADR's decision text is touched, because a story does not rewrite an ADR. Whether those decisions are superseded is theirs to answer. `.docs/adrs/ADR-048-scp-multi-instance.md` carries the same kind of note for the `SCP-VALID-7009` seed contract this change supersedes.
2. **OQ-9** — the `"file"` versus `"software"` spelling, below.
3. **Three custody defaults disagree** across the four SDKs (Python `FILE`, TypeScript `"in_memory"`, Swift and Kotlin none). CLAUDE.md forbids silent security defaults. Removing them changes every call site and is a separate decision.
