author: takumin
body:
All fifteen `Process::Sys` methods CRuby has, over a HAL that answers separately for what a port was built with and what the running system refused.

## Two answers, not one

| situation | how | raised |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the port was built without the call | method body is `mrb_notimplement_m` | `NotImplementedError` |
| the port has it and the system refused | `errno` | `Errno::*` |

The first is asked once at initialization through the new `mrb_hal_process_supported()` and never comes from an `errno`. That is what keeps a seccomp filter's `ENOSYS` — a refusal at run time, for a call the kernel has — from being reported as a fact about the binary.

Measured against CRuby 3.3.6 on glibc, where `issetugid`, `setrgid` and `setruid` answer `respond_to?` with false and raise `NotImplementedError` naming the method, and the other twelve work:

```
$ ./build/host/bin/mruby -e 'p Process::Sys.respond_to?(:issetugid); Process::Sys.issetugid'
false
NotImplementedError: issetugid() function is unimplemented on this machine
```

## Why `src/sys.c` picks its bodies at run time

The tree writes an unimplemented method as a `#define` around the function with the platform test outside it, as `mruby-io`'s `File#flock` and `mruby-socket`'s `BasicSocket#getpeereid` do. This one cannot: what calls exist is a fact about the port, and the common sources are above the HAL and may not test for one at compile time. So it walks a table at initialization and installs either the real body or `mrb_notimplement_m`.

A caller cannot tell the difference — the body is the mark either way — and an external `hal-process-*` gem can replace the port without `src/sys.c` being rebuilt, which is the same argument read the other way.

The marked ones take every argument shape rather than their own. mruby checks the shape before the body runs, so keeping the real one would answer a call written with the wrong count by complaining about the count; CRuby gives these an arity of -1 for the same reason.

## Arguments

An ID is 32 bits read as unsigned, and Ruby also lets one be written as the negative those bits read as — the only way to spell the `(uid_t)-1` that `setreuid(2)` and `setresuid(2)` take for "leave this one alone". `mrb_process_id_arg()` spans both readings; `mrb_process_int_arg()` is left to the pids and signals it was written for. -1 is given no meaning in the common layer.

An ID may be named instead of numbered, and a name no account table knows is an `ArgumentError` — nothing was asked of the system, so there is no errno for the call to have failed with. That is why the two name lookups have no `mrb_process_op` of their own: a port with no table just fails every one of them.

A credential call names no object it was working on, so a failure reports the error alone, as `Process.kill` and `Process.waitpid` do since #7413.

## Ports

The POSIX port answers for what the host has — `setresuid`/`setresgid` on Linux and most BSDs, `setruid`/`setrgid` on the BSDs alone, `issetugid` where it is not glibc — naming the platforms known to have each call rather than inferring one from the absence of another, since a false negative costs a method and a false positive costs a link error.

The Windows port has none of them. A Windows process has an access token holding SIDs, not a `uid_t` and a `gid_t`. CRuby answers 0 there; reporting the operations as absent is the honest answer, since 0 is what a privileged POSIX process reports and a program reading it would conclude it is running as root.

## The amalgam commit

`setresuid(2)` needs `_GNU_SOURCE` on glibc, and a feature-test macro has to precede every header — which the amalgam's concatenation into one translation unit denies to every source but the first. The first commit hoists them to the top of the amalgamated header, where they hold for the whole file, and takes them out of the two blocks that wrote them too late. A build whose gems ask for no feature-test macro generates a byte for byte identical amalgam.

## Verified

- `rake test` and the full `ci/gcc-clang` matrix — `full-debug`, `bintest`, `cxx_abi`, `byte-string`, `ascii-ctype`: 0 KO, 0 crash, 0 warnings.
- `MRB_INT32`, with and without `mruby-bigint`, to cover both sides of the range guards.
- The test suite run unprivileged, which is what reaches the `Errno` assertion.
- `rake amalgam`, then compiled with `-Wall` and linked into a program that calls `Process::Sys.getuid`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01PFfobZoryByo6fYJ72N4Ri

author: mewclouds
body: Users had to find and paste their Marvel Rivals mod folder by hand before Cratebug could do anything. BentoMod could find the game itself, so this brings that behavior over with a design of our own: a "Detect Steam library" button in the library toolbar that locates the game through Steam's install records and points Cratebug at its `~mods` folder. Detection is built around a small provider seam in `internal/gamedetect`, so the Epic Games provider can land later without touching call sites. Steam is the only implementation for now: it reads the install root from the Windows registry, parses `steamapps/libraryfolders.vdf` for every library, and verifies the known install shape before reporting anything. Detection is read-only and reports one of three states: - Library found: offered as a switch when a library is already configured, applied directly when none is - Install found but no `~mods`: a dialog asks "No mod library was found for Steam" and offers to create it, re-verifying the install server-side and creating exactly that one empty folder - Nothing found: a clear message, with the pasted-path flow unchanged as a fallback The active store is a persisted setting (Settings > Mod library detection, defaulting to Steam). Epic Games appears in the selector as disabled until its provider ships, which is gated on testing against a real Epic installation. Store logos are Simple Icons path data drawn with `currentColor`, and NOTICE.md records the Valve and Epic trademarks. The branch also carries the phase 12 documentation (roadmap entry, tasks, approved review with screenshots) and two process changes: a no-magic-numbers rule in CODING_GUIDELINES.md, and agent verification switched from this repo's Playwright MCP servers to playwright-cli, with `.mcp.json` removed. ## Verification - `.\check.ps1` passes: gofmt, Biome format and lint, TypeScript typecheck, Vite build, `go vet`, and the full Go suite, including new coverage for `internal/gamedetect` (vdf parsing, all three detection states, install shape edge cases, confirmed-creation constraints) and the settings round trip - `bun test`: 52 tests pass, including the detection outcome branching and the case-insensitive Windows path comparison - Verified live against `wails dev` with playwright-cli: with `~mods` deliberately moved aside, detect produced the create dialog showing the real install path, confirming created exactly one empty `~mods` folder (checked on disk) and rescanned to the empty state, re-detect then reported "This library is already active" without a dialog, and the Settings selector showed Steam selected and Epic disabled - Screenshots of the toolbar control, create dialog, post-create scan, and Settings section are in `docs/screenshots/phase-12/` and are part of this diff --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added automatic Marvel Rivals mod-library detection for Steam installations. - Added confirmation options to switch to a detected library or create a missing `~mods` folder. - Added library-provider selection in Settings, with Steam supported and Epic Games planned. - Added detection controls to the toolbar and empty-library view. - **Documentation** - Added user guidance, troubleshooting steps, trademark attributions, and roadmap updates. - **Chores** - Updated Playwright CLI guidance and ignored related local files.

author: nhomyk
body:
Phase 1 means standing up a new deployment. A new deployment means an empty database. **The migration chain could not fill one.**

It stopped three separate times, and each break hid the next.

| Migration | What broke |
|---|---|
| **125** | Seeds a `ceo` row into `instinct_team_members`, whose CHECK from `001` permits only `cto, dev, sales, ops`. `145` widens it, twenty migrations too late |
| **129** | Asserts three named principles are present. A new database has none, so a schema migration failed on the absence of seed data |
| **137** | Adds an FK to `instinct_workspace`. Its own comment says workspace `default` was "created by migration 015". `015` creates the **table** and never inserts that row |

**None of this was red anywhere.** Every existing deployment predates these files, so the chain had never been replayed from zero. We were one client onboarding away from finding this out live, in front of them.

## Each fix keeps the original intent

Not one of these deletes a check.

- **125** drops the narrow constraint before seeding, idempotently, rather than editing `001` to claim something that wasn't true when it was written.
- **129** accepts **zero** as a fresh database while still failing on **one or two**. That's genuine drift and precisely the case the assertion was written to catch. The inserts it guards are `INSERT ... SELECT` against the same titles, so they were already no-ops when the principles are absent.
- **137** inserts the default workspace row it already assumed existed, with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so it's a no-op on every database that already has it.

## Verified, not assumed

```
228 migrations applied to an empty Postgres
second run: done (0 new, 228 previously applied)
```

## CI now checks it on every PR

Two steps added to `db-contract.yml`, deliberately **before** the contract tests so a broken chain reports as a broken chain rather than as a hundred confusing downstream failures:

1. **A fresh database can be built from the migrations** — creates an empty database and runs the chain
2. **Running them again changes nothing** — fails if a replay applies anything, because a non-idempotent migration breaks the *next* deploy rather than this one, which is the worst time to find out

That second check is the one that would have caught all three of these before they reached main.

`scripts/verify.sh` green, all 9 stages.

author: scalarion
body:
The cascade was going to rewrite every registration holding a renamed item and clear every one
holding a removed item. It is abandoned, and the in-use rule it was meant to replace is kept and
made sound instead.

Renaming "Vegetarisch" to "Vegan" rewrites what a hundred students said they wanted, and no
automatic rewrite can know whether they still mean it; removing an option leaves them holding
nothing. The honest outcome in both cases is that the answers are asked for again — the school's
decision, not something a fan-out can paper over.

What makes that affordable is that the rule stops being obstructive once the lists belong to one
series. The original complaint — a class mistyped in October cannot be fixed in November — was a
symptom of the lists being **global**, so another season's registration froze this season's
identically-named item. Scoped per series it bites only where this series' own students have
already answered, and during setup, when mistakes are actually caught, nothing is in use at all.

## The race, which is most of this change

The guard checked before the transaction, and that is a real TOCTOU: a student choosing the value
being removed in between would be left holding something the series no longer offers, and with no
cascade nothing repairs it. A guard with that hole is worse than none, because it claims an
invariant it does not hold.

- **The in-use check now runs inside the transaction that writes the list**, and queries narrowly
  — the registrations holding the one value being touched, rather than the whole series. Firestore
  locks that index range, so a student answering anything else never conflicts, and the only save
  that does is one choosing the very item being edited.
- **Saving a registration became a transaction too.** It reads the event series inside it and
  validates every answer against it, which closes the other direction: a teacher's edit writes
  that document, so a save which read the older one retries and is refused rather than storing a
  value nothing offers.
- Either order is safe — whichever commits first invalidates the other's read.
- **The student never pays.** A transaction retries by itself, so a save caught by a concurrent
  edit re-reads, re-validates and commits unnoticed. The one refusal they see is the one that
  deserves it: the option they chose has just been removed, and they are asked to reload.
- **The teacher pays**, which is the right way round: theirs is the rare and questionable request.

The guard's equality is exact rather than normalised, and deliberately so: a student picks from
the list, so what they store is the list's own spelling, and a rename is refused while the item is
held — so no second spelling can arise. The reasoning is in the file, and the test that used to
assert normalised matching now states the new contract instead of being deleted.

## Indexes

The narrow queries bring one composite index per answer a list supplies, plus one for the
rentals. They are temporary: once a registration lives beneath the series it belongs to, the
series is the path rather than a field, and every one of them goes.

## Spec

US-24 becomes the refusal and US-27 the two-sided transaction; US-25 keeps only its storage half.
**Q4 reverses** — with nothing rewriting stored answers, US-11's "changes to the list do not alter
already-stored records" is simply true again, so the contradiction Q4 existed to resolve
disappears rather than being decided. Q15 is withdrawn along with the whole `functions/` codebase
it justified, including the IAM widening it would have required. Q16 is subsumed: the class was
not an exception but the case that generalised. Slice 3a is gone and the slices renumber to 1–8.

## Tests

1492 unit tests and 100 rules tests pass. The new ones pin the race specifically, since neither
direction is visible in a single-threaded run: the guard reads *through* the transaction it is
given rather than around it, the read is ordered before the write, a save is refused when its
answer is no longer offered, and food's "Sonstiges" is accepted beside a non-empty list and
refused beside an empty one.

`FakeFirestore` gained `array-contains`. It already refused a read after a write, which is what
catches a guard that queries outside its transaction.

author: jvoisin
body:
Problem:  NFA regexp matching is slower than necessary because
          fast_breakcheck() is called for every state in the list.
Solution: Only call fast_breakcheck() once every 100 states, using a
          static counter, like exec_instructions().

The inner loop of nfa_regmatch() that computes the next state list called fast_breakcheck() on every iteration. fast_breakcheck() lives in a separate translation unit and thus cannot be inlined, so each state paid the cost of a function call merely to increment a counter that only reaches ui_breakcheck() once in ten thousand calls. During syntax highlighting, where the state lists can grow long, this has a measurable overhead. Guarding the call behind a static counter, like done with the breakcheck_count variable in src/vim9execute.c make things less worse.

A "perf stat -e instructions" on a full scroll of a 60000 line C file with syntax highlighting enabled shows a 2% reduction.

author: tgmaurer
body:
Four of the five open issues, plus two follow-ups you asked for. #11 (the
README screenshot) is left for you.

## Help tags — #10

Every icon-only control now answers a resting pointer, and says what the
click does rather than repeating the label it sits under:

- **Toolbars** — the education and semester menus, both filter menus, every
  New button, Edit, Delete, and the failing-only toggle. Where a button is
  disabled the tag is the *reason* it is disabled, which is the one thing a
  greyed-out glyph cannot say. The toggle names the state it is about to move
  to, since a toggle's ambiguity is always which way it is going.
- **Grade chips on the dashboard** carry the grade's date, and **subject
  names** carry the subject's weight. The row has width for neither, and both
  are otherwise only readable by opening the record.
- **The `+` beside a subject's grades** says what it adds.

Two things worth knowing, both learned the hard way. A help tag has to be
attached to the control rather than to a wrapper around it — `DetailButton`
takes it as a parameter for that reason. And a tag is verified by reading
`AXHelp` off the element, not by watching for the bubble: the bubble does not
reliably draw for a pointer moved by `CGEvent`, which produced one confident
wrong conclusion about modifier order before the attribute was checked
instead.

## Weights of 0% — spec change

Amends SPEC §2 and §3: `CHECK (weight > 0)` becomes `CHECK (weight >= 0)` on
both Subjects and Grades. A weight of 0 means "on the record, counts for
nothing" — a practice paper, a mark that was later dropped, a subject you sit
that carries no marks.

- Migration `v2.zeroWeights` rebuilds both tables, since SQLite cannot alter a
  CHECK. `MigrationTests` starts at v1 *with rows in it* and pins what a
  rebuild can destroy: rows and their ids, both cascades, all three indexes.
- The averages already returned `nil` for a zero total weight as a guard
  against a bad row. That branch is now reachable and meant: where nothing
  counts there is no average, so the screen reads N/A rather than falling back
  to an unweighted mean and inventing a weighting nobody asked for.
- 0% joins the quick-picks last — the field always took any number, but nobody
  thinks to try a weight of nothing unless the list says it is allowed.

author: mguptahub
body:
## Summary
- **Server** (`apps/api/plane/utils/path_validator.py`, `validate_next_path`): calls `urlparse(next_path)` and only extracts `.path` when `scheme` or `netloc` is truthy. For `"///example.com/"` (three or more leading slashes), `urlparse()` returns both `scheme` and `netloc` empty — verified directly — so that branch never fires and the raw string passes every remaining check unchanged. Fixed by rejecting any `next_path` starting with `//` outright, right after the existing "must start with `/`" check.
- **Client** (`apps/web/core/lib/wrappers/authentication-wrapper.tsx`, `isValidURL`): only regex-blocked a literal `http(s)`/`ftp` scheme prefix, so the same authority-relative string passed and was handed to `router.push()`. Fixed by resolving the URL against `location.origin` and requiring the result to actually still be same-origin, instead of pattern-matching the input string.
- Browsers resolve a leading `//` as authority-relative even when neither validator's own URL parsing detected a host — the accepted value silently navigates off-domain post-login, a same-origin-trust phishing vector (attacker link visibly belongs to the Plane host; victim is already authenticated; click lands on attacker content).
- Checked the advisory's other listed `next_path` consumers (auth-form components, oauth hooks, `api.service.ts`) — they only forward the value to a server-side auth redirect or a hidden form field, no independent client-side navigation, so they're covered by the server-side fix and don't need changes.

## Test plan
- [x] 8 new server-side tests in `apps/api/plane/tests/unit/utils/test_path_validator.py`: rejects 3/4/5-leading-slash forms, positive controls confirming the pre-existing 2-slash and scheme-prefixed cases still safely downgrade to a bare path (not a new rejection), genuine relative paths still accepted
- [x] Verified fail-before/pass-after via `git stash` — all 3 malicious-path cases fail against pre-fix code
- [x] Client-side fix verified empirically via Node's URL parser (WHATWG-compliant, matches browser behavior) — confirmed it rejects all authority-relative forms and the original blocked absolute-scheme forms, while still accepting genuine relative paths. No test harness exists for `apps/web` in this repo to add an automated regression test.
- [x] `ruff check`/`ruff format --check` clean (Python); `oxlint`/`oxfmt --check` clean (TypeScript); the file doesn't appear in `check:types` output (all pre-existing errors there are unrelated missing-export issues in `@plane/constants`/`@plane/types`)

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved redirect validation to block authority-relative paths that could navigate users to an external domain.
  * Strengthened URL validation against obfuscated paths containing tab, carriage return, or line feed characters.
  * Ensured navigation remains within the current site while preserving valid relative paths and supported URL formats.

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for unsafe multi-slash and obfuscated paths, supported URL cases, and genuine relative paths.

author: edward-lcl
body:
## Owner summary

This PR makes the historical KA59-Simple evidence auditable and any future
camera-ready runs resumable, but it does **not** make the accepted Figure 3
camera-ready as written. The audit supports a narrower story and exposes a
small set of author decisions that engineering must not make silently.

Start with the [five-minute owner brief](https://github.com/KaaustaaubShankar/BreakingAgentsIntoPOMDP/blob/camera-ready/ka59-truth/camera_ready/README.md). The generated
truth table and candidate-level manifest remain the detailed evidence layer.

## Canonical history

1. The 2026-05-13 GPT-5.2 run produced N=5 per effort for each main condition.
2. An early figure pooled `none`+`medium` into baseline 9/10 and feedback 8/10.
   The accepted figure later kept those pooled values for the `none` row, but
   changed the `medium` percentages to the raw medium rates while still printing
   N=10: 8/10 from 4/5 and 10/10 from 5/5. Neither row is an independent
   effort-specific N=10 sample.
3. DeepSeek `none` produced an infrastructure-clean N=20 matrix. DeepSeek
   `medium` attempts encountered provider-empty responses and HTTP 402
   insufficient balance; nominal N=20 summaries later treated disrupted trials
   as model losses.
4. The historical runner swallowed provider/parse failures, consumed the turn,
   and continued. A completed file therefore did not necessarily represent a
   clean model trial.
5. The accepted `HARD_FORMAT_ONLY`/no-rules runs predate the prompt branch that
   retained the detailed action protocol. Historical no-rules and the control
   described in the paper are different protocols.

## What the trial-level audit found

| Slice | Audited result | Reporting status |
|---|---:|---|
| DeepSeek `none` baseline | 12/20 | Supported |
| DeepSeek `none` world | 0/20 | Supported |
| DeepSeek `none` mechanics | 4/20 candidate; 4/19 strict | Supported, denominator choice needed |
| DeepSeek `none` historical no-rules tag | 4/20 | Outcome supported only as another mechanics-hard-prompt run, not the paper-described control |
| DeepSeek `none` feedback | 15/20 | Supported |
| GPT-5.2 `none` | baseline 5/5; world 0/2; mechanics 0/2; feedback 3/5 | Directional, small-N |
| GPT-5.2 `medium` | world 0/3; mechanics 0/3 | Directional, small-N; no clean baseline or feedback denominator |
| DeepSeek `medium` | no clean accepted cell | Infrastructure diagnosis only; published rates unsupported |
| GPT-5.2 no-rules | no clean accepted cell | No camera-ready performance claim |

Of 47 trials previously labelled `parse_error`, 46 explicitly record DeepSeek
empty content and are infrastructure failures. One DeepSeek `none` mechanics
trial contains a malformed model response at turn 100, then recovers for 27
actions and ends in a normal loss. The candidate denominator scores it as model
behavior (4/20); the strict sensitivity excludes it (4/19). No reviewed trial
supports a harness parse failure or indeterminate classification.

## What remains scientifically defensible

The existing evidence supports the directional importance of world information
and strong mechanics disruption in the audited slices. It also supports relative
feedback robustness for DeepSeek `none` and GPT-5.2 `none`.

It does **not** support:

- independent GPT N=10 rows for both efforts;
- the exact DeepSeek `medium` percentages;
- the no-rules causal claim about separating rule discovery from action-protocol
  discovery; or
- universal full-matrix wording at the displayed denominators.

## Author decisions required before paid runs or manuscript edits

1. **Reporting unit:** effort-specific rows with honest N, or one explicitly
   pooled exploratory GPT row shown once.
2. **Response to reviewer/PI increased-N feedback:** narrow/correct the existing
   claims, or run a clean target-N matrix. The repository does not record the
   exact requested scope, so N=20-per-effort is currently an operational scenario,
   not an automatic scientific recommendation.
3. **No-rules estimand:** remove/relabel the historical implementation duplicate,
   or run the later paper-intended control under a distinct protocol ID.
4. **Denominator:** candidate main view with strict sensitivity, or strict-only.
   This changes only DeepSeek `none` mechanics: 4/20 versus 4/19.
5. **DeepSeek `medium`:** omit/mark unsupported, or rerun under a pinned identity.
6. **Rerun identity/scope:** exact model slug, provider/upstream, reasoning
   semantics, target cells, and target N. The requested “5.6 Luna” run remains
   blocked on the same identity decision.

## Camera-ready end state

If new evidence is required, freeze the estimand and identity first; run/top up
only protocol-compatible valid trials; keep infrastructure failures as excluded
audit evidence; regenerate the manifest; generate the paper figure from audited
counts rather than hand-entered percentages; then edit Methods/Figure 3/Results.

If no new runs are authorized, the defensible end state is a narrower paper:
use the clean existing denominators, remove unsupported DeepSeek-medium exact
rates, remove/relabel the no-rules causal interpretation, and soften universal
model-by-effort claims.

## What this PR changes

- deterministic per-trial audit, dual denominator views, manifest, and generated
  truth table;
- evidence-based review of all prior parse-error records;
- accepted-data protocol lock with observed versus recovered metadata;
- resume-safe, identity-hashed runner with `--plan`, `--smoke`, `--resume`,
  duplicate/incompatibility refusal, and infrastructure-failure aborts;
- exact local environment sources required by the accepted runner;
- owner brief, claim-by-claim paper reconciliation, and guarded execution appendix;
- corrected generated metadata for the final accepted GPT figure lineage.

No paid/external model call was made, no hypothetical result was inserted, and
the accepted manuscript prose was not silently rewritten.

## Verification

- generated audit `--check` passes;
- offline environment `--smoke` passes with zero model calls;
- 14/14 unit tests pass;
- `compileall` and `git diff --check` pass;
- GitNexus change detection: medium overall; four affected flows are confined to
  audit manifest generation and runner plan imports. Regression tests confirm
  scientific counts and target-N math are unchanged by the historical-display
  wording correction.

author: jubacch
body:
## What the binary says about itself

```
You may only use this Speedtest software and information generated
from it for personal, non-commercial use, through a command line
interface on a personal computer.
```

That is stronger than "redistribution restricted". It is a **use** restriction,
it names *personal, non-commercial* use only, and it covers the **measurements**
as well as the tool.

For Nodeglow sold as a product, Ookla is out regardless of whether the image
carries the binary or the customer installs it themselves — unless there is a
commercial agreement with Ookla.

## My mistake

I added this to the image earlier today to fix implausible speedtest data. It
was the right call for debugging and the wrong one to ship.

## Fix

Bundling is opt-in via `BUNDLE_OOKLA=1`, passed through compose from `.env`:

```yaml
build:
  context: ./backend
  args:
    BUNDLE_OOKLA: ${BUNDLE_OOKLA:-0}
```

The default build carries nothing proprietary. A personal installation sets the
flag and keeps Ookla's accuracy.

Without it the integration falls back to `speedtest-cli` (Apache-2.0), which is
unmaintained since 2021 and reports a fixed 1800000 ms ping on some connections.
That is a reason an operator may want to opt in — not a reason to make shipping
proprietary software the default.

## Not resolved by this PR

The real question is a licensing decision: a commercial agreement with Ookla, or
a different measurement source for the product build. This only stops the
default from being the wrong one.

author: hunterdsp
body:
Fixes the generator side of [doppler#1052](https://github.com/doppler-dsp/doppler/issues/1052).

`realtime` is a **sample rate in Hz**, handed straight to the project's
`clock_create` as its `fs`. Nothing said so:

| face | what it said |
| --- | --- |
| C docstring | `stream(block=4096, realtime=0.0) -> iterator (realtime=fs paces)` |
| `.pyi` | `"""Iterate the sequence in blocks."""` — no mention of the argument at all |

The parenthetical reads as prose about what pacing *does*, not as "the value
you pass **is** fs", and a default of `0.0` reads like a disabled boolean or a
0–1 scale. So every natural misreading — scale factor, speed multiplier, enable
flag — is **silent**. Measured on doppler:

```
c.stream(block=1000, realtime=1.0)    next() never returned  (1 sample/sec,
                                      so the first block is 1000 s)
c.stream(block=1000, realtime=10e6)   first block in 0.2 ms
```

No exception, no warning, nothing to grep for. It reads exactly like a hang,
and the process is genuinely asleep rather than spinning, so a profiler points
nowhere either.

## Three changes; the second is the one that matters

**1. Both faces name the unit.** The docstring now says *"realtime is the
SAMPLE RATE in Hz … not a speed multiplier"*, and the `.pyi` gains a numpy
`Parameters` block instead of a one-liner that omitted the parameter:

```python
    realtime : float
        Sample rate in **Hz** to pace against — pass
        your ``fs`` (e.g. ``realtime=10e6``), not a
        speed multiplier. ``0`` (the default) streams
        as fast as possible.
```

**2. The condition is already computed, so expose it rather than document it.**
`block` and `realtime` are both in hand at `stream()`, so the wait is one
division. A first block over 60 s of wall clock warns, naming the rate, the
block, the seconds and the unit:

```
stream(realtime=1) paces at 1 sample(s)/sec, so the first block of 1000
would take 1000 s. realtime is the SAMPLE RATE in Hz -- pass your fs
(e.g. realtime=10e6), not a speed multiplier; 0 streams as fast as possible.
```

A **warning**, not an error — a 1 Hz telemetry stream is legitimate and this is
silenceable — but silence is not an option, because silence *is* the defect. A
documented footgun is still a footgun: the reader has to already suspect it to
go looking.

**3. `realtime < 0` is now a `ValueError`.** It used to fall through the
`> 0.0` guard and quietly disable pacing — a third silent misread.

## Mechanics worth keeping

- The message uses `snprintf` + `PyErr_WarnEx`, **not** `PyErr_WarnFormat`:
  `PyUnicode_FromFormat` has no floating-point conversion, and the numbers
  *are* the message. The reason ships in the generated C so the next reader
  does not simplify it back.
- `<stdio.h>` now follows the **realtime** feature rather than the JSON one.
  They are independent, and a composer with realtime and without generated
  JSON would have called `snprintf` undeclared.

## Off by default, still

A composer with no `realtime` gets none of it — pinned by
`test_plain_stream_has_no_realtime_check`.

## Verification

`make test-fast` → **6435 passed, 5 skipped**. `make lint` → 0.

Verified end-to-end by regenerating doppler's `wfm_compose` binding against
this branch and rebuilding: the issue's exact repro now warns with the real
numbers, correct usage stays silent and returns in 0.2 ms, and `realtime=-1.0`
raises.

author: maksimyugai
body:
## Summary

Fixes #123.

`computeFingerprint()` in `worker/modules/ingest/fingerprint.ts` fell back to the literal string `"unknown"` (via `messageText()`) whenever an exception had no `stacktrace.frames` — even when the exception itself carried a perfectly good `type`/`value`. Two completely different frameless exceptions (e.g. `QARegressionMarker99` vs `QANegativeControl99`) ended up with the identical fingerprint `message:unknown` and got merged into one issue, inflating its `event_count`.

- Mirrors `deriveTitle()`'s existing `exceptionValue.type`/`.value` handling: when an exception value is present but has no stack frames, the fingerprint is now built as `exception:<type>:<value>` (or `exception:<type>` if there's no value) instead of falling through to `messageText()`.
- Only falls through to `messageText()`/`"unknown"` when there is genuinely no exception value present at all (a bare message-only event) — unchanged behavior for that case.
- Exceptions **with** stack frames are untouched — still use the existing `stack:<type>:<signature>` grouping.

## Test plan

- [x] Extended `tests/unit/fingerprint.test.ts`:
  - two distinct frameless exceptions now get distinct fingerprints (neither containing `"unknown"`)
  - an exception with frames still uses the existing stack-based fingerprint unchanged (no regression)
  - a bare message-only event (no exception at all) still falls back to `message:unknown` as before
- [x] `deno fmt` / `deno lint` / `deno check` pass on both changed files
- [x] `deno task test` — all 212 tests pass (13 in `fingerprint.test.ts`)
- [x] Live verification: built the client, ran `wrangler dev` against a locally migrated preview D1, POSTed two distinct frameless-exception envelopes (`QARegressionMarker99` / `QANegativeControl99`) to `/api/1/envelope`, then queried `/api/internal/v1/issues?project=1` (via a locally minted session token) and confirmed **two separate issues** were created (`eventCount: 1` each), instead of merging into one.

author: kiderazenon
body:
**💡 What**:
Replaced the `window.addEventListener('scroll')` and `getBoundingClientRect()` implementation for the reveal animations with `IntersectionObserver`.

**🎯 Why**:
The original implementation ran on every scroll event and queried `getBoundingClientRect().top` on multiple elements. This is a synchronous, main-thread-blocking operation that causes layout thrashing, severely degrading scroll performance. `IntersectionObserver` evaluates visibility asynchronously off the main thread.

**📊 Impact**:
Massively reduces main-thread blocking during scrolling. Prevents layout thrashing by eliminating synchronous DOM layout reads (`getBoundingClientRect()`) tied to scroll events. The observer is also disconnected (`unobserve`) once the element is revealed, reducing overhead to zero for already-revealed elements.

**🔬 Measurement**:
1. Open the page and open Chrome DevTools Performance tab.
2. Record a performance trace while scrolling up and down the page.
3. Observe the absence of long "Recalculate Style" and "Layout" tasks associated with scroll events that were previously caused by `getBoundingClientRect()`.

---

author: m4v3r4
body:
## Summary

Adds physical copy / stock tracking to Libris without introducing the postponed DB v2 migration system.

## What changes

- Adds a `book_copies` table linked to bibliographic `books`
- Gives each physical copy a unique inventory/barcode identifier
- Adds copy states: `available`, `loaned`, `lost`, and `maintenance`
- Adds nullable `loans.copyId` so each loan can reference a physical copy
- Allows multiple copies of the same title to be loaned at the same time
- Prevents the same physical copy from being loaned twice
- Adds physical copy management to the book detail screen
- Shows copy inventory codes on loan cards and loan queries
- Keeps `books.isAvailable` as a compatibility/cache field derived from copy availability
- Updates README, changelog, and version to `1.2.0+4`

## Backward compatibility

This deliberately stays on the current v1.x database initialization approach.

When an existing Libris database is opened:

- existing book rows are preserved
- books without a physical-copy row receive one automatically
- existing loan history is preserved
- legacy loans with no `copyId` are linked to the generated copy where possible
- active legacy loans mark that copy as loaned

No DB v2 migration framework is introduced in this PR.

## Tests

The test suite now covers:

- automatic initial copy creation
- copy-level availability
- two simultaneous loans when two copies exist
- rejection when all copies are loaned
- copy status changes
- return and active-loan deletion restoring copy availability
- copy deletion rules when loan history exists
- overdue queries including inventory codes
- legacy v1.1 book/loan backfill without data loss

Closes #27

Roadmap: #31

body:
One workflow, honestly amending the "No CI" charter (AGENTS.md section included): a **release robot that only ever opens PRs** — no tests, no gates on human commits, no auto-merge. The human merge + signed `fleet-v<N>` tag remain the promotion.

Triggers: `repository_dispatch` (`plugin-release`, sent by ai-tc's release workflow — akasecurity/ai-tc#346) and `workflow_dispatch` with an exact-version input. The job:
1. **Gate** — exact x.y.z only; same-or-lower than the current pin exits green with a notice (rollback stays a human act).
2. **Registry dist** — one registry-explicit `npm view … dist` (defeats ambient .npmrc rerouting), cross-checked against the dispatch payload when present.
3. **Provenance** — scratch install of exactly that version, `npm audit signatures`; the SLSA attestation must bind to `akasecurity/ai-tc` :: `release-plugin-claude.yml` @ `refs/tags/plugin-claude-v<version>` (pinned node 24 to dodge the older-npm empty-verified-set false positive).
4. **Pin edit** — proves the manifest round-trips byte-stably first, changes only `source.version`, re-parses, runs the charter's own `jq empty`.
5. **PR** — `bot/pin-ai-tc-<version>`, house-style title, evidence in the body, deduped on re-runs. Default `GITHUB_TOKEN` only (job-level contents+PR write).

**Operator action before first use:** enable *Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests* (Settings → Actions → General). Safe smoke test after merge: `workflow_dispatch` with version `0.9.8` — exits green, opens nothing.

Gates run: actionlint clean; every embedded python executed for real; a 7-case version-gate matrix (incl. injection strings); live dist + live provenance verification for 0.9.8; action SHA↔tag pins re-verified via the API.

author: arodiss
body:
The programme's go/no-go: run both paper-faithful arms on our rebuilt T0 bedrock and
compare them against the values *BM25 Wins at Scale* publishes for the same paradigms at
the same rung. The rule was declared before any score was seen — both arms within 3.5
points, BM25 in 71.2–78.2 and the File-System Agent in 73.9–80.9.

## Verdict: the gate fails, and the shape of the failure is the finding

| arm | correctness | completeness | combined | doc recall | published combined |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| File-System Agent | 83.2 | 82.88 | **77.40** | 90.24 | 77.4 |
| BM25 | 81.2 | 68.76 | **64.47** | 88.05 | 74.7 |

One arm reproduces its published value exactly (+0.00); the other misses by 10.23. Both
cells: 500 answered, 500 scored, none corrected, none failed, one session under
`gpt-5.5-2026-04-23` with `--no-correction`, `--parallelism 1`. The agent spent the call
budget on 17 questions (3.4%, against the study's reported "below 7%") and was cut off by
the wall clock on none, so it ran under the budget it names.

The agent landing exactly on 77.4 is what makes the BM25 miss interesting: the bedrock,
the tier construction, the reader, the judge and the scoring path are all shared between
the two arms, so they are not what differs.

## What this PR contains

Three defects found while measuring, each its own commit.

**The agent arm could not make a single LLM call.** `make_tools` emitted tool schemas in
the nested Chat-Completions shape while `_convert_tools` reads the flat Responses-API
shape, so every call raised `KeyError: 'name'` client-side. The reader preflight misses
it because it probes with a tool it builds itself. This arm had never run.

**Neither arm could see the bedrock's two organizational pages.** The study counts them
inside the tier and ten questions have no other evidence. BM25 now indexes them (T0 goes
from 2,011 to 2,016 chunks against the published 2,018) and the agent finds them in the
root it explores. The high-level question type goes from 30.8 to 74.7 combined on BM25,
and 8 of 10 such questions read a scaffold on the agent arm.

**The study's stated reader configuration does not reproduce its published BM25 score,
and the opposite configuration does.** Appendix C says "thinking disabled"; under it BM25
scores 64.47. With reasoning text in the answer — same retrieval, same C.1 prompt, same
judge — it scores 76.63 with completeness 80.66, against the published 74.7 and 80.4.
Answers go from 68 to 762 words with no `<think>` delimiters, so the reasoning is graded
as part of the answer. `READER_ENABLE_THINKING` makes that measurable without letting a
cell claim the stated configuration while running the other one; the default is unchanged.

## What was ruled out first

Retrieval is reproduced, and the check that shows it is not the combined score. Section
4.6 publishes four retrieval-only figures needing no reader and no judge — ours are
92.1 / 52.1 / 71.5 / 88.1 against 94.7 / 56.4 / 75.1 / 90.3, uniformly 2–4 points low and
nowhere near 10. Deleting every one of a question's own traps lifts document recall only
to 89.8 against the published 90.3. Judge choice is worth 3.5 points (63.57 under
`gpt-5.5` against 60.02 under the benchmark's documented `gpt-5.4` default, agreeing on
97.7% of alignment verdicts). Giving the reader whole parent documents instead of chunk
text is worth −0.81, citation stripping +0.5, and all nine `k1`/`b` combinations land
within 1.5 points of each other.

Per the plan, a miss stops the ladder rather than being worked around. It is logged as a
deviation in `docs/plans/2026_08_25_enterprise-rag-bench.md` in the AITaaS repository,
along with the methodology needed to reconstruct any of these numbers.

author: gtapps
body:
## Summary

`hermit-doctor` had no check touching the always-loaded memory surface. The motivating case is `MEMORY.md`: auto-memory loads only its first 200 lines or 25 KB and silently drops the rest, so a hermit's own memory-first dedup degrades with no signal at all. This adds a 28th check, `memory-size`, warning at 80% of that cap so there is room to consolidate before entries start vanishing.

The `CLAUDE.md` half is advisory. The 200-line figure is a docs *recommendation*, not a cutoff — Claude Code loads a `CLAUDE.md` in full up to 4 MiB and skips it only above that — so this leg warns and points at native `/doctor`'s trim flow rather than reimplementing grading or reporting a healthy install as broken.

Closes #832.

## Changes

- `scripts/doctor-check.ts` — new `checkMemorySize()`, registered in `runAllChecks()` between `model-pricing-known` and `context-scan`. Warns on either project CLAUDE file at >=200 lines, or `MEMORY.md` at >=160 lines or >=20 KB. Per-file `try/catch` so one unreadable file degrades to a warn instead of collapsing the check, matching the sibling checks' convention.
- `skills/hermit-doctor/SKILL.md` — check count 27 to 28, new table row, output cap 30 to 31 lines.
- `tests/contracts.test.ts`, `tests/hooks.contract.test.ts` — both pinned check-id lists updated (the second one lives inline in the hooks contract test).
- `tests/doctor-memory-size.test.ts` — new, 9 cases.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — one `### Added` bullet.

Two details worth a reviewer's eye:

- **Path key.** The auto-memory key replaces every non-alphanumeric character, not just `/`, matching Claude Code's real scheme (`lib/cc-compat.ts` `transcriptDirFor`). Verified against live `~/.claude/projects/` entries, which key this repo's worktrees as `...-claude-code-hermit--claude-worktrees-...`. A `/`-only key resolves to a directory that never exists, which would have made the `MEMORY.md` leg a permanent silent `ok` for any project under a dotted path — including every git worktree.
- **Line counting.** A trailing newline is not counted as a line, so the threshold means what `wc -l` means rather than firing one line early on every normally-saved file.

Both have regression tests; neither was visible to the original fixtures, which used dot-free temp paths and newline-free strings.

Note: `scripts/docker-preflight.ts:46` carries the same `/`-only key derivation. Pre-existing and left alone here.

## Test plan

- `cd plugins/claude-code-hermit && bun test` → 4642 pass, 0 fail
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` (repo root) → exit 0
- `bun scripts/doctor-check.ts <hermit-dir> | jq '.checks[] | select(.id=="memory-size")'` → emits the new check with live figures in `detail`

Reviewers: the `contracts.test.ts` count pin plus its three doc-sync assertions are the real gate — they fail if any doc or test surface for a new check id is missed.

author: yefch3
body:
收付队列改造**阶段 3 · 最后一刀**（#285 认差结清 → #287 收款结清 → 本 PR）。**依赖 #287 先合**——退款会让合同"复活"，收款结清是它的安全网。

## 界面

收款对账顶部一个切换：**核销收款 | 客户退款**。

- **核销收款**：原来的页面，一字未变（进账对合同）
- **客户退款**：出账对合同。挑合同时看的是"**已收**"（退的上限），按钮叫"对到合同"，确认叫"确认退款核销"。没有"与应收无关"档、没有补足差额列、没有合同号建议——这三样对退款都讲不通

登记流水的"出账"选项恢复（阶段 0 临时摘掉的）——它现在有去处了。

## 五个关键决定

**1. 退款落库为负数。** 六处"已收 = 求和"一个字不用改，负行自动把合同已收拉下来。界面上填的都是正数（"退多少"），符号只在写入那一行翻。

**2. 符号只在一个函数里翻**（`coveredOf`）。"这一行被说清了多少"统一翻成正数再进守门算式。调查预言的**无限核销洞**（负数一进 `adding > remaining` 比较，闸形同虚设）由此根本不会打开：输入必须为正，比较全在正数域。

**3. 退款队列只出明确归到"客户往来"的出账**，服务端强制盖掉任何档位的归属筛选。两个理由：待处理的出账绝大多数是付给供应商的钱；而"与应收无关"那档的归属列表配上出账方向，捞出来的**正好是全部供应商付款流水**。

**4. 退款框在已收里。** 一张合同退出去的不能超过它收到的净额——没收过钱的合同退 100 等于凭空造钱。历史退款已经是负行，连续退几笔也框得住。

**5. claimed 报量不报向**（Abs）。账本的 claimed_amount 语义是"被认下来了多少"，冲销重算后的负和直接报会撞账本的 `CHECK(claimed >= 0)`。

## 测试

- 新集成测试一条走全退款生命周期：收 10000 → 退 3000 → **合同已收 7000（求和自动算对）** → 退 9000 被框住 → 退 7000 + 认差结清 2000 → 冲销退款、钱回到已收 → 退款视图不混入其他归属
- 两条旧断言**改成新语义**而不是删掉：出账核销从"一律拒绝"变成"没收过钱的合同不能退"；出账认差从"一律拒绝"变成"归属未定的进不来"——每道旧闸都有新闸接班
- export / procurement / gateway 全绿（含 DB 集成），`vue-tsc` + 前端测试 + build 绿
- 无迁移、无 proto 破坏性改动（只加字段）；新 UI 是现有已验证布局的换词，未做浏览器截图验证

author: pavlo-flamingo
body:
## Проблема

Бэк на test-env уже отдаёт `ScriptExecutionStatus.QUEUED`, а в закоммиченном SDL его не было. Статус проваливался в `default:` обоих свитчей: в таблице выполнений рисовался серый тег с сырым `QUEUED`, а детальная страница не поллилась — `isRunning` сравнивался ровно с `RUNNING`, так что запуск в очереди висел мёртвым до ручного релоада.

## Причина

Маппинг статусов был написан свитчами с `default:`. Такой `default` молча принимает любое новое значение enum, поэтому расширение схемы не ломает сборку, а тихо меняет то, что видит пользователь.

## Что сделано

**Схема** перепулена с test-env: `ScriptExecutionStatus` +`QUEUED`, `NotificationSettingGroup` +`TICKET_CREATED`, новый тип `TicketCreatedByClientContext`.

**Свитчи → исчерпывающие таблицы.** `{ … } satisfies Record<Enum, T>` вместо `switch`: следующее значение enum роняет `tsc`, пока ему не пропишут ответ. Проверено — удаление ключа даёт `TS1360: Property 'QUEUED' is missing`.

- `execution-helpers.ts` — статусы выполнения и privilege level. У статуса появилось третье поле `inFlight`, чтобы решение «поллить или нет» тоже было колонкой таблицы, а не отдельным сравнением с `RUNNING`.
- `invoices-history.tsx` — статусы счетов. Тут `default` заодно склеивал `OPEN` (реально не оплачен) и `null` (легаси-строки), так что новый статус от Stripe показался бы клиенту как «Unpaid». `OPEN` прописан явно, фолбэк оставлен только под `null`.

**`src/lib/exhaustive-map.ts`** — `presentationFor()`, общий на оба домена. Нужен потому, что ключ на вызове — обычная строка: Relay типизирует enum как union + `"%future added value"`, а инлайн-фрагменты под `node(id:)` делают все поля опциональными. Каст живёт в одном месте и возвращает честный `V | undefined`.

**`notification-settings-modal.tsx`** — лейбл для `TICKET_CREATED`. Там уже был `Record<NotificationSettingGroup, string>`, и он честно уронил билд после пула схемы — ровно тот механизм, который вводит этот ПР.

Заодно бамп core 0.0.572 → 0.0.576 (лежал в рабочей копии).

## Оговорки

- Новый `TicketCreatedByClientContext` нигде не рендерится — карточка такого уведомления упадёт в дефолтную ветку `notifications-helpers.ts`. Отдельная задача.
- `severityToVariant` в `notifications-helpers.ts` — такой же свитч, но по локальному `KnownSeverity`, дублирующему схемный `NotificationSeverity`. Мигрировать имеет смысл вместе с выпиливанием дубля, здесь не трогал.
- Фильтры статусов не правились: в таблице выполнений они приходят из серверных фасетов, в фолбэке расписаний — из `Object.values(ScriptExecutionStatus)`. `QUEUED` появился там сам.

`npm run type-check` и Biome по изменённым файлам зелёные.

author: tuanhqv123
body:
`media/image/generate` now serves two models. A request picks with `"model"`; omitting it still gets
Krea 2, so every caller written before this keeps working unchanged.

```
"model": "comfyui:krea2"     Krea 2 Turbo   (also "comfyui:image_generation")
"model": "comfyui:z_image"   Z-Image Turbo
```

Z-Image returns as its own `z_image` bundle rather than a variant of `image_generation`: the two
share nothing — different UNet, different text encoder, different VAE — and together they are ~57 GB,
so a host should be able to pull one without the other.

### Design notes

`ENDPOINT_MODELS` is deliberately untouched. It stays the route's single default, and because the
new names are not in it, `is_builtin_model` is false for them and the route guard lets them through
to engine selection — the path `doggi:*` API media models already take. Making that map one-to-many
would break the "ONE definition" invariant its own comment protects.

`image_generation` is advertised under two names: `comfyui:image_generation` names the task and is
what the route resolves to, `comfyui:krea2` names the model and reads correctly beside
`comfyui:z_image`. Same bundle, same graph.

Node ids move into a table beside the workflow filename, because the two graphs number their own
nodes — Krea 2 uses 1..10, Z-Image carries "34:*" subgraph ids.

`steps` no longer defaults in the handler or the CLI: each workflow already carries the count its
model was distilled for, and writing one from our side overrides a graph that knows better. An
explicit `--steps` still wins. Same now applies to edit.

### Testing

2059 unit tests pass, including two new ones (prompt lands in the right node per model; an omitted
`steps` leaves the graph's own value).

Verified end to end on Apple Silicon against a real grid: `grid engine pull z_image` fetches all
three files, a grid serving both advertises `comfyui:image_generation`, `comfyui:krea2` and
`comfyui:z_image`, and the same prompt through `grid image -m …` produces visibly different images.
ComfyUI's history confirms the routing rather than the eye — `z_image_turbo_bf16` with
`res_multistep` for one, `krea2_turbo_bf16` with `euler` for the other.

### Known, out of scope

The Flutter app filters chat models with a lookup table of the three known `comfyui:*` names rather
than by prefix, so the two new names would show up in its chat picker. One line on the app side; not
changed here.

author: jiaqia
body:
## 摘要

develop **此前尚未合入 main**（自 0.4.0 起 15 个提交，含 #212/#213/#211/#208/#195/#198 及本次 #214）——本 PR 将 develop 累积一次性合入 main，为 v0.4.1 发布作准备。

**本次核心：#214 [smcp-computer] 支持 Computer 级 MCP 有限并发启动**

单个启动、批量启动与 Plugin 治理恢复共享同一 Computer 级并发控制器（`McpStartGate`：tokio Semaphore——无丢失唤醒、无 detached startup task；未配置保持既有串行行为，零行为差异）。

- 运行时策略：`Computer::with_mcp_start_concurrency(n)`（构造期；0→1 夹取；启动后调用即 panic，fail-closed）
- 批量 API：`start_mcp_clients_batch(&[BundleId]) -> Vec<(BundleId, ComputerResult<()>)>`——输入序逐项结果、单项失败不阻塞（协议 §4.6.5 partial-failure）、重复启动幂等（§5.13 不重解析）
- `start_all_mcp_clients` 委托批量：**行为变更**——不再「首错即停」，全量收敛后返回首个错误
- `reconcile_governance`：治理校验/input 注入/挂载全部完成后，统一批量启动（best-effort 降级语义不变）
- Input 解析全局串行锁：并发启动期间交互 resolver 一次只发一个请求（§5.11-13）
- shutdown 先关启动门：排队者即刻失败，在途由生命周期写锁收敛，无进程遗留（§4.7）
- CLI：`--concurrency N` + `start all` 逐项回执
- 测试：6 受控 MCP 矩阵（cap 5→第 6 等待）、未配置串行、失败/输入取消隔离、重复幂等、重叠批次 ≤ 上限、shutdown 排队/在途（15 新测试 + gate 单元 4）

## 协议

**无协议变更**（`runtime-contract.md` §1 进程模型边界；§8「SDK 可新增 public API 而无需改 wire schema」；§4.7/§4.6.5/§5.11-13/§6 约束全部实质遵守，隔离审查逐条验证）。

## 验证

```
cargo test --workspace --all-features   1840 passed / 0 failed（含 REL-01 v022 e2e 矩阵、全部非 ignored E2E）
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings   ✅
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc（--all-features）                 ✅
```（`--ignored` 9 项为既有环境型标记，不在发布判据内）

## 下游

- tfrobot-client#65（blocked by rust-sdk#214）：升级到本版后可接 SDK 统一批量 API（产品默认并发 5）。
- ⚠️ CHANGELOG 需标注 `start_all_mcp_clients` 语义变更。

body:
Closes #963.

## Problem

The canonical README, product-state ledger, and architecture document mixed several materially different states:

```text
implemented
wired in production
proven by a retained run
trusted authority
externally calibrated
```

That drift affected execution guidance, not only wording. The old surfaces preserved the July provider/lane topology as the product model, described generated adoption as a path directly to a required sole gate, and pointed agents at an authority front that had already landed.

Current `main` has immutable current-run revision joins, the pure/replayable TaskLedger, retained contradiction fixtures, and fast/late sensor lifecycle shadowing from #1263/#955. Live execution still belongs to the existing pools, proof broker, workers, leases, and budgets while #956 observes proof/worker execution and #957 reconciles the existing projections.

## Change

- Replace `docs/PRODUCT_STATE.md` with an evidence-backed capability matrix and live authority map.
- Define one target `FinalizedOutcome.ci_evidence_result` truth table (`pass`, `fail`, `not_proven`) and keep it distinct from current `gate-result` (`pass`, `finding`, `not_proven`) and legacy enforced `gate-conclusion` (`pass`, `fail`, `inconclusive`).
- Normalize every `Highest earned state` cell to exactly one of the five defined states.
- Recast `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` around one revision-bound evidence transaction in which models investigate, Rust authorizes proof, receipts update exact claims, editorial compilation prepares one senior review, and deterministic evidence sufficiency remains a separate decision.
- Replace the README's production-preset/sole-gate/provider-panel framing with the product hinge, current maturity, advisory-first adoption posture, and links to the canonical state and execution-order authorities.
- Remove the stale embedded Bun workflow and historical known-good pin while retaining the Bun preset, packet tree, sensors, inputs/outputs, posting contract, and development reference.
- Preserve the live setup-ci contract: `--print-pr` renders the four new files in the migration candidate; `--open-pr` opens that new-files-only PR and never mutates branch protection.

## Product decision

What distinguishes UB Review is not UB branding or a larger panel of model personas. It is **proof-in-the-loop review under deterministic authority**:

```text
exact revision
  -> repository facts and material claims
  -> relevant investigation
  <-> approved proof tasks and revision-bound receipts
  -> claim reconciliation
  -> one concise review
  + one eventual PASS / FAIL / NOT_PROVEN FinalizedOutcome
```

The reviewer gets a controlled lab without receiving shell or gate authority. Review and CI can share the expensive evidence transaction without collapsing publication, judgment, instrument coverage, and merge authority into one model verdict.

## Earned current state

- Revision identity is wired and verifier-joined across core current-run artifacts, but merge-result delivery is not authoritative: `revision.reviewed_commit` is the synthetic merge object while GitHub posting revalidates against `pull.head.sha`.
- Candidate-head delivery transactions are retained; synthetic merge-result delivery remains an explicit #923 gap.
- TaskLedger types, lifecycle/accounting, artifact verification, retained contradiction corpus, and fast/late sensor shadowing exist; TaskLedger is still shadow, not the live scheduler.
- `publication_result = posted` is presently a run-stage prepared-payload projection. Post success/error receipts remain separate and do not recompute `gate_outcome`; #959/#960 own confirmed/failed delivery finalization.
- Additive analysis/publication/gate truth can say `not_proven`; legacy `gate_outcome.conclusion` remains the enforced field until the later FinalizedOutcome switch earns authority.
- Calibration-v0 and economics surfaces are observations, not trusted learning or omission policy.

## Review and CI disposition

Accepted and repaired findings:

1. Current `gate-result` vocabulary was conflated with future FinalizedOutcome vocabulary.
2. The target CI result lacked one canonical semantic/serialized mapping.
3. The matrix state column used informal composites outside its own vocabulary.
4. Synthetic merge-result delivery authority was overstated.
5. Post-confirmed publication truth was described as current although `gate_outcome` is compiled before `post`.

The first hosted gate also found one live README contract deletion: `tests/cli_contract.rs` requires the setup-ci migration to remain described as **four new files**. That operational fact is restored without restoring the obsolete direct-to-sole-gate posture.

## Non-goals

- No runtime, schema, workflow, branch-protection, provider, or release change.
- No weakening of the intended integrated reviewer and sole-gate destination.
- No rewrite of historical design documents into current authority.

## Verification

Current candidate: `2d7fb99661e017de3045baa3f10305afccc78c9a`, one commit based exactly on `main@55e4fbab879b3a83c31f35cdc9f7e5cd99f0a6c8`.

```text
README.md
  blob bbbbfcd23bea4c54561bfba662f5682bbd5fad68

docs/PRODUCT_STATE.md
  blob 72366c5d17be0a4a0f7d1953a697503d326d7ae6

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
  blob 4610e4c94374696d4860ddc74387b6038c3a3220
```

Validated before push:

- balanced Markdown fences and stable cell counts for every Markdown table;
- no trailing whitespace and final newline on the local candidate files;
- complete, unique reference-link definitions in `PRODUCT_STATE.md`;
- every matrix state is one exact vocabulary value;
- target/current/legacy CI result contracts are separately named and mapped;
- candidate-head versus merge-result delivery authority is explicit;
- prepared versus confirmed publication is explicit;
- README retains the `four new files` and no-branch-protection setup-ci contract;
- GitHub compare reports one commit ahead, zero behind, and only the three intended files.

The repository's hosted exact-head gate and fresh exact-head review remain authoritative for merge readiness.

author: lhpaul
body:
## Summary

Refactor item for epic #1647. `reviewer_loop_path_is_non_shipped_artifact` classifies a finding as "small" purely by its path, and both `docs/*` and `*.md` are on the non-shipped list. In a repository whose product *is* its documentation, that makes every finding on the shipped artifact small by construction: two consecutive such rounds with no unresolved threads flip the aggregate to `clean` with reason `small_findings_terminal`, and the PR proceeds carrying live blocking findings.

This plan makes the classification depend on **what the finding is about**, not only where it lives — moving this repository's normative documents onto the shipped side, adding a path-independent contract-surface test, and requiring the counted rounds to have been on the current head.

Plan: `docs/specs/developments/20260828063000_1652-small-finding-terminal-policy/2_1652-small-finding-terminal-policy_implementation-plan.md`
Smoke test runbook: `docs/testing/workflow/1652-small-finding-terminal-policy.smoke-test.md`

**Estimated complexity**: M

## Evidence from this epic

The brief cites PR #1646. This epic's own PRs reproduced the failure at scale, and the plan's Verification Log records it:

**24 loop runs across PRs #1660, #1661 and #1662 exited `RESULT=clean` with reason `small_findings_terminal` while carrying live blocking findings** — 5 on #1660, 18 on #1661, 1 on #1662.

The findings the terminal rule cleared were not typographical. They included a deny-list where the contract claimed fail-closed, an empty check set treated as vacuously passing, an unvalidated bound that defeated its own cap, and a gate that read its dependency's stdout keys as environment variables and would have deferred on every invocation. Each was fixed only because the loop was re-run manually after the rule had already declared the PR clean.

I also confirmed the mechanism directly: sourcing the loop in harness mode and calling the classifier shows `docs/specs/developments/**`, `docs/workflow/**/protocols/*`, `REVIEW.md`, `docs/best-practices/*` and `docs/testing/workflow/*` all return non-shipped today, while `scripts/development-workflow/pr-review-loop.sh` returns shipped.

## The two directions this can fail

The change loosens nothing and tightens a stop condition, so both failure directions are real and both are proved:

- **Too permissive** — the original bug. Four of the six planted-violation proofs plant this direction: removing specs from the normative list, letting the path short-circuit the contract test, inverting the allow-list into a deny-list, and dropping the current-head comparison.
- **Too restrictive** — making every `docs/` path shipped would leave the loop unable to terminate on a genuinely cosmetic tail, which is a different defect rather than a fix. **P6 plants exactly that** and requires three scenarios to fail. The non-shipped list is narrowed, not deleted: `CHANGELOG.md`, fixtures, snapshots and other non-shipped `*.md` outside the normative set stay in the second tier, and scenario 13 replays the #1661 ledger shape with cosmetic bodies and requires the rule to still fire. `docs/project/**` is **not** among them — a later review round moved it into the first tier, because `AGENTS.md` designates those four documents as authoritative guidance agents read before writing code.

## Dependency

**Depends on #1648.** The brief's current-head requirement is the per-reviewer head evidence #1648 introduces. Recorded as a `Conflict` → `Resolved by sequencing` in the Cross-Cutting Operational Assumption Check and enforced by Implementation Order step 0, a hard stop. Plan PRs are independent; only the implementation is ordered.

## Document Quality Gate

- Spec/brief coverage: Checked - all three brief scope bullets map to implementation steps, scenarios and smoke steps. Bullet 1 (reclassify spec/plan contract findings as non-small) → the normative-document predicate and the contract-surface test, scenarios 1-7, Steps 1-3. Bullet 2 (require current-head verification) → the counter change and the terminal guard, scenarios 8-11, Step 4. Bullet 3 (regression tests using #1646-style history) → scenarios 12-13, the two replay ledgers, Steps 6-7, built from #1661's history since it is this epic's own richer instance of the same shape.
- Implementation-order consistency: Checked - the two new predicate names, the renamed aggregate, the counter's new argument, the one new stdout key and its four values, the two documentation targets, and the unchanged round-count variable agree across Summary, Layer-by-Layer, Testing Strategy, Seed Data, Documentation Updates, Risks, Code Samples and Implementation Order, and against the runbook's Steps 1-5 and 9.
- Verification support: Checked - every claim about current behavior cites a Verification Log command with its result at repo SHA `7998d43d`: that the classifier is path-only, that all five normative paths currently return non-shipped (verified by calling the predicate, not by reading it), that the terminal rule requires two rounds and zero threads, that nothing in the path checks the head of the counted rounds, that the round count is already validated with the convention this plan follows, and the 24-run incidence with its per-PR breakdown.
- Behavioral guarantees: Checked - each names its mechanism. "Can only make the loop stricter" → the contract test is an allow-list and an unrecognised body falls through to the path rule, pinned by scenario 4 and proof P3. "An unprovable head cannot extend a run" → absent, empty and placeholder heads each end the consecutive run, pinned by scenario 9 and proof P5. "The mechanism still terminates" → the narrowed non-shipped list plus scenarios 3, 6, 13 and proof P6. "Backward compatible with old ledgers" → an entry without head data ends the run rather than counting, pinned by scenario 14.
- Complex workflow decision-gate matrix: Checked - this plan modifies a decision gate. **Inputs**: each finding's path, each finding's body text, the recorded head of every candidate ledger round, and `loop_head_sha`. **Outcomes**: the terminal rule fires, or it does not with exactly one of four reasons (`shipped_path`, `contract_surface`, `stale_head`, `head_unknown`). **Required next actions**: firing sets `aggregate_result=clean` with `aggregate_reason=small_findings_terminal` as today; not firing leaves the aggregate as `needs_fixes` and reports the cause in `SMALL_FINDINGS_BLOCKED_BY` and in the summary line. **Mirror surfaces**: Protocol 93, the added `REVIEW.md` line, the `--help` block, and the summary's small-findings line — runbook Step 9 reads all three documentation surfaces against each other and against Steps 1-5. **Examples**: the illustrative predicates are part of the changed surface and are asserted by Steps 1-3.
- Parser/API/concurrency checklist: Checked for parser risk — the contract-surface test scans externally-supplied finding text, and the addendum enumerates ten edge cases including the two substring negatives (`delegates`/`gate`, `microscope`/`scope`), case variants, code-fence and URL containment, empty and whitespace-only bodies, a quoted negation, and a last-line match, each mapped to a unit case with its required result. API-surface: the one new stdout key, its four values and its empty case are enumerated and required in `--help`. Concurrency: Not applicable — both predicates are pure functions of their arguments and the counting change reads a ledger the sequential loop already reads at the same point; rationale recorded in the plan.
- CHANGELOG literal format: Checked - Implementation Order step 12 gives the fragment path `changelog.d/1652.changed.small-finding-terminal-policy.md` and the literal body in the project's `**Bold Title** (#N):` bullet format.
- Not-applicable rationale: Checked - the Backend and Frontend layers, the Infrastructure section, the concurrency addendum, and the `AGENTS.md` documentation entry each carry a short rationale.

Closes #1652

author: ccoventry
body:
The probe that produced every measurement in the #65 write-up. **Targets `docs/obs-alternate-capture` (PR #72), not `dev`**, since it builds on that document — retarget if you'd rather it went straight to `dev`.

Adds `native/src/bin/probe_obs.rs` in the same throwaway-shaped style as `probe_decals`, plus `tungstenite` / `sha2` / `base64` (blocking client, reasoning recorded in the manifest comment).

## Three modes

**`probe_obs log <qconsole.log>`** — tails the engine's console log during a live capture and timestamps every `[dod-tools]` marker's arrival against its demo tick. This produced the 21–40 ms latency result across 17 blocks that cleared the last gate on the design, and the demo-time-vs-wall-clock numbers behind the `AUDIO_SYNC` trigger decision.

**`probe_obs obs`** — connects to obs-websocket v5, dumps `availableRequests` (settling `SetRecordDirectory` / `SplitRecordFile` without version archaeology), reports the active recording mode and container, and dumps scenes/sources/`inputKind`s — the read-only data a scene picker in the app would be built from. With `--record` it times the gap to `RecordStateChanged: STARTED`, which is when frames actually begin.

**`probe_obs routing` / `probe_obs ffmpegmode`** — the only parts that write to OBS settings, both backing up first and restoring on every path out. These established that `SetRecordDirectory` steers the standard output but **not** `AdvOut/FFFilePath`, so Custom Output (FFmpeg) and per-block drive routing don't coexist without a profile write.

## Notes for review

- The v5 handshake is pinned by a test against **OpenSSL**, not against a published vector. A wrong handshake fails as a silent "wrong password", so it wants pinning by an implementation that isn't this one — provenance is spelled out in the test so nobody later "fixes" it against a mismatched example.
- Two guards exist because they were earned: `--record` warns when `hl.exe` isn't running (a Game Capture source pointed at a dead process records black into an otherwise-valid file, which cost two rounds of analysis and looked exactly like a hook collision), and the handshake failure path distinguishes close code 4009 from everything else.
- Burst detection is tick-aware rather than time-aware — the first version flagged every block, because commands scheduled one tick apart legitimately arrive ~21 ms apart.

5 tests, `cargo check --workspace` clean.

author: go-to-k
body:
Closes #2369

## What

Widens `gated-command-preamble-gate.sh`'s side-effecting-preamble set with **interpreter one-liners**: `python3 -c` / `node -e` / `perl -e` / `ruby -e`, their clustered spellings (`perl -pi -e`, `node -pe`), and the stdin-script form (`python3 - <<'EOF'`). The code argument is a quoted span (or heredoc body) `strip_noncommand_spans` removes, so the gate cannot see whether it writes — and the measured incident (four preamble-discard firings in one 2026-08-28 run, per the issue) was exactly a `python3 -c` that rewrote the gated command's own body file, was discarded by a gate refusal, and cost a mis-diagnosis round when the retry re-presented the same offending content. Twice.

Treated as an OPAQUE write, conservatively — the family's stated trade is that dropping too little leaves a loud, fixable false positive while the current state was the silent direction. Two anchors, deliberately different: the eval-flag arm allows mid-segment position (`time python3 -c ...`); the bare-`-` stdin arm is segment-START only, because a lone `-` after a word is a common ordinary argument (`grep python3 - <file>`) and the loose anchor would read an interpreter NAME in argument position as an invocation.

## Position-matched false-refusal measurement

The repo's `false-refusal-survey.sh` probes verb constants against corpus texts in ARGUMENT position — the wrong position for this change (the verify.md go-to-k/cdkd#2333 lesson), so its zero would be no evidence. The arm that probes the RIGHT position: a sweep of every command shape this repo's skills / rules / CLAUDE.md prescribe found **ZERO** shapes combining an interpreter one-liner with a gated verb in one call — the false-refusal surface is ad-hoc agent behavior only, and the remediation the refusal prints (split the calls) is the flow's own standing rule. Controls pin the boundaries: a QUOTED mention in a commit message, an interpreter name in argument position, an interpreter AFTER the gated command, and an interpreter with no gated verb all pass.

## Won't-do (recorded here, per the issue's own weighing)

- **`gh issue create` as a gated verb stays OUT** — a documented trade two other designs depend on (`issue-dup-check-gate`'s heredoc fallback and `gh-body-english-gate`'s known-limit note both require the one-call `heredoc -> file -> --body-file` shape staying legal for `gh issue create`). The issue's firing (a) added cost-side evidence, which the issue records; reversing the trade would have to retire the dup-check fallback in the same PR and is a separate decision.
- **Script-file invocations (`python3 script.py`) stay unmatched** — a filename is indistinguishable from any other argument; the eval-flag and stdin forms are the incident spellings. Stated as a known limit in the hook header.

## Verification

- Suite 47 → 60 cases (6 BLOCK + 7 pass controls), green under bash 5.x AND macOS system bash 3.2 (60/60 both).
- Discrimination probe (re-measured on the final 60-case suite): against the pre-change hook (executable `git show origin/main:` copy), EXACTLY the six interpreter BLOCK cases fail (`Pass: 54 Fail: 6`) while every control passes there.
- Direct payload drives of the issue's two gap payloads: rc=0 → rc=2; the issue's covered controls stay rc=2, and five pass-side probes stay rc=0.
- `.claude/rules/hooks.md` entry updated (new kind, the zero-prescribed-shapes measurement, the script-file known limit, case count).

## Review round (1 pr-code-reviewer)

No blockers; all four findings applied in the second commit. Minor: the char-class subtlety (a long option's second dash must be rejected) had no pass-polarity fence — `node --version` / `node --check` / `python3 -m pytest` pass cases added, so a future "simplification" of the cluster class cannot silently start refusing them. Minor: `node --eval='code'` slipped both arms (Node accepts =-joined long options) — `=` added to the terminator class plus a BLOCK case. Minor: two stdin evasions (`echo 'code' | python3` and `python3 <script.py`) recorded as known limits in the header rather than chased — matching a bare-interpreter segment would refuse ordinary invocations. Nit: the `perl -c script.pl` over-match (a syntax check, refused anyway) is now a fenced documented-false-positive case rather than an implied trade. The reviewer independently reproduced the ZERO-prescribed-shapes measurement and verified the wrapper-stripped `time python3 - <<EOF` shape IS caught.

author: yschimke
body:
Three findings from the review on #4542, all on the metadata that tells a sheet how much of a `@CaptureGutter` canvas to crop. Each was verified still open on `main` before fixing.

## The underscore spellings read as LTR

`rendersRightToLeft` handed the tag straight to `Intl.Locale`, which throws on `ar_XB` / `ar_EG` — spellings a catalog actually carries, because it spells a locale the way the annotation did. The `catch` read the throw as LTR, so an asymmetric gutter was published with its left and right edges swapped. The separator is now normalised first, the way `Pseudolocale.fromTag` and `LocaleDirection.isRtl` already do on the renderer side.

## `pickVariantId` never scored the locale

`variantIdentity` has carried `locale` since gutters started publishing physical edges, but nothing compared it. One function with a separate LTR and RTL `@Preview` resolved *both* images to whichever annotation the bundle listed first — the same class of bug as #2883, and a wrong crop rather than a missing one. Now scored in the same two tiers as theme and font scale (constraint when the image names a locale, preference otherwise), compared normalised so `ar_XB` and `ar-XB` rank as the same annotation.

## No density is not 1x

`captureGutterPx` fell back to `scale = 1` when a manifest stated no density. No render uses 1x: the Android gutter path falls back to `params.density ?: 2.0f`, and the ordinary render spec to `DeviceDimensions.DEFAULT_DENSITY` (2.625f). So the published margin was a third to a half of the real one, and a consumer cannot tell a wrong crop from a right one — it just draws the component at the wrong size, which is the complaint the gutter exists to answer.

Guessing is not available either: the two backends fall back differently and this publisher does not reliably know which produced the PNG. It now declines, leaving the preview with the behaviour it had before gutters existed — the whole canvas, un-cropped — rather than a crop that is confidently off by 2x. Both call sites were already null-safe.

This replaces the test that pinned the old behaviour as "not inventing" a density; 1x *is* an invention, so the test encoded the bug.

## Test plan

- `node --test scripts/design-artifacts/bridge-live-preview-ids.test.mjs` — 39 pass. New: `separate LTR and RTL annotations resolve to their own preview, not the first listed`.
- `node --test scripts/design-artifacts/catalog-preview-declarations.test.mjs` — 16 pass. New: `publishes no gutter when a manifest states no density`, `publishes the gutter as soon as a density is stated`, `an underscore-separated RTL locale still swaps the physical edges` (covers `ar-XB`, `ar_XB`, `ar_EG`, `AR_eg`, and the LTR `en_XA` control).
- Each new test confirmed non-vacuous by reverting its fix and watching it go red.
- Dependent suites green: `tag-index.test.mjs` (23), `render-index-html.test.mjs` (10).

No visual surface changes — this is publisher metadata, and the correctness it restores shows up as a sheet cropping the right margin rather than as a different render.

author: withoz
body:
Kayac 의 커서 미니 그리드를 우리 엔진에 옮겼습니다. 그리기 도구가 첫 점을
기다리는 동안, 다음 클릭이 **어느 평면에 떨어지는지** 커서 아래에 작은 붉은
격자 원반으로 보여줍니다. 스펙표 그대로 — 반지름 48 px, 가장자리까지 4칸,
선 반폭 0.5 px.

### 크기는 화면 값이지 월드 값이 아닙니다

호출할 때마다 커서에서 월드 반지름을 다시 계산합니다. 그것이 어떤 줌에서도
같은 크기로 보이게 하는 이유입니다 — 월드 반지름을 고정하면 줌아웃에서
사라지고 줌인에서 모델을 삼킵니다. Kayac 자신의 주석이 기록한 버그입니다.

### ⚠ 직교 분기는 Kayac 에 없는 것입니다

Kayac 주석: *"still perspective projection — true ortho is a separate polish"*.
그래서 그쪽 공식은 `fov_y` 하나뿐입니다. 우리 축 뷰(top / front / right …)는
**실제로 `OrthographicCamera`** 로 돌고, 거기서는 배율이 깊이와 무관합니다.
깊이를 넣으면 화면에서 아무것도 안 변했는데 카메라를 뒤로 뺄수록 원반이
커집니다. 그래서 직교에서는 절두체 높이로 대신 스케일합니다. E2E 한 건이
`top` 으로 전환해 원반이 여전히 유한하고 0 이 아님을 단언합니다.

### 원반이지 사각형이 아닙니다

테두리 링도 축선도 없습니다 — 중심은 커서가 이미 표시하니까. 각 선을
`±√(R² − off²)` 로 원에 잘라내서 격자가 원반으로 읽힙니다. `|offset| == R`
인 두 선은 현(chord) 길이가 0 이라 빠지고, E2E 의 14 세그먼트가 거기서
나옵니다.

### `EdgeFaceStyling` 가드가 제 일을 했습니다

새 `LineMaterial` 을 잡아내고 **"여기 와서 무슨 역할인지 말하라"** 고
막았습니다. 축선처럼 `scene` 에 붙고, 뷰포트가 스스로 소유·해제하고, 두께가
`MiniGridSettings` 에서 오지 엣지 스타일 픽커에서 오지 않는 커서 장식입니다.
그래서 픽커 밖에 두고, 가드에는 숫자만이 아니라 **그 이유**를 적었습니다.

### 검증

| | |
|---|---|
| 기하 단위 | `miniGridGeometry.test.ts` **10/10** |
