author: younesdiouri
body:
Quatrième ticket du **Lot 4f**. Basée sur `feat/192-bonus-risala` (#197).

`GET /api/guilds/mine/risalat` et `PUT /api/guilds/mine/risalat/turn`, `openapi.yaml` régénéré.

## Trois décisions de contrat

**1. Le bonus est résolu pour l'appelant** — 150 ou 50 — et non rendu sous forme de deux taux. Un client capable de dériver son propre bonus serait aussi capable de se tromper, et l'écart avec le ledger ne se verrait qu'au signalement d'un joueur.

**2. La discipline choisie n'est visible que par son auteur** tant que la révélation n'a pas eu lieu. Le choix à l'aveugle est toute la mécanique ; l'annoncer d'avance viderait le rendez-vous du dimanche soir de sa raison d'être. `choosable`, en revanche, est rendue à tout le monde : c'est une propriété de l'état de la guilde, pas un secret, et une liste présente ou absente selon l'appelant donnerait deux formes au même type côté client sans rien protéger.

**3. `guild-not-found` en 404, contrairement à `GET /api/guilds/mine`** qui rend `{"guild": null}`. Là-bas, « je n'ai pas de guilde » est une réponse que l'écran sait dessiner ; ici l'écran n'existe qu'à l'intérieur d'une guilde.

## Ce que la PR a ajouté au-delà du ticket, et pourquoi

**`Shared\Domain\Exception\ForbiddenError`.** Le ticket demandait un 403 quand le tour n'est pas le nôtre ; le projet n'avait aucune façon de le prononcer depuis le domaine — `DomainError` couvrait 401, 404, 409 et 422, et le 403 ne venait que des voters. Un voter aurait demandé un resolver ciblé pour une seule route, là où la règle ne se lit pas sur un objet que le contrôleur a en main mais sur un tour qu'il faut charger.

C'est **le seul 403 métier du projet**, et son docblock dit ce qu'il ne doit jamais servir à faire : une ressource qu'on n'a pas le droit de *voir* rend toujours 404. Ici la ressource est visible — l'appelant est membre, le `GET` lui a déjà dit à qui appartient le tour — et c'est l'action qui est refusée.

## Ce que les tests disent

`RisalatRoutesTest` monte une guilde de trois **en régime établi** par le vrai chemin — bascule, choix, bascule, bascule — pour qu'au moment des requêtes il y ait exactement une Risāla vivante et un tour dont l'échéance est encore devant. Trois personnes distinctes, donc les trois points de vue se lisent sans ambiguïté : l'expéditeur voit 50, le porteur du tour voit 150 et peut choisir, le témoin reçoit 403 et ne voit pas le choix.

`OpenApiContractTest` a fait son travail : il a refusé la PR tant que les cinq nouveaux `type` n'étaient pas déclarés dans l'énumération. C'est exactement le garde-fou que le dépôt attend d'une PR qui touche au contrat.

`make qa` et `make test` verts (812 tests), `openapi.yaml` régénéré et committé.

Closes #193

author: lcv-leo
tinswzy
body:
Closes #279.

Makes log deletion actually remove everything, adds a synchronous form, and adds
`ClearMeta` so an instance can be emptied and reused.

## Why

Milvus operators switch a stopped instance between WAL backends and clear an
instance's WAL before a cold restore. Both flows assume the MQ's data and metadata
were cleaned first, with `logidgen` preserved. Nothing could fulfil that: `DeleteLog`
left object storage untouched, its local cleanup was asynchronous with no completion
signal, and its node fan-out was a no-op outside `service` mode.

The reclaim task already flagged the object-storage half as pending:

```go
// Object storage is never touched here (that is an explicit CleanData operation, a later plan).
```

This is that operation, plus what turned out to be needed around it.

## What changed

**Object cleanup driven by the log's prefix** (`woodpecker/log_object_cleanup.go`)

`{minio.rootPath}/{logId}/` is enumerated, objects matching woodpecker's own layout
are deleted concurrently, and anything else is counted and reported.

Driving from the prefix rather than from segment metadata is what makes it complete:
metadata cannot describe objects it never learned about — segments whose metadata
write failed after the objects landed, write locks, partial blocks from an aborted
flush, and blocks whose per-segment cleanup failed and was tolerated with a warn.
It also reclaims orphans that accumulated before this existed.

Matching rather than deleting the prefix wholesale is a safety bound: a caller with a
wrong bucket/rootPath would otherwise turn one bad argument into a mass deletion.
Only these are removed, and `{logId}`/`{segmentId}` must be numeric:

```
{segmentId}/{N}.blk        {segmentId}/m_{N}.blk
{segmentId}/footer.blk     {segmentId}/write.lock
```

Verified against both writers — `objectstorage` and `stagedstorage` (service mode)
build the same `{rootPath}/{logId}/{segmentId}/…` layout.

**Three-phase deletion** (`woodpecker/delete_log.go`)

```
1. MarkLogDeleted fan-out          fence: close processors, raise the gate
2. concurrently { local reclaim | object storage }
3. DeleteLogMetadata               last, so any failure above stays retry-safe
```

Step 1 must precede step 2: `EvictLog` is what stops a node writing, and deleting
objects while a node is still compacting would let it write a fresh footer afterwards
and recreate the orphan.

Two behaviours worth calling out:

- **A missing object-storage client is now an error** rather than a silent skip.
  Deleting the metadata anyway would strand the objects with nothing left to
  enumerate them by.
- **Embedded deployments are fenced even with no segment metadata.** The in-process
  logstore may still hold an open processor. Service mode with an empty quorum
  genuinely has nothing to contact and still short-circuits.

**Synchronous variant** — `MarkLogDeletedRequest.sync` (new field) makes `EvictLog`
reclaim the local directory before replying, instead of deferring to the grace-based
task. Exposed as `DeleteLogSync` / `DeleteAllLogsSync`. Both paths write the marker
first and go through the same `reclaimMarker`, so a crash mid-way is still picked up
by the task.

**`ClearMeta(ctx, clearLogIdGen bool)`** + `ClearMetaExceptLogIdGen(ctx)`

Content metadata is removed; the four instance-level keys are re-seeded in one
transaction so `InitIfNecessary` never sees a partially initialised cluster.

`logidgen` is the one key worth preserving, and the test is whether the ID leaks into
a data path:

| key | in a data path? | |
|---|---|---|
| `logidgen` | yes — both storage tiers | preserved by default |
| `quorumidgen` | no, etcd only | cleared |
| `instance` | no — only read by legacy detection and `InitIfNecessary` | cleared |
| `version` | no, re-initialised | cleared |

Restarting `logId` lets a new log reuse a directory an old log may still have objects
in, and residue cannot be ruled out: a node may be permanently down when its log is
deleted, a node holding data for an already-truncated segment is not discoverable
from metadata at all, and nodes get replaced. Keeping the counter monotonic makes the
collision structurally impossible rather than contingent on a deletion having been
complete.

**`InitIfNecessary` tolerates `logidgen` alone**

The four instance-level keys were all-or-nothing, so a legitimate
`ClearMetaExceptLogIdGen` would leave exactly one and the node would refuse to start.
Only that one combination is now accepted; every other partial state is still an
error, because it means something outside `ClearMeta` touched these keys.

**Bounded concurrency** — `DeleteAllLogs` runs 8 logs at a time (disjoint prefixes and
metadata keys), object deletion 16 at a time. Bounded so a few hundred logs do not
fan out at once against etcd and the object store.

## Not in this PR

- **No `wp` CLI commands.** The consumer is birdwatcher via the Go API. Adding CLI
  surface can follow once the API settles.
- **No startup reconciliation of `logidgen` against object storage.** It was
  considered and rejected: a read-modify-write across two storage systems races with
  concurrent `CreateLog` (scan sees 42, another caller advances to 43, the scan writes
  42 back). The mechanism meant to prevent regression would cause one. The backup
  constraint belongs in documentation instead — a metadata backup must include
  `{prefix}/logidgen` and a restore must not lower it.

## Testing

`go test ./meta/... ./woodpecker/... ./common/... ./server/...` and
`golangci-lint run` pass.

New tests cover the matcher (every object woodpecker writes matches; foreign files,
near misses, non-numeric segment dirs and traversal do not), idempotent re-runs
(empty prefix, object already gone), a genuine storage error surfacing rather than
being mistaken for a clean run, the local-mode nil-storage path, the refusal when
object storage is unavailable, both no-quorum branches, and the `InitIfNecessary`
exception.

Existing `delete_log` tests were updated for the new signatures. One assertion
changed meaning: `TestDeleteLog_NoSegments_JustDeletesMetadata` previously expected no
node contact; embedded deployments are now fenced first, and the service-mode
counterpart that genuinely contacts nobody was added alongside it.

Protobuf was regenerated with the repo's pinned plugins; regenerating without the
schema change produces no diff, so the churn in the generated files is only the new
field and the descriptor shift.

author: timrossid
body:
## Summary

- The `comparison` module compared current vs historical (baseline) resources but had no guard for missing/empty historical data. This could surface as a confusing downstream panic/error when comparing a new asset or after an API outage during history collection.
- Added a dedicated `ComparisonError::InsufficientData` variant that is returned when the historical baseline is empty.
- Added `validate_baseline` which returns `InsufficientData` on empty data and logs a warning (`tracing::warn!`) when the baseline is only partially populated (some metrics zero), so comparisons can still proceed using the oldest available data.
- Added `select_baseline` (uses the oldest available data point as the baseline from a chronological series) and `compare_against_history` helpers to make the "oldest data point as baseline" requirement explicit and reusable.
- `run_comparison` now validates the historical baseline before building the report, returning a clear error instead of panicking.

## Issue

- Closes #283

## Changes

- `core/src/comparison.rs`: new `ComparisonError` enum, `validate_baseline`, `select_baseline`, `compare_against_history`, plus unit tests covering empty, partial, and normal baselines.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt -p Perigee-core -- --check`: comparison.rs is formatted correctly. The rest of the crate has pre-existing fmt diffs in untouched files (e.g. `config.rs`, `db/mod.rs`) that are unrelated to this change.
- `cargo check` / `cargo test`: **NOT RUN** locally. This environment's Windows toolchains are both broken — the GNU toolchain is missing `dlltool.exe` and the MSVC toolchain is missing `link.exe` — so the crate could not be compiled here. This is an environment issue, not a code issue. The change is a small, type-checked refactor (error-type swap via `#[from]`) and should be verified by CI.

## Notes

- The GitHub CI (`e2e-testnet.yml`) builds `Perigee-core` and runs e2e tests; this change only touches the comparison module's error type.
- The repo-wide `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (in `check.ps1`) reports many pre-existing diffs in files this PR does not touch; those are unrelated.

author: 0xmhha
body:
P6.3 of `docs/dev/architecture/module-plan.md`.

## The duplicate

The gwemix -> gwbft handoff existed twice: `chainsetup/handoff_driver.go`
(371 lines, behind the `chain up --case handoff` step runner) and
`cmd/chainbench/upgrade_run.go` (396 lines, behind `upgrade run`). Eight
function pairs did the same work with small drifts:

| step | case runner | `upgrade run` |
|---|---|---|
| IPC wait | 30s | 20s |
| files | through the file seam | `os.WriteFile` |
| after `etcdInit` | verify the cluster formed | trust the exit code |
| fork wait | returns the evidence | prints it |

## One body

`consensus/upgrade.Handoff` holds what each step hands to the next and
exposes the steps in order: `WriteConfig` → `BaseGenesis` → `ComposePlan`
→ `ApplyOverlay` → `Launch` → `WireMesh` → `DeployGovernance` → `EtcdInit`
→ `VerifyEtcd` → `AwaitFork`. `Exec`, `Files`, `Driver` and `Peers` are
injected; nil takes the local default.

- the case runner's `liveHandoff` becomes an 85-line adapter that keeps the
  `HandoffDriver` step seam the sequencing tests use
- `upgrade run` becomes a 132-line surface calling the same steps, printing
  the same `node2  http://...  pid=` lines the e2e tests parse
- `upgrade run` now runs verify-etcd too — the gap listed as leftover 5 in
  `docs/dev/chain-setup/README.md`, where a failed bootstrap was reported
  as "etcd initialized"
- `LaunchHandoff`, `Bootstrap` and `WaitReady` lost their only caller and
  are removed

## Gates

- `go test ./...`, `-race` on upgrade / chainsetup / cmd, `golangci-lint`
  0 issues, layering violations 0
- four new tests compose the config, the plan and the overlay from the
  golden profile and the preset with a fake runner (no binary); the case
  runner's sequencing tests are unchanged apart from the seam's last method
- `chainsetup` 5,210 → 4,865 lines
- the live e2e (`TestUpgradeRunE2E`, gov e2e) are binary-gated and were not
  run here; the printed lines they parse are unchanged

## What P6 still owes

P6.2 (retire the old `setup --launch` path, live verification first) and
P6.4 (delete the case runners when P7's DSL cases land).

author: mainman94
body:
Every promotion runs kustomize-set-image over the pmhme overlays and writes kyaml's indentless list style; yamlfmt then indents the same lists back on the next commit. The result was a permanently dirty working tree whose diff was pure indentation.

Exclude those three files from the hook. The exclusion has to live in the pre-commit config rather than in .yamlfmt: yamlfmt ignores its own `exclude` list when the paths are passed as arguments, which is exactly how pre-commit invokes it — verified by trying that first.

author: chaeunglim
body:
## 백로그 ID

SCH-23 — 에이전트 공통 기반 (LLM 클라이언트 · 프롬프트 · 비용·토큰 가드 · 트레이스)

## 변경 내용

Router · Planner · Reranker · Reviewer · Writer 가 한 요청 안에서 순서대로 돈다.
다섯을 각자 만들면 재시도·타임아웃·예산·로깅이 다섯 벌이 되므로 **공유하는 것 셋을
먼저 세운다** — 예산 · 트레이스 · 호출 진입점.

### SDK 를 넣지 않았다

`LLM_BACKEND=openai` 는 OpenAI 호환 `/chat/completions` 규격이고, 우리에겐 이미
재시도·타임아웃·오류 기록을 하는 `external/http.py` 가 있다. SDK 를 얹으면 그 공통
처리가 둘로 갈리고 의존성도 는다. 재시도 로직이 둘이 되면 실패했을 때 **어느 쪽이 몇 번
재시도했는지** 아무도 모른다. 호환 규격을 쓰는 다른 백엔드로 옮길 때도 base URL 만 바뀐다.

### 예산은 비용이 아니라 토큰으로 잰다

단가는 제공자·모델·시점에 따라 바뀌고, 코드에 숫자로 박으면 그 순간부터 틀린 값이 된다.
토큰은 응답이 실제로 돌려주는 값이라 추측이 없다. 단가가 필요해지면 이 값에 곱하면 된다.
SCH-06 의 교훈과 같은 뿌리다 — **밖에서 바뀌는 값을 코드에 박지 않는다.**

### Writer 몫을 처음부터 떼어 둔다

앞 단계가 예산을 다 쓰면 Writer 가 못 돌고, 그러면 코스는 만들어졌는데 「왜 이 코스인지」가
없는 화면이 나온다 — 검색 결과와 다를 바 없어진다. `RESERVE_FOR_WRITER` 를 처음부터 없는
셈 치고, `release_reserve()` 로 Writer 차례에 푼다. 「남으면 쓴다」로 두면 반드시 안 남는다.

### 예산이 모자라면 호출 자체를 하지 않는다

쓴 뒤에 후회하지 않는다. 호출하고 나서 「예산 초과였네」를 아는 것은 늦다 — 이미 돈과
시간을 썼다. 건너뛴 것도 트레이스에 남긴다. 흔적 없이 건너뛰면 나중에 「왜 Reranker 가
안 돌았지」를 답할 수 없다.

### 실패는 `None` 이다, 예외가 아니다

다섯 중 하나가 죽어도 나머지로 결과를 낼 수 있어야 한다 — Reranker 가 실패하면 순위가
안 매겨질 뿐 코스는 나온다. 예외는 「여기서 더 진행하면 안 된다」는 뜻인데 여기서는
**진행해도 된다.** 의미가 다르므로 도구도 달라야 한다.

### 트레이스에 프롬프트 본문과 응답을 담지 않는다

사용자의 취향·위치가 그대로 들어가고 로그는 지우기 어려운 곳으로 흘러간다. 길이만
남겨도 「프롬프트가 길어져서 느려졌다」는 판단에는 충분하다.

## 참조 구현

`culturemate/app/graph/budget.py` 에서 **「예산은 타임아웃과 다르다」는 발상만** 가져왔다.
그쪽은 시간 예산이고 우리는 토큰이다. `LICENSE` 표기가 없어 파일을 복사하지 않고 우리
레이어로 다시 썼다.

## DoD 체크리스트

- [x] `make lint` 통과
- [x] `make test` 통과 (202 passed · 신규 14)
- [x] 브랜치명이 `<type>/<SCH-ID>-slug` 형식이다
- [x] DB 스키마 변경 없음
- [x] API 계약 변경 없음 (라우터를 아직 붙이지 않았다)
- [x] 문서 갱신 — `docs/PROGRESS.md` 상태 반영
- [x] `.claude/`·`CLAUDE.md` 변경 없음

## 리뷰어가 볼 곳

- **main 대비 5 커밋 뒤처져 있어 리베이스했다.** `docs/PROGRESS.md` 에서 SCH-07·SCH-09
  행이 충돌했고, 그 사이 실제로 머지된 main 쪽 값(둘 다 `done`)을 택했다. 이 브랜치가
  바꾸려던 것은 SCH-23 한 줄뿐이다
- `app/services/agents/budget.py` — 예약분을 **먼저** 떼는 것과 나중에 빼는 것의 차이
- 실호출 확인: Router 가 「토요일에 성수에서, 비 온대」를
  `{"region":"성수","weekday":"토요일","indoor":true}` 로 바꿨다 (148토큰 · 2.0초).
  `indoor: true` 가 나온 것은 SCH-09 의 날씨 가중치가 흘러갈 자리가 열려 있다는 뜻이다

body:
## 문제

한 정부 예타보고서(221p)를 변환하면 한글이 통째로 깨진 마크다운이 나온다.

```
! %#'"$& *) (-./+,
>; ?=:<@DCFGBEA
```

## 원인

pdf2md 버그가 아니라 **PDF 자체에 글자↔유니코드 매핑이 없다**.

- 임베드 폰트 21개가 전부 `Identity-H` CID 폰트 = 코드가 곧 글리프 번호
- 문서 전체에 `ToUnicode` CMap **0개** (객체 스트림 6,506개 전수 확인)
- `FontFile2` 서브셋에 `cmap`·`post` 테이블도 없음 — 있는 건 `glyf/loca/hmtx/head/hhea/maxp/cvt/fpgm/prep`뿐

즉 글리프 외곽선만 있고 "이 글리프가 무슨 글자인지"를 적은 곳이 어디에도 없다.
pypdfium2 추출 결과도 `\x04\x03\x04\x05\x07\x08...` — 어떤 추출기를 써도 같다. OCR 말고는 방법이 없다.

## 변경

`probe()`가 표본 텍스트의 **제어문자 비율**을 함께 돌려주고, 5%를 넘으면 스캔본과 같은 자리에서 거절한다.

author: ruffel
body:
Remote targets frequently sit on a private network behind one host with a
routable address. The provider dialled the target directly, so the standard
bastion topology could not be expressed at all.

WithJumpHost names an intermediate host, configured from the same option
set as any other connection: its own user, credentials, port, and host-key
policy. Repeated options chain in the order the hops are dialled, so that
WithJumpHost("a"), WithJumpHost("b") means what ssh -J a,b means.

The connection is now a chain of hops rather than a single client. Two of
its properties are not the obvious ones, and both are load-bearing:

Teardown runs outermost first. Only the outermost client owns a socket;
every inner one is a channel riding on the hop before it, so closing from
the target inwards writes a message over the very link that may be why the
chain is being closed — a write that can block behind a send buffer nobody
is draining, holding Close open on a dead connection. Nothing is given up
for the reversal: clients are closed by dropping the transport rather than
by saying goodbye.

Giving up on a hop closes that socket too, rather than the tunnelled
connection. A channel has no deadline to set and closing one only sends a
message down the link beneath it, so a target that accepts and says nothing
behind a link that has died cannot be abandoned any other way. Without it
New hangs past its timeout, which the new test demonstrates by hanging when
the socket close is removed.

One keepalive loop still covers the whole chain: a probe to the target
crosses every hop, so a jump host that dies silently strands it exactly as
a dead target does. What changed is the response — an unanswered probe now
closes the chain rather than the target alone, which would have left the
jump host's socket held.

Failures name the hop they came from. A refusal reported against the
target's address alone reads as the target being down when the target was
never contacted, so a hop is named inside the transport error rather than
around it, leaving one transport failure per chain as the taxonomy asks.

The contract suite runs unchanged against a jumped environment.

## Summary

Last-minute driver substitutions are now a first-class concept. Results are always recorded against the **real** driver who raced; a new `driver_substitutions` table maps each affected seat to its substitute per race, and scoring resolves picks seat-based at computation time — the player who drafted a seat's regular driver scores whoever actually drove that seat.

- **Schema** (`007_driver_substitutions.sql`): `driver_substitutions` table (unique per seat and per substitute per race, RLS mirroring `race_results`, changelog trigger) + `drivers.is_substitute` flag
- **Scoring**: pure `applySubstitutions()` re-keys substitute result rows to the seat driver — race-scoped, non-transitive (handles chained swaps), immune to results re-imports; wired into all four scoring consumers (race page, season leaderboard, finalize flow, performance draft-order generation)
- **Draft pool**: substitutes excluded from draftable drivers; results import/manual entry still sees them
- **Admin UI**: Substitutions card on the race results page (add/remove, locked after finalize, inconsistency warning), substitute checkbox on the driver form, clone/delete/changelog handling
- **Display**: race results show real drivers with "subbing for X" badges; pick rows show "scored by Y"

Design spec and implementation plan are included under `docs/superpowers/`.

## Deploy notes

1. Apply `supabase/migrations/007_driver_substitutions.sql` to the live DB (then reload the PostgREST schema cache so the FK-hinted embeds resolve)
2. Backfill the affected race: create the reserve driver (substitute checkbox, correct driver number), add the two substitution rows, import results from OpenF1 as normal, verify, finalize

- [x] `npm test` — 39/39 passing (7 new unit tests for `applySubstitutions`: identity, single sub, chained double-sub, flag preservation, sub without result row, multi-race scoping, immutability)

author: csrinaldi
body:
## Linked issue (required)

Closes #792

## Pull request type

- [ ] New feature (`type:feature`)
- [ ] Bug fix (`type:bug`)
- [ ] Documentation only (`type:docs`)
- [ ] Code refactoring (`type:refactor`)
- [ ] Maintenance / tooling (`type:chore`)
- [x] Governance / process (`type:governance`)

## Summary

- **Compuerta 1 is taken: amendment, not supersede.** M8's `stage → engine` router amends ADR-0019 rather than superseding it.
- **Two amendments, because two signed documents said incompatible things** — ADR-0019's first rejected alternative and ADR-0024's prediction about it.
- Both promoted by the maintainer with `brain:promote`, in order, with the `brain/HOME.md` markers and a regenerated `AGENTS.md`.

## The ruling

**ADR-0019 Amendment 1** annotates the first rejected alternative to say what it was rejecting — a **forked layout**, not a routed producer:

| | the rejected alternative | M8's router |
|---|---|---|
| who writes `spec.md` | a per-backend `scaffold` op | an engine named in `sdd.map` |
| **where it lands** | **per harness** | `openspec/changes/issue-<id>-<slug>/spec.md` |
| **what a gate must know** | **which harness produced this change** | nothing |

The rejection's own words name the harm: *"the SDD artifact lifecycle would **fork per harness**"*. Routing the producer is not a fork as long as the third row stays empty.

It permits routing a lifecycle stage under **four conditions**, and the fourth carries the weight:

> `assertRoutableStage`'s refusal is **replaced, not removed** — the conditions go somewhere a reader enforces them. **Everything above is doctrine until something refuses on its behalf.**

**ADR-0024 Amendment 1** corrects a **prediction**, not a decision. The three axes are untouched. What is corrected is `:53-55`, which forecast *"its own ADR superseding ADR-0019's single-lifecycle decision"* — a forecast `ROADMAP-M5-M8.md` §3 had already begun to read as doctrine. A signed document predicting a supersede must be either fulfilled or corrected; leaving it is how a plan of record acquires a claim nobody checked.

## Why an amendment is the honest option, not the cheap one

ADR-0019 already refused to treat its op surface as a ceiling, two bullets below the one being amended:

> *"the four surfaces are the invariant, **the op count is just today's state**."*

And the precedent is already in `main`: **ADR-0033 grew `VALID_OPS` from `['init']` to `['init', 'run-stage']` with no supersede**, on exactly that argument. `stage-engine.mjs`'s header records why it could — *"`cold-review` produces none of the four"*.

Superseding a decision in order to add a permission it already allowed would have retired a norm — *four surfaces, artefacts neutral by design* — that is unchanged and still load-bearing.

## What this deliberately does NOT authorise, and both texts say so

**A new artefact joining the evidence contract.** Declaring more stages is already permitted and already done: `cold-review` is a fifth stage, routed in `sdd.map`, writing to its own root (`findings-artifact.mjs:180,201`), gitignored, read only by its own chain. Nothing shared learned anything.

A stage writing INTO `openspec/changes/**` and expecting the twelve shared readers to find it changes what the gates demand. That is **#456**, named in both amendments so "more stages" is never read as authorised by "routed stages".

**A forked verifier.** Condition 2 is not a preference: if verification forks per engine, every gate learns N shapes and the contract is gone.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `brain-drafts/adr-0019-amendment-1.draft.md` · `adr-0024-amendment-1.draft.md` | **new.** The signed inputs to the two promotions |
| `brain/project/decisions/adr-0019-harness-port.md` | Status line, the annotated bullet, and the signed Amendment 1 |
| `brain/project/decisions/adr-0024-three-axis-decoupling.md` | Status line, the corrected prediction, and the signed Amendment 1 |
| `brain/HOME.md` · `AGENTS.md` | the §1b index markers and the §1d cascade, both produced by the verb |

## Verified before opening

- Both drafts parsed by `parseAmendmentDraft` before promotion: one edit each, **each anchor resolving exactly once** in its target.
- Promoted **in order** — ADR-0019 first, because ADR-0024's text asserts that ADR-0019 Amendment 1 exists. Two commits, not one: two decisions about two documents.
- Both amended bullets keep their **original text** and append the marker, so a reader who never scrolls to the amendment is not left with the superseded reading.
- `npm test` — **4431 pass, 0 fail**, including the `AGENTS.md` byte-equality drift guard.

## Diff size budget

- [x] Diff is under the tier's budget (or `size:exception` label added with justification — not available at `regulated`)

## Decision / ADR

Two ADRs are **modified**, not added, and `brain/HOME.md` is in the diff alongside them — `decision-gate` passes on both of its failure cases. The `decision` label is applied: this is a decision, and no gate can tell.

`brain-writes-reviewed` is load-bearing here — the diff is `brain/project/**` and `brain/core`'s compiled output.

## What this unblocks, and what it does not

**Unblocks:** #323's S2 onward (the `sdd.map` schema, the resolver, the config verb), and **#790** — the orchestrator contract, which needed a stage-running surface to exist before it could specify one.

**Does not touch:** the other four gates of `ROADMAP-M5-M8.md` §3 — the `model_tier` shape, the n=2 parity set, the single config surface, and ratifying Q3. This PR takes one of five.

**#323 stays open.** It is M8; this is its S1.

author: artemlevin
gilcu2
body:
### Problem

The Companion BT Proxy Android app scans with `startScan(emptyList(), ...)` and exposes no allow-list, so it uploads **every** advertisement it hears. That is fine for a phone sitting in one room, but on a phone that leaves the house it means strangers' phones, earbuds and cars all land in HA's Bluetooth stack — where they surface as discoverable integrations and clutter the registry.

In my case a single 5-second scan in a public place collected ~20 devices, 2 of which were mine.

Since the app cannot filter, the webhook is the only place this can be stopped today.

### Change

Adds an **options flow** with an "Only forward these addresses" field. When set, advertisements from other addresses are dropped in `_async_handle_webhook` before reaching the scanner.

- Empty option → empty set → **current accept-everything behaviour is unchanged**.
- Addresses are split on commas/semicolons/whitespace, upper-cased, and validated against a MAC regex; malformed entries are skipped with a warning instead of silently voiding the whole filter.
- An update listener reloads the entry, so edits take effect without restarting HA.
- The parsed set lives in `hass.data[DOMAIN]["filters"]` alongside the existing `scanners`/`webhooks` maps and is cleaned up on unload.

Four files, ~83 lines.

### What it does and does not solve

This stops HA *acting* on unwanted devices. It does **not** reduce the phone's battery or mobile-data use, because the app still scans and uploads everything. For that the app itself needs `ScanFilter` support — I have opened kvj/hass_Bluetooth_Proxy_Companion#11 for that, and the two changes are complementary: the app-side filter saves radio and data, this one protects HA regardless of which app build is installed.

### Testing

Running on HA 2026.8.3 with a Pixel 8 Pro proxying two ThermoBeacons over WireGuard.

- With the option set to two addresses, a POST for an unlisted address returns 200 and creates no device or entity, while the two listed beacons continue to report normally.
- Malformed entries log `Ignoring malformed addresses in filter: [...]` and the valid ones still apply.
- Clearing the option restores unfiltered forwarding.

Thanks for the `advertisement_monotonic_time` and scanner-source fixes — I switched to this fork because of them.

body:
…rries

Creating an agent and replacing its workspace disagreed on the default access tier: creation reads `gitAccess ?? 'write'`, while `SetAgentWorkspaceBody` declared `.default('read')`. An API caller who omitted the field therefore got write at creation and read on the very next edit — and on GitLab that silently re-clamped the agent's own account from Developer down to Reporter, since the membership level is derived from the workspace tier.

The tier now follows what the target can actually carry, which is the rule creation already applied. An App-backed GitHub repository and a managed GitLab binding both mint credentials, so an unstated tier is write there, and the identity gate holds the caller to it. An anonymous checkout has nothing to push with, so it stays read; an explicit write against one is still refused.

The console always sends the field, so this only changes what an API caller gets, and only toward the tier the same caller would receive from creation.

author: ash-krnl
body:
## Why

OpenRouter tells its users two true things that pull in opposite directions. **Trust:** prompts only go to the models and providers you choose. **Reliability:** 80+ providers, and if one is down your call is quietly sent to another that works.

The second is why the first cannot be checked. The provider serving any single call is chosen at request time and **never appears in the response**. So a developer who promised their own customers that data stays with one provider, or in one region, has no way to show it happened.

This SDK governs both ends of that.

## Both ends

**Before the call — enforceable.** Where a call is going is stated on the call itself, as a span, before the request is built. A policy can refuse it, or attach narrower routing to use instead; the SDK writes that allowlist into the outgoing request so the gateway fails closed rather than falling back to someone you did not approve.

A directive can only ever **narrow**: `only` and `models` intersect with what the caller named, `allow_fallbacks` is false if either side says so. This is the one directive the SDK applies on its own initiative, and that constraint is why — it cannot make a request do anything the caller did not ask for, only send it to fewer places.

**After the answer — evidence.** OpenRouter publishes the answer at `GET /api/v1/generation?id=<gen-id>`: provider, region, cost, BYOK, and the failover trail. The SDK reads it for every governed call and records it as span attributes, which is what Core hashes into the session's Merkle tree — so it lands inside the attestation rather than beside it.

## What a reviewer should push back on

**The residency check is weaker than the provider check, deliberately.** Nothing the SDK writes into a request influences where a call lands, so a region constraint is never applied to a request. It produces evidence: the breach lands on the record and a policy refuses the *next* call, halting the session. One call later than you would like. The README says so, and so does the dashboard.

**A redirect is spelled as a BLOCK.** A directive reaches the SDK only on a refusing arm, because the verdict is what Core records against the call, and a call about to be re-routed did not run as asked. So the refused attempt closes on the same verdict it was refused on, routing happens as its own activity, and the corrected call is a new one. A start that said BLOCK and a completion that said ALLOW would be a record contradicting itself.

**`captureRequestObjectBody` stays off by default.** Reading a body off a `Request` requires cloning it, which leaves the caller's object unusable by their retry logic — roughly a quarter of real runs died with `Cannot construct a Request with a Request object that has already been used`.

## Three-valued comparisons

`openbox.routing.honored` and `openbox.model.honored` are **absent**, not `false`, when there was nothing to compare — no allowlist, or `openrouter/auto`. A rule must test `== false`; `!= true` would sweep in calls that promised nothing. `openrouter/auto` is reported as *unchecked*, never as a pass, because choosing the model is the promise there.

## Timing

The generation record is written shortly *after* the response — a lookup at turn close returns 404. Collection runs in the background with backoff and is drained before the session closes, so it never delays an answer and still lands inside the attestation. Do **not** `unref()` those timers: with them unref'd Node exited mid-collection and silently lost provenance on 2 of 3 calls.

## New in this branch

`receiptRefs()` returns, per finished run, the ids needed to resolve its run receipt. The locator, not the document — a receipt is assembled from records sealed at session close, so one the SDK built for itself would prove only that the SDK can hash, and fetching it needs dashboard credentials this SDK does not hold.

## Verification

184 tests pass against a fake engine and fake transport — no network, no keys. The suite replays the engine's real hook order, covering event ordering, verdict enforcement and halt semantics. Everything above was also exercised against the real OpenRouter API on a live stack.

## Related

Requires the companion PRs in `openbox-core`, `openbox-backend` and `openbox-fe`. Documentation on `docs/openrouter-proof-of-routing` in `openbox-document`.

body:
## Срез 1.4 — Проекты, OG и клики

Критерий готовности (`08 План разработки.md`): можно создать запись, увидеть её в витрине с подтянутым превью, а переход по ссылке увеличивает счётчик ровно один раз в сутки.

### Осознанное сужение — только Free Top
Платный вход — это по сути открывающий Raise-платёж (минимум ставки, `initial_stake` как база для floor будущих атак), а не голая вставка строки. Завести paid-запись с `paid_amount=0` в обход платежа значило бы пробить инвариант, на который опирается floor Attack. На Paid Top «Add my project» остаётся неактивной — откроется вместе с 1.5.

### SSRF-защита OG-фетча
`_shared/og.ts`: allowlist схем, DNS-проверка через `Deno.resolveDns` до похода за страницей (блокирует приватные/loopback/link-local диапазоны, включая cloud metadata `169.254.169.254`), лимит редиректов с перепроверкой каждого хопа, лимиты размера ответа и content-type.

author: ysetbon
body:
## Why

The pan fast path in #24 made the steady state fast but left **three ~800ms freezes in every gesture**. Per frame on `three_strand_braid`, 60 moves over 620px:

| | before |
|---|---|
| frame 1 | **820.6ms** — initial snapshot |
| frame 32 | **838.6ms** — re-snapshot, travel crossed `PAN_MARGIN` |
| pointer-up | **802.5ms** — release render |
| every other frame | 16.5ms |

All three are a full `renderFixture`, and 91% of the gesture was spent in them. The snapshot never addressed the actual cost — it moved it.

## What OSS does

Nothing. `mouseMoveEvent` (`strand_drawing_canvas.py:4430`) sets `pan_offset_x/y` and calls `update()`; `_paintEventInner` does a **full repaint** with `painter.translate(self.pan_offset_x, self.pan_offset_y)` in front of it. No snapshot, no cache, no fast path — a pan is a matrix, and every path is rebuilt every frame.

That's affordable there because a Qt repaint is cheap: a body is `QPainterPathStroker.createStroke()` + `drawPath()` with `WindingFill`, native C++, and end caps are `addPath`'d rather than united — the fill rule resolves the overlap at scan-convert time.

Ours is not cheap. Profiling one 702ms render:

| paper.js op | calls | ms |
|---|---|---|
| `resolveCrossings` | 225 | 363.8 |
| `unite` | 72 | 293.5 |
| `intersect` | 6 | 92.1 |
| `getLocationAt` (~1px sampling) | 12,580 | 23.8 |

~95% is boolean algebra. Shadows are 7% (693.8ms on vs 643.9ms off); rasterization is noise.

## What this does

Takes the half of OSS's design that matters — **the pan is a transform, not an input to the geometry** — and keeps the geometry across frames, since rebuilding it is the part we can't afford.

`renderFixture` now paints into two layers: a viewport-space **backdrop** (background + grid, matching where Qt computes them) and a **content** layer holding every strand, whose matrix carries the pan. `renderPanFrame` serves any later offset by moving that matrix, repainting the grid and re-rasterizing.

Deleted with it: `PAN_SNAP`, `PAN_MARGIN`, `renderPanBackground`, the oversized snapshot canvas, the whole-pixel delta requirement, `meta.target`, the `panGesture` flag, and the pointer-up release render. The scheduler's pan branch and its resting branch collapse into one path, because OSS has one.

## Result

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| frame 1 | 820.6ms | **12.5ms** |
| pointer-up | 802.5ms | **16.0ms** |
| stall frames | 3/60 | **0/60** |
| gesture total | 3436ms | **1039ms** |
| full renders | 3 | **0** |

`bench_pan_e2e` A/Bs the same gesture against a build with `renderPanFrame` removed: **41.7× faster** end to end, was 16.5×.

## One deviation, deliberate

Building the content at a bare `pt * S` with no offset at all — literally OSS's canvas coordinates — walks `three_strand_braid` straight into this renderer's known black-band degeneracy. paper.js boolean ops use **absolute** epsilons, so their output is sensitive to coordinate magnitude.

The content layer is therefore *anchored* at the offset its scene was built for, and the matrix carries the delta from there. The property a reused scene needs is that the geometry not depend on the **current** pan, and an anchor fixed for the scene's lifetime gives that just as well as zero — while keeping every full render bit-identical to before.

Also fixes a real bug found on the way: `computeGridLines` accumulated `x += g`, so the same grid line came out a few ULPs apart depending on which offset the walk started from — enough to move a 1px line onto different anti-aliasing. It indexes `i * g` now.

## Verification

`pan_fidelity` is rewritten. Its old premise (a deviation budget against a full render) is obsolete, and the obvious replacement is wrong too: *"a pan frame equals `renderFixture` at that offset"* is the wrong oracle, because `renderFixture` is not offset-invariant — measured against it, the pan frame is the **stable** side.

The gate now asserts what is exactly true and actually constrains the code:
- a delta-0 frame reproduces its render **bit-exactly**
- the same frame twice is **identical**
- a frame at delta *d* is the anchor image shifted by **exactly** *d* — residual bounded **and** the alignment uniquely best at that delta
- a scene is **refused** for a wrong key, a missing key, a resize or a zoom change
- a **control** per fixture: the same frame scored against a deliberately wrong delta (*d+1*) must be rejected, while *d* is accepted

That control is not decoration. The first version of the alignment test passed every fixture I showed it — including a wrong delta — and the second commit here is the fix. It read discriminability off colour variety rather than edge density, and took its floor from the neighbours alone; a frame misaligned by one pixel has the *true* delta among its neighbours scoring ~0, so a neighbours-only floor calls the one defect this test exists to catch "indistinguishable". The control caught that on its first run. Control and cases now share one `verdict()` predicate so they cannot drift apart.

The registration residual is not zero and is not claimed to be: reaching the rasterizer through a transform rather than as pre-added coordinates lands curve edges on marginally different anti-aliasing. Worst observed is 747 of 712k pixels (`box_stitch` @z1.35), verified by eye to be invisible; the alignment half is what rules out anything structural.

`drag_perf_check` gains two guards for the risk this introduces — `renderFixture` retains its paper project now instead of removing it. Six pan gestures with a scene-invalidating edit between each: zero project growth, zero canvas growth.

**Verified across all 26 fixtures:** `pan_fidelity` **1092/1092** (controls included) · `render_identity` **104/104 identical** · `drag_perf_check` **14/14** · `tsc` clean · editor build clean.

## Not fixed here

The black-band degeneracy is pre-existing and untouched. This change **reduces** exposure to it — one build serves a whole gesture instead of every frame rolling the dice at a new offset.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Performance**
  - Improved pan rendering by reusing retained scenes, reducing unnecessary full redraws during viewport movement.
  - Reduced rendering overhead and canvas growth across repeated pan gestures.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved pan accuracy, image alignment, determinism, and handling of zoom or resize changes.
  - Added safer fallback rendering when a retained scene cannot be reused.

- **Quality**
  - Expanded automated checks for pan correctness, multi-frame gestures, scene reuse, and resource stability.

body:
Refs #791 · M6-25 (partial delivery, issue stays open)

A first-run ceiling must survive process exits and linked worktree changes. This adds a local, Git-common SQLite ledger with exclusive initialization, immutable approval/spec/cap identity, serialized write-ahead reservations, conservative unknown/failed-charge accounting and monotonic task receipts. Retexturing requires one recorded human selection after the four-candidate sweep. It is operator tooling only, not application persistence.

The new `assets:meshy-run` command exposes only `init`, `status` and an explicitly capped, GET-only Meshy balance check. The balance transport uses one fixed HTTPS origin, refuses redirects, bounds response bytes/deadlines/retries and emits only a numeric readiness projection. The existing dry-run remains offline and never infers authorization. No paid submission, polling, download or promotion command exists.

Quarantine-only provenance descriptors bind the specification, approval, task/input-task IDs and artifact digests without changing the aircraft admission or livery schemas. Missing evidence stays explicit. ADR-0024 documents the local-disk trust/recovery limits: this is not distributed accounting or protection from a malicious workstation owner, and descriptors do not prove the underlying artifact bytes.

The user approved one hard 40-credit first-run ceiling. It was recorded privately, and a single successful read-only API balance request verified readiness. No credentials/approval artifacts/receipt/ledger entered Git, and no generation credits were spent. No dev/production or candidate/registry changes.

Tests cover process-level write exclusion, committed-reservation crash recovery, shared worktree state, reset/cap/spec refusal, uncertain and duplicate operations, changed charges, immutable human selection, tampered/corrupt history, provenance rejection, account response/retry/redaction bounds, the compiled command's refusal paths, duplicate round-robin receipts leaving the database byte-identical, and private PDF evidence remaining quarantined. CI exercises both CLI entry points without keys/network.

---

**Schema** — No application/shared asset/livery schema changes. New local SQLite format and quarantine-only sidecar descriptor; no migration.

**Runtime and deploy** — Operator tooling only on pinned Node 24.19.0; no new dependency, server secret, service, port or deployment. Dev's unrelated unmerged logo-editor preview is preserved.

**Verified** — Final CI at `734f64e`: all six checks green, including 206 test files, 93 focused Meshy tests, full PostgreSQL verification on disposable `tailfin_test`, Caddy policy, production/asset builds, performance, CodeQL and dependency review. Chromium: 10 passed against disposable `tailfin_e2e_ci`. [CI run](https://github.com/simmeh024/tailfinsim/actions/runs/33176919126).

Locally, `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4 pnpm verify` passed before the last receipt/idempotence additions (2,782 passed / 697 skipped; no DATABASE_URL). Final assets typecheck/lint/format/build and all 93 focused tests pass. Subsequent full Windows runs exposed a five-second ZIP compression timeout and a fleet sentence-query wait failure (final run: 2,783 passed / one fleet failure / 697 skipped); both unchanged suites then passed together in isolation, 42 tests, with their ordinary timeouts. CI passed with unchanged defaults. These failed local runs are not reported as green. An initial overlapping diagnostic coverage run was discarded. The live balance GET authenticated; zero generation credits were spent.

**Changed only on the server** — none.

**Docs** — ADR-0024, aircraft factory runbook, threat model, deploy guidance and local-only environment example.

**E2E coverage** — None added (not player-facing); existing CI Chromium smoke suite remains required by this delivery's review gate.

author: spencerjireh
body:
The logger decision 37 describes. **Stacked on #25** — review that one first; this targets it, not `main`.

**Nothing imports this yet, on purpose.** It adds a workspace importer and a lockfile entry, and all three docker builds install with `--frozen-lockfile`, so a mistake there is five red checks at once. Proving it in isolation is cheaper than finding it underneath a conversion. The docker matrix runs all three images on every PR regardless of what changed, which is exactly what makes this PR worth its own round trip.

**Shape follows `packages/gh-app-auth` exactly** — raw TypeScript, `exports` pointing at `src/index.ts`, no build step, no `dist`. tsup already inlines workspace deps for `cujo` and `github-mcp` (`noExternal: [/(.*)/]`), and all three Dockerfiles already `COPY packages ./packages` and install with `--filter <app>...`, so **no Dockerfile changes are needed**. Zero dependencies, which also keeps it clear of the pinning rule.

**The two rules that carry the weight:**

- A field must be declared in `FIELD_NAMES` *and* classified in `FIELD_CLASS`. `Record<FieldName, FieldClass>` is exhaustive, so a new name stops `fields.ts` compiling until somebody says what it is — the same fail-closed shape as `PUBLIC_SOURCE_FIELDS` in the public serializer. At runtime an undeclared key is dropped and its **name** — never its value — is reported in `dropped_fields`, because a silent drop is a debugging trap.
- A field value is a scalar: `string | number | boolean | null`. Not an object, not an `Error`, not the `Config`. This is what stops a wide object being spread into a call, which is how a logger leaks. `agent-spec.ts` already reasons this way and takes two fields rather than a config, "which turns a future `...config` spread into a compile error instead of a leak"; this takes zero.

**Rejected:** handing the logger the process's real secrets to redact by exact match. More precise than patterns, and it makes a bug in the logging path a total disclosure. The logger is given nothing to lose.

**Conventions followed rather than invented:** the sink and the clock are injected, matching `GitHubReader`'s `fetchImpl` and `bootstrapUntilReady`'s `sleep`, so tests capture into an array and nothing here spies on `console` — consistent with a repo that has zero console spying. The default sink writes to `process.stdout` rather than through `console`, which also means this package will need no `noConsole` exemption when that rule is enabled later in the sweep.

`emit` never throws. It will sit in the path `Runner.refold` already guards because "a subscriber must never be able to fail a run", and `process.stdout.write` can throw on EPIPE when the container's log reader goes away.

**Verification:** 50 new tests; `pnpm lint`, `typecheck`, `test` and `build` all green (458 tests across the workspace). The sentinel sweep runs seven real credential shapes through the scrubber and asserts no 12-character run of the original survives, with the companion assertion that an ordinary message returns byte-identical — a scrubber that mangles normal text is one somebody turns off. Two findings from writing it, both worth a reviewer's eye: the Discord token pattern was initially pinned to a 27-character trailing segment, which is the historical length and silently stops matching tokens minted since (now open-ended); and `noDelete` pushed `error_stack` from "removed afterwards" to "never added", which is what the rule actually wanted.

**Known limit, stated in the source:** TypeScript's excess-property check fires on object literals only, so a value widened to `Fields` elsewhere slips past the compiler. That is why `emit` filters at runtime too, where the equivalent check in the public serializer is belt-and-braces.

**Not done here:** nothing calls it. The event vocabulary is declared in full because it is the design, so `EVENT_NAMES` currently lists names no code emits yet; the guard test that closes both directions of that lands after the last conversion.

author: starknetdev
body:
## Why

`IMetagameContext` and its siblings took a bare `token_id`. A token id is unique only within the contract that minted it — identity is `(game_address, token_id)` — so a metagame serving two games can hold two registrations under the same packed id, and a bare-id lookup has to guess or refuse.

This is the same unsound key `#127` fixed in registration storage, and it is why `3647904` **deleted** the display-only reverse index rather than repairing it. That commit's closing line names this change as the fix:

> *"If a caller ever genuinely needs context-from-bare-token, the honest answer is the one already documented as the real fix — carry the game address in IMetagameContext — not a best-effort index that has to lie or refuse."*

## The change

`has_context`, `context_details` and `context_svg` all take `game_address` first. Changing only one would leave the same defect in the others.

**`IMETAGAME_CONTEXT_ID` moves with the signature:**

| | |
|---|---|
| old | `0x1633419b5abcc4c0bbed8bd37a363fbe6de5bd25908761ab6dcda6a9b598ca9` |
| new | `0x1619dc3272af5ae7e632e00012211abb89ee97571405c6714125b4c4eb77bb4` |

That is deliberate, not collateral. A metagame built against the old shape registers the **old** id, so `supports_interface` answers false and a caller skips it — instead of dispatching and reverting on an argument-count mismatch. Derived as the extended selector of `has_context(ContractAddress,felt252)->E((),())`, verified by first reproducing the old id from `has_context(felt252)->E((),())`.

## Cost

**Interface-only. No storage, and no gas imposed on any metagame.** A metagame that wants to answer these keeps its own `(game, token) -> context` index; one that does not simply never registers the interface. That is deliberately *not* put in `RegistrationComponent`, so the cost falls only on implementers.

For reference, the Budokan-side index measures **+41,410 l2_gas (+0.27%)** and **+96 l1_data_gas** per entry — a plain unconditional SSTORE, versus the ~72,980 the deleted component index cost with its extra SLOAD and ambiguity handling.

## Blast radius

Nothing dispatched to these methods and nothing probed the id, so there are no runtime caller changes. The mocks carry the parameter and ignore it, with a note that a real metagame must key on the pair.

`IMETAGAME_CONTEXT_ID` is **not** one of the two game-acceptance ids, so deployed games stay valid and need no rebuild.

## Verification

`scarb fmt --check --workspace` clean, `scarb build` clean, **1313 passed / 2 failed** — both failures are `distribution::tests::test_payout`, confirmed failing identically on unmodified `main` (baselined by stashing this change).

- Linear interpolation between samples: hardware shows none of the images a nearest-sample fetch produces (mayjinsn/mayjisn2 samples play at 5.6-16 kHz on the 62.5 kHz output).
- Non-linear (mu-law like, 3-bit exponent / 4-bit mantissa float) sample format, enabled by voice 7 register $1f bit 1: set by renju, srmp5, gostop, koikois, nratechu, dcrown; clear in mayjinsn, mayjisn2, speglsht, macs, jclub2.  Matches the byte statistics of the sample banks and renju PCB footage.
- Exponential volume law (~6 dB per 8 steps, 0 = mute) instead of linear; fitted to mayjisn2/renju PCB footage

body:
## Summary

Three E2E failure clusters from CI run [33115618031](https://github.com/candrikanich/recruiting-compass-web/actions/runs/33115618031):

### 1. AnimatedCheck WebKit hit-test (3 failures — user-story-9-1)
`sr-only` clips the native `<input type="checkbox">` to 0×0 — WebKit can't route mouse events to clipped elements. Chromium is more lenient (routes by layout box). Fixed by replacing `sr-only` with `absolute inset-0 opacity-0` so the input covers the SVG overlay and receives clicks in all browsers. No visual change.

### 2. WebKit timing flakes (school-detail-notes, inbound-interaction)
Both specs used `domcontentloaded` which fires before Vue fetches data. Assertions with the default 5s timeout expire in WebKit's slower rendering pipeline. Fixed: `domcontentloaded` → `networkidle` + explicit 15s timeouts on bare `toBeVisible()` calls.

### 3. templates-crud-atomic schema drift (both browsers)
Test Supabase project `ahpethltxopkjxxzwmmb` was missing migration `20260906000000_family_shared_communication_templates` — no `family_unit_id` column on `communication_templates`, old RLS policies. author: micmarty-deepsense
body: ## Why The pinned `2.6.2` predates two upstream fixes this repo has been working around or blocked by. **`Message.unique_body` did not exist before 3.0.0.** Graph exposes `uniqueBody`, the part of a message body that excludes quoted thread history. Without the property there was no supported way to request it, so any work on thread-aware email extraction was blocked on a library upgrade rather than on our own code. 3.0.0 adds it, correctly keyed to Graph's `uniqueBody` and decorated for `$select`. **`IdentitySet`'s mutable-default-arg singleton is fixed.** That bug collapsed every `Permission` identity to whichever user happened to deserialize last in the process, which is why the OneDrive connector bypasses the SDK and fetches raw permission JSON through Graph `/$batch`. ## The one failing test is the point `test_office365_sdk_typed_accessor_is_corrupted` is a canary. It asserts the SDK is *still broken*, so that the day upstream fixes it, CI says so. It now fails: ``` AssertionError: Upstream office365 IdentitySet may have been fixed; consider removing the raw-JSON workaround in onedrive.py assert 3 == 1 ``` That is the canary doing its job, not a regression. Removing the workaround is a behaviour change with its own review surface, so this PR deliberately does not fold it in. **It should be the immediate follow-up**, and this PR should probably not merge until that is decided, since it otherwise lands a knowingly red test. ## Risk Low, and narrower than a major version bump suggests. The lock delta is this package alone, with no transitive movement. 174 of 175 unit tests across the outlook, onedrive and sharepoint connectors pass unchanged; the 175th is the canary above. ## What this does not fix `OutlookItem.change_key` still reads `properties.get("ChangeKey")` while Graph returns `changeKey`, so it continues to resolve to `None`. Sibling properties in the same class use Graph's casing correctly, so this looks like an upstream typo rather than a convention. Anything relying on `change_key` as a version or change-detection signal is unaffected by this upgrade and still needs attention.

author: bmxcode
body:
Closes #4.

The NRG pregap tests did not exercise the [ADR-0005](docs/adr/0005-probe-for-the-filesystem-origin.md) origin probe. `make_nrg()` writes the DAOX track start at the *end* of the 150-sector pregap, and `NrgImage` hands `FlatImage` exactly that range, so the container strips the pregap before the probe runs. The header is found at offset 0 of the cooked stream and a test named for the pregap passed for a reason unrelated to a non-zero origin. The model D13 established for Roland is to keep the NRG test (it covers the container path) and add a flat-image variant with the zeros genuinely in the stream, asserting a non-zero `origin.offset`. This does that for the backends that lacked it.

## Audit of the three named files

- **test_containers.py** — clean. `test_nrg_finds_the_track_behind_the_pregap` asserts `image.track.start == 150 * SECTOR_SIZE` and reads at 0; it is the backend-agnostic container-path test and makes no false origin claim.
- **test_akai_fs.py** — already covered on both halves. `test_origin_probe_finds_a_partition_behind_a_pregap` is the container path (NRG strips the pregap, resolves at 0); `test_origin_probe_finds_a_partition_offset_into_the_image` is already a genuine flat-image variant — zeros in the stream, `origin.offset == len(padding)` (non-zero). Only the two docstrings changed, to name which half each covers.
- **test_emu3.py** — the real hole. Its only origin test asserted `origin.offset == 0`, so it never exercised a non-zero origin at all.

## What each added test now proves

**`test_emu3.py::test_origin_resolves_when_the_pregap_is_inside_the_cooked_stream`** — an EIII disc behind 150 zeroed sectors in the stream resolves to `origin.offset == 150 * 2048` **and** its samples list from that origin (`Proteus1Presets` → `Piano E0`, `Piano A0`). Before the fix below, the bank listing came back empty.

**`test_emu3.py::test_eiv_samples_resolve_when_the_pregap_is_inside_the_cooked_stream`** — the same for the E-IV path, which locates records by a whole-image scan and an `E3S1` directory. E-IV records are read from an in-memory scan window, so a bank still *lists* under the old scan; the tell is the PCM. The test asserts `read_file` returns the sample's audio, which under the bug was 1 024 **zero** bytes read out of the pregap — a silent empty sample of the right length.

**`test_extract.py::test_names_differing_only_in_case_extract_to_distinct_files_by_content`** — two Roland samples whose names differ only in case (`C_6E` / `C_6e`) both survive extraction as distinct files, verified by a **multiset of the PCM read back from the written WAVs** against the two source clusters — not by name. Holds on a case-insensitive filesystem (the second lands under a `_2` suffix) and a case-sensitive one alike.

Both EMU3 tests were confirmed to **fail against the pre-fix scans and pass against the fixed ones**; the case-collision test fails if extraction is made to key its writes on the sanitised name.

## The EMU3 bug this uncovered

`_bank_headers` and `_eiv_scan` scanned from absolute position 0 and returned **absolute** addresses, while every read that consumes them — `_samples`, `_declared_run`, `_eiv_samples`, `read_file` — is taken at `offset + address`. At `offset == 0` (every real EMU3 disc, and NRG discs after the container strips the pregap) the two coincide, so nothing shipped was wrong. At a genuine non-zero origin (a hybrid disc, or a raw rip with the pregap left in) they double-count: the bank listing comes back empty on EIII, and on E-IV the records list but their audio reads as zeros. That is exactly the silent empty-disc failure ADR-0005 exists to prevent, reached this time from inside the filesystem rather than at the container seam — and it was invisible precisely because no test drove the probe to a non-zero origin.

The fix makes both scans begin at `offset` and report addresses relative to it, so the whole backend speaks one coordinate system. It is self-consistent by construction: `_placement`/`_bank_offsets` and `_eiv_unit` fit `address == unit * start + bias`, and the `bias` term absorbs the origin shift, so the located addresses come out origin-relative and match the `offset + address` reads. No format constant or byte meaning changed; `docs/formats/emu3.md` is untouched. The opt-in disc-backed suite (which resolves every EMU3 reference disc at offset 0) is unaffected, and all 339 synthetic tests pass.

## The filename-keyed verification gap (#4, second item)

Audited and found nothing to fix in the repo: the committed code already verifies by content, not by sanitised path. `extract.py` deduplicates on `sha256` of PCM and the stereo joiner deliberately uses a list rather than a name-keyed dict (issue #11); the synthetic extraction tests compare content-sets (`{p.read_bytes() for p in written} == set(...)`); and the disc-backed suite pins per-disc SHA-256 digests over payloads, the same "multisets of hashes over PCM" the 0.2.0 notes describe. The byte-identity sweep that reported 6 false mismatches on the Roland discs (two names differing only in case folding onto one file on macOS) was an external measurement pass, not committed here. The new `test_extract.py` test is what now keeps that guarantee from regressing.

## Verify

`uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`, `uv run pytest -q` (339 passed, 112 skipped), and `uv tool install --editable . && samplerdisc --version` all pass.

author: aleksandrgarnov
body:
## Why

Consolidated fixes for the four "done badly" findings from the self-audit, in **one PR** so it can be merged and taken straight into a real-world validation run.

## What's in it

1. **Oracle gate was a blacklist masquerading as a structural guarantee** — `matches current behavior` / `= system output` / `per the running app` passed as "independent" (proven by running the script). Now honest: **structural (column present + non-empty) + best-effort tripwire** (widened), with header/message/`COVERAGE-OK` all saying so; **true independence moved to the step-6.5 semantic review** (flags a citation-less `spec §4`, an arithmetic-less "hand calc", a code-restating "invariant"). Antipattern was the same blacklist-vs-whitelist P0 fixed for skip statuses.
2. **References were dead prose** (#3) — slimming moved method into `references/*.md` but nothing made the model open them. Steps now open with an explicit "**`Read` the reference before the step**" block naming which file loads before which step.
3. **Verifier-reliability's honest limit** (#2) — probe-gating is prompted of the same unreliable model, so "probe ✓" is just another LLM assertion. The reference now says so and requires the probe to be **executable** (raw output as an artifact), not a claim.
4. **CI example validated** (#6) — `qa-gate.yml`'s `jqr` parsing + gate invocation run locally against a real bundle (green → `fail=0`, red → `fail=1`); README records the status honestly.
5. Fixed a **false-green test** (P0's `n/r` status made a slash-path, passing on "report missing" not the status check) → `pending`.

## Consciously NOT done here
- **#5 ceremony** (growing column count) — no new required fields added in this PR; left as a known design trade-off rather than piling on more.

## Test plan
- [x] The three previously-bypassing oracle fakes now FAIL (run directly)
- [x] `bash scripts/tests/run-all.sh` → ALL SUITES PASSED (coverage 19→24)
- [x] All `references/*.md` links in SKILL.md resolve; version ↔ changelog lockstep
- [x] CI-example gate logic validated locally against a real bundle

author: wagnerra23
body:
Onda 1 do Ponto, PR-A2 + PR-A3 juntos: os dois tocam `Ponto/Espelho/Show.tsx`, então rodar em paralelo daria conflito. **2 commits**, um por intent.

## PR-A2 · sinal não-cor na divergência

O scorecard punha `a11y_wcag` em 74 com o motivo escrito: *"Heatmap+divergencia so por cor (amber); add icone/label nao-cor p/ daltonico"*.

**Medi antes de mexer, porque metade já estava feita:**

| Onde | Sinal ANTES | Não-cor? |
|---|---|---|
| Banner do topo | `AlertTriangle` + "N dia(s) com divergência" | já tinha |
| Tabela · coluna `Estado` | palavra `divergencia` | já tinha (UC-ESPSH-01) |
| Tabela · Atraso/HE | o próprio número | já tinha |
| Tabela · linha divergente | `bg-warning/5` (tint de 5%) | **não** |
| Heatmap · estado da célula | só o fundo | **não** |
| Heatmap · divergência | só `ring-amber-500` | **não** |
| Heatmap · legenda | swatch de cor; divergência ausente | **não** |
| Heatmap · tooltip | "· divergência" | exige hover — não existe no toque nem no papel |

O `UC-ESPSH-01` estava certo: a tabela já carregava a palavra. **O gap real era o heatmap.**

Entrou: glifo por estado na célula (`X` falta · `Clock` atraso · `ChevronsUp`/`ChevronUp` HE · `Check` normal); `AlertTriangle` no canto da célula divergente herdando `currentColor`; `aria-label` com estado · valor · divergência; entrada de Divergência na legenda com contador; e um ícone no começo da linha divergente da tabela.

**CORES INTOCADAS** — `stateStyles` não mudou uma classe. O verde de HE é semântica de estado e o token é decisão pendente do [W].

### Critério de aceite provado por medição, não no olho

Renderizei o `MonthHeatmap` **real** (importado, não uma cópia — §5 2026-08-14) num harness e medi a luminância Rec.601 do fundo de cada estado, resolvendo `oklab` por canvas:

| Estado | Cinza (0–255) | Células com glifo |
|---|---|---|
| Fim de semana | 249,8 | — (por design) |
| Normal | 226,8 | 9/9 |
| **Atraso** | **191,7** | 4/4 |
| **HE** | **186,6** | 3/3 |
| Falta | 132,2 | 2/2 |
| HE alta | 101,4 | 4/4 |

**Atraso e HE colidem em greyscale — Δ = 5,1.** É exatamente a falha que o PR ataca; o que os separa agora é forma (glifo + sinal do número: `01:35` vs `+00:45`). Divergência: **3/3 com marcador não-cor, 0 falsos-positivos** nas 27 restantes.

> A primeira medição deu luminância 0 em tudo. O **controle positivo** mostrou que nenhuma utility do Tailwind havia aplicado no harness (`borderRadius: 0px`, `display: inline-block`). O número acima é o de depois do conserto. Harness removido antes do commit.

## PR-A3 · mobile-fit do dia-a-dia

Correção de fato ao medir: a tabela tem **8 colunas**, não 6 — `Dia · Previsto · Realizado · Marcações · Atraso · HE · BH (+/−) · Estado`. O scorecard é de 2026-07-05 e o F3 acrescentou colunas depois; o diagnóstico segue certo, o número é que envelheceu.

Abaixo de `md`, lista de cartões por dia — mesmos campos, mesmos rótulos, empilhados. Cada cartão traz data + dia da semana, badge `Divergência` com ícone, estado, as marcações e os totais em grade 2×; linhas de ≥44px.

**Desktop intocado**: a tabela só ganhou `hidden md:block`. É ela que carrega a copy do contrato, e o `−` de `BH (+/−)` é **U+2212 conferido por codepoint** nos 6 sites — o gate compara string exata e um hífen ASCII passa despercebido no olho.

### A armadilha, e como fica resolvida

Com as duas renderizações no DOM, o dia passa a existir em **dois nós**, e `getElementById` devolveria sempre o primeiro — no telefone, justamente o invisível, quebrando o clique do heatmap. Ids distintos (`dia-` / `dia-m-`) + `alvoDoDia()`, que escolhe pelo que o browser **layoutou**.

Uso `getClientRects()`, **não** `getComputedStyle().display`: quem esconde aqui é o **ancestral**, e o `display` computado do descendente segue `table-row` — a sonda canônica mentiria neste caso, e isso está escrito no código.

## `casos.md` — G-6

`last_run` bumpado cobrindo A2 e A3, declarando **0 UC executado por mim** (Pest é CT 100/CI, ADR 0062). A revalidação é forte **por medição**: abri o `EspelhoContratoTest` e os 5 UC asseveram **exclusivamente sobre o payload Inertia** (`props.totais`, `props.linhas`, status 404) — nenhum toca DOM, HTML ou CSS, e os dois PRs são 100% client-side sem encostar em Controller/Service/prop.

Dois `[BACKLOG]` novos, registrados para não virarem "descoberta" depois:
- teste **futuro** de nível DOM vai contar o dia em dobro se não filtrar por visibilidade;
- alvo de toque do heatmap a 375px é **~41px** (calculado, com a aritmética escrita). Passa WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 (24px), fica abaixo dos 44px de plataforma. **Não corrigido de propósito** — é layout do `MonthHeatmap`, fenceado pela Onda 1 a a11y-only, e a saída mudaria a semântica de calendário.

## ⚠️ O gate visual está CEGO a este PR — e isso não é falha dele

Não regenerei a baseline de pixel, e a razão é medida, não preguiça. O `VisregPontoSeeder` cria o colaborador **sem marcação e sem apuração, explicitamente de propósito** — o docblock dele diz: *"Se um dia a baseline precisar exercitar divergência (UC-ESPSH-01), isso é fixture nova e decisão própria"*. Na rota que o manifesto fixa (`/ponto/espelho/900001?mes=2026-06`):

- o modo default é `tabela` → **o heatmap não renderiza**, e todo o A2 fica fora do quadro;
- as 30 linhas têm `divergencia: false` → **o ícone da linha nunca dispara**;
- os cartões do A3 são `md:hidden` → **zero pixel** no viewport desktop.

**Predição: diff de pixel zero** — predição, não veredito; o CI é o oráculo. O corolário importa mais que o diff: **se o gate ficar verde, isso não é evidência de nada sobre estes dois PRs.** Exercitar de verdade exige a fixture com dia divergente que o próprio seeder nomeia — trabalho separado e decisão [W].

## Verificação local

Pest e PHPStan **não** rodei — CT 100/CI ([ADR 0062](memory/decisions/0062-separacao-runtime-hostinger-ct100.md)).

| Check | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `typecheck:baseline:check` | 278/278 · **Delta +0** |
| `lint:baseline:check` | 2066 vs 2100 · −34 |
| `a11y:check` | 246/246 (ratchet OK) |
| `casos:check` | stale do G-6 resolvido · 109, sem violações novas |
| `ds:canon:check` | 49 arquivos sem paleta crua |
| `components:check` · `layout:check` | verdes |
| `contrato-de-tela ponto-espelho` | 5/5 seções, ordem coerente |
| `build:inertia` | compila |

Nenhum `blue-*`/`violet-*`/`emerald-*` reintroduzido; sem toque em cálculo de apuração ou em `ponto_marcacoes`.

<!-- no-ui-smoke: o painel do browser não compõe frames nesta sessão (screenshot indisponível, medido). A verificação foi feita por MEDIÇÃO de DOM/CSS computado no componente real, que é prova mais forte que print pro critério em causa (luminância greyscale + cobertura de glifo + 0 falsos-positivos). Números na seção PR-A2. -->

author: marianocappucci
body:
El módulo de caja como el de Contalibra, con las dos decisiones que tomó el humano: **la caja pertenece a una sucursal y una sede puede tener más de una**, y los turnos anteriores quedan en la caja por defecto.

Necesita [libracore v1.57.0](https://github.com/marianocappucci/libracore/pull/139) — pin subido de v1.55.0.

## Lo que ya estaba y no se usaba

**El detalle del turno llegaba de la API y la pantalla lo tiraba.** `get_resumen_turno_caja` devuelve `movimientos` con concepto, monto y medio desde siempre, el tipo del frontend lo declaraba, y `Caja.tsx` mostraba sólo los totales por medio: el operador **cobraba a ciegas** y un monto mal tipeado sólo aparecía como una diferencia al cerrar, cuando ya no se sabía cuál era.

Ahora se ve, y se puede **anular** — sólo del turno abierto de quien pide: un arqueo cerrado es un hecho que alguien firmó.

## 🔴 Los egresos

El resumen del motor ya los neteaba —`SUM(CASE WHEN tipo='egreso' THEN -monto ELSE monto END)`— y este producto **no tenía forma de registrar uno**: el arqueo sólo podía subir, y sacar plata del cajón dejaba el cierre con un faltante indistinguible de un error de conteo o de un robo.

El motivo sale de una **lista cerrada del backend**, no de constantes de la pantalla: si divergieran, la pantalla ofrecería un motivo que el POST rechaza con 422.

## El turno, sobre un mostrador

El movimiento hereda la caja **del turno** y no del pedido: dejarlo en el payload permitiría cargar plata en la caja de otra sede desde la sesión de ésta.

**La migración corre al arrancar y es idempotente**: una caja por cada sucursal que no tenga ninguna. Sin eso, subir esta versión dejaba al mostrador **sin poder abrir el turno** — no habría caja que elegir, y crearla es de admin.

`registrar_ingreso` pasa a delegar en `registrar_movimiento`: tener dos INSERT es cómo uno de los dos se queda sin una columna nueva y nadie se entera.

## Verificación

**Catorce mutaciones**, cada una en rojo sobre su test: el filtro por sede en el router y en el servicio, los medios sin validar, la caja dada de baja, el egreso registrado como ingreso, el motivo sin validar, la anulación de un movimiento ajeno, el movimiento que no hereda la caja, la caja que no viaja al abrir, los movimientos sin dibujar, el egreso sin signo, el `anular` con id fijo, el botón habilitado sin mostradores, y los motivos desde una constante.

> ⚠️ **Dos mutaciones no mordían y hubo que rehacerlas.** Una porque el `or` que agregué nunca se ejecutaba —la lista venía llena—, y la del `anular` porque el test anulaba **el primero** de la lista: un `anular(11)` hardcodeado pasaba igual. Ahora anula el segundo.

Backend **569**, frontend **213**, ruff y lint limpios, build con `dist/` generado.

## De paso

El fondo verde del encabezado de cancha lleva las esquinas de arriba redondeadas —reportado hoy—, con el radio **un píxel más chico** que el de la sección para quedar concéntrico con su borde.

## Lo que NO entra

`recibos` y `tesorería`, las otras dos opciones del [análisis](https://github.com/marianocappucci/llm-wiki-proyectos): la primera puede esperar, la segunda es un módulo propio y no debería empezarse hasta que un complejo real lo pida.

body:
## The bug

GATE Q — "the Python/Rust trainer harness plays the same game as the Godot
oracle seed-for-seed" — read **0/20** against the freshly recorded
`~/selfplay_out/m3_ref_v4` (20 seeds, recorded at `c94f825` by
`tools/core_selfplay.gd` after #451).

**The search was never the problem.** Replaying all **1023** recorded
activations of those 20 seeds through `plan_with_rollout` on the corpus's own
states, with `test_parity.diff`'s full field list — menus, `trace.scored`,
`trace.pool_idx`, `trace.rs`, `best_idx`, `runner_idx`, `pick`,
`expectation.before/after`, `runner_up`, `rolled_units` — is **1023/1023
clean**. Nothing in the port's menu or EV moved. The divergence is in the
harness's own game loop, and specifically in its POOL.

Since #451 (NML-1105) `tools/core_selfplay.gd` builds its units through the
table's import path, so every host in its corpus carries `attached`,
`attached_to` and `attached_hero_rules`. It still never FOLDS: `_pick_for`
(:431-436) is the planner's own `player / activated / alive` filter, and
`BattleSim.hero_fold` is never set. So its header stamps `hero_attach: false`
over a fully joined roster — a game the trainer's two modes (`off`, `table`)
could not describe between them.

## What changed

**1. `State.pool` asks the fold seam** (`core/nml-core-py/src/lib.rs`). It
called `can_activate(i, player, true)` unconditionally, on the written argument
that "under `hero_attach="off"` no unit has a host anyway". True until
NML-1105, false since: it swallowed one activation per joined hero. The seam is
now a parameter defaulting to `true`, so every caller written before this
ticket is byte-identical.

**2. `hero_attach` gains the middle mode `"join"`** (`selfplay.py`) — derive
the roster attachment, fold nothing. That is what `tools/core_selfplay.gd` has
PLAYED since #451. `resolve_hero_attach` stays the FOLD bit (what the header
knob and `Seams::hero_attach` mean); the new `hero_join` is the JOIN bit.

**3. The gate reads the mode off the corpus.** `selfplay_gate.py
--hero-attach` defaults to `auto` and calls the new
`selfplay.hero_attach_of_corpus`: the header's `hero_attach` key is the fold
(`act_recorder.gd:176`), the first act's `attached_to` is the join. A recording
is self-describing; a gate should not have to be told twice.

## GATE M3-5

    python core/nml-core-py/tools/selfplay_gate.py \
      --ref ~/selfplay_out/m3_ref_v4 --bank ~/selfplay_out/terrain_bank \
      --army1 ~/ai_lists_gf/robot_legions_1000.json \
      --army2 ~/ai_lists_gf/blessed_sisters_1000.json --seeds 27-46

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| seeds seed-for-seed equal | **0/20** | **20/20** |

`hero_attach   join (read off .../m3_ref_v4/acts_27/acts.jsonl)`; python
1.39 s/game vs godot 513.5 s/game — **371x**.

## RED PROOF

Put the unconditional `true` back and rebuild:

* `test_the_harness_pool_folds_a_joined_hero_only_under_the_seam` FAILS;
* the gate diverges at seed 27 **pick#8**: ref `(1, 2, 'p2_0_BT_-pdh', 2)`,
  got `(1, 1, 'p1_2_PkAB3lE', 2)` — the joined hero the pool swallowed, and p1
  handed a second activation in a row because p2 read as dry.

`test_hero_attach_of_corpus_reads_the_join_and_the_fold_apart` pins all three
modes off a written corpus, so a reader that collapsed join and fold again
would fail here too.

## What did NOT move

* `m3_ref_v3` was **already 0/20 on `origin/main`**, with a byte-identical
  first divergence (seed 27 `pick#2` ref `(1, 2, 'p2_3_QPkxzTG', 1)` got
  `(1, 2, 'p2_4_fi5ZHtl', 2)`). It is a stale pre-NML-1105 corpus, not a
  regression here; its replay lives in `test_selfplay.py` under
  `LEGACY_CORE_SELFPLAY`.
* `cargo test --release` on all three crates: nml-core, nml-core-py,
  nml-core-godot — **0 failed**.
* `pytest core/nml-core-py/tests/python` — **140 passed**.

author: alicoding
body:
## Summary
- `keyByName` (`internal/adapters/hotkey/hotkey_desktop.go`) only mapped letters/digits/Space; global hotkey registration for a punctuation combo (e.g. Cmd+Shift+,) failed with "unsupported key" even though the frontend recorder already produces `,` `/` `[` `]` `+` `-` via `keyFromEventCode` (`frontend/src/shared/keybinding.ts`).
- Adds the six raw `kVK_ANSI_*` Carbon keycodes to `keyByName`, matching exactly the punctuation strings the frontend can send. No frontend change needed — it was never the gate.
- Adds a table-driven Go test pinning each new entry to its exact keycode.

## Root cause detail
- `golang.design/x/hotkey` v0.6.1 defines its `Key` type as a raw platform keycode with no named constant for punctuation on any platform (darwin/windows/x11 all checked). Letters/digits keep using the library's portable `KeyA`-style constants; the six new entries use numeric Carbon literals, valid because macOS is desktop mode's only real build target today (`hotkey_desktop.go`'s `!server` tag never resolves to Windows/Linux in this repo's CI). Comment in the diff notes the platform-asymmetry honestly for if that ever changes.
- No other validation layer exists between the frontend combo and this map (checked `triggersvc.FormatBinding`, `settingssvc` keymap/summon-hotkey code, `internal/domain/trigger`) — `keyByName` was the sole chokepoint.

## Manual verification (owner, on an installed build — Accessibility-gated, can't run headless)
Set the summon hotkey (or a workflow trigger hotkey) to Cmd+Shift+, in Settings and confirm it registers and fires — this is the live proof; e2e can't reach real OS hotkey registration.

## Test plan
- [x] `go build ./internal/adapters/hotkey/...` / `go vet` / `golangci-lint run ./internal/adapters/hotkey/...`
- [x] `go test ./internal/adapters/hotkey/...` — new table-driven test covers all 6 punctuation keycodes

## Summary

- close the job edit dialog immediately after the app save instead of blocking on downstream Flex synchronization
