## Why

Job edits were persisted in the app, but the dialog stayed in its saving state while duplicate/unbounded Flex updates ran. The sync also skipped crew calls, traversed the same standard-job subtree repeatedly, and could erase a suffix when Flex omitted the queried root.

Regression controls were run before implementation and failed for duplicate standard-tree traversal, missing-root suffix preservation, and crew-call sync. They pass with this change.

- restricted local timeouts to idempotent reads and Flex header updates, avoiding late non-idempotent folder creation

author: machine-blac9216
body:
Closes #1013

Part of #726

## Summary

A run purge involving on-disk artifacts (any real scan run) deleted all evidence
correctly but never auto-finalized: `runs.purged_at` stayed NULL, no
`run_purge_tombstones` row was written, the `run_purges` in-flight row was never
cleared, and `GET /runs/{id}/purge` reported `InProgress` forever. The only way to
finalize was for an operator to manually re-POST the purge.

**Mechanism bug**: `RunPurgeService.ResumeAsync` enqueues the artifact-deletion job
and returns `InProgress` — correct for that call. `PurgeJobHandler`
(compliance-runner) later reports the job's own outcome via
`IRunPurgeRepository.ReportArtifactOutcomeAsync`, which durably flips
`artifacts_phase` to `done`/`failed` in `run_purges`. But nothing then re-entered
`RunPurgeService` to observe "both phases done" and reach the finalization code path
(`IRunPurgeRepository.CompleteAsync` — tombstone + `purged_at` + row deletion).
`GET /runs/{id}/purge` only *reports* status; it never finalizes. So a purge with
artifacts silently stalled one phase short of completion until a human re-POSTed —
exactly the round-8 live-proven stuck state, and exactly the workaround the
zero-workaround bar disallows.

**Fix (round 2 — API-side, preserving migration 0042's security posture)**: the
round-1 approach (runner-side finalize call inside `PurgeJobHandler`) violated
migration 0042's documented least-privilege posture — `waypoint_compliance_runner`
holds only SELECT + a column-limited UPDATE on `run_purges`; INSERT on
`run_purge_tombstones` and DELETE on `run_purges` are deliberately API-only
("nothing runner-side ever removes a run_purges row"), and the round-1 call failed
42501 under the real role. Round 2 keeps that posture intact instead of widening it:

- `PurgeJobHandler` is reverted to exactly its granted write — the durable
  `artifacts_phase` outcome report. No new runner privileges, no runner-side
  finalization.
- New `RunPurgeFinalizeHostedService` (API process only, registered in
  `AddWaypointApiSurface` alongside `RunSecretCleanupHostedService` — the same
  placement whose doc comment documents why runner hosts must never start sweeps
  their DB roles cannot perform) periodically sweeps
  `IRunPurgeRepository.ListPendingFinalizeRunIdsAsync` (rows with
  `db_phase_done AND artifacts_phase = 'done'`) and finalizes each via
  `RunPurgeService.FinalizePendingAsync` under the owner connection — the same
  connection that performs every other purge write. Default sweep interval 5s
  (`RunPurgeFinalizeOptions`, bindable via the `RunPurgeFinalize` config section).
- `FinalizePendingAsync` is guarded to the `done` phase only and re-reads fresh
  state, so it can never finalize (or re-enqueue) a `failed` pass and races safely
  with a concurrent operator re-POST (`CompleteAsync`'s tombstone INSERT is
  `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`). ADR-0019's retryable contract is unchanged: a genuine
  mid-phase failure stays an honest, operator-visible `Failed` requiring a re-POST.

No security-posture amendment is needed or made: the runner's grant surface is
byte-identical to migration 0042.

## Risk

- New always-on API hosted service: one indexed primary-key SELECT per interval on
  a table that is empty except mid-purge. Failure of one run's finalization is
  logged and retried next tick (the row only disappears on success).
- `IRunPurgeRepository` gained `ListPendingFinalizeRunIdsAsync` — the two test
  fakes implementing the interface were extended; no other implementations exist.
- Multiple API instances sweeping concurrently is safe (idempotent finalization,
  `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, delete-by-key), same posture as the sibling sweeps.
- No schema/migration changes; `PurgeJobHandler` and the runner grant surface are
  unchanged from main.

## Rollback

`git revert` the two commits — no schema or data migration involved. A purge stuck
at `InProgress` post-revert would return to needing a manual re-POST, as before.

## Suggested Test Steps

1. Run a scan to completion, then `POST /runs/{id}/purge` with
   `{"confirmation": "PURGE"}` — expected: within one sweep interval (~5s) of the
   artifact job finishing, `GET /runs/{id}/purge` returns `outcome: Completed`,
   `runs.purged_at` is set, and a `run_purge_tombstones` row exists — with no second
   POST. Check API logs for `Finalized purge for run …`.
2. Confirm compliance-runner logs show NO permission-denied (42501) entries during
   the purge — the runner made only its granted `artifacts_phase` UPDATE.
3. `dotnet test backend/Waypoint.sln --filter FullyQualifiedName~RunPurgeServiceTests` —
   expected: all pass, including
   `PurgeRunAsync_RunWithArtifacts_FinalizesInOneOperatorActionWithoutASecondPurgeCall`
   and `PurgeRunAsync_RealHandlerMidPhaseFailure_LeavesHonestlyInProgressThenRetryCompletes`
   (both drive the real `PurgeJobHandler` under the real
   `waypoint_compliance_runner` role, then one `RunPurgeFinalizeHostedService`
   sweep pass), plus the grant-drift denials
   `ComplianceRunnerRole_InsertRunPurgeTombstone_IsDenied` and
   `ComplianceRunnerRole_DeleteRunPurgesRow_IsDenied` (42501 pinned in both
   directions).
4. `dotnet build backend/Waypoint.sln -warnaserror` and
   `dotnet test backend/Waypoint.sln` — expected: clean build, full suite green
   (2566/2566 at head).

**Failing-test-first proof**: the two e2e tests were run against pre-fix `main`
and failed with `Assert.Equal() Failure — Expected: Completed, Actual: InProgress`
at the exact point the second (never-arriving) finalization would have been needed —
the same stuck state #1013 reports. After the fix, both pass with no second
operator call.

author: ronaldtse
body:
## What

**Cached namespace binding sets** — the last per-query churn on
the search path. No upstream release (1.9.9 probe 404s).

### The problem

Every namespaced query built its binding set from scratch:

```ruby
flat_map → CStringArray wire format → ns_set_new_from_pairs → eval → free
```

~6.7 µs of construction per query — 2.6× the same query without
namespaces on a small document. SVG/DocBook/RDF-shaped workloads
pay it on every `xpath`/`at_xpath`/`css` with a namespace hash.

### The fix

The XPath VM casts the set to a **const map** during evaluation
(`vm.c:251`) and never mutates it — so one set per distinct
prefix/URI vocabulary serves the whole process, across queries and
threads. Cache keyed by canonical pairs (single-pair fast path
skips the sort); failed builds raise before caching; benign build
races leave a valid unused set, never freed — the same trade the
CSS translation cache makes.

### Measured (2,000-query loops, CPU)

| query | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xpath("//x:rect", ns)` | 10.9 µs | 6.9 µs | **−38%** |
| `at_xpath("//x:rect", ns)` | 9.1 µs | 6.7 µs | **−26%** |
| `xpath("//rect")` (no ns) | 4.2 µs | 3.9 µs | reference |

The remaining gap vs no-ns is the VM's prefix resolution itself.

### Also this round: `inner_html` declined as a feature

The binding has no `inner_html`; the tempting
`children.map(&:to_s).join` is wrong twice over (Text/Comment have
no `to_s`; correct inner HTML needs per-kind serialization with
escaping). That's a designed API, not a perf fix — proposing it
explicitly in a future round.

## Verification

- `bundle exec rspec`: **360 examples, 0 failures** (+4: stable
  repeated results, cross-vocabulary isolation with XPath 1.0
  unprefixed-name semantics pinned, symbol/string key equivalence,
  four-thread concurrent smoke).
- `rake compile audit:symbols`: 247/247 (no C surface change).
- Report: `architecture-review-20260828-nsset.html`, opened
  locally.

author: apx-vero
body:
Closes Appmixer-ai/appmixer-components#2813

Part of the AI connector contract work. `ai/openai` had 28 validator failures — the most of any AI connector — and, being the component source most other AI connectors were copied from, its defects had fanned out. `node scripts/validate.js --connector ai` now reports **zero failures for `ai/openai`**.

## What changed

**1. `embeddingTemplate` deleted** — declared in the inPort schema of `GenerateEmbeddings` and `GenerateEmbeddingsFromFile`, present in no inspector and no behaviour file. Also removed from `gemini/GenerateEmbeddingsFromFile`, which inherited it by copy.

**2. `examples` → `example`** — every outPort option used the JSON Schema plural array, which Appmixer does not read, instead of the singular `example` that drives the variable-picker preview. Converted across all 13 components, with realistic values.

**3. `AIAgent`: `model` and `instructions` moved from `properties` to `inPorts`** so they can be bound to a flow variable, matching `ai/claude` and `ai/gemini`. This is the breaking part, hence the major bump. The behaviour falls back to the old `context.properties` values, so agents configured before 2.0.0 keep working — they just need a re-save to pick up the new inputs.

**4. `SendPrompt`: added `instructions`** — the system message was hardcoded to `'You are a helpful assistant.'` with no way to change it. That string is now the default rather than the only option.

**5. `SendPrompt`: added the five sampling inputs** `temperature`, `maxTokens`, `topP`, `frequencyPenalty`, `presencePenalty`, matching groq and requesty. They live in a collapsed "Advanced" group, and only the ones the user actually sets are sent, so the model's own defaults are otherwise untouched.

**6. Embeddings `index` typed `integer`** — the behaviour always writes `i + index`, a number.

**7. `required` now matches the behaviour** — `["text"]` on `GenerateEmbeddings` and `["fileId"]` on `GenerateEmbeddingsFromFile`, both of which the code already asserts.

**8. `ignoreAuth=true`** added to the `TransformTextToJSON` and `VariableExtractor` dynamic outPort `source.url`. Both build their options before any API call, so no authenticated account is needed.

## Two adjacent defects found while auditing the same files

- **`TransformTextToJSON` crashed on every execution.** The required-input guard read `jsonSchema` four lines above the `let jsonSchema` declaration, so each call died in the temporal dead zone with `Cannot access 'jsonSchema' before initialization`. It now guards on the raw `jsonSchemaString`, which is what was intended.
- **`DescribeImages`'s `model` input was invisible.** Its inspector entry was nested inside the `images` field object rather than alongside it, so the schema declared a `model` input the Designer never rendered — the same ghost-input shape as finding 1. Lifted to a top-level input.

Also flipped `AIAgent`'s `storeId` from `select` to `text` (typeahead), the remaining `no-select-with-source` failure in the connector's 28.

## Not done, deliberately

Issue item 8 also notes that `TransformTextToJSON` binds `in/jsonSchema` to a flow variable, which the validator warns about. For `TransformTextToJSON` and `VariableExtractor` that bound value *is* what the output schema is derived from — replacing it with the literal `"dummy"` the warning suggests would produce an empty picker. Left as-is; these two warnings are the only findings remaining on `ai/openai`.

The `examples` → `example` conversion in gemini, voyageai, claude and openrouter is left to their own issues, as #2813 scopes it to the copy source. The one gemini file touched here (`GenerateEmbeddingsFromFile`) got the full treatment so the branch stays green under `--changed`.

## Versions

- `appmixer.ai.openai` 1.4.0 → **2.0.0** (breaking: `properties` → `inPorts`)
- `appmixer.ai.gemini` 1.1.0 → **1.1.1** (ghost input removal only)

## Verification

- `npm run lint` — passes
- `node scripts/validate.js --changed --base origin/dev` — passes
- `node scripts/validate.js --connector ai` — zero failures for `ai/openai` (down from 28)
- `appmixer connector verify --offline` — skipped, the connector ships no `artifacts/samples/`
- `npm run test-unit` — **not run**: not on this environment's command allow-list. The existing `SendPrompt.test.js` asserts `data.messages[1].content`, which the unconditional system message keeps in place, and `AIAgent.test.js` only covers `mcpCallTool`/`isMCPserver`, neither of which was touched — but this is reasoning, not a green run, so please confirm in CI.

No E2E flows generated and nothing published; that is phase 2.

author: azayati
body:
Part of eXIP 7.3.0.22 — Digest Mail Notifications. Task EXO-89484 (US03).

Social half of US03. Depends on Meeds-io/commons#772 — **merge that one first**, this PR compiles against the `DigestCategoryProvider` SPI it introduces.

## What the user gets

The digest entry added in US02 now opens a drawer with the two frequencies. Switching one on proposes every category the user can receive; he unchecks what he doesn't want. Both frequencies carry their own independent list, and the same category block is shown under each, per the design.

An enabled frequency with no category is refused by the drawer (Apply disabled) as well as by the server — an empty digest is never worth an email.

## Server side

`DigestRest` returns the administrator switch, the categories and the user's own choices in a single call, and saves those choices. When the administrator has not allowed the digest, the payload carries nothing else and the PATCH is refused with a 403.

**Category labels are translated on the server.** The settings page loads only two resource bundles, so an addon label would simply never resolve in the browser. `DigestCategoryLabelResolver` reads the label from the bundle the category's own notification plugins already declare — which is exactly how the notification groups are displayed today, and means an addon has nothing new to declare beyond its category provider.

The language is taken from the request. The social webapp does not declare `LocalizationFilter`, so the portal locale of the thread is empty here — unlike the `/rest` webapp, where the JAX-RS notification settings service can rely on it. `request.getLocale()` is what every other Spring controller in this module uses, and a unit test now pins a non-English label.

`DigestTimeZoneResolver` reads the `user.timeZone` profile attribute and hands it to the digest. Commons owns the digest but cannot read a user profile, so the timezone is resolved here. Note this is the organization profile attribute, not social's `Profile.TIME_ZONE`, which nothing writes outside the CSV import.

Worth knowing for the review: `user.timeZone` is today written by the **agenda addon alone**, on every page load. Without agenda nothing fills it and the digest falls back to server time. That is recorded in the javadoc, and moving the synchronization into the platform is planned with the sending itself (US08).

## Categories

Social contributes **Spaces** and **Feed**. The four others — News, Tasks, Agenda, Process — arrive with their own addon PRs, and the drawer shows only what is installed.

## Also in here

The digest entry now opens the drawer through a `ref`, like the muted-spaces one, instead of the root event US02 left as a placeholder. That closes finding G from the US02 review.

## Checks

- Backend compiles; `DigestCategoryLabelResolverTest` green (4 tests, covering the translated label, the English fallback and the two id fallbacks); frontend bundles with webpack; ESLint reports 0 errors on the touched app (the 5 remaining warnings are pre-existing in files this PR does not change).

author: jesse-elderlinksolutions
body:
One config file, two readers, and only one of them honoured the override.

`sync-once.ts` has always read `ARTICLES_CONFIG ?? cwd/articles.json`.
`sync-cron.sh` read `articles.json` from the repo root, hardcoded.

That was harmless while both lived in the same repository as the config. It
stopped being harmless when the portal moved into this **public** repo and
`articles.json` stayed in the **private** one — which is where it belongs: it
names three machine-local absolute paths and the products they belong to.

Both now resolve identically, and the cron script passes what it resolved down
to `npm run sync` explicitly rather than trusting the child to inherit a value
this script may itself have defaulted.

## The missing-config case is named, not silent

A config that is **absent** and a config that **lists nothing** both refresh no
trees, and only one of those is a mistake. Without the warning, a cron job
pointed at the wrong path reports the same `nothing to refresh` as a
deliberately empty one — hourly, into a log, forever.

## Verified in both directions, from the portal's new location

| | |
|---|---|
| `ARTICLES_CONFIG` → the private repo | resolves all three source trees and their refresh targets |
| `ARTICLES_CONFIG` → a nonexistent path | the warning fires |

Gate green: library 152 passed, portal 103 passed, exit 0.

## Why this lands before `howto` is emptied

The live crontab entry still runs `howto/scripts/sync-cron.sh`. Emptying that
repo first would break the hourly sync with nothing to say so. Order is: this
merges → the crontab is repointed at `portal/scripts/sync-cron.sh` with
`ARTICLES_CONFIG` set → the sync is confirmed working → only then is `howto`
stripped to a data repo.

author: sh3n0bi
body:
Answers a question the README couldn't: *"do we use this with Wireshark, or tshark?"*

## Which binaries are used

The old text said "install Wireshark" without naming the binaries or saying that `tshark` alone is enough — so it read as though the desktop GUI were a requirement. It isn't. Adds a table making the split explicit:

| Binary | Used for | Without it |
|---|---|---|
| `tshark` | Dissection, display filters, slices, object export | Falls back to the scapy engine |
| `dumpcap` | Live capture | Falls back to the scapy sniffer |
| `Wireshark` (GUI) | The `wireshark open` pivot only | `--print` still gives the command |

Plus per-platform install commands — a server, container, or CI runner needs `apt install tshark` and nothing else, no Qt or desktop stack — and a short "tshark, not the GUI" note at the top of the integration section.

## A worked investigation

The command reference lists every command but never showed them in order against one piece of evidence. Adds an end-to-end walkthrough: case → evidence → analyze → timeline → entity pivot → display-filter slice → packet pivot → finding → report → custody verify.

**Every command and every block of output in it was produced by running it**, not written by hand. That caught a mistake: the finding step cited `EVT-EV-0001-000003`, which is the TLS handshake, not the HTTP request it claimed to be about.

## One limitation now documented

tshark's object export reports the recovered file but not the frame it completed on, so those `file_transfer` events sort at the end of the timeline as `unknown`. No timestamp is invented — a wrong timestamp on forensic evidence is worse than an absent one, and the parent flow's events carry the timing.

Docs only; no code touched.

author: githublarskomo
body:
## Summary

Integrates the Hume/Garmin comparison into the existing Sport Athlete Management architecture without creating a parallel Health Twin. Garmin remains a provider of observations and optional provider-derived context; Skillz remains the sport-science decision layer.

### Canonical domain changes
- classifies objective/passive metrics as `direct_sensor`, `provider_derived`, `journal_derived`, `reference_measurement` or `manual_measurement`
- adds explicit decision roles so vendor scores cannot silently become training regulators
- adds biometric baseline and anomaly/Health Drift contract structures
- adds method-aware body measurements with BIA/DXA/scale/tape provenance
- expands P1 longitudinal outputs into five domains: Recovery, Training Tolerance, Performance Capacity, Physiological Stability and Body/Energy Context
- extends adaptation decisions with responsible signals, provider-score context and multi-signal confirmation

### Sport skill behavior
Updates the canonical sport skills so the contract is reflected in executable reasoning guidance:
- `sport-daily-athlete-monitoring`: Morning Check + passive data coexistence, provenance, baseline eligibility and vendor-score classification
- `sport-recovery-sleep`: personal baselines, Physiological Stability and multisignal Health Drift
- `sport-adaptation-analysis`: five-domain longitudinal analysis with method/device comparability
- `sport-training-adaptation-engine`: vendor scores and isolated biomarkers cannot independently control GREEN/YELLOW/ORANGE/RED or plan revision
- `sport-nutrition-fueling`: method-aware body composition and multisignal body/energy/RED-S interpretation

### Explicit exclusions
Biological Age, Pace of Aging, Lifespan/“days gained”, Metabolic Capacity/Momentum and universal health/readiness scores are not authoritative constructs or adaptation regulators. Garmin Training Readiness, Body Battery, Sleep Score, Training Status and Fitness Age may be retained as secondary provider context but cannot independently change training.

### Architecture
Adds `docs/SPORT-ATHLETE-MANAGEMENT-GARMIN-HEALTH-BASELINES.md` as a normative extension of the existing sport architecture. It specifies Morning Check + passive data coexistence, personal baseline rules, multisignal Health Drift, body-composition method separation, provider-score limits, five UI/analysis domains, Garmin adapter boundaries and audit requirements.

### Portable distribution and validation
Root skills, OpenAI agent metadata, portable plugin copies, Obsidian mirrors, `.skill-sync.json`, capability metadata and related generated artifacts are synchronized through the repository's existing generation pipeline. Compatibility evaluations were updated only where renamed/strengthened anchors required it; the prior safety behavior remains enforced.

### Product dependency
The paired Sports Journal PR #18 updates PRODUCT/SPEC/README and product architecture. Per `contracts/PROVENANCE.md`, its copied P0/P1 contracts should be synchronized only after this canonical Skillz change is merged.

author: davinnsc
body:
Version bump only. No behaviour changes — the six lines are `package.json`, `package-lock.json` (×2), `tauri.conf.json`, `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`.

Once this is on `main`, pushing the tag `v0.4.0` is what actually cuts the release: `release.yml` opens a draft, builds and signs Linux + Windows, assembles `latest.json`, and only then lifts the draft.

## Why the bump has to land before the tag

The manifest takes its version from the tag, but the app takes its own from `tauri.conf.json`. Tagging without this commit would advertise 0.4.0 to a copy that still reports 0.3.1 — it would install the update and be offered the very same one again, forever.

## What 0.4.0 carries, since v0.3.1

| PR | |
|----|--|
| #3, #5 | read a QR that is transparent or inverted |
| #6 | read a dense QR from a screenshot that was shrunk, plus a spinner while it reads |
| #7 | a success and a failure stop showing at the same time |
| #8 | check for new releases and install them |
| #9 | drag an account onto a folder |
| #10 | the header gets its own icons |
| #11 | right-click a folder to act on it |

Minor rather than patch: #8, #9 and #11 are new features.

## Worth knowing before publishing

- **v0.3.1 has no updater** — it shipped before #8. Everyone on 0.3.1 installs 0.4.0 by hand one last time; 0.4.0 onwards updates itself.
- **`TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` is not set** in the repository secrets, only the key itself. That is correct if the key was generated without a passphrase, and both build jobs fail if it wasn't. This release is the first time that path runs.
- The `pubkey` in `tauri.conf.json` has to be the public half of that secret, or installed copies will reject every update as unsigned. Nothing in CI checks this — the first successful self-update is the proof.

author: volscente
body:
## Description

The PR resolves the issue #69 by creating the aggregation engine for the holdings upload.

## Changelog

### Added

- **Backend**: New `POST /portfolio/holdings/exposure`-backing logic in `backend/src/backend/routers/portfolio.py` — `_build_holdings_exposure_query()` and `get_holdings_exposure()` aggregate look-through single-stock exposure across all owned ETFs: each ETF's share of total portfolio value (derived the same way as `_build_portfolio_query`, but grouped by ISIN alone rather than per owner/broker) is multiplied by each holding's `weight_percentage` in its latest `EtfHolding` snapshot, then summed per distinct stock across all contributing ETFs. An ETF with no price record is excluded from the aggregation and reported in `skipped_etfs` rather than nulling the whole response.
- **Backend**: New `HoldingContribution`, `HoldingExposureResponse`, `HoldingsExposureResponse` Pydantic v2 schemas in `backend/src/backend/schemas/portfolio.py`.
- **Backend**: `stock_country` column (nullable, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) added to `etf_holdings` via `backend/alembic/versions/004_add_etf_holdings_stock_country.py` and `EtfHolding.stock_country` in `models.py` — used to disambiguate stock identity when reconciling identifiers across issuers.
- **Backend**: `resolve_stock_isin_aliases(session, http_client)` in `backend/src/backend/converters/holdings_xlsx.py` — since iShares/Vanguard holdings only ever report a ticker and Amundi only ever reports an ISIN for the same underlying stocks, this resolves every distinct ISIN already stored in `etf_holdings` to its ticker via the free OpenFIGI mapping API (`POST /v3/mapping`, `idType=ID_ISIN` — the only direction OpenFIGI's API supports; a ticker cannot be resolved to an ISIN) and backfills `stock_isin` on any row across all ETFs still missing it whose `(stock_ticker, stock_country)` matches. Matching on country as well as ticker avoids merging unrelated companies that coincidentally share a ticker on different exchanges. Called from `upload_holdings` in `routers/etfs.py` after every successful holdings upload (any issuer), so it is insensitive to upload order; a failure (e.g. OpenFIGI unreachable) is caught and does not fail the upload.
- **Backend**: Each converter in `holdings_xlsx.py` now also emits `stock_country`: Amundi rows get it free from their own ISIN's first two characters (`_country_from_isin`); iShares rows are mapped from the German `Standort` column via a new static `GERMAN_COUNTRY_TO_ISO` dict (`_german_country_to_iso`); Vanguard rows use the `Region` column directly (already ISO 3166-1 alpha-2).
- **Backend**: `httpx>=0.27` moved from the `dev` dependency group to runtime `dependencies` in `backend/pyproject.toml`, since it is now used at request time to call OpenFIGI.
- **Tests**: `backend/tests/converters/test_holdings_xlsx.py` — new tests for `_country_from_isin`, `_german_country_to_iso`, and `resolve_stock_isin_aliases` (successful backfill, country-mismatch not backfilled, unresolvable ISIN, no-ISINs short-circuit).
- **Tests**: `backend/tests/routers/test_etfs.py` — new tests verifying `upload_holdings` calls the ISIN reconciliation step and that a reconciliation failure does not fail the upload.
- **Tests**: `backend/tests/routers/test_portfolio.py` — 5 new tests for `GET /portfolio/holdings/exposure` covering ISIN-based merging, ticker-fallback merging, the residual ISIN/ticker gap, missing-price `skipped_etfs`, and the empty case.

### Changed

- **Backend**: `backend/tests/converters/test_holdings_xlsx.py` — the three `test_convert_*_valid` tests updated to expect `stock_country` in each converter's output.
- **Backend**: `backend/tests/conftest.py` — `mock_session_with_etfs` now also stubs `result.all` so the new reconciliation step's distinct-ISIN lookup short-circuits harmlessly (no real network call) in existing upload tests.

## Что чинится

**Бэкенд слушал все интерфейсы.** `listen(PORT)` без хоста поднимал node на `*:8787`. Из интернета его закрывал ufw (проверено с внешнего адреса — порт недоступен, 443 отвечает), но этот же бокс терминирует VPN со своим выходом, и всё, что уже на хосте, доходило до node напрямую, мимо Caddy. А мимо Caddy `trust proxy 1` верит `X-Forwarded-For` вызывающего: замер показал, что каждое подставленное значение открывает свой счётчик лимитера (`remaining=119, 119, 118` для 9.9.9.9 / 8.8.8.8 / 9.9.9.9) — per-IP лимиты обходятся по кругу. Через Caddy тот же зонд делит один счётчик (119→118→117). Лечение — слушать `127.0.0.1`.

**WebView оплаты пускал куда угодно.** Теперь только https, файловый доступ выключен, mixed content запрещён, попапы закрыты. Список доменов намеренно НЕ прибит: 3-D Secure уходит на банк-эмитент, пиннинг на ЮKassa отклонял бы реальные платежи.

**Возврат из оплаты** определялся `url.includes('/billing/done')` — любая страница с этой подстрокой в query завершала оплату досрочно. Теперь сверяются origin и path.

**`X-Powered-By: Express`** снят.

## Проверки (fam)

- клиент: `tsc` чист, jest **856/856**
- сервер: `tsc` чист, тесты **434/434**
- внешняя проверка с физического интерфейса: 8787 недоступен, https 200
- подмена XFF через Caddy счётчик не сбрасывает (119→118→117→116)

author: thepig96
body:
Closes #410. Ticket 5 of 22 in slice 5 (#187), off `origin/main` = `2e61093` (#409 merged as PR #432).

`POST /api/v1/tasks` is **new** — the first `POST` the task surface has ever had. Registering a unit of work was a side effect of a flag on the billing-gated affordability call, so a metering-only tenant could not begin any at all. This is not a prefix move; it is a route being built.

## What lands

- **The key is required and its claim is permanent.** `UNIQUE(tenant, customer, idempotency_key)`, enforced by the database as a partial rule (nullable column, the top-up's exact shape) so historic rows sit outside it rather than colliding at a shared `""`. No release at terminal, no expiry window.
- **Replay versus conflict.** An identical repeat answers `200` with the original unit and `replayed: true`; a repeat describing a different unit answers `409 idempotency_key_conflict` **naming the request field that differs**. The comparison re-derives no policy — which is what makes the retry work forever rather than until a tenant next edits a default or retires a kind of work.
- **A replay reaches nothing.** The claim is read before the wallet checks, before the concurrency cap and before any grouping value is recorded.
- **A refused start spends nothing.** `DimensionService` splits into `resolve` (pure) and `admit` (resolve + record) over one shared walk, and the whole start runs in one transaction with every refusal raised.
- **The money-shaped half is conditioned on a wallet, inside the call** — never a product flag at the door, and conditioned on the tenant's *product* rather than on whether a `Wallet` row exists.
- **Today's creation path is retired, not redirected.** The flag and every field that served it are gone from the contract, the console and the SDK.

The COGS ceiling is unchanged in every particular — the only thing that moved is that its ladder is now one call rather than two places.

## ⚠ One obligation of §16 did NOT land, and it is not hidden

Obligation 1 — *"the prepaid reservation taken atomically with the job write"* — **is outstanding**. Nothing here reserves, and nothing can: the agreed price a reservation would be taken against arrives with the whole-unit pricing regime (#415). The AC that pairs with it is discharged by a test whose two sides are both zero, and both the test's name and the second commit's message now say exactly that rather than implying coverage. It is written at the address the strong claim will live at, because the day a start reserves is the day a silent second reservation becomes a double charge.

## The review pass (second commit)

Two axes over the build commit. It found a real defect and two guards that had silently lost their claims:

- A conflicting retry that **also changed altitude** answered `422` about grouping scope instead of `409` naming `parent_task_id`. The bag is now resolved *last*, below every comparison that needs no database. Measured with the old ordering restored.
- The **concurrency cap was no longer wired-tested** — deleting the call from the start gate left the whole suite green.
- A **billing customer with no `Wallet` row** lost its case; my first replacement was itself vacuous against the mutation it existed for, and was replaced with one that discriminates.
- Four **living documents** the build commit falsified (two tenant-facing guarantee docs, the audit-exempt enumeration in both of its homes), two registry values restated as literals, and a `concurrency_limit` literal that would have been a fourth file on another slice's spread ceiling.

## Verified

| | |
|---|---|
| platform | 4,269 passed / 3 skipped / 1,913 subtests |
| contracts | 681 |
| SDK | 346 / 4 subtests |
| console | 511 across 69 files, `tsc -b` clean, lint 0 errors |
| breaking gate | 86 breaks since `api-v1-launch`, **86 reviewed, 0 unreviewed** (run locally with the pinned oasdiff) |
| sweep | 1,696 swept / 2,100 tracked / 404 excluded across 7 declared rules; 27 terms in 92 sites |
| `units` | unmoved at 45 files / 123 occurrences |

`manage.py check` clean; `makemigrations --check --dry-run` reports "No changes detected"; every generated artifact regenerates byte-identically to what is committed; the SDK coverage ratchet is signed for its one new gap; no BOM or mixed line endings in any touched file.

⚠ **This opens the §23 window.** #411 deletes the retired correlation value across five surfaces and is the ticket immediately after this one. This commit adds no file spelling it — the backend entry stands at its **65-file** ceiling, with a file set identical to `main`.

author: glb99
body:
Slice two of the MVP, in Option B's language: a conversation column on the left, the scene in the middle, boundaries on the right.

**No new dependency.** The console still has exactly one runtime dependency, and dialogue 10 decided that a graph-drawing package runs hard against that grain. The layering below is about sixty lines of hand-rolled SVG.

## Packages, not modules

97 modules and 249 imports drawn plainly is a hairball, and the boundaries are stated *about* packages — so that is the level the scene works at. Which depth counts as a package is chosen per repository rather than fixed: a flat project has everything one segment down, this workspace has its features at three.

## Two layout defects, both found by looking at it

Neither is visible from a passing build.

**Sorting a band by module count ignores the graph.** The first render put nineteen packages wherever their size placed them, however far that was from everything they import — a hairball of long crossing beams. The fix is the classic barycentre heuristic: six alternating passes of *move to the average x of your neighbours*, then re-space. Crossings dropped visibly.

**Drum sub-labels sat inside the bottom disc.** A drum is 20px taller below the centre than a slab, and both used the same offset.

## Colour before text, four states

Crossed, holds, undecidable, inapplicable get four *treatments* rather than four shades of one. A contradiction is a thing to resolve, an undecidable boundary is a question nothing asked, an inapplicable one is a rule about code that is not here. A severity ramp would say the last two are milder versions of the first.

## What is deliberately absent

**The left column is not the agent.** It scopes the scene by name and says so. A column answering in sentences it had made up would be worse than one that admits its range — wiring it to a model is slice 3.

**Accepting a crossing is not offered.** That write route does not exist, and a button that only looked like it recorded a decision is worse than no button. The card says so.

**Its own palette, scoped to `.arch`.** The memory tabs have not been reworked, and two half-applied visual languages read worse than two whole ones.

## Four e2e tests, because a build renders nothing

Every failure this surface has is one a type checker cannot see: an empty `<svg>`, a layout that stacks every package on one point, a listener attached to a node that gets replaced on redraw. So the tests assert that glyph positions *differ* and that the scene actually dims — counting glyphs would pass while the scope did nothing.

Verified by hand against a real server with this repository added as a project: 97 modules, 19 packages, 18 tables, 249 imports, 4 boundaries holding and 4 undecidable.

`just check-all` green: 496 app, 111 agent. Playwright: 5 passed, 3 skipped (the graph specs need their own fixtures).

author: j4rs
body:
Fixes #1236.

`setPortAsync` reset `pdata.screenlogic` to defaults for `portId === 0` before reading anything from the request, and the only place it is written back from the body is guarded by `pdata.type === 'screenlogic'`. On a `local` RS-485 port that branch never runs, so **every** `PUT /app/rs485Port` erased `screenlogic.password` and reset `systemName`, regardless of what the caller sent. Nothing in the response or the log said so.

The fix is to seed the block only when it is absent — which is the form the `cfg.screenlogic` initialiser already uses about ninety lines further down in the same function:

```ts
if (portId === 0 && !cfg.screenlogic) { ... }
```

so this makes the two consistent rather than introducing a new convention.

### Verified

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, against v10.0.1 on a Raspberry Pi 4B.
- Before the change, on that box: `PUT /app/rs485Port` echoing the whole comms object with only `enabled` flipped took `screenlogic.password` from `1234` to `""`. Observed twice — the other time while moving `rs485Port` from `/dev/ttyUSB0` to `/dev/serial0`.

### No test, and why

`test/integration` is a comparison harness that boots njsPC against a live OCP over WebSocket and diffs the two, so it is not somewhere a `setPortAsync` regression fits, and I have no OCP to run it against. A unit test for this would mean adding a second, non-integration vitest project, which felt like the wrong thing to introduce uninvited on a first PR. Happy to add one in whatever shape you would prefer.

### Scope

One guard, one comment. I have not audited whether other `config.getSection` consumers reset sibling blocks the same way — worth a look, but not something I can test broadly.

author: jeremyfuksa
body:
## Summary

Every `STS` frame from a BC75XLT was dropped — **5,450 in a single session**, one per poll at 5 Hz.

## Cause

That model sends no status block:

```
BC75XLT   STS,1, 145.1300      ,,0,1
BC125AT   STS,...,<LCD cells>,...,SQL,MUT,_,_,_,_,SIG_LVL,_,BK_DIMMER
```

`find_sts_tail_start` requires **≥ 10 fields** because it anchors on that nine-field tail. A six-field frame can never match, so `parse_sts_frame` returned `None` every time.

## Why it went unnoticed through the entire BC75XLT bring-up

`STS` supplies `squelch_open` and `sig_lvl` **only as fallbacks** behind `GLG` and `PWR`, and this model answers both. Live state was correct all along.

So the cost was a wasted command round-trip five times a second on a 57600 link, and 5,450 warnings burying real ones. The warning text literally asked someone to verify the parser — *"firmware truncation is documented but verify the parser"* — and nobody had.

## The fix is structural, not model-gated

`parse_sts_frame` is pure and has no capability descriptor — the same constraint recorded for `parse_cin_response`. A frame too short to hold a status block, ending in two 0/1 digits, is unambiguous on its own terms.

The trailing pair is SQL and MUT, confirmed against two captures whose values matched the squelch/mute of the `GLG` frame taken alongside each:

```
STS,1, 145.1300      ,,0,1     GLG,145.1300,NFM,,,,,,0,1,,,
STS,1, 464.5000      ,,1,0     GLG,464.5000,NFM,,,,,,1,0,,,
                       ^ ^                          ^ ^
```

## Verified on hardware

The drop counter climbed ~50 every 36 seconds. Over 90 seconds after the fix it did not move, and live state stayed healthy (`145.13 MHz, sql_open true, rssi 38`).

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p bearpaw-api --lib` — 253 passed (4 new)
  - `a_short_sts_frame_parses_its_squelch_and_mute` — **confirmed to fail** with the short path removed, then reverted
  - `a_long_unanchorable_sts_frame_still_fails` — a long frame that fails to anchor is real corruption worth re-polling, not a short frame; collapsing the two would hide it
  - `a_short_sts_frame_needs_two_trailing_bits` — strictness
  - `a_long_sts_frame_still_reads_its_status_block` — the BC125AT path is untouched and still reads `SIG_LVL`, which the short path cannot supply
- [x] `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` / `cargo fmt` — clean

author: gaborbernat
body:
[#4045](https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/4045) asks for two things: a default for a labelled factor group, so `{factor:label}` does not need `{factor:label:fallback}` spelled out at every use site, and a way to run the matrix against a value it does not list, sketched there as `tox -f "django_version:'==6.0'"` or `TOX_F_django_version`.

The default half becomes a table form for a labelled group, carrying either `values` or a range alongside `default`: `{ django_version = { values = ["django42", "django50"], default = "django50" } }`. The default has to be one of the group's own factors, which is checked at load, so it can never resolve to a name no environment produces. It applies when no factor of the group is active in the current environment name, and a `{factor:label:fallback}` at the use site still wins over it.

The injection half arrives as `TOX_FACTOR_<label>`, read for labels the configuration declares. `env TOX_FACTOR_django_version=django61 tox run -e django-py314-django50` runs the environment the matrix generated while `{factor:django_version}` resolves to `django61`. The literal syntax from the issue, a version specifier passed through `-f`, does not work in tox's model, since labelled factor values are environment-name components and `>=4.2,<4.3` cannot be one. Keeping the override out of the name sidesteps that, at the cost that the environment name no longer tells the whole story of a run.

Closes #4045

author: cravenceiling
body:
Fixes PRODUCT-1573 (Sentry HOUSTON-APP-4Z1: `integration_connect` 400 `toolkit_no_auth` for `composio` — 73 users, 256 events).

## Root cause

Composio's catalog contains toolkits with no auth at all — including a toolkit literally named `composio`. Agents author in-chat connect cards (`#houston_toolkit=composio` links and `request_connection` steps) for it, and the chat card computed "connected" **only** from the connections list. A no-auth toolkit can never hold a connection row, so the card always offered a Connect button. Every click POSTed `/v1/integrations/composio/connect`, which correctly refuses with the typed 400 `toolkit_no_auth` — but the frontend treated that expected refusal as an unexpected error: Sentry report + a "could not be connected" red toast for something that was never broken.

(The Integrations page already hides no-auth toolkits, and host search already stamps their matches `connected` — the chat card was the remaining surface that ignored `noAuth`.)

## Fix

- **Card honors `noAuth`**: `isToolkitConnected` now counts a no-auth catalog toolkit as connected, so both in-chat connect surfaces render the Connected badge instead of a doomed Connect button (and the stepper's connect step auto-advances instead of soft-locking).
- **Typed refusal is an expected state**: a `toolkit_no_auth` 400 that still slips through (catalog not yet settled / catalog miss) is silenced from Sentry — mirroring the existing `toolkit_oauth_unavailable` handling — and surfaced as a friendly info toast ("{app} is ready to use", en/es/pt).
- `lib/toolkit-oauth-unavailable.ts` generalized into `lib/toolkit-connect-refusals.ts` (both typed refusal codes, shared body parsing).

## Repro (before)

1. In chat, get the agent to offer a connect card for a no-auth toolkit (e.g. ask it to "connect Composio"; the card renders with a Connect button).
2. Click **Connect** → red "could not be connected" toast, row shows failed, and a Sentry `integration_connect: engine request failed (400): {"code":"toolkit_no_auth"...}` event fires.

## Verify (after)

## Summary

This branch moves all Beacon node state into one service. It also rebuilds
the home page, and adds a public list of demonstration nodes.

## Changes

**Node state service** (`src/lib/services/`)
- `beacon-instance.ts` is the single owner of the node configuration.
  It persists the node list and the id of the selection.
- `beacon-instance-connect.ts` holds the network code. It tests a node,
  and runs one health monitor for the whole app.
- `beacon-instance-health.ts` holds the health in memory. The app persists
  no status and no latency.
- `beacon-instance-url.ts` normalizes a URL. The compare ignores case and
  a trailing slash.
- `stores/config.ts` is now a deprecated read-only bridge to the service.

**Status and latency**
- `BeaconInstanceStatus.svelte` shows the status of one node in three
  variants: full, compact and dot.
- The sidebar and the node modal show the status.
- The monitor checks every node each hour. A stale result triggers a check
  at the point of use.

**Home page**
- The page shows the current node, a launchpad, and a table of public nodes.
- `open-instances.ts` reads the public node list from
  `https://beacon-datalake.org/open-instances.json`. MARIS can change that
  list without a release of the app.
- The app does not persist a public node. The user adds one with the
  Connect button. A node that the user removes stays out.

**Style**
- Add the Manrope font as local woff2 files.
- Add a `--card-border` token, and give the card tokens for its background
  and border.
- Correct the H1 and H2 levels on all pages.
- Update the lucide icons, 
- Remove the line chart from the plot options.

## Breaking change

The app changes its local storage keys. It kept a full copy of the selected
node under `current-beacon-instance`. It now keeps the id under
`current-beacon-instance-id`. `beacon-instance.ts` migrates the old key once,
then deletes it. Users keep their nodes and their selection.

## Check

- Open the app with an empty local storage. The public node table must show
  a status for each node.
- Push Connect on a public node. The app must add the node and select it.
- Open the app with a selection from an older version. The selection must stay.
- Change the name of the selected node. The sidebar must show the new name.

author: zippy
body:
Adds a customer-maintained host allow-list to `holo_hosting_proof_of_service`, a guard that stops parked work being consumed unpaid, and an actionable shortfall message.

## What changed

**Allow-list (default-deny)** — an execution pays only the hosts its effective list names.

- Seeded by the new Fixed input `initial_allow_list`, which may be `[]` when the hosters aren't known at agreement creation.
- Updated by consumable `ParkedData` parks from the new `list_publisher` role, payload `allow_list_deltas: {add, remove}`. All adds apply before all removes, so the result never depends on park discovery order.
- Carried forward in each RAVE's `carryover.allow_list`, alongside the locked funds.

**Unpayable-invoice guard.** A settlement that would consume an invoice for a host the list does not name now throws instead. A successful no-payee run would delete those parks, and Rule 5 bars re-consumption, so the hosts' work would be destroyed unpaid and silently. One rule covers all three routes into that state: an unseeded list, a mid-period removal of a host that already parked work, and a mistyped key. The new optional `discard_unpayable` executor input settles anyway when dropping that work is deliberate. The guard sits **below** the `unlock` branch, so reclaiming funding stays available even while unpayable invoices are parked — that is the only recovery from a mis-set `funds_owner_pubkey`.

**`funds_owner_pubkey`** (new required Fixed input, the customer's key) is paid by `unlock`, receives the per-dimension metering credit, and gates whose deltas count. Both previously followed `executor_pub_key`, which pays the *harvester* under the canonical instance.

**Shortfall report.** The insufficient-funding error keeps its leading phrase but now reports the actionable shortfall (outstanding − available funding including any carried lock), accumulated in exact fuel arithmetic rather than f64.

## Scope of enforcement

Stating this precisely, because the obvious reading overclaims:

- **This run's deltas are chain-enforced.** Role qualification on parked links (#481) stops an unqualified agent from creating one — so qualify `list_publisher` to the customer at instantiation — and consumed-input binding ties each delta's value to the parked link it names, so the executor can neither forge a delta nor rewrite one.
- **The carried list is not.** It arrives through `previous_execution`, a `Custom` input. Validation re-derives `locked` from the real predecessor (Rule 7) and does nothing equivalent for `carryover`, so a dishonest executor can present a carried list the customer never authored and have it accepted. That is provable after the fact from the customer's signed parks, but it is not prevented. Closing it needs DNA-side re-derivation of `carryover`. Two mitigations today: re-state the full list as a fresh delta each period, which keeps the enforced portion current and the forgeable window short; or execute the agreement yourself (sole `AuthorizedExecutor` = the customer), which keeps carry-forward but gives up Holo-runs-settlement.

Delta entries are shape-checked in the script rather than in `runtime_input_signature.json`, deliberately: a schema violation fails Rule 2 *before* the script runs, so a single malformed park would deadlock every settlement, a consumable park being deleted only by a successful execution. Skipping in-script cannot wedge the agreement, and the guard above then surfaces the mistake loudly.

## Canonical instance

The Log Harvester is the sole executor — the agreement locks unspent funding, which the DNA rejects under `ExecutorRules::Any` — so Holo settles on its own cadence while the customer keeps exclusive control of funding and of the allow-list through their own parks.

## Verification

Exercised end to end against the real engine by the parent app's sweettest: unytco/unyt-app#487 (that PR carries the coverage detail).

author: myoun99
body:
유저: 「무언가를 바꾸는 동작은 기본 이럼 … **눈을 껏다키든 뭐든 다 언두**」,
then 「접기도 마찬가지야. 폴더든 어태치든」, then 「fx접기도 마찬가지고.
아무튼 **레이어에 있는 버튼 싹다**」.

The code agreed with the first one. This repo already had **eighteen**
undoable layer commands — name, mark, kind, effects, timesheet, timeline,
transform — while the eye, the opacity, the blend and the mute wrote
straight through the repository under "the visibility-toggle precedent".
Renaming a layer undid; hiding it did not.

### The nine buttons on a layer row

| button | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| eye · opacity · blend · mute | direct write | `UpdateLayerDisplayCommand` |
| twirl (folder **and attach**) | direct write | same command |
| lane twirl (the **fx** one) · onion | a `Set` on a notifier | `ToggleIdInSetCommand` |
| timesheet · fill reference · mark · fx switch | already undoable | unchanged |

Two names turned out to be one control each. **Attach-fold is the folder
fold** — the row's own comment says "They are one control: a row that
holds other rows, folding them", and both go through `Layer.collapsed`.
And **`onToggleLayerFx` is a switch, not a twirl**; the "fx 펼치기" the
user meant is the property-lane twirl.

### The precedent is narrower than its name

Two writers cite it and must NOT become undoable: export scope is a
setting, and paging a reference *"must never be undoable"* (유저 확정 ⑤㉑).
What they rely on is that **view state and settings** are not document
edits — still true. The wording is corrected so they carry their own
reason.

### Bulk paths are the other half

「일괄로 버튼 조작하고 언두하면 바꼈던 레이어들 **다 한번에 언두되야하는데
안됨**」. A bulk action that loops a per-layer call needs one press per
row — the same complaint in a new place. Seven bulk paths now land as one
`CompositeCommand`: Solo (both directions), the master opacity bar, and
the legend's visibility, blend, SE mute, opacity and **onion**.

⚠️The onion one was found by the user **after I said all nine were done**:
「조작끝낸 모든 레이어가 안돌아간단거야 설마?」. It wrote the set directly
and undid nothing. I had counted the row buttons and not re-counted their
bulk paths — the matrix has two axes, and adding an item means counting
both again.

### Two opposite decisions about restoring state, both correct

- `_DisplayState` restores **all four fields**: they are set one at a time
  on one layer, so the snapshot's other three are already whatever earlier
  commands left.
- `ToggleIdInSetCommand` restores **only this id's membership**: a set is
  shared by every row, so a whole-set restore would un-toggle a row the
  user touched afterwards.

### Preserved on purpose

**Per-use (T9)**: none of this walks `linkMirrorTargets`. A linked layer's
eye, opacity and blend belong to the use, not the group.

### The repo's ratchet caught a regression

`hidden_folder_is_hidden_test` holds a **downward** ratchet on how many
places re-derive "is this row shown". Splitting Solo into two batches read
the eye twice and pushed 11 → 13. One pass now builds both lists.
⚠️That scanner does not skip comments — after the loop was fixed the count
was still 12, and the offender was the symbol named inside the comment
explaining the fix.

### Verification

- `flutter analyze` (no arguments) — No issues found
- `dart run tool/affected_tests.dart` — 410 passed, exit 0 (`~1` benchmark)
- Mutation 3/3 KILLED, lines confirmed with `git diff --numstat`:
  | mutation | killed by |
  |---|---|
  | revert a batch to a per-layer loop | `ONE undo restored every row` **and** `two presses reached two actions` |
  | make `undo()` a no-op | all five of the original tests |
  | restore the whole set instead of one id | `the other row stayed where the later undo left it` |

author: ngovus-inetsoft
body:
### Problem

`SSOSettingsService.validateSAMLAttributes` put nine entries into its settings map — the six real
`onelogin.saml2.*` settings plus `saml.roles.attribute`, `saml.groups.attribute` and
`saml.orgID.attribute` — then built a `Saml2Settings` via `SettingsBuilder.fromValues` and called
`checkSettings()`.

`Saml2Settings` has no member for any of the three claim attributes, and `fromValues` silently drops
keys it does not recognise, so those three puts had no effect on the validation result. Dead code
rather than a defect in behaviour — but it read as though the claim names were validated on save,
which is the opposite of what happens.

### Verification that the puts are inert

`javap` against `java-saml-core-3.0.0.jar`, the version on the compile classpath:

```
javap -classpath java-saml-core-3.0.0.jar com.onelogin.saml2.settings.Saml2Settings
  -> only allowRepeatAttributeName / trimAttributeValues match "attribute"; nothing matches "claim"

javap -classpath java-saml-core-3.0.0.jar -p com.onelogin.saml2.settings.SettingsBuilder
  -> the *_PROPERTY_KEY constants cover onelogin.saml2.* only; no claim/attribute key
```

### Change

Removed the three puts and left a comment recording that nothing validates a claim name, so the code
no longer implies a check it does not perform. The `SreeEnv.setProperty` calls that actually persist
the three properties are untouched.

No behaviour change: `checkSettings()` sees the same six settings and returns an identical error list.
`validateSAMLAttributes` is private with a single caller (`updateSSOSettings`), its `boolean` result is
unchanged for every input, and `settingsMap` is a local built and consumed in the same method.

### Why not validate the claim names instead

A non-empty check would reject working configurations. `SAMLFilter.ClaimNames.current()` reads all
three properties with **no default**, and each use is null-guarded — blank legitimately means "do not
map roles / groups / org". Validating against IdP metadata is not possible at this point either: no
metadata is fetched at save time, the admin hand-enters the certificate and URLs.

Also worth noting for whoever picks up the related ticket: **#76163 (name claim read without a null
guard) appears already fixed** — `SAMLFilter` now has a null guard, a blank-value guard and a
special-character check, each producing a distinct `claimError` recorded in the session audit record.

### Testing

- `./mvnw -pl core compile` — clean.
- `./mvnw -pl core test -Dtest=SSOSettingsControllerTest` — 2/2 pass (delegation-only coverage; it does
  not exercise `validateSAMLAttributes`). No new test added for a dead-code deletion with a provably
  identical result.

author: chisanan232
body:
## Jira
FORNX-27

## Why
Deterministic claim verification is the epic's first practical verifier family. Implements the canonical aha scenario: agent claims "All tests passed", observed evidence has `exit_code != 0` → `CONTRADICTED`.

## Scope
`fornax-verify` crate: `Verifier` trait (`name`/`applies_to`/`verify`), `TestResultVerifier`. Pure — no I/O, no hidden state.

## Non-goals
Claim extraction (adapters' job, FORNX-28/29), storage (FORNX-26), other claim families (file-changed, git-state, http-health — future tickets).

## Changes
One commit: crate + workspace registration + 6 tests together (implementation and its tests are one semantic unit here, matching the archived bootstrap's granularity).

## Design decisions
`Verifier::verify` takes `&self, claim, evidence, capabilities` and returns an owned `Finding` — no mutation, no shared state, so replay (FORNX-49) can call it repeatedly against the same persisted inputs safely.

## Security / privacy
None — pure function, no I/O.

## Tests
6 unit tests: `Contradicted` on mismatched exit code, `Verified` on exit_code=0, `Unverified` when no test evidence exists, `Unavailable` when the runtime can't observe tool results, claim-text heuristic matching, and a **replay-determinism test** (added — the original bootstrap replay was missing this AC): re-running `verify()` against identical inputs twice yields an identical `Finding`.

`cargo test --workspace`: 6/6 pass. fmt/clippy clean.

## E2E / manual verification
N/A at this layer.

## AC checklist
- [x] Registry/provider seam exists (the `Verifier` trait) without dynamic-plugin overengineering
- [x] `tests passed` claim produces VERIFIED/UNVERIFIED/CONTRADICTED deterministically
- [x] Missing evidence never becomes failure by default (→ Unverified, not Contradicted)
- [x] Verifier version/name recorded on every Finding
- [x] Unit tests cover positive/negative/ambiguous cases
- [x] A replay test can recompute findings from the same inputs deterministically

## Known limitations
Only one verifier family (test-runner exit code) exists — file-changed/git-state/http-health verifiers are future tickets, not blocking.

## Rollback notes
Revert this PR; FORNX-24/26 are unaffected.

author: yoadelkayam
body:
Closes #96

## What & why

`echostash mcp audit --command "npx -y @acme/server"` spawned the server with our **entire** `process.env`, overriding the MCP SDK's `getDefaultEnvironment()` allow-list. Any audited server — usually somebody else's code — silently inherited `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `NPM_TOKEN`, etc. Since the whole pitch is "point it at a server you didn't write", this had to be fixed before the first npm tag.

## Changes

- **`@echostash/mcp`** — stdio servers now get the SDK allow-list (`PATH`, `HOME`, `SHELL`, … what a process needs to start) plus whatever is explicitly passed in `target.env`. Full inheritance only with the new `inheritEnv` flag on the target. Logic extracted into a pure `stdioEnv()` helper.
- **`@echostash/cli`** — `--env k=v` (repeatable) to hand specific variables to a `--command` server; `--inherit-env` as the explicit opt-in for the old behaviour.
- **Tests** — `packages/mcp/src/client.test.ts`: default excludes secrets, `--env` adds on top, `inheritEnv` forwards everything, plus `parseTarget` coverage (mcp: 10 → 15 tests).
- **Docs** — flags table + a short "Environment of a spawned server" section in `packages/cli/README.md`; one-line note in the root README.

## Verification

`pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` green.

End-to-end against a throwaway stdio server that records which variables it can see, with `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `NPM_TOKEN` exported in the parent shell:

| flags | server sees |
|---|---|
| *(default)* | `PATH,HOME` |
| `--env ACME_ENDPOINT=x` | `ACME_ENDPOINT,PATH,HOME` |
| `--inherit-env` | `OPENAI_API_KEY,NPM_TOKEN,PATH,HOME` |

## Affected packages
mcp, cli, docs

body:
## Summary

- add a POST-only, server-authorized Stripe Billing Portal entry for eligible Owner users
- require exactly one active client Account with an active Editor membership and an eligible Self Managed lifecycle phase
- create Portal Sessions from server-resolved Stripe Customer and Portal configuration identifiers only
- validate the returned Portal Session before performing a non-Turbo, full-page external redirect
- add a dashboard **Manage billing** action for eligible owners while preserving the existing plans link for everyone else
- document the required environment-specific Portal configuration and the staging validation checklist

Part of #59
Part of #60
Prerequisite for #172

## Authorization And Lifecycle Rules

Portal access is available only when the signed-in user is an Owner with exactly one active client Account, an active Editor membership, and an eligible Self Managed lifecycle phase:

- current entitlement
- payment recovery pending

Read-only owners, inactive users/accounts/memberships, internal users, ambiguous account selection, terminal lifecycle states, and unverified or non-Stripe subscriptions are denied before any Stripe request is made. This does not change existing write authorization or lifecycle evaluation.

## Security And Correlation

- accepts no browser-supplied Account, Customer, Subscription, Price, or Portal configuration identifiers
- resolves the existing Stripe Customer from the authorized local Subscription
- sends a trusted application return URL
- validates the returned Customer, Portal configuration, livemode, return URL, and hosted URL shape
- permits redirects only to HTTPS URLs on `billing.stripe.com`
- keeps Rails CSRF protection enabled and submits the Portal form without Turbo
- filters the short-lived Portal URL from Rails redirect notification logging
- shows generic user-safe errors while logging only the Stripe exception class
- does not mutate Account, Subscription, CheckoutAttempt, or entitlement state

## Configuration

This slice requires `STRIPE_BILLING_PORTAL_CONFIGURATION_ID`. Test/staging and production must use separate Stripe Portal configuration IDs matching their Stripe mode. The Portal configuration is created and maintained in Stripe, not by Boat Binder.

The approved first slice enables payment-method and invoice recovery, cancellation at period end, and supported reversal of scheduled cancellation. Keep plan switching, quantity changes, promotion codes, and new-trial behavior disabled. Cancellation must preserve access through the verified paid-through boundary. Stripe webhooks remain authoritative for local lifecycle synchronization.

## Verification

- `bin/rails test test/services/billing/stripe_portal_session_creator_test.rb test/integration/billing_portal_test.rb` — 16 runs, 167 assertions
- `bin/rails test test/services/billing/self_managed_entitlement_test.rb` — 30 runs, 176 assertions

- `bin/rails test test/integration/owner_write_entitlement_test.rb` — 8 runs, 158 assertions
- `bin/rails test test/integration/owner_read_lifecycle_test.rb` — 14 runs, 721 assertions

author: juanjocop
body:
Zara cerró `products-details` con una regla de edge de Akamai y la pasada diaria de prod murió
entera: el 31,5 % del catálogo (6.242 productos / 65.938 variantes) lleva sin ingerir desde el
26/08. El detalle pasa a leerse de la **ficha pública navegada con Chromium**.

## Que no es una regresión, y cómo se descarta

La coincidencia invita a sospechar del despliegue: prod saltó de `v0.7.2` a `v0.8.3` el 27/08 a
las 07:52 UTC y la pasada murió esa misma noche a las 23:15. No fue eso —
`git diff v0.7.2 v0.8.3 -- services/scraper/` toca solo `sfera.py`, `vigia.py` y tests de Sfera.
`zara.py` no se tocaba desde el 16/08 y con ese mismo código las pasadas del 22 al 26 salieron
`success`.

El 403 se reproduce con `curl` desnudo (o sea, **no** es el fingerprint TLS de httpx), desde dos
redes y desde un pod del cluster (**no** es la IP), en la primera petición en frío (**no** es el
rate) y con `bm_sz`/`_abck` ya sembradas. Es una regla del edge.

## Las tres salidas que planteaba la issue, medidas

| medición (28/08/2026) | resultado |
|---|---|
| `products-details` con httpx / curl / Chromium con cookies | **403** siempre |
| listado `category/{id}/products` con UA de navegador | **200** |
| ficha con httpx o `session.pedir()` | 200 pero **2,3 KB de interstitial** (`bm-verify`) |
| ficha **navegada** con Chromium | **200, ~490 KB, con `"sizes"`** |
| tallas en el listado | **no existen** |

O sea: la salida 1 (ficha con httpx) no existe —el escaparate entero, home incluido, está tras el
reto JS— y la salida 2 (rescatar del listado) pierde la talla, que es requisito del brief y la
unidad de `variant`. Las salidas 1 y 3 eran la misma.

La buena noticia: el JSON de `window.zara.viewPayload` tiene la **misma forma** que devolvía el
endpoint, así que `parse_detail_product` no cambia de cuerpo.

## La trampa que decide el diseño

El `discernProductId` de la ficha **no es el del listado**:

```
   listado        ficha  igual   seoPid   nombre
575623471    545456637  False  12414830  BAMBA BAREFOOT
575623472    545447180  False  12331830  ZAPATILLA DEPORTIVA REJILLA BAREFOOT
575623549    545447180  False  12331830  ZAPATILLA DEPORTIVA REJILLA BAREFOOT  <- dos ids -> una ficha
575623474    545422895  False  12440830  BAMBA ANIMAL PRINT BAREFOOT
575623936    545456659  False  12516830  BAILARINA BAREFOOT PIEL
545422640    545422640  True   12531730  BAILARINA BAREFOOT
```

Leerlo del payload —que es lo que hacía el parser, correctamente, mientras el endpoint devolvía el
id por el que se le preguntaba— habría dado de alta el catálogo entero como nuevo y mandado los
6.242 viejos a la baja, **sin romper ni un test de parseo**. La identidad la pone ahora el
`ListingEntry`.

Lo que **sí** es estable, medido comparando el fixture del endpoint muerto contra la ficha de hoy
del mismo producto: los ids de color, los de talla y los **11 skus** son idénticos. Así que
`retailer_variant_id` no se mueve y **el cambio no fuerza ninguna pasada en frío**.

## El sondeo de bajas, y la comprobación de identidad

`probe_alive` usaba la misma URL bloqueada, así que estaba igual de muerto. Pasa a navegar la
ficha, y ahí **el status deja de servir**: un id inventado responde 200 con la página de búsqueda.
Decide `clasificar_ficha()`, y solo su señal positiva de retirada autoriza una baja; interstitial,
timeout o rediseño salen sin veredicto.

El segundo commit sale de la auditoría de `revisor-robustez-scraper`: al moverse a la ficha, Zara
pasó del grupo de los que sondean **por id** al de los que sondean **por URL**, y el contrato de
`SupportsAliveProbe` le exige a ese grupo comprobar que lo servido es lo pedido antes de emitir
`ALIVE`. Sin eso, el 301 de un id reciclado (medido en Deditos, #454) dejaría un producto retirado
en catálogo para siempre. La comprobación vive en `clasificar_ficha()` y no solo en el sondeo,
porque la fase 2 la necesita por otro motivo: escribiría el precio de otra prenda bajo nuestro id.

Se añade además el tope de fichas seguidas ilegibles que Hipercor ya tenía — la red que justamente
faltaba cuando esto pasó: aborta diciendo que la tienda no nos deja ver, en vez de guardar un
catálogo mutilado que parece sano.

## Verificación

- Pasada real contra la tienda (2 hojas): **57 productos / 618 variantes / 488 en stock**, y
  **0 fichas ilegibles** — la identidad casa en las 57.
- Segunda pasada seguida: **0 altas, 0 bajas**, 57 sin cambios. Es la prueba directa de que la
  identidad no se rompió.
- Sondeo real: vivo → `ALIVE`, id inventado → `DEAD`, **slug falso con id vivo → `ALIVE`** (la
  llave es el id, no el slug, así que un cambio de slug no descataloga), URL sin forma de ficha →
  sin veredicto.
- `ruff` + `ruff format` + `mypy` + `pytest` con `TEST_DATABASE_URL` puesto (tests de ingesta
  incluidos): verde.

## Va con esto, en el repo de manifiestos

Este CronJob era el perfil httpx ligero y ya no puede serlo. PR aparte en
`k3s-local-apps-manifests`: `emptyDir` con `HOME`/`TMPDIR`, 512Mi/2Gi, y
`activeDeadlineSeconds` de 7200 a **14400** por aritmética (1,3 s por ficha × 6.242 = ~2h15m, que
no cabía en 2h). **Sin ese PR, la pasada en el cluster no arranca el navegador.**

## Lo que queda fuera, dicho

- Una prenda cuya ficha no se pueda leer no recibe `last_seen_at` y suma racha de ausencia
  (`_advance_missing` decide por SQL sin mirar el listado). No llega a baja —el sondeo fallará
  igual y `blocked_ids` la protege— pero se queda congelada. Se deja rastro en el log de la fase 2;
  darle una columna de `scrape_run` le vendría bien también a Hipercor y va en issue aparte.
- El vigía comparará contra su propio histórico y dirá durante unas semanas que Zara «nos deja
  entrar más despacio». Es cierto y esperado: pasa de AJAX a navegar. Solo avisa, no abre issue.

Refs #634

author: fastrevmd-lab
body:
Relates to #89. Does not close it — the default path is still the rule list.

#89 was stuck on a policy question, not a technical one: replacing the hand-written validation rules with a conforming parse costs a runtime dependency, and #77 is actively trying to shrink the graph. **Making it opt-in dissolves that.**

```
default              142 crates
strict-validation    143 crates
```

## What it does

`validate_xml_fragment_strict` asks a conforming parser whether the fragment actually embeds into a well-formed document, so the property holds by construction rather than by enumeration.

The tests assert **both halves** — that the rule list accepts three specific inputs and that this rejects them:

| input | rule list | strict |
|---|---|---|
| `<a b="&cmp;"/>` — undefined entity in an attribute | accepts | rejects |
| `<a b=""/>` — out-of-range char ref | accepts | rejects |
| `<a xmlns:p="urn:x" xmlns:q="urn:x" p:x="1" q:x="2"/>` — duplicate *expanded* names | accepts | rejects |

All three are from `fuzz/README.md`'s residual table. If the rule list ever grows to catch one, the test fails loudly rather than passing quietly.

## The fragment is embedded verbatim — no rewriting, no synthesised bindings

That reverses two earlier versions of this branch, and the reversal is the interesting part.

**v1** scanned prefixes with `Name` rules, which include `:`, so it walked backwards across the colons *inside a URI* and synthesised an illegal `xmlns:urn:ietf=`. It rejected `<filter xmlns="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:netconf:base:1.0"/>` — the most ordinary fragment in NETCONF. The fuzz oracle in #90 had already hit and fixed exactly this; rewriting it from the same understanding reproduced it.

**v2** fixed the scan and added more surgery — renaming the reserved `xml` prefix, deriving a collision-free URI stem. All of it operates on the fragment as a **string**, and string surgery is defeatable by encoding: a URI spelling `xml:` literally alongside one spelling it `xml:` had only one side rewritten, converting a real duplicate-expanded-name error into a pass. Closing that means decoding entities and tracking QName positions — reimplementing the parser this function exists to delegate to.

**v3** removes the surgery. Verified 14 cases in both directions, zero wrong, including the encoded-URI case v2 got wrong — now caught precisely because there is nothing left to defeat.

The cost, stated rather than hidden: a fragment relying on a prefix the *envelope* declares stops being checked at that point, since roxmltree reports only the first error. That is the safe direction — incomplete checking never rejects valid configuration, a rewriting bug does — and the rule list still covers the whole fragment.

## One rule the strict path cannot cover

`xmlns:p=""` undeclares a prefixed namespace, which Namespaces in XML §5 forbids and roxmltree 0.20 accepts. The attribute iteration needed to see it already happens in `validate_attributes`. `xmlns=""` stays legal — it resets the default namespace.

623 tests pass, clippy `-D warnings` clean, fmt clean.

author: liyanfeng129
body:
## Why

Promoting the analytics fix (#40) to `main` ran Production Release in **22s**
and skipped every deploy job. `main` had the fix; nothing had run it, so
production kept serving the deployment built the old way and analytics stayed
uncollected.

```
✓ Detect production changes        8s
✓ Production validation gate       2s
- Webapp validation                     (skipped)
- Webapp deployment / Deploy production (skipped)
```

Change detection emitted `validate_webapp=true` but `deploy_webapp=false`.

## The gap

`.github/workflows/webapp-release.yml` was classified validate-only. That is the
right instinct for a workflow file — normally it describes how the site is
*checked*, not what the site *is*.

But this job also defines **how the deploy is performed**. A change to it only
reaches production by deploying. Validating alone leaves the previous deployment
in place and the change inert — silently, because the site keeps working and
nothing fails.

## The change

One line: `webapp-release.yml` now also sets `deploy_webapp=true`.

Verified against the exact range that was skipped (`8868d028..85751352`), which
now yields `deploy_webapp=true`. Re-checked a frontend-only change and a
migration change to confirm their classifications are unchanged.

## Note

The analytics fix is already live — it was deployed via `workflow_dispatch`
after this skip was found. This PR prevents the next change to deploy behaviour
from silently not deploying.

body: ## Product contract (Aaron Crain, 2026-08-28) Join must be seamless and grant full site access. 1. Adding an angler email (on register or Invite) fires the **Join the boat** email. 2. Click the link → create account or sign in if needed → on that boat. 3. After join they can see the team **and** have full site features (Livewell post, no second unlock, no PIN, no extra confirm gate). 4. Join still does not make them captain and is still not the paid Angler roster. Still locked (unchanged): - The person who creates the team adds the captain and invites teammates. Creator is not assumed to be the captain. Captains might never log in. - Email on a seat is optional. Name-only walk-ups still use PIN / shared link. - `EMAIL_FROM` / `RESEND_API_KEY` untouched. From-address stays Official-ish Tournament ``. - No Venmo/payment changes. Teams stay unpaid. - Not piled onto PR #7 (unlock 307 → `/catches?unlocked=1`). This branches from `main`. ## What was wrong - Register stored `Angler.email` only. Invite mail fired only from My team Invite (`POST /api/team/invite`). - `/join` required signup/signin, created `TeamMember`, landed `/team?joined=1`. - Join did **not** set `jenns40_event`. - Livewell post still needed confirmed account email. Event unlock (captain magic link or Friday PIN) was a second path. QA smoke treated join ≠ unlock / ≠ paid roster, so it passed on `/team?joined=1` and never asserted a Livewell post after join. ## What this PR does Hypothesis checked: posting does **not** currently read `jenns40_event` (`EventPinGate` / `requireEventUnlock` are unused on Livewell). The live post gate is `emailVerified` (`CatchLogger` + `requireVerifiedUser` on `POST /api/catches`). Granting the cookie alone would not unblock posting. Smallest matching change: - Register now sends Join the boat for each unique angler email (same Resend path as Invite). Name-only seats get no mail. - Invite from My team is unchanged. - A successful `POST /api/team/join` still only creates `TeamMember`, then grants `jenns40_event` **and** marks the account email verified so Livewell post works with no PIN, no second unlock, and no confirm-email panel. - Re-clicking a valid join link grants the same access if they are already on the boat. - Join does not set captain, `claimedByUserId`, Angler roster rows, or payment status. ## Test plan 1. Register an unpaid **TEST QA** team with one emailed angler + one name-only seat. Do not mark paid. Do not rewrite live teams. 2. Confirm the emailed angler receives **Join the boat** (register-time, not only My team Invite). Name-only seat gets no email. 3. Emailed angler clicks Join the boat, creates an account (or signs in), and lands on the boat (`/team?joined=1`). 4. That joiner can open Livewell and post **without** PIN, captain unlock, or a confirm-email step. Expect `Set-Cookie: jenns40_event=…` on the join POST and a verified account so `POST /api/catches` is not `needsConfirmation`. 5. Name-only still needs PIN or the shared invite link — they do not get Join the boat. 6. Joiner is **not** captain and is **not** on the paid Angler roster. Team stays unpaid. Creator still adds the captain and invites. Unit coverage (`npm test`, 26/26): emailed-vs-name-only recipients, Join the boat link verifies as a team invite, join contract (unlock + verify email, not captain, not roster).
