author: scotwells
body:
A consumer listing locations in their own control plane sees one condition, `Available`. It says a location is unusable. It never says why.

The condition that says why is `Ready`, and we only write it on the platform Location, which the consumer cannot read.

`datumctl get locations` shows the cost. Its READY and REASON columns read a `Ready` condition, so they render blank on every location a consumer sees, including ones that are fully available.

This PR mirrors the platform Location's conditions onto the projection, next to `Available`. Mirroring runs on every reconcile, not just at creation, so a status change on the platform copy reaches the consumer.

`Available` stays this reconciler's verdict over the three gates. We drop any `Available` that arrives from the source.

`LocationBinding` keeps its current status. It has its own contract, which the network-services operator reads.

Follows #78, which added the `locations.miloapis.com` projection. Related: milo-os/locations#14, datum-cloud/infra#4283.

## Test plan

Four new tests. Full suite and `golangci-lint` pass.

To check the tests are not vacuous, I reverted the controller and re-ran them. The mirroring and source-tracking tests fail without the change. The `LocationBinding` and `Available`-ownership tests pass either way by design, guarding behaviour the change had to preserve.

author: guillaume-lombardo
body:
### 1. Objective

Allow authenticated users to convert Markdown to DOCX, PDF, or both without first creating or selecting a Word template. Template-free jobs use Pandoc's native default reference document while the existing immutable versioned-template path remains available.

This removes an unnecessary onboarding blocker and keeps job identity, persistence, traceability, and both deployment profiles explicit and reproducible.

### 2. Scope of Changes

- Add an explicit `Pandoc default` template mode to the conversion UI and API.
- Accept either no template identifiers or a complete immutable template/version pair; reject partial pairs.
- Persist nullable template pairs in SQLite and PostgreSQL with database-level integrity guards.
- Run Pandoc without `--reference-doc` for template-free conversions.
- Extend PDF traceability to schema v2 with an explicit template mode while retaining strict v1 read compatibility for historical versioned jobs.
- Preserve pre-T29 idempotency replay compatibility for versioned jobs.
- Add unit, functional, SQLite/PostgreSQL integration, browser, container smoke, and both-profile final-image E2E coverage.
- Update product, API, user, architecture, job, template, PDF, Pandoc, observability, and deployment documentation.

No template administration workflow is removed or deprecated.

### 3. Technical Details

- `template_id` and `template_version_id` form one nullable all-or-none pair throughout domain and persistence boundaries.
- `TemplateMode` exposes `pandoc-default` or `versioned` without synthetic identifiers.
- The frozen-template processor bypasses the resolver only for a complete absent pair. Versioned jobs still resolve and verify exact immutable bytes.

- The browser clears a preselected preferred/fallback template when `Use Pandoc default` is chosen.

### 4. Impact Analysis

- Backward compatible: existing versioned jobs and legacy idempotency replays remain supported.
- Database migration required on upgrade; downgrade refuses data that cannot satisfy the old non-null contract.
- No material performance impact.
- Security boundaries remain unchanged: authentication, authorization, upload validation, scanning, leases, and retention still apply.
- Traceability is stricter: workers reject manifests whose mode, template ID, resolved version, or SHA-256 do not match the claimed job and verified template.
- Operators do not need a bootstrap template for new conversions.

### 6. Code Quality Checklist

- Error behavior and traceability rejection are explicit and deterministic.

Пятый прогон отработал правильно и упал **по деловой причине**: квота аккаунта на число одновременно работающих серверов исчерпана. Занимают её обе боевые ноды. Это первый отказ не по моей вине.

## Что чинится

Печатается каждая строка из ответа, где бы она ни лежала, кроме полей с именами вроде password, secret, key, token.

Проверено на трёх формах ответа:

| форма | новая версия | прежняя |
|---|---|---|
| сообщение в корне | печатает | молчит |
| в массиве объектов | печатает | молчит |
| вложено на два уровня | печатает | молчит |

Секреты не печатаются ни в одной.

Это третий раз, когда я предположил форму чужого ответа — и на сей раз в коде, вся работа которого объяснять две предыдущие ошибки.

author: pickysaurus
body:
Nothing else was safe until there was a way to know something broke. All five workstreams shipped in 4.0.0. Two bugs surfaced that were not in the plan: the tsconfig omitted lib, so TypeScript pulled the DOM library into a Node-only project and Response.json() resolved to any — every fetch body trusted without anyone deciding to; and expires_in is optional on every OAuth response we model, so Date.now() + expires_in * 1000 yielded NaN, and since every comparison against NaN is false, a token that arrived without it would never have been refreshed.

Build pipeline
The build is clean.cjs → tsc → add-js-extensions.cjs → three copyfiles calls. That middle step regex-rewrites every quoted relative path in dist/ to append .js, because moduleResolution: "node" is paired with ESM output.

Switch to moduleResolution: "bundler" and delete add-js-extensions.cjs and clean.cjs — two files, ~90 lines of homegrown post-processing.
Better: replace tsc emit with tsup or esbuild. Seconds become milliseconds, and the asset copy becomes one config line.
Fix the copy-assets globs — copyfiles -f flattens and the globs are single-level, so any new subdirectory is silently dropped from dist.
Drop path (a deprecated shim for the Node builtin) and jsonwebtoken (zero references in src/). Move eight @types/* packages to devDependencies.
Delete build.sh — it installs @discordjs/uws and request@^2.34 and runs a non-existent index.js. A pre-TypeScript fossil.
Logging
Replace the hand-rolled 36-line Logger with pino: structured JSON in production, real levels (which fixes B18 and B19 by construction), and redaction paths for values, nexus_access, nexus_refresh, discord_access, discord_refresh — which fixes S5 without hunting call sites. Child loggers carry the shard ID, so the module-level mutable logger singleton disappears. Then sweep the 20 remaining raw console.* calls.

Errors
There are five mutually incompatible conventions in the data layer alone: swallow-and-return-empty; mutate-the-caught-error-and-rethrow; Promise.reject with a string or a bare false; wrap-in-a-generic-Error-discarding-the-cause; and handleDatabaseError, which is typed to return string — so throw handleDatabaseError(err) throws a bare string with no stack.

One taxonomy: AppError with cause, a code, and isOperational. Always throw Error subclasses, never strings, never booleans. Callers must be able to tell "no results" from "the API is down" — right now they cannot, because around 18 query files return [] on failure.

Tests
Add vitest. The single biggest obstacle first: api/dbConnect.ts:3 imports logger from ../DiscordBot, so the data layer cannot be imported without booting the Discord client module. Breaking that import is a two-line change that unlocks everything else. Then start where the value is highest — the 731-line embed builders in types/subscriptions.ts (pure functions, zero I/O), the parsing helpers in api/util.ts, and the GraphQL modules against recorded fixtures, which catches B8, B9 and B10.

CI
The current workflow builds and pushes a Docker image on every master push with no lint, no typecheck, no test, and only a :latest tag. Add a required checks job, tag images with the git SHA so rollback is possible, and pin joelwmale/webhook-action@master to a commit.

author: dhobi
body:
Closes #319, closes #320 — the two things still visibly wrong when a port-written `.rtd` loads in `DF.EXE`. Both turned out to be fields the port never wrote, and both were found by reading the original's actor draw path as those issues prescribed.

## Cast +18 is `is3d` (#319, and half of #320)

The props' documented field, same offset. The per-actor draw gate at `0x414fd0` branches on it before anything else:

- **nonzero** → the world path: the actor's set (+100) is strcmp'd against the standpoint's set name (c1+482) — **the out-of-room filter the issues went looking for** — and the screen rect is recomputed by projecting the world position and scale. The cached rect at +56…+70 is where the result is stored, never a load-time input, which is why correlating it against the corpus went nowhere.
- **zero** → the screen-anchored path at `0x4151f8`: no set filter, no projection, the rect read straight off the anchor words +20/+22 — (0, 0) in a never-placed record — at raw per-mille scale.

So one stale bit presented as two bugs: a fragment of a town horse in the top-left of an interior, and a 3.6× Mayor's wife. Corpus: no visible record in the 61 shipped saves holds 0 here (2,650 records), and 1,521 invisible ones hold 1 — it is a sticky "has ever been placed". The writer now sets it for every actor the port has placed; the round-trip test asserts it and a corpus canary holds the invariant.

## c1+430 is the room's camera height (the hover in #320)

Every drawn actor goes through the projection at `0x433c60`, whose camera is the c1 trio +472/474/476 — eye x, y, **height**. A load rebuilds x/y from the grid cell (`0x433d20`) but copies the height from **c1+430**, which is the set header's own `eyeHeight` (c0+0x1a): 62 in the town, 130 upstairs at the mayor's, 230 in the laundry. A save patched from a town base kept 62, so `mayupper`'s cast hung `(130 − 62) · focal / depth` pixels up the wall.

The writer now sends the room's `eyeHeight` and `cameraSetback` (c1+428, 64 everywhere) alongside the registers and palette it already sends, and writes the eye trio the way all 61 shipped saves hold it — cell centre pushed back 64 along the facing, at the room's height (zero mismatches corpus-wide, now a test).

## Verified in the original

Byte-patched A/B saves loaded in `DF.EXE`: the +18 fix alone drew a clean room with the Mayor's wife still hovering; adding +430 and the trio stood her on the floor.

## Ce que fait la PR

`GET /api/guilds/mine/risalat` (et `PUT .../turn`, qui rend la même charge via `RisalatBoardProvider::of()`) rend désormais `nextRevealAt` : le prochain rendez-vous hebdomadaire, calculé par `RisalaRules::nextRevealAfter($now)` où `$now` est l'instant de la requête — jamais dérivé de `turn->deadline()` ni d'une dernière bascule enregistrée, pour qu'une bascule ratée ou en retard ne rende jamais un rendez-vous déjà passé.

Le champ est en dernier dans `RisalatBoard`, `RisalatResource` (constructeur et `toArray()`) et le schéma `Risalat`, toujours présent et non nullable — même raison que `loot`/`streak`/`unlockableNodes` dans `SyncSummary`. Le schéma OpenAPI porte les deux raisons du ticket : pourquoi il est toujours là, et pourquoi rendre `reveal_day`/`reveal_hour`/`week_timezone` inviterait le client à diverger.

## Cases cochées

- [x] `RisalatBoard` porte l'instant, `RisalatResource` le rend, `make openapi` le décrit.
- [x] Calculé à partir de l'instant de la requête, pas de la dernière bascule enregistrée.
- [x] Test : une guilde sans Risāla ni tour rend quand même `nextRevealAt`, strictement dans le futur.
- [x] Test : quand un tour existe, `nextRevealAt` vaut `turn.deadline` — avec une note dans le test qui rappelle que cette égalité n'est vraie que parce que la mise en place bascule à l'heure, pas un invariant du système (le ticket le dit déjà autrement).

Rien du périmètre laissé de côté. « Ce qu'on ne fait pas » respecté : ni `reveal_day`, ni `reveal_hour`, ni `week_timezone` ne sont rendus, et `config/game/v1/community.yaml` n'a pas bougé.

## Un point à signaler, pas un choix caché

Le test « `nextRevealAt` vaut `turn.deadline` » compare les deux valeurs comme des instants (`assertEquals` sur deux `DateTimeImmutable`, via le comparateur de dates de PHPUnit) plutôt que comme des chaînes identiques : `turn.deadline` est rendu dans le fuseau où l'entité `Risala` a été hydratée, `nextRevealAt` dans celui de `RisalaRules::$weekTimezone` (`nextRevealAfter()` convertit explicitement via `setTimezone()`). Les deux représentent le même instant avec un offset ATOM différent — ce n'est pas un choix structurant, juste la bonne façon de comparer deux dates qui ne sont fausses ni l'une ni l'autre.

## À vérifier

- `make qa`, `make test` (825 tests) et `make openapi` passent tous ; `git diff openapi.yaml` ne contient que le nouveau champ et sa description.
- Rien à vérifier contre un vrai client au-delà de ce que le ticket demandait déjà : la valeur est un contrat de forme (un instant ATOM), pas une mécanique nouvelle à observer en usage réel.

Closes #202

author: kreucher
body:
### Problem

On slower dashboard clients, the Home Assistant header and sidebar can remain visible after View Assist starts, even though the client is authenticated and already on the configured View Assist home view.

The frontend installs its `location-changed` listener only after `connect()` completes. The initial `registered` configuration can arrive during that connection, navigate to the home view, and emit `location-changed` before the listener exists. The only initial hide pass is therefore timing-dependent.

### Changes

- Register the connection and location lifecycle listeners before connecting.
- Reapply the configured display hiding when each configuration payload is delivered, including initial registration.
- Fix the `hide_sidebar_timerout` typo so retries replace the intended timeout.
- Fix the malformed `--ha-sidebar -width` cleanup property name.

This keeps the existing hiding implementation and event model; it only makes the initial application deterministic and fixes two cleanup/retry typos in the same code path.

### Validation

- `node --check custom_components/view_assist/js_modules/view_assist.js`
- `git diff --check origin/dev...39fe305`
- Deployed commit `39fe305` as a reversible Home Assistant frontend-module canary.
- Verified three physical Android WebView displays (two Echo Show 8 devices and one Echo Show 5) remained authenticated on `/view-assist/baby` for an approximately 24-hour soak.
- At the soak gate, all three showed the View Assist hamburger with no Home Assistant header or sidebar. Each had one foreground VACA activity, one WebView, an active Home Assistant connection, HTTP 200 reachability, and no VACA fatal teardown loop.
- The module served by Home Assistant matched the patched source byte-for-byte (SHA-256 `57aa63695d22cfc98db82c5755a09b7df61a256dd885dfc953e3fc770b500e8e`).
- Bounded device and Home Assistant logs showed no relevant View Assist/frontend initialization errors.

The physical screenshots and secret-safe maintenance summaries are retained locally; they are not attached because the dashboard contains private camera imagery.

### Related work

PR #253 updated the Home Assistant 2026.6 sidebar variable name. This change preserves that behavior and fixes its cleanup spelling while addressing the separate initial-registration race. No overlapping open issue or pull request was found as of 2026-08-27.

### Non-goals

- No backend, navigation, dashboard, authentication, VACA, or network behavior changes.
- No new automatic recovery or polling.
- This finite soak validates the observed startup path on the stated devices; it is not a claim that all client timing combinations are covered.

### Compatibility and rollback

The change uses the existing events, timers, and display-hiding methods and does not change the configuration schema or public API. Rollback is a one-file revert to the previous `view_assist.js`; the pre-change deployed module was retained and verified separately during the canary.

### AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used during the investigation, implementation, validation scripting, evidence analysis, and drafting of this report. All reported measurements came from the stated physical test systems. Nicholas Kreucher reviewed the proposed change and final report before submission.

author: claude[bot]
body:
**CLI change, no output change for the programmatic API and none for the CLI when no Prettier config is in scope:** the CLI now applies the closest Prettier configuration for the generated `.d.ts` (resolved for the output path; a virtual `.d.ts` next to the input when writing to stdout, `<cwd>/stdin.d.ts` for piped input). Explicit `--style.*` / `--no-style.*` flags still win; a configured `parser` is ignored so output is always parsed as TypeScript; `overrides` keyed to `*.ts`/`*.d.ts` apply and ones keyed to `*.json` do not; `--cwd` stays for `$ref` resolution only and does not move the lookup. A configuration that cannot be loaded (invalid syntax, a plugin that is not installed) fails the run with exit code 1, where master exits 0.

Closes #217.

This is #729 by @hafzism brought onto current master. Their commit `001d52d` is kept as-is in the history (authorship and message untouched); on top of it sit one merge commit and one small fix:

- **Merge commit** — the only textual conflict was `CHANGELOG.md` (both sides appended under `## Next`); it is left as master has it and the entry moves into this description (see *Changelog* below), the same as the other open PRs.
- **`src/cli.ts`, 9 lines** — a semantic conflict with #766, which registered `style.singleQuote` as a minimist boolean. A registered boolean defaults to `false` when the flag is absent, and with #729's `{...prettierConfig, ...argv.style}` merge that default shadowed a project's `singleQuote: true` (two of #729's own tests caught it: `output Prettier config takes precedence` and `Prettier overrides for the generated .d.ts apply`). The fix drops the registration and instead coerces the strings `'true'`/`'false'` to booleans for every `--style.*` flag right after parsing, so #766's three spellings (`--no-style.singleQuote`, `--style.singleQuote false`, `--style.singleQuote=false`) keep passing and an absent flag no longer overrides the config.

Everything else — `src/cli.ts` config loading, README, the five CLI tests and their fixtures — is #729's diff verbatim.

From #729:

> - resolve the closest Prettier configuration for the generated `.d.ts` output path
> - use a virtual `.d.ts` beside the input when writing to stdout, or `<cwd>/stdin.d.ts` for piped input
> - ignore a discovered `parser` so generated output is always parsed as TypeScript
> - let explicit `--style.*` flags override discovered configuration values
> - keep the programmatic `compile` API behavior unchanged
> - isolate existing CLI snapshots behind a default-style fixture config, so this PR causes no unrelated snapshot churn
>
> This brings the earlier approach from #278 forward against the current v16 CLI and test suite.

`bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run build:server && CI=true bun run test` (Bun 1.4.0): **459 pass / 0 fail**, 232 snapshots, snapshot files unchanged from master `d86f285`; `format-check` clean. The CLI × Prettier-config scenario table (no config, `.prettierrc`, `--style.*`/`--no-style.*` precedence, `--cwd` elsewhere, input elsewhere, stdin, invalid YAML, `overrides` for `*.json` vs `*.d.ts` with and without `-o`, missing plugin, top-level `parser`, `.prettierrc.yaml`) reads the same as it did on #729's head, and byte-identical to master where no config is in scope.

Supersedes #729, which can close once this lands.

## Changelog

For `CHANGELOG.md` under `## Next` (kept out of the diff so armed PRs do not conflict on that file):

- New (CLI): Automatically load the closest Prettier configuration for generated output; explicit `--style.*` flags still take precedence. A configuration that cannot be loaded, such as one with invalid syntax or a missing plugin, now fails the CLI run (#217, #729 by @hafzism)

author: ntcoding
body:
## Problem

Architecture documentation generation was owned by `apps/docs` even though it is standalone architecture tooling. This mixed the documentation site with reusable architecture analysis and left no CLI boundary for the existing architecture summary and pull request architecture diff use cases.

## Proposed outcome

The existing architecture summary and pull request architecture diff are exposed through a standalone `living-documentation` CLI subdomain. The tool follows the same role, lint, test, typecheck, coverage, and workspace conventions as every other package.

## Changes

- Added the `living-documentation` domain model and query use cases for architecture summaries and pull request architecture diffs.
- Added a standalone CLI with feature entrypoints and shell command wiring.
- Moved the existing analysers and tests out of `apps/docs`, then rewired documentation generation and the pull request workflow to use the CLI.
- Structured the pull request architecture report around subdomains, entrypoints, command use cases, query use cases, external clients grouped by client, query models, domain changes, and explicit uncategorised fallthrough changes.
- Marked new subdomains as `NEW` and made entrypoint and use case details collapsed by default.
- Upgraded Nx to 23.1.1 and applied its migrations.
- Included every new project in the standard lint, typecheck, test, Knip, and role enforcement conventions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The CLI exposes the existing architecture summary use case.
- [x] The CLI exposes the existing pull request architecture diff use case.
- [x] Documentation generation and the pull request architecture workflow use the standalone CLI rather than implementations owned by `apps/docs`.
- [x] The architecture review marks `living-documentation` as `NEW` and presents the agreed hierarchy with collapsed entrypoint and use case details.
- [x] External client changes are grouped by their configured client location.
- [x] All `living-documentation` projects participate in the repository role and lint conventions.
- [x] The full repository verification suite passes.

## Validation

- `CI=true pnpm verify`: passed.
- Role check: passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- All three `living-documentation` projects retain 100% test coverage.
- Production CLI smoke tests for both commands passed.
- Pull request CI, browser tests, security checks, SonarCloud, and the architecture comment workflow passed.

## Design decisions and constraints

- The shell owns CLI parsing and wiring. Feature entrypoints invoke the application use cases and format their responses.
- Command and query use cases are separate sibling sections in the generated review.
- External client grouping follows the repository role configuration and client directory, with no inferred grouping.
- Architecture dependencies are deliberately not included in this change.
- `Uncategorised changes` is retained only as an explicit fallthrough reminder.

## Out of scope

- Architecture dependency reporting.
- New architecture analysis use cases beyond the existing summary and pull request diff.

  - Added a living documentation tool for generating architecture summaries and pull-request architecture differences.

  - Improved TypeScript architecture discovery with relationship tracking and support for additional source file types.
- **Documentation**
  - Updated the domain guide with living-documentation capabilities and newly available CLI use cases.

author: kyung83
body:
Adds a Cloudflare/D1-controlled Twilio breakdown texting system.

- New Diagnostics -> Breakdown Texting admin page.
- Admin can save/replace Twilio Account SID, Auth Token, and sender; Auth Token is encrypted at rest and never displayed back.
- Live texting can be enabled/paused without a deploy and includes a test-text control.
- Breakdown SMS recipients are managed from the admin page; only active configured numbers receive alerts.
- SMS wording is stored in D1 templates and editable from the admin page without a deploy.
- New breakdown alerts use the saved template before Twilio sends them.
- Inbound Twilio webhook validates X-Twilio-Signature and only allows active configured breakdown-text users to claim by replying with the breakdown number.
- First-reply claims are recorded against the configured SMS contact and protected from later overwrite.
- Adds migration 0112 and deterministic regression coverage.

Twilio credentials are intentionally not copied into source control. The existing Apps Script project cannot be read through the connected Drive API, so the same Account SID/Auth Token/sender can be entered once on the new admin page after deploy.

### Tier 1 owner-current history + recovery invariants

1. Provider finality/currentness comes only from durable owner-controlled `provider_authority`.
2. Reconciliation coverage is bound to exact current `authority_generation`, exact current `provider_dataset_revision`, and owner-required snapshot currentness.
3. Authority-generation changes and owner-visible provider dataset mutations invalidate prior coverage; provider mutation and sweep serialize on the same authority row.
4. Stable reconciled identity is immutable; conflict validation precedes provider-time windowing whenever either accepted or owner-current timestamp intersects the sweep window.
5. Stable identity rewrite rejects; destructive DELETE and statement-level TRUNCATE fail closed.
6. Reconciliation worker has no direct provider INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE, owner membership, or trigger-administration authority.
7. Every existing `00[4-9]_history_*.sql` hardening module must be wired into the extended runner; CI fails if a current module is orphaned.
8. PITR restore to `R` remains fail-closed until authenticated surviving `(R,F]` authority is established.
9. Recovery claim/verification surfaces are ID-only; restore principals cannot read grant state directly or submit target/principal identity or signed grant facts as authority.
10. Surviving authority loads/verifies grant facts internally and atomically binds each grant to the first authenticated `session_user`; same-principal retry converges and another authenticated principal is rejected.

### Canonicalization + relocation invariants

- structured crypto messages use deterministic self-delimiting field representation;
- typed canonical values must be total/injective over the full accepted domain;
- relocation `timestamptz`: finite UTC + microseconds + explicit `AD`/`BC`; exact `-infinity` / `infinity` sentinels;
- relocation `numeric`: normalized finite values plus exact `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity` sentinels;
- placement is locked before `F` is derived;

- effective checkpoint signing key is generated inside Tier 2 target authority; controller does not provision/retain it;
- Tier 1 verifies but cannot mint target attestations;
- verifier/automation principals cannot read target signing key or restricted cross-authority capability state;
- verifier secrets are absent from SQL function source;
- raw asynchronous verifier transport is owner-only;
- connection setup and established-response time are independently bounded; stalled authenticated peers fail closed under caller-local deadline;
- remote verification occurs before local authority locks;
- Tier 1 atomically commits successor placement + activation grant bound to tenant, `F`, checkpoint id/generation, target attestation and successor placement version;
- injected grant conflict rolls back placement and leaves target sealed;
- target cannot self-activate; `sealed → activated` requires exact committed Tier 1 grant verification;
- after activation, existing history is immutable and only new append `>F` is eligible.

The evidence uses pinned PostgreSQL/Timescale images, random evidence LOGIN credentials, asynchronous `dblink`, restricted capability tables, HMAC/SHA and bounded laboratory deadlines only as C2 falsification machinery. body:
## Summary

This release adds Instagram as a third publishing platform (OAuth connect flow plus posting support), introduces a standalone MCP server so AI agents can query an organization's projects through a new API-key-authenticated external endpoint, and rebuilds the organization overview dashboard to pull real channel/webhook/activity/storage data instead of hardcoded metrics. It also closes a security gap by adding an organization-membership check across nearly every internal API route, restructuring URLs that were missing the organization slug and updating every matching frontend caller to match.

## What's included

### Features
- Instagram OAuth connect flow (`request-instagram-integration-url`, `instagram-callback`, `connect-instagram`) plus `INSTAGRAM` as a selectable provider on the create-post form ([859d051](../../commit/859d051), [e30a14d](../../commit/e30a14d))
- Standalone MCP server (`mcp/`) exposing a `get-projects-tool`, backed by a new API-key-authenticated external route `GET /api/v1/projects` and `checkApiKey` middleware ([81923e6](../../commit/81923e6), [e3f2dd1](../../commit/e3f2dd1), [a4dedd5](../../commit/a4dedd5))
- Organization overview page rebuilt on a single `getOverview` endpoint aggregating channels, members, usage, storage, recent activities and webhooks, replacing the old `get-metrics` endpoint and hardcoded widgets ([fe10f77](../../commit/fe10f77))
- `checkMembership` enforcement added to ~40 internal routes (channel, folder, integration, inspirational-thumbnail, organization, post, project, webhook, best-moment), with URL paths restructured to include `organizations/:slug/...` where it was missing, and every frontend `.http.ts` caller updated to match ([a845fb9](../../commit/a845fb9))

### Bug fixes

author: muranoia
body:
Traz para dentro do CRM a conversa que a supervisão hoje faz **fora** dele: pedir um público em uma frase ("200 de cada vendedor do inside sales que não compraram nesse mês, que não receberam template hoje, que não estão em conversa aberta"), receber uma planilha, e subir a planilha no painel do RD para disparar.

Agora a mesma conversa acontece em `/admin` → Templates → **Disparo em massa** → bloco **Montar conversando**, e o disparo sai daqui.

## Como funciona

O assistente **propõe** os filtros num cartão com botão **Aplicar nos filtros**. Nada muda na tela sem um clique, e depois de aplicado o público ainda passa por **Revisar** e **Confirmar** — mesmo freio do "marcar não aplica" da §29.4, porque 800 disparos custam ~R$ 344 e são irreversíveis.

## Decisões

- **Uma peneira só.** A lógica do público saiu da rota para `lib/publicoDisparo.ts`, porque passou a ter dois donos (a tela e o assistente). Com duas, o número prometido na conversa e o da prévia divergiriam — e só depois do envio. Um bug assim apareceu no teste: `canal` não vem do modelo, vem do template marcado na tela.
- **A única ferramenta do modelo é `montar_publico`, que só LÊ.** Não existe caminho de código até `/api/send-template`.
- **Nenhum nome de cliente vai para o modelo** — o `tool_result` devolve contagens. A lista com nome e telefone é desenhada pela tela a partir da prévia, que roda no nosso servidor. Conferido no payload real.
- **Sem `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` nada quebra**: o bloco aparece com um recado explicando o que falta e a rota responde 501; os filtros seguem funcionando.

## Filtros novos

`times` (IS/ISR/GC) · "não compraram no período" (nota fiscal, o mesmo número da coluna Pedido emitido) · "pular quem está em conversa aberta" · cota por vendedor. Teto do disparo de 500 → 1000, com o tempo estimado de aba aberta na prévia.

## Testado

- chamada **real** à API, dois turnos: tradução correta, e o assistente avisa do custo e oferece lote menor
- navegador: pergunta → cartão → Aplicar → prévia recontada (1.496 elegíveis → 800), zero erro no console
- guardas: 401 sem sessão, 403 para vendedor, 501 sem chave
- `tsc` e `next build` limpos

## Antes de usar em produção

Configurar **`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`** nas Environment Variables da Vercel e redeployar (variável nova só vale para deploy novo).

author: pajew-ski
body:
Die Prüfschicht. Sie schließt die Lücke zwischen „unbelegt" und „geprüft und nicht gestützt", und sie öffnet den Weg für Forschungsartikel, ohne die Quellenregel zu lockern.

## Keine Hypothesenklasse

Bewusst nicht gebaut. Die Siddhis stehen bereits im Graphen, mit Bezeugungsmodus und Stelle, und nichts daran behauptet oder verwirft sie. Eine eigene Klasse für Unbelegtes wäre die Tür, durch die alles zurückkommt, was die Quellenregel draußen hält: „noch nicht belegt, aber nicht zu verwerfen" beschreibt beliebiges Material, sobald jemand es behalten will.

Was fehlte, war nicht ein Platz für die Behauptung, sondern eine Unterscheidung auf der Prüfseite.

## Vier Stände, die nicht zusammenfallen dürfen

`pm:ExaminationState` mit `pm:noProcedureDevised`, `pm:procedureWithoutCases`, `pm:casesWithoutDeviation`, `pm:casesWithDeviation`.

Der erste ist der wichtigste und der einzige, den man aus Bequemlichkeit weglässt. Eine Behauptung, für die niemand ein Prüfverfahren ersonnen hat, ist keine Behauptung, die geprüft und nicht gestützt wurde. Fielen die beiden zusammen, würde der Bestand mit der Zeit genau die Ansprüche stillschweigend entwerten, die er halten soll, und dabei nicht einen Befund über Siddhis melden, sondern einen über die Reichweite seiner eigenen Instrumente.

`FalsifierRequiredShape` hält das strukturell: die Falsifikationsbedingung darf genau dann fehlen, wenn der Stand ausdrücklich `pm:noProcedureDevised` sagt. Überall sonst schlägt die Validierung fehl. Ein Knoten kann also nicht unbemerkt von ungeprüft nach ungestützt rutschen.

## Evidenz ist nicht Quelle

`pm:evidenceFrom` statt `dcterms:source`, mit Domain `pm:Testing`. Ein moderner Aufsatz ist nie Zeuge einer Tradition und darf nie als Quelle einer ihrer Behauptungen erscheinen; er trägt zu einer Behauptung von außen bei, und das ist eine andere Rolle. Die Trennung der beiden Prädikate ist genau das, was Forschung überhaupt in den Bestand lässt, ohne die Regel aufzuweichen, dass Quellen überlieferte Werke sind.

Damit ist auch der DOI wieder zulässig, ohne dass ein Link zurückkommt: `doi:10.1371/...` ist eine Werkkennung, keine Ortsangabe. `EvidenceIsLiteratureShape` weist `http`-Präfixe genauso ab wie bei `dcterms:source`.

Dazu `pm:examinedBy`: ein Protokoll ohne benannten Urheber ist unzurechenbar, und ein unzurechenbares Protokoll ist kein Beleg für irgendetwas. Von `TestingShape` erzwungen.

## Die erste Prüfung

`examinations/tummo-heat.ttl`, gerichtet auf `pmc:TummoYieldsInnerHeat`. Die eine Paarung im Bestand, deren Vermögen eine äußere Seite hat, an die Instrumente kommen. Evidenz aus Benson 1982 und Kozhevnikov 2013, Stand `pm:casesWithDeviation`.

Der Knoten sagt ausdrücklich, wie weit das trägt: gemessen ist die somatische Behauptung und nichts darüber hinaus, und der berichtete Effekt hängt am Zusammenspiel von Atemtechnik und Visualisierung, womit die gestützte Behauptung enger ist als die, die die Tradition macht. Ohne diesen Vermerk läse der Knoten als Bestätigung von etwas, das nicht gemessen wurde.

`pmc:TestingOfThoughts` bekommt Stand und Urheber nachgetragen: `pm:procedureWithoutCases`, weil Cassian ein Verfahren mit Kriterium liefert und keine Fallzählung.

## Sparregel

`examinations/` bekommt keinen Stub pro Behauptung. Ein Prüfknoten entsteht erst, wenn jemand die Prüfung aufnimmt. Ein Bestand, der zu jeder Paarung automatisch einen Knoten mit Stand „ungeprüft" anlegt, verdoppelt seine Größe und sagt nichts, was das Fehlen des Knotens nicht schon sagt. Die Regel steht im Dateikopf.

## Vier neue Fixtures

Ein Prüfknoten ohne Stand wird abgewiesen. Ein Prüfknoten ohne Falsifikator wird abgewiesen. Ein Prüfknoten ohne Falsifikator mit Stand `noProcedureDevised` **konformiert** — das ist der einzige positive Fixture im Bestand, und er prüft genau die Ausnahme, um die es geht. Eine URL in `pm:evidenceFrom` wird abgewiesen.

`compile.py`, `publish.py`, `validate.py` und der Substanzklassen-Scan nehmen `examinations/` in ihre Standardeingaben auf.

## Offen

`pm:presupposesPractice` fehlt weiterhin. Die Wegbedingung ist für die Frage, welche Vermögen sich entwickeln lassen, ebenso tragend wie die Paarung selbst, aber ich habe für keine Voraussetzungsangabe eine geprüfte Stelle. Unbelegtes Vokabular anzulegen wäre derselbe Fehler wie ein unbelegter Knoten, eine Ebene höher. Gehört in den nächsten Rechercheauftrag.

author: kibanamachine
body:
Fixes #287866

### Summary
- The `all privileges > with model setup > loads conversations UI with ability to chat` test failed with `expected 'true' to equal null`.
- It read the chat input's `disabled` attribute the instant the element was found, before the async connectors fetch enabled it — snapshotting the transient disabled state.
- This patch waits for the input's *enabled* state (the exact signal the assertion cares about) via a bounded `retry.waitFor` poll, then asserts implicitly by that wait.

### Context
- Follows the [Failed Test Investigator's proposed fix](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/287866#issuecomment-5454417335) verbatim; the analysis was posted the same day and no failures arrived after it, so it is current.
- Root cause confirmed in the app code: `PromptEditor`'s `disabled={!connectors.selectedConnector || !hasCorrectLicense}` (`x-pack/platform/packages/shared/kbn-ai-assistant/src/chat/chat_body.tsx:627`) renders `disabled` until the async `useLoadConnectors` fetch resolves. The `enterprise` config has a valid license and `before()` creates a connector, so the input reliably enables — this is a test-timing bug, not a product bug.
- `retry.waitFor` polling the boolean `testSubjects.isEnabled` is a bounded wait on a value (not a re-issued action or a retried throwing block), so it stays within the fix guardrails.
- Failed twice in [kibana-on-merge build 108064](https://buildkite.com/elastic/kibana-on-merge/builds/108064) on `main` (the original job and its retry) with the identical signature.

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

#### Verified locally

✅ Passed: `node scripts/eslint x-pack/solutions/observability/test/observability_ai_assistant_functional/tests/feature_controls/assistant_security.spec.ts`

#### Not verified locally

- This is an FTR test requiring a live Elasticsearch + Kibana, which cannot run in this environment, so the reliability of the fix under CI parallel load was not measured here. The change is a straightforward swap from a one-shot attribute read to a bounded wait on the same enabled state.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Backporting guidance</summary>

Applied `backport:all-open`. The test file exists on every open release branch in `versions.json` (`9.5`, `9.4`, `8.19`) and each carries the same one-shot `getAttribute('disabled')` pattern in the identical surrounding code, so this patch applies unchanged across all of them.

</details>

> Requested by @kibanamachine. Share feedback in #kibana-qa. Mention `@copilot` to make quick changes.

author: ywatanabe1989
body:
Removes the per-node bearer feature and the `node_tokens` table it stored.
Operator-approved 2026-08-28 (「はい、紛らわしいものは削除でお願いします」);
decision card `node-tokens-gate-never-armed-decision-20260828`.

## The measurement

WI-2's "identity cannot be spoofed via a metadata field" acceptance was
implemented as a bearer token per node: `mint_node_token` wrote a row,
`resolve_node_token` mapped an incoming `Authorization: Bearer` back to a
name, and `check_send_acl` refused a `metadata.from_agent` that disagreed
with it.

It was never armed:

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| `node_tokens` rows on compute-01 / -03 / -04, nas-03 | **0** (runtime/state.db, 2026-08-28 11:40Z) |
| `mint_node_token` callers in `src/` | **0** (tests only) |

So `resolve_node_token` always returned `None`, `request.state.authenticated_node`
was always `None`, and the anti-spoof branch never once fired on any request
the fleet has served. What gates a send is the host-wide bearer at the
perimeter plus the NAME-based ACL — which is what gated it all along.

## Why this is a no-behaviour-change deletion

Every branch removed is one that could not be reached:

1. **`auth.BearerAuthMiddleware`** — the second branch resolved the presented
   bearer against `node_tokens`. With no row ever written it could only fall
   through to the `403 invalid bearer token` on the next line. The host-wide
   token check is untouched.
2. **`_acl.NodeAuthMiddleware`** — its only job was that lookup, so it could
   only ever write `authenticated_node = None`. Every reader of that attribute
   goes through `getattr(request.state, "authenticated_node", None)` and keeps
   getting `None` with the layer gone. One middleware fewer per request.
3. **`check_send_acl`'s `authenticated_node` parameter and its spoof deny** —
   `None` on every real call, so the live path was, and remains, the
   `claimed_from_agent` branch. Kept byte-for-byte, including the
   "no identity at all" deny.

The one production call site (`_node_channel.node_message_send`) passed
`getattr(request.state, "authenticated_node", None)`; it now passes only the
claim. `sender_id = authenticated_node or sac_meta.get("from_agent")` becomes
`sac_meta.get("from_agent")` — the same value, since the left operand was
always `None`.

## Export hole closed by construction

`export_state` ships every column of a `KNOWN_TABLES` member — the `token`
column included — and the MCP `db_export` tool exposes no `tables` parameter
with which to withhold one. With the table gone, that is a structural
guarantee rather than a dependency on nobody calling export.

`_store_plugin.NEVER_SYNCED` **keeps** its refusal of the name (tense updated,
removal noted): a table leaving `KNOWN_TABLES` must not read as the refusal
being withdrawn, and that entry is where a future per-node credential store
would arrive.

## Table count 7 -> 6

`KNOWN_TABLES` goes from 7 names to 6. Fresh-DB proof, via sac's own
`init_schema` on an empty file:

```
TABLES CREATED BY init_schema (6):
   channel_events  definitions  events  instance_heartbeats  instances  lineage

INDEXES (6):
   idx_channel_events_target_id  idx_channel_events_target_undelivered
   idx_events_instance  idx_instances_active  idx_instances_host
   idx_lineage_parent

node_tokens present: False
idx_node_tokens_token present: False
KNOWN_TABLES members MISSING from a fresh DB: []
```

The `--table` choice list follows `KNOWN_TABLES`, so the CLI refuses with the
valid set:

```
$ sac db query --table=node_tokens
Error: Invalid value for '--table': 'node_tokens' is not one of 'definitions',
'instances', 'instance_heartbeats', 'events', 'channel_events', 'lineage'.
```

## Something the deletion made legible

`agent_delete` and `agent_tail` derive their caller **only** from
`request.state.authenticated_node` — no body, no query parameter. With no
per-node identity, `check_lineage_acl` receives `caller=None` on every HTTP
request to those two routes and admits it as administrative. **This was
equally true before this PR** (the table had no rows); what changes is that
the minted-bearer test fixture, which existed nowhere but in the test suite,
is no longer there to make those routes look gated against a caller shape
production has never produced. The gate is kept and the situation is now
stated in the code rather than implied against it.

`agent_restart` and `host_exec` also read a body `caller` field, so their
gates stay reachable and their tests still drive them end-to-end.

## Tests

The four token-minting files now cover what remains — the host-wide bearer
perimeter (admitted / `403 invalid bearer token` / `401` on absence) and the
ACL by name.

- `test__acl.py` — every `check_send_acl` call drops the `authenticated_node`
  kwarg (each already passed the same value in both, so decisions are
  unchanged). Three HTTP per-node-bearer tests replaced by four covering the
  real perimeter.
- `test__acl_group.py` / `test__acl_phase3.py` — kwarg dropped, 15 call sites,
  same decisions.
- `test_server_lineage_acl.py` — HTTP admin-path tests kept; the deny cases
  move to direct `check_lineage_acl` assertions (where a non-admin caller can
  still be constructed) plus direct `deny_response` wire-shape assertions, and
  new HTTP tests pin that a non-host bearer is refused by the perimeter with a
  body distinguishable from an ACL deny.
- `test_server_restart_route.py` — `_node_headers` -> body `{"caller": ...}`;
  still end-to-end over HTTP.
- `tests/smoke/_node_comms.py` — setup helpers keep the `{name: bearer}` shape
  so call sites are unchanged; every entry is now the host bearer, which is
  what a real sac agent presents. Identity travels in `metadata.from_agent`.

**Deleted outright, and only these — five assertions covering the branch that
is gone:** `test_acl_denies_identity_spoof`,
`test_acl_spoof_deny_reason_names_both_identities`, the `spoof_deny_scenario`
fixture's three tests (in `test__acl.py`), and the two smoke spoof cases. Each
asserted a guarantee that was never in force in production, and none can be
re-pointed: there is no second identity left to contradict a claim with. Every
assertion about `claimed_from_agent` is untouched.

## Verification

Local, worktree source (`PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src`), `_state` + `_listen` +
`test__store_plugin.py` + `tests/smoke`:

```
1856 passed, 619 skipped, 0 failed   (rebased onto 8becdd23)
```

**Honest caveat on the skips.** This container's loopback PostgreSQL is a
read-only replica of the fleet cluster, so the store-isolation plugin skips
every test needing the `pg_schema` fixture. Across the files this PR touches
that is 69 passed / 138 skipped locally — including all 23 smoke
`node_comms` tests and six of the new `check_lineage_acl` gate tests. Those
execute in CI, which has a writable store; CI is the real signal for them.

Grep census — zero references to `node_tokens` / `mint_node_token` /
`resolve_node_token` remain outside departure comments, the ADRs and the kept
`NEVER_SYNCED` entry. `rg 'mint_node_token\(|resolve_node_token\(|list_node_tokens\('`
over `src/` and `tests/` returns nothing. The `authenticated_node` hits in
`test__host_exec*.py` are that suite's own `_FakeRequest` kwarg for the
surviving request-state attribute, not token references.

`docs/adr/0022` open question 8 is resolved in place (the credential story is
that there was no credential); `docs/adr/0015`'s receiver-side ACL paragraph
carries a dated note that its conclusion is unchanged.

author: jameswnl
body:
## Summary

Fixes #224: `reconcile_orphaned_sandboxes()` (runs at workflow-runner startup to clean up sandboxes left by a crash/OOM/deploy rollout) relied on `OpenShellSpawner.list_active()`, but `_do_list_active()` only read the current process's in-memory `_sandbox_names` dict — always empty after a restart, so real orphans were never found and silently leaked. Separately, `spawned-by=workflow-runner` (the label `reconcile_orphaned_sandboxes()` filters on) was never actually attached to any spawned sandbox, so the filter had nothing to match even in principle.

- `_do_spawn()` now attaches durable labels to `CreateSandboxRequest.labels` (merged with caller-supplied labels): a fixed `spawned-by=workflow-runner`, and a `cloud-agents/agent-name` label carrying the real `agent_name`. `CreateSandboxRequest.name` is left empty, same as before this PR — the gateway auto-assigns a short, valid, routable name (an earlier version of this PR tried sending a deterministic `ca-agent-<agent_name>` name, but the gateway caps caller-supplied names at 19 characters, which real `agent_name` values already approach on their own; see review discussion below).
- `_do_list_active()` now queries the gateway directly via `SandboxClient.list(label_selector=...)` (a real `ListSandboxes` gRPC RPC) instead of local state, recovering `agent_name` from the `cloud-agents/agent-name` label. Sandboxes without that label (pre-fix, or created by another tool) fall back to their raw sandbox name so they're still visible rather than silently dropped.
- `_do_destroy()` looks up the sandbox by that label via the gateway when `agent_name` isn't locally tracked (the orphan-recovery path, where local tracking is by definition empty on a restarted process), deletes every match, and falls back to treating `agent_name` as a literal sandbox name if no label match is found.

## Review history

An independent reviewer (`beesarmy`) checked this against the real `openshell` gateway source (`crates/openshell-server`), not just the mocked SDK:
- First pass caught a real blocker: an earlier version of this fix sent a deterministic `name=` to `CreateSandboxRequest`, which exceeds the gateway's 19-character routable-name limit (`MAX_ROUTABLE_NAME_LEN`, `crates/openshell-server/src/grpc/mod.rs`) and would have failed every real spawn. Fixed by dropping the deterministic name in favor of the label-based recovery described above.
- Second pass approved the fix, confirming the label scheme matches the gateway's validators (`validate_label_key`/`validate_label_value`) and that the list→destroy round-trip works for both labeled and pre-fix/unlabeled sandboxes.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests in `tests/unit/spawner/test_openshell_spawner.py`: label passthrough at spawn (including the `cloud-agents/agent-name` label), gateway-backed `list_active` (including restart simulation via a fresh spawner instance with no local tracking), label-based destroy lookup with multi-match and literal-name fallback
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/unit/spawner/test_openshell_spawner.py tests/unit/workflow/temporal/test_startup_reconciliation.py -q` — 138 passed, 7 skipped
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/unit/ -q` (full regression) — 1797 passed, 12 skipped
- [x] CI (build, unit-tests, e2e) green on `09113ea`
- [ ] Live-gateway smoke test (spawn → process restart → `list_active` → `destroy`) — not done in this PR; reviewer confirms gateway-source review is sufficient to approve the name-length fix, but this is still recommended per `docs/testing-against-openshell-gateways.md` before treating this as production-proven

## Known follow-ups (not blocking, called out in review)

- Orphan destroy on a restarted process can't detach the sandbox's credential Provider (`_provider_ids` is empty for untracked agents) — `DeleteSandbox` doesn't fail closed on attached providers, so the sandbox itself is still destroyed, but the Provider may leak (same family as #214).
- Startup reconcile destroys *all* `spawned-by=workflow-runner` sandboxes, including another replica's live ones under a hypothetical multi-replica deployment — pre-existing behavior, not introduced by this PR, but worth a deliberate decision before any HA deployment of this runner.

author: morphqdd
body:
`Asked` read the locator the dispatch settled on. Once a caller applies the formation, `Filled` has already put the argument in there, so the locator was the argument and not the void, and `Demands` wrote nothing. A demand present in the tables therefore disappeared the moment somebody applied the formation.

It now works the answer out from the receiver instead: the receiver is walked to the formation it is a copy of and `Provided` is asked what that formation keeps under the name, which is the same answer the caller-free program gives. What fills a void does not change what is asked of it.

The pack is the program from the report, with a `leaf` that does have a `size`, since that is the case where the substitution used to hide the demand.

Closes #7758

author: bmck
body: This PR adds a GitHub Actions CI workflow to run automated checks on pull requests and pushes to the `main` branch. ## Changes - Creates `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with a basic CI pipeline - Replaces the legacy Travis CI configuration with modern GitHub Actions ## Workflow Details The CI workflow: - **Triggers**: Runs on `pull_request` and `push` events to the `main` branch - **Ruby versions**: Tests against Ruby 3.0, 3.2, and 3.3 (gem requires >= 2.3.0) - **Dependency installation**: Uses `ruby/setup-ruby@v1` with automatic bundler caching for faster runs - **Test execution**: - Runs `bundle exec rake` (default task) - Verifies the gem loads successfully with `require 'philly_frb_as_dataframe'` ## Ruby 3.1 Compatibility Note Ruby 3.1 is intentionally excluded from CI due to an incompatibility with the `polars-df` dependency (version 0.15.0). The gem fails to load on Ruby 3.1 with: ``` uninitialized constant Polars::Set (NameError) ``` This is a known issue where Ruby 3.1 moved the `Set` class to a separate gem, and the polars-df gem doesn't properly require it. Ruby 3.0 (which auto-loads Set) and Ruby 3.2+ (which restored the auto-load for compatibility) both work correctly. The `.ruby-version` file currently specifies 3.1.2, but the gem is not compatible with that version until the polars-df dependency is updated or pinned to a compatible version. ## Repository Test Suite Status This repository currently has no test suite (no `test/` or `spec/` directories, and the Rakefile has an empty default task). The CI workflow focuses on: 1. Ensuring dependencies install correctly across Ruby versions 2. Verifying the gem can be required without errors This provides a foundation for future test additions. When tests are added to the repository, they can be invoked by updating the Rakefile's default task or adding additional steps to the workflow. ## Testing The workflow runs automatically on this PR, demonstrating the CI checks in action. All configured Ruby versions (3.0, 3.2, 3.3) pass successfully.

author: carljm
body:
A generic subclass with a defaulted type parameter can incorrectly fail the implicit `__init_subclass__` receiver check. The receiver is default-specialized while the inherited method's `Self` bound retains the subclass's type variables, producing a comparison such as `Child[int]` against `Base[T@Child]`.

Use the subclass's identity specialization for the implicit `cls` argument so the receiver and inherited hook use the same type parameters. This accepts valid class definitions while retaining explicit receiver restrictions and keyword argument validation.

Closes astral-sh/ty#4411.

## Test plan

Added mdtests covering:

- Generic subclass receivers with no defaults, all-default parameters, and mixed required and defaulted parameters.
- Legacy `TypeVar` defaults and explicit `cls` annotations, including rejection of incompatible receiver specializations.
- Class keyword arguments, including values typed using a subclass parameter and rejection of incompatible values.

author: moazzumali
body:
The extension is built against the newest Quarkus but declares support for an older floor. Nothing checked that claim: a build step using an API added after the floor compiles here, passes every existing job, and fails only in a user's own build on the LTS, when Quarkus runs augmentation and executes the extension's build steps against their older classes.

Add an application pinned to that floor and build it on every commit, which reproduces exactly that situation. Assertions read Agroal's configuration rather than opening a connection, so no database is needed: the resolved driver class shows the build items applied, and the exception sorter shows the runtime connection configurer was resolved and ran.

The project deliberately has no parent and is not a module of the root pom. Inheriting either would bring the newest Quarkus version along, and the check would resolve that while appearing to test the oldest.

It lives in its own workflow rather than in build.yml, which follows the Quarkiverse template and is updated in bulk across repositories: a rewrite of that file should not be able to drop this check.

Verified the check is not vacuous. Quarkus 3.39 declares 150 build items to 3.33's 143. Referencing one of the 3.39-only items (GeneratedServiceProviderBuildItem) from a build step made the main build pass and this check fail with NoClassDefFoundError, naming the offending build step — exactly what a user on the LTS would see. Reverted before committing.

author: mfreeman451
body:
## Summary

`helm unittest ./helm/serviceradar` reported **10 failed suites / 26 failed tests** on `staging`, and is invoked by **no CI job** — the Helm Lint workflow runs `helm lint`, which executes no assertions. This makes the suite green and puts it behind a Bazel test target so it cannot rot again.

## Triage: zero chart regressions

All 26 are test defects. Extracting the chart at `a93025e11e` (the commit that introduced these suites) and running the plugin there reproduces the **identical** 10/26 failure set — so every one of these assertions has been failing since the day it was written. They were authored by reading `helm template` output rather than by running the plugin, and the two differ in exactly the ways the failures describe.

| Root cause | Suites | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Document order: `helm template` prints Helm's kind-sorted install order, helm-unittest indexes raw template order — `documentIndex: 1` was the Gateway in one, the GatewayClass in the other | `agent_gateway_gateway_routes` | select documents by name/kind, never by index |
| Release namespace: `helm template` defaults to `default`, the plugin to the literal `NAMESPACE` | `agent_gateway_gateway_routes`, `collector_gateway_routes` | pin `release.namespace` explicitly |
| Ambiguous `documentSelector` — `web.yaml` renders a ServiceAccount, a Service and a Deployment all named `serviceradar-web-ng`; job templates render four same-named objects (`multiple indexes found` / `document not found`) | `automation_callback_{keyring,response_policy,runtime}`, `partition_coalesce`, `remote_access_{rdp_webrtc,ssh_ca_signer,ssh_certificate_policy}` | select on a path unique within the template, scope with `template:` |
| Unscoped `failedTemplate`: `fail` fires while rendering exactly one template, so the others report `No failed document` | `automation_callback_response_policy`, `remote_access_{rdp_webrtc,ssh_certificate_policy}` | scope to the template that raises |
| Stale literal version: pinned `v1.4.29` against a chart at `v1.4.46` | `web_ng_release_version` | override `.Chart.AppVersion` per test |

**All six validation guards exist and work** — `failedTemplate` was failing on attribution, not on a missing guard.

Two deliberate choices worth review:

- The gateway suites pin `release.namespace: serviceradar-test`, not `default`. Asserting a plausible default cannot distinguish `.Release.Namespace` from a hardcoded string; with `default` the assertion was vacuous, and a mutation hardcoding the namespace now fails.
- `web_ng_release_version` now overrides `.Chart.AppVersion` per test, asserting *where the value is derived from* rather than which release is checked in. Pinning the live version is what made it stale, and it would have gone red again at the next release bump.

## The gate

`//helm/serviceradar:helm_unittest_suite_test` — a `py_test` running **helm-unittest 0.7.2**'s `untt` binary, pinned in `MODULE.bazel` and fetched by Bazel. It is picked up by `bazel test //...` (buildbuddy.yaml:60) and therefore by `make test`; no workflow step installs anything.

It runs `untt` directly rather than `helm unittest`, which needs no helm binary at all. That is the same code path — `plugin.yaml` declares `command: "$HELM_PLUGIN_DIR/untt"` with `ignoreFlags: false`, so helm does nothing but exec it — and `untt` links the Helm libraries itself. It also makes the result independent of whichever helm a developer has installed. The deciding constraint was CI: a first attempt pinning helm 3.14.4 **failed BazelCI on a `get.helm.sh` read timeout**, a host the runners cannot reach (github.com, where the plugin lives, is fine).

The test also cross-checks the suite count the plugin reports against the `tests/*_test.yaml` files in runfiles, so **a suite that never runs fails instead of passing by omission** — the mode that allowed this in the first place. `tests/README.md` documents the four traps.

## Verification

- 26/26 suites, 80/80 tests pass under the locally installed helm 4.1.4, the pinned 3.14.4, and `untt` standalone with helm absent from `PATH`.
- Bazel target passes locally (darwin/arm64) and on RBE; **BazelCI green on this PR**.
- `make test` green: **201/201**.
- **Mutation-tested** — six deliberate chart breakages each turn the suite red: release version following the image tag, hardcoded parentRef namespace, a dropped validator include, two renamed env vars, a renamed partition variable. A newly added failing suite file is picked up with no BUILD change.

## Observation, not changed here

`serviceradar.validateRemoteAccessDesktopWebRTC` is included only from `web.yaml`, while the other three validators are included from both `core.yaml` and `web.yaml`; it also sits inside the `webNg.enabled` gate, so `webNg.enabled: false` skips WebRTC validation entirely. Harmless today (web-ng is the only consumer, and any `helm install` renders `web.yaml`), but flagging it for the chart owners rather than changing validation behaviour in a test-fix PR.

author: hasanmoosavi814
body:
## Summary

Event capacity, refresh-token rotation, OTP consumption, active carts, wishlist writes, review aggregates, content-linked PDU activities, and outbox delivery were each guarded by a preflight read followed by an unconditional write. Every one of those windows is losable under overlapping requests, so each invariant now rests on a database constraint or a conditional write. The reads that remain exist only to produce a readable error rather than a constraint violation.

| Invariant | Now enforced by |
| --- | --- |
| Attendees never exceed capacity | `UPDATE "Event" SET attendees = attendees + 1 WHERE … attendees < capacity` inside the registration transaction |
| A seat is released once | `updateMany` on the attending statuses, `count === 1` before a `GREATEST(attendees - 1, 0)` decrement |
| At most one committed refresh rotation | `AuthSession.rotationCounter` compare-and-swap |
| An OTP is consumed once, and the attempt limit holds | Attempt spent by `UPDATE … WHERE attempts < maxAttempts` before verification; consumption is a conditional `deleteMany` on the verified hash in the user-create transaction |
| One active cart per user | Partial unique index `Cart_userId_active_key` |
| One content-linked PDU activity per user | Partial unique index `PDUActivity_user_content_key` |
| No permanently stale rating aggregate | `pg_advisory_xact_lock` held across aggregate and publish |
| One outbox delivery per event | Existing `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claim, plus a configurable lease, `renewLease()`, and a stable per-event idempotency key |

Two defects surfaced while the tests were being written, not while designing: reuse detection originally ran *after* the hash check, but a superseded token no longer matches the stored hash, so every replay was reported as an ordinary invalid token and nothing was ever revoked. And Prisma's `upsert` falls back to read-then-write for the wishlist shape — exactly the race being closed — so the unique constraint arbitrates instead.

## Impact

- **GraphQL contract unchanged.** No new operations, no payload changes; `schema.gql` is byte-identical to `develop`, so no frontend codegen.
- Conflicts return the existing domain codes (`EVENT_CAPACITY_REACHED`, `OTP_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED`, `REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID`, …). No raw Prisma error reaches a client.
- The four engagement APIs gained an optional writer parameter so a rating can be published inside the transaction that computed it. It is typed structurally, keeping ORM types out of `/public/` as `module-boundaries.spec.ts` requires.
- `OUTBOX_LEASE_MS` is new and documented in `.env.example`; it defaults to the previous hard-coded 60s.
- E2E now runs `maxWorkers: 1`. Eight suites each booting a full application against one database exhausted the connection pool and turned real assertions into transaction timeouts. The reason is asserted in `e2e-config.spec.ts`, since JSON cannot carry a comment.

### Decisions worth a reviewer's attention

- **Refresh replay revokes the session; losing the compare-and-swap does not.** A `rot` claim behind the stored counter means the token should no longer exist anywhere. Merely losing the swap is two browser tabs refreshing at once, which should not sign the user out.
- **`toggleWishlist` is retained.** A toggle is genuinely ambiguous under concurrency and no implementation resolves that. What is guaranteed is narrower and sufficient: one atomic operation per call, no duplicate-row or missing-row errors, and a final state a caller asked for. Idempotent add/remove sit behind it, so exposing explicit mutations later is a resolver change only.
- **Backfill winners:** newest active cart (inherits the losers' items; collisions resolved in favour of the winner's newer price snapshot; emptied carts marked `ABANDONED`, not deleted) and most recently updated content-linked PDU activity (inherits the losers' evidence files before they are removed, so uploaded proof is never destroyed).

## Tests

Run against an isolated throwaway PostgreSQL 16 instance, removed afterwards.

- `npm run lint` — pass
- `npm run check-types` — pass
- `npm run test --workspace api` — pass (65 suites, 697 tests)
- `npm run test:e2e --workspace api` — pass (8 suites, 58 tests)
- `npm run build` — pass

New PostgreSQL-backed suites in `apps/api/test/concurrency/` start their operations from a shared barrier so they genuinely overlap inside Postgres, and assert final database state rather than only which promises rejected — an implementation that oversells a room and reports success to everyone would pass a response-only check. Coverage includes registration at `capacity - 1` with 2–20 racers, cancellation and reactivation, same-token refresh, OTP consumption and attempt limits, cart and PDU uniqueness against the real constraints, aggregate convergence after concurrent create/update/delete, and two `OutboxProcessor` instances exercising claim behaviour, lease expiry, renewal, crash-after-side-effect, and idempotency-key reuse.

Pre-existing flakiness, unrelated and left alone: `auth-password.service.spec.ts` and `auth-organization-activation.service.spec.ts` intermittently exceed the 5s default timeout under full-suite CPU contention. Both are argon2-bound and pass in isolation; the first reproduces on a clean `develop` checkout.

## Migration

`20260828140000_concurrency_safety` adds `AuthSession.rotationCounter`, reconciles `Event.attendees` from its registration rows, collapses duplicate active carts and content-linked PDU activities, and then creates the two partial unique indexes. Ordering matters: duplicates are collapsed before the indexes that would reject them, and counters are reconciled before registration starts trusting them. Every statement is idempotent and Prisma runs the file in one transaction, so a failure rolls back whole.

**Before deploying**, run the duplicate audit in `apps/api/docs/concurrency-operations.md` against production-like data and confirm the winner policy suits it. Both indexes build without `CONCURRENTLY`, taking a brief `SHARE` lock; on a large `PDUActivity` table, build the index out of band first and the migration's `IF NOT EXISTS` will find it. Rollback is dropping the two indexes and the column — the backfills leave data the previous code also accepts.

Both partial indexes are unmanaged, since Prisma cannot express them in `schema.prisma`. `prisma migrate dev` will report them as drift and offer to drop them; the model docstrings say not to accept.

author: duyhnynh
body:
## Problem

On macOS, OpenKey sometimes stops converting Vietnamese in **every** app at once. The menu bar icon still shows the current mode and the switch key still toggles it, but no keystroke is converted. Quitting and relaunching OpenKey is the only way back.

This matches #258, which describes the same thing ("Tất cả các ứng dụng đều không gõ được VI ... khắc phục: reboot lại OS và bật lại OpenKey").

## Root cause

`initEventTap` creates an **active** event tap:

```objc
eventTap = CGEventTapCreate(kCGSessionEventTap,
                            kCGHeadInsertEventTap,
                            0,                    // active tap
                            eventMask,
                            OpenKeyCallback,
                            NULL);
```

macOS puts a deadline on an active tap's callback. If `OpenKeyCallback` does not return in time — which happens when the machine is under sustained load — the system **switches the tap off** and reports it back through the same callback as the pseudo event type `kCGEventTapDisabledByTimeout`. `kCGEventTapDisabledByUserInput` is the other case.

Two things then go wrong on `master`:

1. `OpenKeyCallback` never checks `type` against those two values, so the notification falls through the normal key-handling path and is ignored.
2. `CGEventTapEnable` is called exactly once, at the end of `initEventTap`.

```
$ grep -rn "kCGEventTapDisabled" .
(no matches)
```

So once macOS turns the tap off, nothing ever turns it back on. Everything else in the app keeps working — which is why the menu bar and the switch key still respond, and why it looks like OpenKey is running fine.

## Fix

Handle both notifications at the top of the callback and re-enable the tap. `eventTap` is file-static in `OpenKeyManager.m`, so re-enabling goes through a small C function there, in the same style as the existing cross-file `extern` declarations.

The normal event path is untouched — the guard returns before any existing logic runs.

## Testing

- `xcodebuild -project Sources/OpenKey/macOS/OpenKey.xcodeproj -scheme OpenKey -configuration Release` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED** (Xcode 26.1.1, macOS 26.3)
- `nm` on the built binary confirms the new path is present and `CGEventTapEnable` now has two call sites instead of one.
- No new warnings.

Note: `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` in the project is `10.14`, which no longer builds on current Xcode (`SDK does not contain 'libarclite'`). I built with an override; that is a pre-existing issue unrelated to this change and I have not touched the project file.

## What I did not verify

I have not captured the moment the tap flips to disabled. The failure needs the callback to be mid-flight during a CPU stall, so it only happens while you are actually typing, and I could not force it on demand. The evidence here is the code path plus the symptom match with #258, not a recorded transition.

For anyone wanting to check their own machine, `CGGetEventTapList()` reports an `enabled` flag per tap and will show OpenKey's tap as disabled while the process is still alive.

Refs #258

author: matheusmedrado
body:
## The report

Hovering the dock glitched, and the Hyprland window animation blinked as the dock revealed and hid — but only while a terminal running an agent CLI was open.

## What was happening

That terminal puts a spinner in its window title. Captured from the live compositor, one such window produces a burst of four events roughly once a second:

```
windowtitle>>5570bf035620
windowtitlev2>>5570bf035620,◑ Dock performance with codex terminal
activewindow>>com.mitchellh.ghostty,◑ Dock performance with codex terminal
activewindowv2>>5570bf035620
```

All four were treated as model changes — `activewindow` because its payload carries the focused window's title, so it is re-emitted whenever that title changes.

Each burst cost a `refreshToplevels()` round trip, which Hyprland answers on its own event loop, and then republished the window records. That rebuilt the item strip, and since the strip's `Repeater` is backed by a plain JavaScript array — which QML cannot diff — **every dock item was destroyed and recreated**. Under the pointer that means `hovered` resets, the 120 ms `itemColor` easing restarts, an open tooltip blinks, and a drag in progress is cancelled by `DockItem.Component.onDestruction`.

Separately, `rebuild()` assigned `records` *before* the guard that rejects an incomplete refresh. A record without a workspace fails `sameWorkspace()`, so `Geometry.conflicts()` reads it as "no window in the band" — Smart Hide revealed, then hid again 60 ms later when the real geometry landed. With `behavior.reserveSpace` enabled, each of those false reveals toggled the exclusive zone and made Hyprland reflow and re-animate the tiled windows.

## The fix

- **Titles are neither listened for nor compared.** Nothing in the dock reads a window title; glyphs, labels, ordering, and every Smart Hide decision come from the application id, the workspace, and the geometry.
- **Focus is tracked by address.** `activewindowv2` names the window; the v1 form only carries class and title, and cannot distinguish two windows of one application anyway. `Hyprland.onActiveToplevelChanged` and `ToplevelManager.onActiveToplevelChanged` remain as backstops.
- **Record and item lists are compared by value**, so a rebuild that lands on the same answer is not republished.
- **Items are compared on the window fields the strip actually draws from** — which keeps a window drag, moving geometry every frame, out of the strip entirely.
- **Incomplete record sets are held back** until the retries are spent, instead of being published and then retried.

A dock sitting next to an idle agent terminal now makes no IPC calls at all, where it previously made one a second.

## Notes

Event classification and both comparisons moved into `models/` so they are covered by the suite — `tests/tst_windowmodel.qml` is new and `tests/tst_dockmodel.qml` gained the item comparison cases, including one asserting that a title-only change is not a change. 107 tests pass; `./scripts/check` is green.

No configuration change, so the CHANGELOG entry sits under `## [Unreleased]` and `manifest.json` is untouched.

author: dknowles2
body:
## What

The Awards page's ballot-sharing step built the share address from `window.location.origin`. On the documented setup — one machine at the venue — that is `http://localhost:8000`, which no phone on the venue wifi can open. This PR:

1. Adds a `networkAddresses` GraphQL query, backed by `backend/services/network.py`, that returns the machine's own best-effort LAN address(es) (a hostname lookup plus a UDP-connect trick, combined since neither alone is reliable on every OS).
2. Adds a pure `frontend/src/features/awards/shareAddress.ts` that substitutes one of those addresses in only when the browser's own origin is `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`/`::1`, keeping the browser's own protocol/port/path, and always reports whether the result is actually reachable.
3. Replaces the plain-text address on the Awards voting panel with a new `BallotShare` component: the (possibly substituted) address, a **Copy** button (`frontend/src/utils/clipboard.ts` — Clipboard API with an `execCommand` fallback), a warning when nothing reachable could be found, and a QR code otherwise.
4. Reuses the existing check-in-code QR machinery (`backend/services/printables.py`, split into a shared `_qr_png` helper) via a new `GET /printables/vote-qr/{race_id}.png` endpoint, which encodes the URL the frontend already computed rather than recomputing it a second way on the backend.

## Why

The newest headline feature's sharing step failed in the default setup — the one thing the sentence told the operator to do (share the address) was the one thing that address could not do. The backend is the thing bound to the network, so it is the one place that can actually answer "what address can a phone reach this at."

Neither the new query nor the new REST endpoint needs an auth/demo classification: the voting page itself is already reachable with no PIN (a `VIEWER` may cast a vote), so an address and a QR code that only point at it need no more protection than the page they point to.

## Docs

- `docs/awards.md`'s voting step now describes the address check, the Copy button and the QR code.
- New "Finding this machine's address" section in `docs/access-and-network.md`, linked from the awards step and from the existing display-setup paragraph, for when the app cannot work the address out for itself.

## Tests

- `backend/tests/test_network.py` — the LAN-address heuristics (faked `socket`) and the GraphQL query.
- New cases in `backend/tests/test_printables.py` — QR rendering and the REST endpoint, including its race-scoping refusal.
- `frontend/src/features/awards/shareAddress.test.ts`, `frontend/src/utils/clipboard.test.ts`, `frontend/src/features/awards/components/BallotShare.test.tsx`.
- Verified the frontend tests fail without the fix: reverted `shareAddress.ts`'s substitution logic and re-ran — 12 of 18 tests failed.

Suites run: `uv run pytest -n auto` (6108 passed), `ruff check`/`format --check`, `mypy backend`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test -- --run` (1094 passed), `npm run lint`, `npm run codegen` (no diff), `uv run mkdocs build --strict`.

Playwright suites were **not** run per instructions. No existing screenshot changed subject, so no new screenshot spec is needed as a follow-up.

Closes #414
