author: mpscholten
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #686, which raised `maxBufferSizeBytes` to 1 GiB. Codex flagged on that PR that `readBoundedLine` accumulates a record with `buffered <> chunk` for every 8 KiB pipe read, copying the whole record each time. With a 1 GiB cap that quadratic cost is now reachable by any large tool result Claude Code echoes on stdout (image `Read` as base64, large file reads): a 64 MiB record allocates 275 GB and burns 10 s of CPU before it can even be parsed.

## Change

- `Claude.Agent.SDK.Internal.Transport.OutputBuffer`: keep the chunks of the current record in a list with a running length, scan only the newly read bytes for a newline, and join the chunks once when the newline (or EOF) arrives. A record that arrives in one read is still returned as a slice without copying.
- `SubprocessCLI.readBoundedLine` delegates to it; oversize detection (`> maximumBytes`, checked as soon as the record is read past the limit), EOF/empty-read handling, `min 8192 (remaining + 1)` read sizing, non-EOF `IOException` reporting, and per-read persistence of buffered input are unchanged.
- Unit spec for the reader (single-read records, split records, newline at read boundaries, EOF exception, read failure keeps buffered input, oversize before/after newline, read-size bounding, 1 MB record over 1,000 reads).
- Benchmark `output-buffer-bench` running the old strict-append reader and the new one through the same IO loop and chunk source, with the production 1 GiB cap.

## Relation to #633 / #645

#633 was reverted in #645 because its chunked buffer had no common-path benefit and cost tens of ns per small record. Two things differ here: the 1 GiB cap turns the large-record case from a stress test into a real failure mode, and the per-record branch is kept strict so the single-read path is at parity (below).

## Benchmark

`nix develop -c cabal build --offline claude-agent-sdk-haskell:bench:output-buffer-bench` (`-O2`, GHC 9.10.3, aarch64-darwin), then `output-buffer-bench <legacy|chunked> RECORD_BYTES 8192 RECORDS SAMPLES +RTS -T`. Reads are capped at 8 KiB like `hGetSome` in production. Medians over 15 samples (≤ 64 KiB) / 7 (1 MiB) / 5 (16 MiB) / 3 (≥ 64 MiB); the 4 KiB and 1 MiB rows were run twice to check stability.

| Record | Records | Legacy wall | Chunked wall | Legacy alloc | Chunked alloc |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 256 B (one read) | 10,000 | 0.178 ms | 0.170 ms | 1.47 MB | 1.56 MB |
| 1 KiB (one read) | 10,000 | 0.382 ms | 0.412 ms | 2.02 MB | 2.17 MB |
| 4 KiB (one read) | 10,000 | 1.483 / 1.513 ms | 1.704 / 1.498 ms | 4.24 MB | 4.60 MB |
| 8 KiB (one read) | 5,000 | 1.393 ms | 1.285 ms | 3.60 MB | 3.92 MB |
| 16 KiB (2 reads) | 2,000 | 2.459 ms | 1.976 ms | 35.6 MB | 36.0 MB |
| 64 KiB (8 reads) | 500 | 6.385 ms | 1.948 ms | 146 MB | 35.7 MB |
| 1 MiB (128 reads) | 10 | 23.6 / 23.1 ms | 0.758 / 0.769 ms | 677 MB | 11.4 MB |
| 4 MiB | 4 | 142.6 ms | 1.116 ms | 4.30 GB | 18.2 MB |
| 16 MiB | 2 | 1,235.6 ms | 2.187 ms | 34.4 GB | 36.4 MB |
| 64 MiB | 1 | 9,985.9 ms | 5.904 ms | 275 GB | 72.8 MB |
| 256 MiB | 1 | not run | 23.6 ms | — | 291 MB |

Single-read records (the common Claude NDJSON case) are within noise on time and cost about one extra small record allocation per read (~+10–36 B per record). Everything spanning more than one read is faster and allocates less; the chunked reader scales linearly (≈0.09 ms and ≈1.1 MB allocated per MiB of record).

## Validation

- `cabal test claude-agent-sdk-haskell:test:claude-agent-sdk-haskell-test`: 66 examples, 0 failures (includes the 2 MiB end-to-end subprocess record test from #686).
- `git diff --check` clean; `package.nix` regenerated with `cabal2nix`.

author: g4bs2006
body:
## Problema
Na Lista e no board Kanban de tarefas, a ordenação repriorizava tudo por prioridade e depois por prazo — uma tarefa recém-criada podia pular na frente de tarefas mais antigas em vez de entrar no fim.

## Ajuste
Os dois critérios (prioridade, prazo) saem da ordenação de `filtered` em `task-board.tsx` (array compartilhado pela Lista e pelo `<KanbanBoard>`). Agora a ordem é: status concluído/cancelado por último e, dentro disso, `created_at` ascendente — tarefa nova sempre no fim da lista/coluna. Prazo e prioridade continuam visíveis no card, só não influenciam mais a posição.

Não mexi na Agenda "Minha Semana", que agrupa por prazo por design (essa é a proposta da aba).

body:
## Ticket objective

Complete the bounded homepage hero assembly sequence using the motion architecture validated in PORT-901 without delaying content, navigation, or accessibility semantics.

## What changed

- Passes the server-rendered identity rail and primary content sheet through the existing route-local Motion leaf as rendered slots.
- Sequences the decorative blueprint, identity rail, raised backsheet, primary sheet, and existing diagram reveal.
- Keeps identity and primary content fully visible during transform-only settling motion.
- Uses route-local CSS guarded by `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` for primary-content settling, so server HTML remains in its final position and reduced-motion users do not receive a hydration snap.
- Preserves the existing fine-pointer parallax, scroll-linked paper alignment, authored layer rotation, and lazy Motion feature bundle.
- Documents architecture, accessibility behavior, scope boundaries, bundle impact, and production frame results.
- Adds regression coverage for the server/client boundary, non-gated primary content, and final-position server render.

## Verification

author: prasad-d-ware
body:
## What this does

Lets a phone reach the daemon from any network, without the user knowing what a LAN address or a tailnet is.

The QR code previously carried a single address — in practice the LAN one. Off that network, pairing failed and the user landed in manual entry, Tailscale setup, or a certificate problem. The code now carries **every** endpoint the machine has, and the phone races them concurrently, verifying it reached the right machine before trusting any of them.

Same three onboarding steps as before. The change is that they now work from cellular.

## How it works

Three endpoint kinds are advertised and raced, preferred cheapest-first (`lan > tailscale > tunnel`):

- **LAN** — every reachable interface address, not just one
- **Tailscale** — when present
- **Tunnel** — a `cloudflared` quick tunnel the daemon supervises, giving reach from anywhere plus a publicly trusted certificate (which also satisfies iOS ATS and retired the MagicDNS/tailnet-certificate branch of the old flow)

The race verifies host identity on every candidate via a new `GET /api/v1/identity`, so a phone cannot be steered onto the wrong machine by a stale or reused address. Endpoints are refreshed on every successful connect, so a rotated tunnel hostname or a changed DHCP lease heals without re-pairing.

Multiple machines are supported end to end — per-host tokens in SecureStore, per-host event cursors — with the existing single-server config migrated on first launch.

## Notable decisions

**One unauthenticated route.** `GET /api/v1/identity` returns only `{hostId, apiVersion}` and is exempt from the bearer-password middleware, because the race must be able to tell machines apart *before* it has a credential to offer. Documented in `docs/adr/0003-unauthenticated-identity-probe.md`, with `AGENTS.md` amended to name it as the single exemption; any further unauthenticated route needs its own ADR.

**Settle delay, not a probe.** The tunnel is advertised 25s after registration rather than when a probe succeeds. Probing before the DNS record exists caches an NXDOMAIN locally that outlives propagation — measured: `curl` still failed 30s after `dig` had begun resolving the same name.

**Cloudflare terminates TLS.** The phone's session is with Cloudflare, not with the user's machine, so tunnel traffic is encrypted in transit but not end to end. What that exposes, when the tunnel is chosen, and what would change it are written up in `docs/adr/0004-cloudflare-tunnel-for-remote-mobile-access.md`. The race preference is what keeps the tunnel to a last resort.

## Known limitation: SSE does not stream over the tunnel

Measured against a live quick tunnel: response bodies are forwarded in ~128 KB chunks (a 121 KB replay produced nothing; larger ones arrived in exact multiples of 128 KB). A chat event is a few hundred bytes, so it is held indefinitely. WebSocket is unaffected — 11 ms round trips for small frames — because after the upgrade it is a raw tunneled stream rather than a buffered response body. That is why terminals felt normal over the tunnel while chat did not.

Two polling intervals compensate, **both stopgaps**, both active only while the tunnel is the chosen endpoint:

- the main poll drops 8s → 2s (`lib/pollInterval.ts`)
- the chat screen polls its conversation, which it otherwise never does (`lib/chat/conversationPoll.ts`)

They turn "over a minute, and only after reopening the screen" into roughly two seconds, at a cost in battery and data.

**The intended fix is to carry conversation events over the existing `/mux` WebSocket instead of SSE.** It already reaches the same daemon, already carries terminal traffic, already round-trips in 11 ms over the tunnel, and already has topic subscription. That removes both stopgaps and needs neither a named tunnel nor a relay. Deliberately deferred, not forgotten — see ADR 0004.

## Verified on a physical device

Identity probe · race · migration from the single-server config · LAN → Tailscale → tunnel failover (~4s) · terminal following the raced endpoint · chat on all three paths · agent input prompts over the tunnel · sustained terminal output over the tunnel · tunnel crash detection and restart (new hostname in 7s) · hostname rotation picked up without re-pairing · orphaned connector reaped · enable/disable.

Two defects were found this way and fixed in the final commit:

- **Sticky endpoint** — once on the tunnel the app never returned to LAN, because only failure re-raced. Observed holding a Cloudflare connection with a working LAN unused. That also quietly broke ADR 0004's "only when nothing else works" claim.
- **Endpoint lists losing a kind by accident of timing** — a quick tunnel takes ~34s to restart and settle, and a refresh landing in that window dropped the tunnel from the stored list.

## Not covered

- The store effect driving the upgrade race is not unit-tested — it needs a device. The predicates it calls are.
- Multi-machine has full unit coverage but has not been exercised with two physical machines.
- Battery and data cost of the 2s tunnel poll is unmeasured.
- Quick-tunnel hostnames rotate on restart, and a phone with no other working path cannot learn the new one. Nothing client-side can fix that; it needs a stable hostname (named tunnel).

## Testing

`go test ./...`, `npm test` in `packages/mobile` (626), frontend typecheck, `npm run api` reproduces the committed spec with no diff.

author: lilyshen0722
body:
Closes TASK-067. Sam ratified the decision on 2026-08-26 — **suppress on leading; mid and trailing keep strip-and-post**. This is the implementation only; the semantics are not re-litigated here.

## The change

**Position is the discriminator.** `sanitizeAgentContent` now silences a reply that IS the sentinel (unchanged, total-match) *or that OPENS with it* (new). A bare sentinel anywhere else keeps PR #785's behaviour: stripped as producer leakage, whitespace-preserving, and the rest posts.

## Why

AX audit entry 43. A seat wrote `NO_REPLY.\n\n<private reasoning about why it was staying silent>`, believing the leading token silenced the turn. Under total-match-only the kernel stripped the token and published the reasoning — 11 times in one day, one long enough to become an attachment. Several of the published messages *say* "no decision pending, so no post." They were posted. The orphan `.` opening each is the period after `NO_REPLY`, surviving the strip.

Both halves of #785's argument survive intact:
- At the **head**, the agent's intent is unambiguous — suppressing is right.
- **Anywhere else**, the token really is producer leakage inside a reply the agent meant to send, and swallowing a genuine reply is the worse error. That half is untouched and now has a test that fails if it ever starts returning `''`.

## Placement, and why it matters

The check sits **below the outer-fence return**, so a fenced or backticked sentinel stays a deliberate mention in every position, leading included — the "backtick a sentinel to mention it" rule is unchanged. A fenced sentinel-only reply was already suppressed by total-match above, so nothing can bypass silence by wrapping the token in a transport fence. A mutant that moves the check above the fence return turns two tests red.

The word-boundary rule is now **one shared helper** instead of two copies. A leading sentinel and a mid-reply one must agree on what "bare" means, differing only in position; two definitions would drift.

## Observability

The new suppression warns under its own message text, so it cannot inflate the existing strip metric. That metric counts replies we *rewrote*; this is one we *withheld*. Pinned by a test asserting the strip warn stays silent on the leading shape.

## Scope note — the fourth file

Sam's task note scoped this to `sanitizeAgentContent` + chatNoise tests + the CLAUDE.md note. I also updated the three wake frames in `agentMentionService.ts`, which assert *"anything you write after the token WILL be posted publicly."* That is now false for the leading case.

Shipping the semantics change while leaving three frames stating the opposite mechanism would recreate the exact divergence AX-43 names as the root cause — "the contract and the teaching diverge exactly at 'reply that STARTS with the sentinel'." Fixing one side only is half a fix. The frames keep the "as your ENTIRE reply" habit, which is still the right advice and works in every position; only the mechanism clause changed. Say the word and I will split it out.

## Verification

- `agentMessageService.chatNoise.test.js` — 18/18. Six new cases: the exact AX-43 shape, a leading run, mid/trailing unchanged, backticked and fenced mentions preserved, and both word-boundary controls (`NO_REPLYING`, `NO_REPLY_MODE`).
- All `agentMessageService` + `agentMentionService` suites — 221/221.
- `systemExchangeTriggers` + `threadWakeScope` — 30/30. `findPreviousNonSilentMessage` re-sanitizes stored history, so it is the one read-time consumer that changes behaviour.
- **Mutation-tested, three mutants, each caught by the test that names its line:** helper always-false → 3 red; word boundary dropped → 1 red (the boundary control); check hoisted above the fence return → 2 red (both mention tests).
- `tsc --noEmit`: 51 errors before, 51 after, none in either changed service.
- eslint on the changed files: byte-identical output to the baseline (backend `.ts` lint is separately known-broken — its own board item).

## What I did not verify

- Behaviour against a real gateway or wrapper. Everything here is unit-level against `sanitizeAgentContent` directly.
- Whether any stored message currently *opens* with a bare sentinel and would newly read as silent through `findPreviousNonSilentMessage`. The AX-43 leaks specifically are not affected — they were stored with the token already stripped — but I did not query the message store for other rows.
- Frontend or CLI copy that may restate the old total-match-only contract; I grepped `backend/` only.

## Summary

### Problem

`cli/src/main/java/io/github/cdsap/artifacttransform/cli/report/ArtifactTransformReport.kt` and `cli/src/main/java/io/github/cdsap/artifacttransform/cli/report/SingleArtifactTransformReport.kt` both own the same output workflow: create a timestamp, print a summary line, render `ArtifactTransformView`, write CSV, and write HTML. This duplicates presentation/infrastructure coordination inside the two report application flows.

### Why this matters

The next output format or filename/timestamp change must be applied in multiple places, which increases drift risk between aggregated and single-build reports. It also makes the report classes harder to test because fetching artifact transforms is coupled to filesystem-producing output fan-out.

### Proposed change

Extract the common output fan-out into a small CLI-layer collaborator, for example `ReportOutputWriter`, that accepts `transforms`, `single`, `timestamp`, and a summary message or report metadata. Keep `ArtifactTransformReport` and `SingleArtifactTransformReport` responsible for selecting/fetching transforms, then delegate rendering and file writes to the shared writer.

### Notes

Clean architecture lens: this keeps use-case selection/fetching separate from output infrastructure coordination without changing the repository's current package style or public behavior.

Fixes #90

author: nosmoht
body:
Closes #167.

## What changed

`tofu/modules/talos-cluster/README.md` gains a §"Staged machine-config roll
(Day-2)" section stating the contract a `staged` window imposes. The three
supporting edits: `examples/complete/main.tf` re-exports `node_apply_mode` (it
declared no outputs at all, so the shipped reference root could not produce the
signal the section relies on), `cluster.yaml.example`'s apply-mode comment
shrinks to two hard rules plus a pointer instead of a third prose copy, and one
CHANGELOG sentence is corrected.

## Why

#167 records a 2026-07-11 incident: a worker machine-config change rebooted a
whole worker set at once. Its three asks stand as follows.

- **Tier 1 (`-parallelism=1`)** is a consumer/orchestrator surface. This repo
  ships no apply lane — `grep -rn parallelism` over `tofu/`, `Taskfile.yml`,
  `scripts/` and `.github/` returns nothing. The issue's 2026-08-28 comment
  reports the guard live downstream; that is a tracker comment about another
  repository, unobservable from base, and is recorded here as **reported, not
  verified**.
- **Tier 2 (health-gated rolling in-module)** stays blocked and belongs to #129.
  The module pins `siderolabs/talos >= 0.7.0, < 1.0.0` with `0.11.0` in the
  lockfile; `talos_machine` exists only in the unreleased 0.12.x line and
  ADR-0026 §"Option 3" records that it has no `apply_mode` at all, so adopting it
  would remove the capability #239 added.
- **The third ask** — *"consider whether a worker machine-config change should be
  a manual `talosctl`-per-node lane"* — is what this PR answers. #166 closed via
  #239 shipped the mechanism; nothing then told a consumer what opening a window
  commits them to.

## Why the procedure itself is not here

An earlier revision of this branch carried a 340-line command-level runbook. It
was cut deliberately. The reboot sequence needs a health gate only the workload's
owner can define, and rehearsing it needs a cluster this repository does not
have; three review rounds could not stabilise it, with each round's findings
being defects introduced by the previous round's fixes — twice including factual
errors, about which Cilium taints the operator tolerates and about which patches
reach a worker. The invariants below survived all three rounds untouched, which
is the evidence for drawing the boundary where it now sits. The sequence is named
as a consumer-side procedure.

## What the section states

Revert last, or the un-gated nodes reboot together. Which inputs reach which
role, as an exclusion rule so it cannot go stale — only the two role patch lists
and a per-node patch are role-scoped; the controlplane-seed inputs (ArgoCD,
Gateway API, cert-approver, every Cilium input but `deploy_cilium` /
`cilium_kube_proxy_replacement`) have no Day-2 effect at all. Open the window
before the content or with it, never after. `node_apply_mode` reports
configuration and never node state, so the adoption ledger is the operator's.
Adoption is proven by reading the effective value back against a pre-window
baseline. Any boot adopts, so no upgrade and no new node while a window is open.
Cluster-shape bounds: single controlplane, `(n-1)/2` for etcd, and the Cilium
operator's second replica Pending for the duration of a drain (transient, clears
on uncordon).

Two facts are called out because they invert what an operator would assume:
from **Talos 1.14** apply-config never reboots on its own, so closing a window
reboots nothing and reboot-bound settings wait for an explicit `talosctl reboot`
— the risk moves from mass reboot to silent non-application; and
**`-parallelism=1` serialises the apply calls, not the reboots**, because the
apply resource returns without waiting for the node.

## Impacted components

`tofu/modules/talos-cluster` (README, shipped in the OCI artifact; example root).
No module behaviour change, no schema change, no spec `primary` source touched —
`spec:check-staleness` does not fire and no `openspec/changes/` proposal is owed.
The behaviour is already spec'd at
`openspec/specs/cluster-bootstrap-lifecycle/spec.md:91-115`.

## Validation

`task docs:lint`, `task tofu:ci` (113 tests), `task gitops:validate`,
`task spec:validate`, `task knowledge:validate` — all exit 0.

Honest scope of that: **`tofu:ci` binds only the `.tf` half of this diff.**
`tofu:fmt:check`, `tofu:validate` and `tofu:lint` sweep `examples/complete/`, so
deleting the module output the new block references turns `tofu:validate` red —
the only red-green binding in the change. For the README prose there is none:
`check-module-readme-parity.sh` scopes to `## Inputs` / `## Outputs`, and
`tofu:lint:yaml` is inert (`|| true` on both stages) and not in the `tofu:ci`
chain. `task docs:lint` is the only target that can fail on the prose, and only
on formatting; `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded by `.markdownlintignore`. A needle-grep
CI fence was considered and rejected: it would bind wording, not correctness.

Every factual claim is read from `siderolabs/talos` at tags `v1.11.0`–`v1.13.0`
and the v1.14 docs, or from this repository at the paths named above.

## Not verified

That a staged configuration is adopted on the next boot — ADR-0026's own open
predicate, which needs a live cluster. Named in the text.

## Breaking changes

None. Documentation plus one additive output in a non-shipped example root.

```
before   87 cases, 0 crashes, 42 divergences
after    87 cases, 0 crashes, 18 divergences
```

All 24 silently-accepted slots are closed. The 18 that remain are the wrong-**code** half, filed separately in `backlog.md` §3.

## Nine slots, six message families

That is the backlog entry's per-slot warning made concrete. Three would have been wrong by inference from a neighbouring slot:

- **`findAndModify.upsert` takes a bool OR any number** — `upsert: 1` and even `upsert: 1.5` are valid — while the adjacent **`update.updates.multi` is a strict bool** that rejects `multi: 1`.
- **`find.let` reports as `FindCommandRequest.let`**, mongod's internal IDL name, while `update.let` / `delete.let` / `findAndModify.let` / `aggregate.let` use their own command's name. Those three also diverged and are fixed here.
- **`find.maxTimeMS` is not a TypeMismatch at all**: code 2, with three distinct messages for a non-number, a non-integral number, and a negative one.

Probing also settled ordering: the type error fires **before** the namespace check, so `collMod` on a missing collection with a bad `index` is still the type error, not `NamespaceNotFound`.

## Two bugs found while probing, fixed with them

An explicit `null` was accepted for `find.filter` / `.sort` / `.projection` and for `aggregate.cursor`, where mongod rejects it. `doc.get(...)` cannot tell an absent option from a null one, so the null form slipped through the checks #1078 and #1080 added. Those slots now test membership; an absent option is still fine.

## Tests

`tests/test_arg_types_accepted_slots.py`, 79 tests — including one asserting **`delete.deletes.limit` stays unchecked**: mongod accepts `{}` / `"x"` / `[1]` / `0` there, so a blanket rule over this sweep would break it.

**Full suite 8303 passed, 36 skipped.** Worth noting how that number was arrived at: the first run reported 6564 passed and was invalid — `_secantus_core` was not installed in this checkout, so 1739 Rust-parity tests silently did not collect and pytest still exited 0. This is the trap `tasks/remaining-work-plan.md` documents. Caught by comparing against #1082's 8213 baseline; the wheel was built and installed and the suite re-run.

Python server, matching the two prior tranches. The Rust server has not been swept for this class and is not measured here.

body:
Adds a compatibility flag for coilbox's relay hosting (design: tomjn/coilbox#1696). A client needs to know before login whether the server has a relay, which is what LISTCOMPFLAGS is for.

This has to merge before any coilbox build starts sending the flag, otherwise the first relay-hosting release would tell its users their client is broken.

'r' goes into both flag_map and optional_flags. _checkCompat treats anything in flag_map but outside optional_flags as mandatory, so without the optional_flags entry every SpringLobby, Chobby and skylobby client not sending 'r' would get a spurious "missing flags" warning.

Also documents the flag in PROTOCOL.md section 4, matching the existing rows.

Closes #26
